articles.title: Does Christianity Make Sense? On God, Evil, and the Ache (with Gavin Ortlund)
articles.summary: Gavin Ortlund joins Collin Hansen to discuss apologetics and why Christianity makes sense.
articles.summary_zh: 加文·奥特伦德（ Gavin Ortlund ）与科林·汉森（ Collin Hansen ）一起讨论了护教学以及基督教为什么有意义。
articles.title_zh: 基督教有意义吗？论上帝、邪恶和痛苦（与Gavin Ortlund合作）
articles.content: Not long ago, my son asked me about all the people King David killed in 2 Samuel 8. We’ve been reading through that book during family devotions before bed. He’s right to be disturbed. So we had a conversation about why he’s unnerved, how we develop moral instincts, and how we’d respond to someone who rejects God because of these and similar accounts in the Old Testament. We did apologetics together. As he gets a little older, I’ll point him toward the YouTube channel of my friend Gavin Ortlund, who does an excellent job of answering many hard questions about Christianity and the Bible. Then, a few years later, I’ll point him to Gavin’s books, including his latest, Why Christianity Makes Sense: A Book About Jesus, the Mysteries of the World, and the Longings in Your Heart (Zondervan Reflective). He’s back on Gospelbound to discuss all things apologetics, from the multiverse, to slavery, to morality as merely a taste for sugar, to winning the lottery 10 billion times in a row. In This Episode 00:00 – Why people may be more open to spiritual answers today 03:36 – “The ache” and the longing for transcendence 09:29 – What about Christianity makes the least sense to Gavin? 11:39 – The problem of evil and the limits of tidy answers 19:09 – The growing challenge of divine hiddenness 24:34 – Fine-tuning and the odds of a life-permitting universe 32:07 – Is morality without God just a matter of taste? 37:25 – Slavery, the Bible, and the Christian roots of human equality 42:23 – Why fulfilled prophecy surprised Gavin 48:00 – What apologetic questions should Christians prepare for next? articles.title: I Was a Justice Warrior. I Needed the Whole Gospel. You Do Too.
articles.summary: Most Christians today see these two gospel aspects as part of the same biblical pie. But we often fail to see them as necessarily intertwined.
articles.summary_zh: 今天，大多数基督徒将这两个福音方面视为同一个圣经馅饼的一部分。但我们往往看不到它们必然交织在一起。
articles.title_zh: 我是一名正义战士。我需要完整的福音。你也是。
articles.content: From 2016 to 2018, I was a social media justice warrior. I spent my time on Facebook and Twitter confronting the powerful and comfortable, championing justice issues, and fighting for racial and political reconciliation. If you read my posts, you might not have guessed that I grew up in a conservative Christian home nestled in suburbia, or that I spent every day of my education, starting at age 4, in Christian schools. In my upbringing, I learned the rich depths of the Christian faith. I surrendered my life to Jesus, and I learned that Jesus came to seek to save the lost. Yet that evangelistically oriented world of my youth was intentionally sanitized and separated from the painful realities of poverty and injustice just 10 minutes down the road. When I discovered this disparity, I became a justice warrior online. And while that posture was certainly a reaction to my upbringing, I wasn’t being a hypocrite. My social media advocacy reflected my actual life. I’ve lived and worked in an underresourced neighborhood since 2001. During my first 15 years in the neighborhood, I grew burdened over the disconnect I saw between the conditions my neighbors faced daily and how many in the American church live. The political, racial, and socioeconomic divide between my church life and neighborhood gutted me. So when I went online, I was convinced I was sharing the true gospel. Yet that “gospel” I shared was merely centered on producing tangible results in the here and now, not on affecting eternity. What I needed instead was a holistic gospel, one that centers around both God’s kingdom mission and also his sacrificial death for sinners on the cross. Two Gospel Aspects I began to see two aspects in the biblical gospel. Let’s call them the gospel of the cross and the gospel of the kingdom . The gospel of the cross is the good news that Jesus Christ saves and adopts believers as his children through his substitutionary death and glorious resurrection. We’re all born alienated from God. In sin, we’re his enemies. In Christ, as we believe the good news, we’re reconciled to God (Rom. 5:6–10) and assured of eternal life with him (John 3:16). As Peter writes, “Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring us to God” (1 Pet. 3:18). Moreover, the cross aspect of the gospel emphasizes that those entrusted with this message must share it with a lost and dying world (Matt. 28:18–20). The gospel of the cross must be heralded; it must be proclaimed. It is the priority. From this gospel flows every good gift. What I needed instead was a holistic gospel, one that centers around both God’s kingdom mission and also his sacrificial death for sinners on the cross. The gospel of the kingdom is the good news that God’s will for justice, goodness, and peace is already being unleashed. As God’s children, believers are invited to play a part in seeing that kingdom mission come to fruition. Jesus begins his ministry by preaching a message that proclaims “good news to the poor” and “liberty to the . . . oppressed” (Luke 4:18). He calls his hearers to repent, including from ways they’ve oppressed and neglected the poor (Matt. 3:2; 4:17). He specifically rebukes the Pharisees for neglecting “the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faithfulness” (23:23). Paul, too, teaches that the gospel not only reunites us to God but also works justice by reconciling divided peoples to one another in the church. He writes, “For [Christ] himself is our peace, who has made us both [ethnic groups] one and has broken down in his flesh the dividing wall of hostility” (Eph. 2:14). We fulfill the law and live out the gospel’s kingdom implications through our identity as shalom -makers (Matt. 5:9). The kingdom aspect of the gospel equips us with a vision for pursuing God’s will “on earth as it is in heaven” (6:10), that is, for seeing all things made new (Rev. 21:5). 2016年至2018年,任社交媒体正义战士. 我花时间在脸书和推特上,

如果你读过我的文章, 你可能没有猜到 我成长在一个保守的基督教家庭 在郊区, 或者我每天的教育, 从4岁开始在基督教学校。 在我成长的过程中,我学会了基督教信仰的丰富深度. 我把自己的生命交给耶稣,我得知耶稣是来寻求拯救失落者.

然而,这个以福音为本的我青年世界被故意洗涤,并在仅仅10分钟之内就脱离了贫困和不公正的痛苦现实。 当我发现这种差距时,我成了在线上的正义战士。 虽然这种姿态无疑是对我的成长的反应, 我的社交媒体宣传反映了我的真实生活.

自2001年起, 在附近15年里, 我对邻居每天面临的状况 和美国教堂里有多少人的生活脱节感到负担沉重。 我的教会生活和邻居之间的政治、种族和社会经济鸿沟使我心碎。

所以当我上网时,我确信我分享了真正的福音。 然而,我所分享的“神灵”仅仅集中于在这里和现在产生实际结果,而不是影响永恒。 我所需要的是一个全方位的福音,它既围绕上帝的王国使命,也围绕着他为十字架上的罪人而牺牲的死亡。

我开始看到圣经福音中的两个方面。 让我们称之为十字架的福音和王国的福音。 十字架的福音是好消息,耶稣基督通过他的替代死亡和光荣的复活来拯救和接纳信徒作为自己的孩子. 我们天生都与上帝隔绝。 在罪恶中,我们是他的敌人。

在基督中,我们相信好消息,我们与上帝和解(5:6-10室),并保证与上帝永生(John 3:16). 正如彼得所写的那样,“基督也曾因罪恶而受苦,善人因不义者而受苦,以便他把我们带到上帝面前”(第3:18页)。

此外,福音的交叉方面强调,受委托传达这一信息的人必须与一个迷失和垂死的世界分享(Matt. 28:18-20)。 十字架的福音必须预告;必须宣布。 这是优先事项。 从这个福音中流传着每一个好礼物.

我所需要的是一个全方位的福音,它既围绕上帝的王国使命,也围绕着他为十字架上的罪人而牺牲的死亡。 王国的福音是好消息,上帝对正义、善良与和平的意志已经释放。 作为上帝的子孙,信徒们被邀请在确保王国使命取得成果方面发挥作用。

耶稣在部里首先发出一个信息,宣称“向穷人提供好消息”和“向......受压迫的人提供自由”(公爵4:18)。 他呼吁他的听众悔改,包括他们压迫和忽视穷人的方式(Matt. 3:2;4:17)。 他特别斥责法利赛人忽视“较重要的法律事项:正义、慈悲和忠诚”(23:23)。

保罗也教导道,福音不仅使我们与上帝团聚,而且通过在教会中调和分裂的人民来伸张正义。 他写道,“[基督]自己是我们的和平,他使我们两个[种族群 都成了和平,并用他的肉体打破了敌对的分隔墙”(Eph 2:14)。

我们履行法律,通过我们作为立法者的身份,活出福音的王国影响(马特:9)。 福音的王国方面为我们提供了追求上帝的旨意的愿景,即 " 在地上像在天上一样 " (6:10),即看到一切事物都变新(Rev.21:5)。 王国的福音 必须通过神圣的 行动而存在

articles.title: Lessons from Lloyd-Jones on Preaching and Politics
articles.summary: Here are three lessons we can learn from Martyn Lloyd-Jones’s ministry in a time of political crisis.
articles.summary_zh: 在政治危机时期，我们可以从马丁·劳埃德-琼斯（ Martyn Lloyd-Jones ）的事工中学到三个教训。
articles.title_zh: 劳埃德-琼斯关于讲道和政治的教训
articles.content: “I was never worried for a second about a man like Hitler.” This isn’t the statement of a madman or of someone privileged enough to be removed from the horrors of the war. These are the words of a pastor who was under immediate threat from the Nazi leader and who’d put on the full armor of God and prepared for battle. Adolf Hitler invaded Poland on September 1, 1939; the very next day, Martyn Lloyd-Jones was installed as an associate pastor at Westminster Chapel in London, where he would faithfully preach for the next 30 years. One year after the preacher took the pulpit, Hitler began his bombing campaign over London. Of the roughly 700 churches in the area, 624 were damaged by the bombings and 91 were totally destroyed. To the surprise of many, Westminster Chapel, one of London’s largest churches at the time, wasn’t destroyed in the bombing blitz. Iain Murray, in his classic biography on Lloyd-Jones , writes about one Sunday morning when a bomb hit close to the Chapel right in the middle of Lloyd-Jones’s Lord’s Day prayer. The bomb shook the entire building, and plaster and dust fell down on the congregation, including on “the Doctor,” as Lloyd-Jones was known. After a pause, Lloyd-Jones simply continued his prayer and the service went forward unimpeded. Lloyd-Jones offers a needed corrective to our politically anxious times. Some Christians resort to despair, while others attempt revolution. What we need is a political theology that still preaches Christ when the bombs go off. Here are three lessons we can learn from Lloyd-Jones’s ministry in a time of political crisis. Refuse Saul’s Armour When it became apparent that England was entering the war, Lloyd-Jones sent his wife and their two children back to Wales and away from the city, not knowing what would become of it. In a brief and urgent correspondence to his wife, he writes , “Leave yourself and me too, and everything in God’s hand and you will find peace and rest.” With bombs flying overhead, many in the church were calling for a revolution, but Lloyd-Jones was calling for prayer. With bombs flying overhead, many in the church were calling for a revolution, but Lloyd-Jones was calling for prayer. Because of fear and panic, many began to abandon the weapons of the church and replace them with the weapons of the state. But Lloyd-Jones refused to blur the lines. When the war was at its worst and his congregation had been reduced to few because of death and displacement, he remained resolute in affirming 2 Corinthians 10:4: “The weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds” (KJV). Lloyd-Jones refused to allow revolutionary alliances and tactics to infiltrate the church: Alas, far too often the church has tried to meet the world and its persecuting power with like weapons to those employed by the enemy. She has made alliances with the state and she has tried to strengthen herself in a material sense. She has been slow to discover what David discovered long ago in his fight with Goliath, that she cannot fight in the armour of Saul, but must ever use her own weapons with which she is familiar and with which she is meant to use. Lloyd-Jones saw a parallel between those in Saul’s armory who were looking to outfit David for battle with new calls from within the church to align herself with the state. Like David’s pitiful sling, prayer may appear in the world’s eyes woefully insufficient weaponry against fascism. But God’s weapons are greater than the weapons of men. Reject the Partisan Gospel Lloyd-Jones saw that the church was particularly vulnerable to political idolatry when fear had gripped the people. Like the Israelites shaking at the sight of Goliath, we often feel the only reasonable response is to find our own “strong man” to fight our battles. 由于恐惧和恐慌,许多人开始放弃教会的武器,代之以国家的武器. 但劳埃德-琼斯拒绝模糊界限.

当战争处于最糟糕的状态,他的集会由于死亡和流离失所而减少到极少数时,他仍然坚决申明2科林斯人10:4:“我们战争的武器不是肉体的,而是通过上帝而强大的力量来拉倒坚固的控制力”(KJV)。

劳埃德-琼斯拒绝让革命联盟和战术渗透到教会中:唉,教会经常试图用类似武器来对付世界及其迫害敌人者的力量. 她与国家结盟,并试图在物质上加强自己。

她一直缓慢地发现大卫很久以前在与高丽的战斗中发现的东西,即她不能在索尔的盔甲中作战,但必须永远使用自己熟悉的,本意使用的武器.

劳埃德-琼斯在索尔的军械库里看到了一个相似之处, 与大卫的悲哀一样,祈祷可能出现在世界的眼中,令人悲哀的是,反对法西斯主义的武器不足。 但上帝的武器比人的武器还要大

拒绝Lloyd-Jones党福音书, 认为当恐惧笼罩人民时, 与在戈利亚斯面前摇晃的以色列人一样,我们常常感到唯一合理的反应是找到我们自己的“强人”来战斗。 在教会历史上,我们经常转向国家政治。

articles.title_zh: 带上你的圣经和你的霰弹枪：认识有史以来最多的佛罗里达教堂植物
articles.content: Sunday services at TruLife Church of Ocala’s newest campus come with a soundtrack of shotguns going off in the distance. Some attendees bring their own and check them at a rack by the door, the way other congregations check strollers. The campus is called BlackJack, like the range it meets at: Blackjack Sporting Clays, a shooting facility in Sumterville, Fla. The facility’s owners came up with the idea and asked pastor Michael Kirby about starting a church plant on the property. Kirby has a handy comparison for the place, which has four courses and a cart. “You rent a golf cart and you drive around and shoot clays at all the different posts,” he said. “It’s like playing golf, but you’re playing with a shotgun.” So it’s golf, but the clubs go off. The sanctuary, loosely speaking, is a pavilion enclosed in thick, clear plastic, with mobile air conditioners keeping the cool air in and the wooded views visible. An 80-inch TV and a full sound system play Kirby’s prerecorded sermon three weeks a month, so three Sundays out of four the preacher arrives by screen. He or another TruLife pastor preaches live once a month, and Kirby’s daughter-in-law, Taylor Kirby, leads worship. Seating is about 40. The church held a soft opening a couple of months ago and had its official launch on Sunday, Oct. 25, with Kirby preaching and a picnic lunch afterward. The day before, during a national competitive shooting event at the facility, volunteers handed out flyers and went door to door in the neighborhood, which is outreach with an unusually loud backdrop. The target audience is the person who came to shoot. “We are hoping to attract unchurched people who are coming to BlackJack to do some shooting,” Kirby said. “Maybe they wouldn’t want to go to your typical church, but they decide they could go over here under the pavilion and hang out.” Evangelism by proximity, in other words: set up next to the people with the shotguns and hope they wander over. Some of them already have noticed the music. Kirby says shooters have told him they can hear the worship from the service, and he is counting on it. “They might not come inside yet, but they’ll be out there worshipping in the middle of the grass,” he said. The worship set, it turns out, doubles as the range’s ambient soundtrack.

该设施的业主想出了这个想法,问牧师Michael Kirby关于在该地产上开办一座教堂工厂的问题。 柯比对该地进行了方便的比较,该地有四门课程和一辆推车. 他说:「你租一辆高尔夫球车, “这就像打高尔夫, 高尔夫球,但俱乐部会爆炸。

松散的说,圣所是一个被厚厚的,清晰的塑料包裹的展厅,移动式空调保持了凉爽的空气,木质的景色也清晰可见. 一个80英寸的电视和一个完整的音响系统每月三个星期播放Kirby预先录制的布道,

他说,“他们可能还没有进屋,但会在草丛中崇拜”。 结果发现,这种崇拜是环境音轨的两倍。

articles.title_zh: “Mogging”是柯林斯词典2026年的年度词汇
articles.content: Your friend’s sourdough mogs the loaf you spent all weekend proving. That sentence now has a dictionary’s blessing, because Collins Dictionary has named “mogging” its Word of the Year for 2026. Collins defines it as “outperforming or outshining someone or something, which can mean making them look inferior in appearance, confidence or status.” The word is believed to be short for AMOG, “alpha male of the group.” It started around 2016 in bodybuilding culture, where it named the most physically dominant guy in the gym, then turned into a verb and made the rounds in the manosphere. It’s everywhere now and mostly used with tongue firmly in cheek, which is the only way anyone should use a word that started as a locker-room pecking order. Carspreading made Collins’ list, which is what they call carmakers building vehicles longer, wider and heavier with every new model. SUVs were well over half of new car sales in 2025, and the parking bays are feeling it. The job market contributed ghost job, an opening posted by an employer with no plan to hire anyone. Collins cites a UK study finding that around a third of advertised roles fit the description, so if your applications keep disappearing into the void, that may be part of why. The lighter entries were friendslop, low-budget indie games built for playing with friends, and fricy, fruity plus spicy, as in pineapple and mango hot sauces. Bixie is the haircut between a bob and a pixie that Zendaya, Jessie Buckley and Helen Mirren have worn. Then there is P(doom), the percentage chance someone thinks AI brings about the collapse of human civilization, which is a strange thing to find on the same list as a haircut and a hot sauce. Collins writer Rachel Quin said much of the shortlist felt like one big mogging contest, with everything competing to be bigger, hotter and more dramatic than whatever came before. Her takeaway for the year is that resilience and a little fun may be the way through. Somewhere, a sourdough loaf is winning.
articles.content_zh:
你整个周末都用在了你朋友身上, 该句现在有一个词典的祝福,因为柯林斯词典已经将2026年的年词命名为"吞吐".

柯林斯将它定义为“表现优异或超越某人或某物,这可能意味着让他们在外表、信心或地位上显得低劣 ” 。 认为这个词对AMOG来说是短的,“群体中的阿尔法男性”。 它于2016年左右在健美文化中开始,在那里它命名了健身房中身体上最占优势的男生,然后变成了动词,并在manosphere进行了轮回.

这也是人们唯一应该使用一个以更衣室啄门为起点的词。 汽车的普及使得柯林斯成为了榜单,他们称之为汽车制造者,用每一个新车型建造更长,更宽,更重的车辆. SUV在2025年的汽车新销量中远超过一半,停车场也感受到了这种感觉.

就业市场为鬼子提供了工作,这是雇主张贴的空缺,没有计划雇用任何人。 柯林斯引用了英国的一项研究 发现大约三分之一的广告角色 符合描述, 所以如果你的申请 不断消失到空虚,

更轻的条目是朋友游戏, 低预算的游戏 与朋友玩, 和fricy,水果加辣, 如菠萝和芒果热酱。 Bixie是Zendaya,Jessie Buckley和Helen Mirren穿戴的波波和精灵之间的发型.

接下来是P(doom),即有人认为AI带来人类文明崩溃的百分率概率,这与理发和热酱一样在同一个列表中找到是一件奇怪的事情. 柯林斯作家瑞秋·昆(英语:Rachel Quin)说,许多入围名单都感觉像是一场大杂耍大赛,一切竞相比以往更大,更热闹,更戏剧化.

她这一年的外卖是 恢复力和一点乐趣 可能是过去的方式。 某处,一个酸面包正在赢得。

articles.title_zh: 德鲁斯基的金钱饥渴的巨型教会牧师正在获得他自己的Netflix系列， 12月1日首映
articles.content: The megachurch pastor Druski has been playing for laughs is getting a promotion. Netflix announced a multiyear deal with the comedian on Nov. 2, and the first project is Collect & Praise, a semi-scripted series built around that character. It premieres Dec. 1. Netflix describes a show where faith comes second to fortune. A money-hungry pastor and his unpredictable deacon scheme their way through scandal, chaos and controversy. Mike Epps plays the deacon. For Druski, the deal is about scale. In the announcement he said Netflix will give him the resources to build on his comedy and reach “a new global audience,” and his company, 4LIFERS Entertainment, will develop original programming for the service. Netflix is also licensing three of his existing projects, Coulda Been Love, Coulda Been Daddy and Coulda Been Records Auditions, along with a selection of his skits. John Derderian, the Netflix VP who oversees Next Gen Content, said Druski “has a gift for building characters that people can’t stop talking about,” and called Collect & Praise “just the beginning.” He started posting skits on Instagram in 2017 and now has nearly 40 million followers across platforms. Along the way he has been a team captain in the Super Bowl LX flag football game, the youngest host in BET Awards history, a TIME100 Next cover star and the top name on Rolling Stone’s list of the most influential creators, all according to Netflix. He has also been to church on screen before, as a co-star of Praise This, the Peacock church musical, and he has appeared in House Party and Livestream from Hell and in music videos for Drake, Jack Harlow and Lil Yachty. RELEVANT last caught him in December, when he and Timothée Chalamet unexpectedly broke into a Kirk Franklin song. He also presented at the NFL Honors, which Netflix says will stream on the service in 2027. Netflix posted an announcement video with the news. Before the series, there is a bigger stage. On Nov. 7, Druski hosts Saturday Night Live, which Netflix says makes him the first digital content creator ever to host the show. The premiere date, Dec. 1, is also Giving Tuesday.

articles.title_zh: Ally Yost ：你的价值从来没有被辩论过
articles.content: For a long time, I thought my worth was something other people could give me—or take away. If someone chose me, loved me, complimented me, or told me I mattered, I felt valuable. If someone rejected me, betrayed me, or made me feel replaceable, I began to wonder what was wrong with me. I didn’t realize how exhausting it was to live that way until I looked back at the patterns in my relationships. When trust was broken, I didn’t just grieve the relationship. I questioned myself. Was I not enough? Had I become boring? Was I somehow less lovable than the person someone chose instead? Rejection became more than a painful experience; it felt like evidence in a case against my worth. I know I’m not the only person who has done this. Maybe you’ve stayed too long in a relationship because being chosen felt like proof that you mattered. Maybe you’ve replayed a conversation, a breakup, or someone’s silence, trying to figure out what you could have done differently. Or maybe you’ve built a version of yourself that seems confident on the outside but still needs constant reassurance that you’re enough. It’s easy to let other people become the mirrors we use to see ourselves. The problem is that people are inconsistent. Their opinions change. Their attention shifts. Even someone who genuinely loves us can’t be responsible for defining us. When we build our identity on what other people think, we end up handing them a job they were never meant to do. I learned this in a particularly public way when my social media presence began to grow. I could spend hours reading comments, taking in every word as if it had the authority to tell me who I was. Positive comments made me feel beautiful, important, and impactful. Then I’d scroll a little farther and find criticism, and suddenly I was questioning my appearance, my choices, and whether anything I was doing mattered at all. The same person could feel on top of the world one minute and completely torn down the next—all because of a stranger’s opinion. Even praise can become an unstable foundation when we need it to tell us who we are. The issue wasn’t simply that some people were unkind. It was that I had given people’s reactions too much power over my identity. I was looking for a lasting answer in something that could change by the hour. At the time, I thought I needed to become more impressive, more secure, or more successful. But underneath all of that was a deeper question: Where could I find an identity that wouldn’t keep shifting? I had tried to find it in relationships, achievement, attention, and the approval of other people. None of those things could carry the weight I was placing on them. My answer began to change when I encountered Jesus in a personal way. I had grown up around Christianity, but knowing about God and understanding His love for me were two different things. As I began to read the Bible and understand the gospel, I started to see that God’s love wasn’t a reward I had to earn by being good enough. It was a love He chose to give. That truth challenged the way I understood worth. So much of the world’s logic tells us that love is something we earn: be attractive enough, successful enough, easy enough to love, and perhaps you’ll be chosen. But the gospel begins somewhere else. First John 4:19 says, “We love because he first loved us.” God’s love comes before our performance. I didn’t have to make myself worthy of His attention. Jesus had already shown me the depth of His love through His sacrifice. This didn’t mean every insecurity disappeared overnight. I still had to notice how quickly I reached for approval and how easily criticism could take over my thoughts. But I was learning to ask a different question. Instead of asking, “What do they think of me?” I could ask, “What am I building my identity on?” Instead of treating rejection as a verdict, I could remember that another person’s decision did not have the authority to define my value. That distinction matters because

articles.summary: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books. articles.summary_zh: 星期二是大多数出版商发行新书的日子. 以下是本周我们走过的基督教书籍, 包括《Prodigal Culture》、《Scroll Less Live More》和《朝圣者的进步》的绘画小说。 也见2026年10月的基督教新书和著名书籍(Plus a preview of 11月的预览) 本周的基督教书籍(2026年10月27日) 关于利维提库斯的最佳评论
articles.title_zh: 本周基督教书籍（ 2026年11月3日）
articles.content: Tuesday is the day most Christian publishers release their new books, so each week I let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. This week brings Andrew Walker’s diagnosis of our prodigal culture, a graphic-novel edition of The Pilgrim’s Progress , and Samuel James’s Scroll Less, Live More . On the academic side, you will find reference works and commentaries. You may also want to consider Trevin Wax’s liturgy for daily prayer. For each book, I’ve included the publisher’s description and its list of endorsers. Books for Everyone Crossway Prodigal Culture A People in Ruins and the Way Back Home Andrew T. Walker Endorsed by: R. Albert Mohler Jr., Carl R. Trueman, Allie Beth Stuckey, Seth Dillon, and Kristen Waggoner Publisher’s description We have forgotten what it means to be human. American men and women are feeling the despair of a counterfeit culture, one where polarization has replaced conversation, pornography is chosen over true intimacy, and marriage and family are postponed indefinitely. The resulting isolation has forced us to confront the truth: individualism and worldly systems cannot take the place of God’s design for humanity. This scholarly yet accessible study examines the effects of secularism, nihilism, and barbarism on culture today, and explains why a biblical worldview is essential for human flourishing. Andrew T. Walker skillfully confronts 10 pressing issues—including loneliness, sexual confusion, anti-institutionalism, and identity. Affirming that shared norms grounded in creation order are the solution to social decline, he champions a return to biblical standards of freedom, human nature, and purpose. Walker compares Western culture to the prodigal son in Scripture—a culture that has squandered its inheritance and must now decide whether it will return to the Father or continue living in squalor. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . Crossway Scroll Less, Live More 10 Healthy Tech Habits for Teens Samuel D. James Endorsed by: Paul David Tripp, Matt Smethurst, and Whitney Newby Publisher’s description Nearly every teenager carries a smartphone in their pocket. What was once an innocent tool, providing a quick escape and a promise of connection, has now become a world that holds us captive. Looking up from the tiny pixels and refraining from the incessant scrolling may be the rest that our souls need. Scroll Less, Live More offers teens and families 10 practical habits for navigating the world of technology from a Christian perspective. From the author of the Christian Book Award winner, Digital Liturgies, tech-realist Samuel James applies his ideas into action steps to help teenagers keep digital tools in their proper place. By addressing how technology affects our social interactions, sleep patterns, critical thinking, and much more, James helps readers see the wisdom in God’s perfect design and, as a result, resist the temptations prevalent in the smartphone age. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . Zondervan Get to Work Seeing Your Daily Grind as God’s Good Gift Jonny Ardavanis Endorsed by: R. Kent Hughes, R. Albert Mohler, Jr., Allie Beth Stuckey, and Colby Parkinson Publisher’s description Learn to avoid both passivity and burnout by discovering God’s glorious design for work—and how to labor, rest, and steward your time in ways that glorify God and maximize your joy. The average person will spend 90,000 hours working—a staggering third of their life. For many, these hours feel like a necessary burden, something we have to do. But what if work isn’t a punishment to endure, but a privilege to embrace—a divine “get to” rather than a grim “got to”? In a time of contradictory messages about work, hurry, and rest, pastor and author Jonny Ardavanis dives into Scripture to help you see work as a divine calling, guiding you to partner with God and find profound meaning and purpose in your daily work, whether you’re a plumber, a CEO, or a stay-at-home mom. Get to W
articles.content_zh:
星期二是大多数基督教出版商发行新书的一天,所以每个星期我都会让大家知道,我最密切地关注的出版商,我们刚刚走过了什么路。 本周安德鲁·沃克(Andrew Walker)对我们浪子文化的诊断,

在学术方面,你会找到参考著作和评论. 您可能也想参考Trevin Wax的礼拜。 每本书我都包括出版商的描述及其认可者名单。 为所有人出版的书 《十字路口的浪荡文化 A Ruins》 和《回家之路》 Andrew T. Walker 由R. Albert Mohler Jr., Carl R.

Trueman、Allie Beth Stuckey、Seth Dillon和Kristen Waggoner出版社的描述 我们忘记了人类的意义。 美国男女都感受到了假冒文化的绝望,这种文化的两极分化取代了对话,色情作品被选择而不是真正的亲密,婚姻和家庭被无限期推迟.

由此产生的孤立迫使我们面对真理:个人主义和世界制度不能取代上帝对人类的设计。 这份学术性但易于获取的研究审查了世俗主义、虚无主义和野蛮主义对当今文化的影响,并解释了为什么圣经世界观对人类繁荣至关重要。 安德鲁·T.

Walker巧妙地面对10个紧迫问题——包括孤独、性混乱、反机构主义和身份认同。 他申明,基于创造秩序的共同准则是解决社会衰退的办法,他支持恢复自由、人性和宗旨的圣经标准。

Walker将西方文化与圣经中的浪子相提并论——一种浪费了遗产的文化,现在必须决定是回到父亲身边还是继续生活在肮脏之中。 在亚马逊或威斯敏斯特书店买的 Crossway Scroll Less, Live More 10 Health Tech Habits for Teens Samuel D. 互联网档案馆的存檔,存档日期2013-12-02., p.

articles.content: Grace and peace to you, my friends. I’ve got a list of great links for you to consider reading today, then a brief look at some of this week’s new Christian books (plus a link to discover many more). Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals are excellent! Concise Reformed Dogmatics is a great deal, since the list price is $40. Also consider Nancy Guthrie’s devotional resource to help you pray for your children. The Discipline of Grace is one of my all-time favorite books. Over at Westminster Books, you can get the best pricing on Dissecting the Heart , a book that “brings some of David Powlison’s best insights to a new generation that is struggling to deal with its relationship to secular psychology and spiritual formation.” Recommended Reading May God Be Gracious to Us: A Prayer Before Election Day. As America heads to the polls, Christian voters may benefit from reminding themselves of the truths in this article and praying the prayer it provides. “On May 17, 1776, John Witherspoon stepped into the pulpit at Princeton on a day of fasting the Continental Congress had appointed for all the colonies. War had already begun and independence was less than two months away. Witherspoon, a Presbyterian minister and soon-to-be signer of the Declaration of Independence, called the occasion a ‘day of solemn humiliation.’ Before he said a word about the conflict, he turned his hearers’ eyes to the sovereign providence of God. He closed with a prayer: ‘God grant that in America true religion and civil liberty may be inseparable, and that the unjust attempts to destroy the one, may in the issue tend to the support and establishment of both.'” Looksmaxxing: The Normalizing of Vanity. Jacob Crouch: “To say it plainly, Christians don’t looksmaxx. However much we may be into fitness or beauty, we reject looksmaxxing on three levels: our worth, our temporality, and our purpose. Our beauty is temporary; and all our beauty is for His glory. Our beauty does not determine our worth, because our value is fixed in Christ.” A Wretch Like Me. This is a very well-written article about John Newton and the reason he chose to describe himself as a wretch. “When Newton wrote what would become one of the best-loved hymns of the Christian church, he was looking back on a life that had taken him to rock bottom – and into the horrors of the Atlantic slave trade. Reading ‘Amazing Grace’ is like witnessing a confession. You are invited into someone’s life, and its darkest parts are laid bare before you. But the hymn doesn’t only dwell on the wretchedness of sin; it celebrates the deep, satisfying transformation of its author. And what a transformation it was!” The Belly Dancer Grandmas. This writer tells about the unfortunate experience of seeing belly-dancing grandmothers and relates it to his experiences on the frontiers of missions. “I remember once seeing a Facebook post from a Melanesian friend, commenting on an American pro-transgender news report. A direct translation of her comment would be, ‘Look at this – the whiteskins have lost their minds!’ Now, it wasn’t that long ago, perhaps even as recently as her great-grandparents’ generation, that her own society was a cannibalistic one, trapped in its own temporary insanity.” Thankfully, God so often interrupts that temporary insanity. On the Naming of Death. Andrew Roycroft has a strong and moving article about the naming of death. “In this short piece, I want to reflect on our obsession and squeamishness about the grotesqueness of death and to suggest some ways our current season of the year might reveal our deeper cultural preoccupations. In a follow-up article, I want to think about the practice of naming the dead, and the importance of measured and authentic memorial.” Reader Responses to ‘What We Know—and Cannot Know—About Elisabeth Elliot’s Sexuality’. articles.title_zh: 问答的七条规则
articles.content: In our interview with Dr Chad Van Dixhoorn, Behind the Scenes at the Westminster Assembly , he mentions the noted catechist 1 Thomas Lye (1621–1684) and his seven rules for catechizing. Here, in an accessible format, is Lye’s explanation of his seven-part method. While some of the advice relates to his published version of the catechism, the seven basic steps or rules may be widely applied. The reader should note that Lye was so accustomed to catechising people by means of a ‘question and answer’ method, that even his instructions concerning catechesis are communicated in sequential questions and answers! Introducing the Rules for Catechizing Q. 1. Are there any rules proposed to be observed in catechizing? A. Yes. Q. 2. Is there a title to those rules? A. Yes. Q. 3. Which is the title to those rules? A. A form of examination according to the rules or method proposed to be observed in catechizing. Q. 4. Is catechizing an ordinance? A. Yes. Q. 5. Whose ordinance? Is it God’s? A. Yes. Q. 6. How do you prove it? A. I prove it out of Proverbs 22:6: ‘Train up (or catechize) a child in the way that he [or she] should go, and when they are old they will not [or at least they should not] depart from it.’ Q. 7. How many rules are there to be observed in catechizing? A. Seven. Rule 1: Read and Return Q. 8. Which is the first rule to be observed in catechizing? A. Let the question be barely propounded, and the answer returned. Rule 2: Yes or No? Q. 9. What is the second rule? A. Try the child’s understanding, whether he (she) doth discern truth from falsehood. Q. 10. How shall the child manifest that? A. Only by saying Yes or No, to such short questions as may be raised from the preceding answer. Q. 11. Where are they set down? A. Next to the answers. Q. 12. Why is this necessary? A. Because to repeat words, and not to understand the truths contained in them, is but to act the parrot, and profits very little. Q. 13. But how must the child be made to say Yes or No? A. Without book only. Q. 14. Why then do we use to read them? 2 A. For two reasons. 1. Because we should learn to read them exactly. 2. Because the oftener we do read them, and the better we do consider them, the more capable we shall be to answer them truly without book, if we should (at any time) be so examined. Rule 3: Check the Words Q. 15. What is the third rule? A. Try the child’s ability to express his (or her) knowledge of the meaning of every hard and difficult word or phrase in the preceding answer. Q. 16. What reason is there for this? A. Because we cannot rightly apprehend truths, unless we clearly understand the meaning of those words in which truths are wrapped up. Q. 17. What may be of special use for an help to the child herein? A. The Alphabetical Table at the end of this catechism Q. 18. How may I find any difficult word in the Table? A. Mark with what letter it begins, and then look for it under the same letter in the Table. Q. 19. How may I know the difficult words in the answers? A. Note, that every difficult word explained in the Table is printed with a black English character in every answer. Rule 4: Prove the Point(s) Q. 20. What is the fourth rule? A. Draw the whole answer into several doctrinal propositions (if it contains more than one) and bid the child prove each or either of them by Scripture. Q. 21. Why should the answer be drawn into several doctrinal propositions? A. For two reasons: 1. Because there are several distinct truths contained in several answers of the catechism. 2. Because the more distinctly and particularly any truth is proposed, the more capable the child’s understanding is to apprehend it. Q. 22. Why must the child prove each of these doctrinal propositions by Scripture? A. Because the Holy Scriptures are the only foundation and proof of infallible and saving truth. Rule 5: Observe the Scriptures Q. 23. What is the fifth rule? A. Take the several Scriptures annexed to the answer, and in order propose them distinctly to the child:

A. 因为我们不能正确地抓住真理,除非我们清楚地理解那些掩盖真理的文字的含义。 问题17. 向儿童提供帮助有何特别用? A. 本目录末尾的字母表 Q 18. 我怎么才能在桌子上找到任何困难的词? A. 标出它开始的字母,然后在表格的同名字母下查找. 问题19. 我怎么会知道答案中的困难? A. 注意,表格中解释的每个困难字,每个答案中都用黑色的英文字符打印出. 第4条:证明问题20。 第四个规则是什么? A. 将整个答案归纳为几个理论性建议(如果包含一个以上),并让儿童通过《圣经》证明每个或其中之一。 问题21. 答案为何应纳入若干理论性建议? articles.title_zh: 我对威斯敏斯特周三有什么期待？
articles.content: Next week marks the launch of a new video and audio resource from the Banner— Westminster Wednesdays . Each week our Communications Manager, Joshua Kellard, will be joined by a special guest for an in-depth conversation on the questions and answers contained in the Westminster Shorter Catechism. Here Joshua answers some questions about what viewers and listeners can expect from the series: Are these podcasts just for Presbyterians, or for a wider audience who may not be as familiar with the Shorter Catechism? These podcasts most certainly are for Presbyterians, but not exclusively so! The Westminster Shorter Catechism is an accessible and crisp statement of the Christian faith as it was recovered and clarified at and shortly after the Reformation. Therefore, I would venture to say that any true believer in the Lord Jesus who takes up the Shorter Catechism will find it to be a document that is rich, biblically rooted, encouraging, and edifying. We hope that these podcast episodes are all these things, too. And, I might add, not all our guests are Presbyterians! The point is to use the Shorter Catechism to help us understand and apply Scripture’s teaching What does each episode include? How long will each episode last? Each episode of Westminster Wednesdays begins with a reading of the question and answer for that week (sometimes there are two or even three, depending on the topic). Then we have an in-depth conversation on the biblical teaching covered by the question and answer with a special guest—usually a local church pastor, but we have a scattering of seminary teachers represented as well. Above: Some of the Westminster Wednesdays guests. The point is to use the Shorter Catechism to help us understand and apply Scripture’s teaching, especially with a view to helping all who listen to teach others in turn. We will often pause, for example, to ask how a father or mother might teach the truths covered on a given week to their children. The episodes are about 15 to 20 minutes in length. There is minimal ‘fluff’—we try to get straight to the topic at hand. How might the series help listeners in their devotions, and as they serve in the church? All biblical truth, seen by the light of faith, should motivate us to thank, praise, and love the Lord more. Given that the Shorter Catechism summarizes scriptural truth for understanding and for devotion, we should be able to see reasons to thank, praise, and stand in awe of God every week. That said, no merely human document should ever take the place of hearing and reading Scripture. The more time anyone spends in a confession or a catechism, the more they should be motivated to return to the Scriptures with fresh perspective and deeper hunger. We also hope the series will be a blessing to churches. For one thing, well–taught Christians are a blessing to the church. They can and should find ways to build up other members in the faith. It may also be the case that we have some pastors and elders watching or listening in. If so, we hope and trust they will be encouraged to consider whether catechesis could be part of their approach to teaching their congregations. Churches that practice both expository preaching and steady catechesis have often found these modes of teaching to be mutually reinforcing. Why did you choose to use the Shorter Catechism as a framework? There are quite a few Reformed catechisms out there, but only a handful are in frequent use today. The Shorter Catechism has the advantage of broad scope (there are 107 questions and answers in this ‘shorter’ document!) coupled with memorable expression. And, as Dr Chad Van Dixhoorn shares in our bonus historical episode Behind the Scenes at the Westminster Assembly (releasing 28 October), each of the questions and answers is a stand-alone unit—one doesn’t have to have read the whole document to understand what is being asked and answered. The reader is often struck by what might clumsily be called the theological or pastoral ‘
articles.content_zh: 下星期将推出来自班纳-威斯敏斯特星期三的新视频和音频资源。 我们的通讯经理Joshua Kellard 每周都会有一位特邀嘉宾参加, 深入讨论威斯敏斯特短卡捷主义的问答。 在这里,约书亚回答了一些关于观众和听众可以从系列中期待什么的问题: 这些播客只是给长老会的,还是给那些可能不太熟悉"更短卡通"的更广大的观众的? 这些播客当然是长老会的, 威斯敏斯特·肖特克·卡特克主义(Westminster Shorter Catechism)是基督教信仰的一种易懂而简洁的表述,因为它在改革期间和之后不久被恢复和澄清. 因此,我冒昧地说,任何真正相信耶稣主的人,如果接受更短的卡德克主义,就会发现它是一份富饶、圣经根基、鼓励和启发性的文件。 我们希望这些播客节目也是这些东西。 还有,我想补充一下,不是所有的客人都是长老会的! 关键在于运用更短的卡德主义来帮助我们理解并应用圣经的教导, 每集会持续多久? 每集"威斯敏斯特周三"以阅读该周的问答开始(有时根据话题的不同会有两集甚至三集). 然后,我们与一位特别的来宾——通常是一位当地教会牧师——深入讨论了问答中包含的圣经教义问题,但我们也有众多神学院教师的代表。 上:一些西敏周三来宾. 重点是利用"更短的卡德克主义"帮助我们理解并应用"圣经"的教义,特别是为了帮助所有倾听者依次教导他人. 例如,我们往往会停下来问,父亲或母亲如何向其子女传授某一周的真相。 剧集长度约15至20分钟. 我们尽量直截了当, 该系列如何帮助听众的奉献,以及他们在教堂中服役? 所有的圣经真理,由信仰之光所见,应该激励我们感谢,赞美,更爱主. 鉴于 " 更短的卡特克主义 " 为理解和奉献总结了文字上的真理,我们应该能够每周看到感谢、赞扬和敬畏上帝的理由。 尽管如此,绝不应仅以人类文件取而代之的是听取和阅读《圣经》。 任何人在忏悔或阴道中花费的时间越多,就越应该以新的视角和更深的饥饿来激励他们回到"圣经". 我们也希望这一系列会给教会带来祝福. 首先,教好基督徒是教会的福分。 他们能够而且应当找到办法,在信仰中培养其他成员。 也可能是有些牧师和长老在看或听。 如果是这样,我们希望并相信,将鼓励他们考虑,天主教会能否成为他们教会的一部分。 既进行说明式传道,又进行平稳天主教的教会往往发现这些教学方式是相辅相成的。 你为什么选择用"更短的卡特主义"作为框架? 那里有很多改革式的天主教,但今天只有很少的宗教经常使用。 Shorter Catechism具有广泛的优势(本文"shorter"文件中有107个问答), 而正如Chad Van Dixhoorn博士在威斯敏斯特大会(10月28日放出)的《幕后新闻》中分享的, 读者常常被俗称神学或牧业所震撼。

articles.title_zh: 讲道中的陷阱：一封关于申请的信
articles.content: The following letter was published in the December 2025 issue of the Banner Magazine. It is published here at the request of a reader who found it helpful, in the hope that its counsel might be blessed to others also. You can also listen to a reading of this letter on the Banner Podcast. Dear J______, Following our conversation about application in preaching, I thought I would send along some thoughts I have had over the years on the subject. I want to point out some pitfalls you may want to keep in mind as you train R______. The only reason I know about them is from spending too much time in them myself! There has been a lot of self–examination and repenting over the years for me in this matter. The first thought is that too often (even in some of the best books on preaching) we hear that the text drives the sermon. This is a half-truth. A potentially dangerous half-truth. I have seen a man so intent on expositing his text well (and he did it very well) that he did not seem to notice or care that a third of the people in the room walked out before he finished preaching because he went on so long and the last meal of the conference was being served to meet the constraint of local train times. A wrong type of focus on the text and its explanation can make us oblivious to the very people the text is for. A preacher who stands up to preach having spent ninety per cent of his sermon preparation time in the week concentrating on the biblical text has not sufficiently realized what preaching actually is. In their book Letters Along the Way D. A. Carson and John Woodbridge put it this way: A chief reason why so much of what passes for evangelical expository preaching is so boring and irrelevant is that the preacher has spent a vastly disproportionate amount of preparation time in exegesis and outlines, and so little in thinking through how the Word of God is to wound and heal (to use the language of Hosea). 1 So preaching is about people. Preaching is about what God has to say to people about their lives . The text for a sermon is what God has to say to people . So the text of a sermon is like the recipe for a dish. A good cook would never be so focused on a recipe that she did not stop to realize that this was not at all the type of food her guests would need or appreciate. She would have her guests in mind from the start. After all, the goal of a good cook is not simply a matter of a recipe or a certain dish. It is feeding and feasting people . People drive the sermon. People are the reason God has given us the message in the biblical text. The biblical text leads the preacher to what the people need to hear from God. But the biblical text is only a means . The goal is people—to bring them somewhere that God wants them to go. To enlighten them, change them, help them, console them, correct them, train them to worship and serve God. People-oriented preaching comes from a God-centred, loving interest in them . Text-oriented preaching may simply come from the preacher’s love for preaching, for exegesis or for theology. A physician may be fascinated by medical treatments. But the good physician’s real interest is not treatments but people whose suffering has called for those treatments. Just so, true preaching is about people. That brings me to a second, related thought. We are often told that in preparing a sermon the key is finding the main idea of the text. To consider this as the key is not a people-oriented point of view and does not produce good preaching. It produces preaching with lots of emphasis on ideas and little emphasis on application. The key to preparing a sermon is not to find the main idea of the text. It is to find the main goal of the text. Not ‘What does the biblical text mainly say?’ But rather ‘What does this text intend to mainly do for people?’ What does the text intend mainly to effect in the lives of people? What does this text aim to move the people to believe, to do, to become? Application! A. T. Pierson, i
articles.content_zh: 以下信件发表于"班纳杂志"2025年12月号. 它应一位读者的要求在这里出版,他觉得它很有帮助,希望它的律师也能得到他人的祝福。 也可以在"班纳·波德克特"上收听对这封信的读取. 亲爱的J-,在我们讨论申请布道后,我想,我将提出一些多年来我对这一问题的看法。 我想指出一些陷阱 你可能想记住 当你训练R. 我了解他们的唯一原因 就是自己花太多时间在他们身上 多年来,我一直以来都在自责自悔。 第一种想法是,太多时候(即使在一些关于布道的好书中),我们听到文字驱动布道. 这是半个事实。 一个潜在的危险 半真相。 我见过一个男人如此有意地公开他的文字(他做得非常好),他似乎没有注意到或关心房间里有三分之一的人在他完成布道之前就离开,因为他走了这么长一段时间,会议的最后一餐是用来应付当地火车时间的限制。 错误地注重案文及其解释会使我们忘记案文所要为的人。 一位挺身而出进行传道的传道者,在一周里,他90%的布道准备时间都集中在圣经文本上,但是他没有充分意识到实际的传道内容。 在他们所著的"沿着路"(Letrys A. A. Carson)和"约翰·伍德布里奇"(John Woodbridge)一书中这样写道: 传福音的宣讲之所以如此之多,实在是无趣而无关紧要的一个主要原因是,传道人花费了大量的不相称的准备时间来解剖和提纲,在思考"上帝之道"是怎样去伤口和愈合(使用"霍西"的语言)时却很少考虑. 1个 故传道以人为事. 意义在于上帝要对人们说 他们的生活 讲道的文字是上帝要对人们说的话。 所以布道的文字就像菜谱。 一个好厨师永远也不会把注意力集中在一个配方上,以至于她不禁意识到这根本不是客人需要或欣赏的食物类型. 她一开始就想着她的客人 毕竟,一个好厨师的目标不仅仅是一个菜谱或某种菜肴的问题. 它在给人们提供食物和盛宴。 人们驱使布道。 人们是上帝给我们圣经文本中的信息的原因。 圣经文本将传道人引向人们需要从上帝那里听到的. 但圣经文本只是一个手段。 目标是人们,把他们带到上帝要他们去的地方去。 为了启蒙他们,改变他们,帮助他们,安慰他们,矫正他们,训练他们去崇拜并服务于上帝. 以人为中心的布道来自以上帝为中心, 以文字为取向的传道可能只是来自传道者对传道、开教或神学的热爱。 医生可能因治疗而着迷。 但好医生的真正兴趣不是治疗,而是那些遭受痛苦需要治疗的人。 所以,真正的传道是关于人的。 这让我想到另一个相关的想法。 我们经常被告知,在准备布道时,关键在于找到案文的主要想法。 将此视为关键不是以人民为导向的观点,也不产生好传道. 它产生许多强调思想的布道,很少强调应用。 准备布道的关键不是找到文本的主要想法. 它是为了找到案文的主要目标。 而非"圣经主要说些什么?" 但更确切地说,“这个文本主要是为了什么?” 案文主要打算如何影响人们的生活? 这个文字的目的是要促使人们相信,去做,变成什么? 申请! A. T. 皮尔逊,i

articles.title_zh: 教条主义者反对教条
articles.content: The following excerpt is from James Walker’s The Theology and Theologians of Scotland , which we have just typeset and republished in a clothbound edition. Walker is here responding to the criticism of Scottish Christianity which faults it for being too doctrinal: Then, again, I think the idea has taken possession of many in our day, that Scotch religion is a religion of speculative dogma, with little in it of the personal Christ. Now it seems to me there is a great deal said at present about Doctrine or Dogma which means nothing. How can you act in regard to or feel about a thing, save as you have some conception and some opinion concerning it? You must have some opinion about the person of Christ, if He is to be an element in your practical life. How can He act on you otherwise? And, therefore, as you are Trinitarian, or Arian, or Unitarian, or Humanitarian, or something else, so will be the effect on you. And, in fact, the man who abuses dogmas is as much a dealer in dogmas as his neighbours. What is it but a dogma—generally asserted, indeed, with a fierce and contemptuous fanaticism, and carried out with a remorseless logic—that there should be no dogmas? Like scepticism, this sort of thing kills itself. Say what men will, all action, all organization, all religious or irreligious fellowship, is based upon a Credo. In regard to many who bring the accusation most readily about Scottish doctrinalism, I assert that there are none more doctrinal than themselves. The Broad Churchman maintains the doctrine of the Divine Fatherhood; puts that doctrine into definite conception; argues on the basis of that doctrine to immense conclusions, which make illusive a large amount of the deepest and most powerful experiences of Christian history. The Unitarian maintains the doctrine of the Divine Unity, and evolves therefrom proposition after proposition, overthrowing, as he thinks, all the life-giving Christian beliefs. The real truth is that orthodoxy is chary of the speculative. Mystery is one of its fundamental ideas. The Theosophic 1 belongs far more to heterodox Alexandrianism than orthodox Augustinianism. I do not think that it can be affirmed of Calvin, that he was as supreme in the metaphysical or speculative as in all else. Certainly our Scottish theology is not in any proper sense a metaphysical system, though there has been often a cloud or a halo of metaphysics about it, but the product in the main of an honest study of the Bible and a practical religious experience. The doctrines which have been prominently taught among us, such as the atonement of Christ, justification, the new birth, the indwelling of the Holy Ghost, are not in any sense speculative human reasonings, but transcendent facts,—mysteries which, according to all experience, tell with prodigious power on the human soul, and take hold of the deepest convictions of the least philosophical and cultured. articles.content_zh: 以下摘录出自詹姆斯·沃克的"苏格兰神学与神学",我们刚刚对它进行打字并重新以布满的版本出版. 沃克在此回应苏格兰基督教的批评, 然后,我再说一遍,我认为这个想法在我们这个时代已经占有了许多人, 苏格兰宗教是一种投机教条的宗教, 很少包含个人的基督。 现在,在我看来,目前关于理论或道格玛的说法很多,这毫无意义。 除了你对某件事有某种概念和看法之外,你怎么能对某件事采取行动或感觉呢? 如果上帝要成为你实际生活中的一个要素,你一定对基督的人有些看法. 怎么会 他对你另当别论? 因此,既然你是三硝基亚人,或亚利安人,或统一人,或人道,或别的东西,那么,对你们的影响也会是这样。 事实上 虐待教条的人 和邻居一样是教条商人 除了一个教条外,什么是不应该有教条的? 教条一般是用一种激烈而可鄙的狂热主义来断言的,并且以毫无悔恨的逻辑来进行。 类似怀疑,这种东西会自杀。 说男人的意志,所有的行动,所有组织,所有宗教或非宗教的研究金,都是建立在克里多之上的. 对于许多最容易指控苏格兰教条主义的人,我断言,没有什么比他们自己更多的教条了。 Broad Churchman坚持了神之父的教义;将该教义置于明确的概念之中;基于该教义而论证了巨大的结论,这些结论使基督教历史上大量最深刻和最强大的经验变得虚幻。 统一主义者坚持"神通统一"的学说,并从中演化出在命题后的建议,推翻了他所想的,所有赋予生命的基督教信仰. 真正的事实是,正统性是投机性的魅力。 神秘主义是其基本思想之一. 相较于正统的奥古斯丁主义,"神话一"更属于异体的亚历山大主义. 我并不认为卡尔文能被证实 他在物理或推测方面 和所有其他方面一样至高无上 当然,我们的苏格兰神学在任何适当的意义上都不是一个元物理系统,尽管关于它经常有云或光环的元物理,但主要产物是对"圣经"进行诚实研究并实践宗教经验. 在我们中间受到突出教导的理论,如赎罪、辩护、新诞生、使圣灵安息等,从任何意义上讲,都不是推测人类的推理,而是超越的事实,根据所有的经验,这些神话以对人类灵魂的超乎寻常的力量加以说明,并信奉哲学和文化最低的信念。 沃克17和18世纪的苏格兰神学和神学家,詹姆斯价格28.00美元 原价:28.00美元 现价:25.20美元 " 在自己的部门里学习更多的加进纸板描述认可 " 。 – NICK NESTHAM Book Direct James Walker(1821–1891)属于能够掌握一个国家神学文献的这一稀有阶层。 这本珍贵的书里有水果... articles.title_zh: 与安息日相关的「良心案例」
articles.content: The following is an excerpt from Walter J. Chantry’s Call the Sabbath a Delight (pages 96–102). When some Christians come to believe that it is their duty to keep the Sabbath Day holy, they become very fearful lest they engage in the wrong activities on the Lord’s Day. Such apprehension often takes the form of wanting very specific answers from a minister or a counsellor. May I go bicycle-riding on Sunday? Is it all right to go jogging on the Lord’s Day? Should I purchase medicine for a child with a sore throat? It is as if the believer is collecting a large list of items, next to which he is writing ‘do’ or ‘don’t’. This sort of inquiry regarding explicit details of behaviour is, unfortunately, encouraged by a type of church leader who feeds his ego by promoting himself as a kind of ethical guru. Wishing to be the ideal elder or conscientious teacher, this ‘leader’ offers direction in minute particulars of living. His style of handling practical issues of living makes his people utterly dependent upon his counsel. His people become incapable of coping with decisions unless the ‘oracle of wisdom’ has decreed exact permission or prohibition. Momentarily, it may seem wonderfully good fortune to have such an involved counsellor giving precise directives, but in the end it makes dependent children of those who ask. At the head of this chapter is printed Paul’s prayer for the Philippians. He asked the Lord to increase his flock’s knowledge and depth of insight. These gifts he desired for them so that they would be able to discern what is best when confronted with any decision. It was never intended that God’s people be given exhaustively itemized delineation of what to do in every circumstance. He did not place elders in leadership so that they might dictate what specific course to follow in every particular. He does not give divine revelation as to which alternative to choose at a given moment. Our Lord has given us the great principles of his word. Also, he has sent the Holy Spirit to assist our understanding, so that, in any given set of alternatives requiring judgment, the individual saint will be exercised in spirit. Only by inner wrestlings will he increase in discernment of what is best. In Hebrews 5:14 we are told that ‘solid food is for the mature, for those who have their powers of discernment trained by constant practice to distinguish good from evil.’ It may seem comfortable to have a list to tick off without thought. However, the truth is that such practice atrophies the mind and heart. General principles from God’s word are adequate guidelines to equip a Christian, aided by the Holy Spirit, to face every eventuality. The Sabbath Day is to be kept in mind. It is to be devoted with joy to the worship and service of God. This day is special and is not to be cluttered with our work or with the employment of others, except so far as will serve in God’s worship, in man’s necessities, and in showing mercy to our fellow human beings. God’s word is a sufficient guide. All that is needed is for the individual Christian to exercise his personal discernment as to what is best. Thus he trains himself to distinguish good from evil. Included in this exercise is the necessity of becoming independent of others. The fear of man’s opinion regarding your application of these principles must not keep you from applying the principles before God. This is a freedom of conscience given us in Jesus Christ. It must not be surrendered to anyone. Being subject to our Lord and his word demands that we keep ourselves free from the tyranny of human opinion, even ‘expert’ opinion. Many of the particular questions men and women ask cannot be given a definite answer. More rests upon motive and intent than upon the outward acts we do on the Sabbath. ‘May I go bicycle-riding on Sunday?’ Because younger children are not equipped to discern their own heart motives or the application of general principles, parents must make some rules for their households.
articles.content_zh: 以下是Walter J. Chantry的《安息日称为欢乐》(第96-102页)的摘录。 当一些基督教徒相信安息日是他们的责任的时候,他们就非常害怕在主日从事不义的活动。 这种担心往往表现为希望部长或顾问作出非常具体的答复。 我可以星期天骑自行车吗? 在主节去慢跑可以吗? 我应该买药给喉咙痛的孩子吗? 似乎信徒正在收集一大堆物品, 不幸的是,这种关于明确行为细节的询问受到某种类型的教会领袖的鼓励,他们通过宣传自己是一种道德的教义来养活自己的自我。 希望成为理想的长辈或良心老师, 他处理生活的实际问题的风格使他的人民完全依赖他的律师。 除非`智慧之神'下达确切的许可或禁止令,否则他的人民将无法应付决定。 暂时来说,让这样一个参赞提供精确的指示似乎是极好的运气,但最后却使那些提出要求的人有受抚养的子女。 保罗为菲利浦人祈祷。 他要求上帝增加他的羊群的知识和洞察力。 他想要给他们这些礼物,以便他们在面对任何决定时能够辨别什么是最好的。 从来没有打算让上帝的子民在每一情况下都详细分门别类地划分应做什么。 他没有安排长辈担任领导职务,以便他们能够决定每一具体过程中应遵循的具体方针。 他没有透露在特定时刻可以选择哪种选择。 我们的主给了我们他所说的伟大原则。 另外,他还派遣了"圣灵"来协助我们的理解,这样,在任何一套需要判断的既定选择中,单个圣人将会在精神上行使. 只有通过内在的摔跤,他才能提高辨别什么是最好的。 在希伯来语:5:14中,我们被告知,`坚固的食物是给成熟的人的,对于那些有辨识能力的人来说,他们通过不断的练习来区分善与恶。 有一份清单可以不经思考地删除,这似乎很舒服。 然而,实际情况是,这种做法会损害心灵和心灵。 从上帝的言语来看,一般原则是适当的准则,可以使一个基督教徒在圣灵的帮助下面对每一次事件。 安息日要记住。 其能以欢喜而奉献于神通之所礼拜及事. 这一天是特别的,我们的工作或他人的工作不会受到干扰,除非在上帝的崇拜中、在人类的必需品中和在对我们的人类同胞表示怜悯中服务。 真主的话足为引导。 需要的只是基督徒个人对什么是最好的个人认识。 于是他训练自己 以区分善与恶。 这项工作包括必须独立于他人。 人类对于你应用这些原则的意见的恐惧,决不能妨碍你在上帝面前应用这些原则。 这是耶稣基督赋予我们的良心自由. 绝不能向任何人投降。 服从我们的主及其言辞,要求我们远离人类观点的暴政,甚至 " 专家 " 观点。 男人和女人提出的许多具体问题不能得到明确的答案。 更多的取决于动机和意图,而不是我们安息日的外在行动。 我星期天可以骑自行车吗? 由于年幼儿童没有能力辨别自己的心脏动机或适用一般原则,父母必须为家庭制定一些规则。

articles.summary_zh: 我们都需要对上帝对所有众生和事件的主权统治有更大的敏感性。亚历山大·卡森（ Alexander Carson ）的研究《圣经所体现的天意的历史》（ The History of Providence as Manifested in Scripture ）可以帮助我们培养这种敏感性。以下是耶利米书第14章中他对犹大饥荒主题的评论：由于饥荒的存在， […]犹大的饥荒后：上帝的普罗维登斯显示首先出现在美国真理的旗帜上。
articles.title_zh: 犹大饥荒：神的普罗维登斯显现
articles.content: We all need a greater sensitivity to God’s sovereign rule over all beings and events. Alexander Carson’s study, The History of Providence as Manifested in Scripture can help train us in such sensitivity. Here are his comments on the subject of famine in Judah from Jeremiah 14: FOR the existence of plenty as of famine, the wisdom of this world looks no higher than to what are called second causes. God, it is considered, is no farther concerned in these matters than as the author of certain general laws. He has set the machine a-going, and it continues to work by its own construction, without any regulation of a superintending hand. Climate, soil, cultivation, need, it is confessed, favourable seasons, but any divine direction of weather is supposed to be unnecessary. Timely rain—or the want of it, is a matter below the attention of the Ruler of the world. The blight and the mildew, the wet and the caterpillar, are enemies with which the farmer is to struggle; but they are never considered as armies of devastation sent into the fields by a righteous Providence. The history of the Old Testament gives us a key to Providence in the production of famine or of plenty. God regulates the supplies of the children of men as exactly as if each individual of the human race had his rations assigned him by the angels of heaven every rising sun: ‘The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah concerning the dearth. Judah mourneth, and the gates thereof languish; they are black unto the ground; and the cry of Jerusalem is gone up. And their nobles have sent their little ones to the waters: they came to the pits, and found no water; they returned with their vessels empty: they were ashamed and confounded, and covered their heads. Because the ground is chapt, for there was no rain in the earth, the ploughmen were ashamed, they covered their heads. Yea, the hind also calved in the field, and forsook it, because there was no grass. And the wild asses did stand in the high places, they snuffed up the wind like dragons; their eyes did fail, because there was no grass. O Lord, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy name’s sake: for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against thee.’—Jer. 14:1–7. As in creation and in Providence, so in redemption, God hides himself in the midst of a blaze of light. In all his works he reveals himself, yet the enmity of the human heart will not allow men to see him. And what is most strange, the savage sees a divine hand in the works of Providence; it is unseen and denied by philosophical wisdom. The illiterate peasant hears God in his voice of thunder and storms, and acknowledges divine wrath in pestilence, sword, and famine. But the philosopher perceives nothing in all these but the course of nature. The wisdom of man makes itself ignorant of what the very beasts seem to feel. articles.content_zh: 我们都需要更加关注上帝对所有生命和事件的主权统治。 Alexander Carson的研究, 《普罗维登斯的历史》, 以下是他从耶利米14号对犹大饥荒主题的评论: 对于饥荒时存在的富足,这个世界的智慧看起来并不比所谓的"第二原因"更高. 据认为,与某些一般法律的制定者相比,上帝在这些事务上没有更多的关切。 他把机器设为正常运行,它继续按自己的构造运作,没有任何管制的上司手. 气候,土壤,种植,需要,是承认的,有利的季节,但是任何神圣的天气方向都应该是不必要的. 及时降雨——或者说,这是世界统治者不关心的问题。 荒凉和温和的、湿润的和毛毛的,是农民要与之斗争的敌人;但他们从未被视为正义的普罗维登斯派入田地的毁灭军队。 "旧约"的历史为我们提供了普罗维登斯产生饥荒或富饶的关键. 真主为世人的给养而加以管理,犹如每个人的给养,每逢太阳升起,就奉天天神所赐给每个人一样。 犹大哀悼而其中的城门枯萎;他们已变成黑色的;耶路撒冷的呼声已升起。 其贵人又将小人送入水中去:来入坑中去,又无取出水来;又以器物入空而回;自惭而自愧,自蒙而出. 因为地是分明的,因为地上没有下雨,犁地人感到羞愧,就把头盖了起来. 有之,后人又以地为牛,而弃之,因有草而去. 野驴们的确站在高处,他们像龙一样把风扑倒;他们的眼睛确实衰败了,因为没有草. 主啊!我们的罪过虽能证明我们的罪过,但求你为你的名字而行之;我们的背负是多的;我们确已犯罪了。 与创造和普罗维登斯一样,在救赎中,上帝将自己隐藏在一束光芒中. 在他的所有作品中,他都暴露了自己,然而人心的敌意却不允许人见到他. 最奇怪的是,野蛮人看到普罗维登斯的作品中有神之手;它是看不见的,被哲学智慧所否定. 文盲农民在雷和风暴中听到上帝的声音,在瘟疫、剑和饥荒中承认神圣的愤怒。 但是哲学家在所有这些事物中,除了自然的走向,什么也看不出来. 人类的智慧使自己对野兽的感受一无所知. 更多信息:卡森所著"普罗维登斯的历史"(The History of Providence As Expressed in Books by Carson, Alexander price from: $ 13.50 学习更多选择选项描述) 基督教徒最感兴趣的话题。 以天经为阅读者,并举出真主赐予信士们的慰藉。 264pp. Featured Photo(当作品在社交媒体上分享时可以看见),

articles.title_zh: 让苦涩的东西变甜的上帝
articles.content: The Israelites had just walked between the walls of the water of the Red Sea and watched as the Lord washed away the whole Egyptian army. They sang a song of triumph on the far shore of the sea, rejoicing in the fear that had fallen on the surrounding nations (Ex. 15:14-16) and looking forward to taking possession of the Promised Land in the near future (Ex. 15:17). But within three days they raised a very different kind of sound—a chorus of grumbling against Moses because there was no water to drink at Marah (Ex. 15:22-26). I wonder what they expected would happen after the Red Sea. A straight, unhindered journey to the land flowing with milk and honey? Instead the first thing the Lord does is to lead his people to the undrinkable water of Marah. There is no question that the Lord is the one who led them there—it is easy enough to take a wrong turn when you are following Google Maps, but not when you are following a towering pillar of cloud or fire! So why did God lead Israel to Marah? Is it because he is sadistic and cruel and takes delight in watching his people suffer dehydration and fear? Is it because he is really bad at geography? Of course not! In fact we’re told why he brought Israel to Marah in Ex. 15:25: There the Lord tested them. In fact, the whole wilderness is a place of testing. That’s the significance of the wilderness—it’s a hard place. Deuteronomy 8:15 calls it ‘the vast and dreadful wilderness, that thirsty and waterless land, with its venomous snakes and scorpions.’ God is training his infant son to trust him—and training is always painful. There are no short cuts, whether in the physical training of our bodies to make them stronger and faster, or in the mental training of our minds to increase our knowledge and understanding, or in the spiritual training of our souls to grow in godliness. Learning to trust God is not something we can do lounging on the sofa. It means being put into situations that are stressful, confusing, messy and complicated, when we don’t understand what is going on or see any answers. Anyone can trust God when things are easy; the real test is if you will trust God when things are tough. Israel’s failure Marah was Israel’s first test and they failed. They have been travelling for three days and haven’t found any water. Supplies are running low. Perhaps as they saw the waters of Marah in the distance they finished up their last reserves: ‘It’ll be OK—we can refill very soon!’ Imagine the relief and joy as the first to reach Marah fall down and scoop the water to their mouths. And imagine them spitting it out as they discover it is foul and undrinkable. They’re not just disappointed—they’re horrified . Panic seizes them. ‘What shall we drink?’ (v. 24) This is not like someone in a restaurant complaining that their steak is a bit on the tough side or that the soup is a tad cold. They are exhausted and dehydrated and they can’t see any way of getting water. Suddenly life is hanging by a thread. There is nothing unreasonable about their concern. That is not why they fail the test. They fail the test because of their attitude. They grumble: the word means ‘hostile complaining, verbal attacks of dissatisfied people.’ Why do they grumble? There are at least two reasons: Faithlessness . They do not trust God. They don’t trust his power (that he can take care of them) or his goodness (that he wants to take care of them). They should have gone to the Lord with their needs, humbly asking him to provide what they needed. And this lack of faith was due to… Forgetfulness . This is the diagnosis of Psalm 78:40ff: How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and grieved him in the desert! … They did not remember his power or the day when he redeemed them from the foe , 43 when he performed his signs in Egypt and his marvels in the fields of Zoan. The people had such short memories! It has only been three days since they walked through the Red Sea! It has been just a few weeks since they witn
articles.content_zh: 以色列人刚刚走入了红海的水墙之间,看着上帝冲走整个埃及军队。 他们在远海岸上唱了一首"胜利之歌",欣喜地感受到了降临于周边民族的恐惧(Ex. 15:14-16)并期待着在不久的将来占有所承诺之地(Ex. 15:17). 但他们在三日内,举出一种非常不同的声音,一种对穆萨抱怨的合唱,因为在马拉没有水可饮(前15:22-26). 不知道红海之后他们会怎样 直走无阻地去 充满牛奶和蜂蜜的土地? 取而代之的是,主所行之事,是引其民入于马拉所出不可饮之水也. 毫无疑问,主是带领他们到那里去的——当你遵循Google地图时,很容易错转,但当你遵循高耸起的云柱或火柱时,就不是了! 那么为什么上帝带领以色列找到马拉? 是不是因为他是虐待狂和残忍的,在看着他的人民遭受脱水和恐惧时感到愉快? 是不是因为他在地理上很不好? 当然不是! 事实上我们被告知他为何在前15:25将以色列带到马拉:上帝在那里测试过他们。 事实上,整个荒地都是试验地. 这是荒野的意义, 8: 15 脱胎手术称之为:"大而可怕的荒野, 渴而无水之地, 有毒蛇和蝎子. 真主正在训练他的儿子,以便他信任他。训练确是痛苦的。 无论是身体锻炼,使其更强而更快,还是心灵修炼,以增进我们的知识和理解,或是心灵修炼,以在教化中成长,都没有任何短短的削减. 学会相信上帝不是我们能在沙发上做的事 这表示当我们不明白发生了什么情况或看到答案时, 当事情变得容易的时候,任何人都可以信任真主;真正的考验是,如果事情变得艰难的时候,你们要信任真主的话。 以色列的失败马拉是以色列的第一个考验, 他们已经旅行了三天, 补给不足。 也许当他们看到马拉的海水, 想象一下,解脱和欢乐是第一个到达马拉的人倒下,把水灌入口中. 想象一下他们发现它肮脏而不可饮用时就吐出它. 他们不仅失望, 恐慌抓住他们。 我们喝什么? (v.24) 这不像餐馆里有人抱怨 他们的牛排有点硬 或者汤有点冷 他们已经精疲力竭并脱水, 突然间,生命被一丝一缕地挂起 他们的关切没有什么不合理的。 这并不是他们失败的原因。 他们因为态度而未能通过测试. 他们抱怨道:这个词的意思是“敌意抱怨, 他们为什么抱怨? 至少有两个原因:失信。 他们不相信上帝。 他们不相信他的能力(他能照顾他们)或善良(他想照顾他们), 他们应该带着自己的需要去主那里,谦卑地要求他提供他们需要的东西. 缺乏信心是因为... 这就是对"诗经"78:40ff的诊断:他们在荒野中频繁地反抗他,在沙漠中为他悲伤!...... 他们不记得他的威力,也不记得他从敌人手中赎回他们的那一天,43岁时他在埃及行过他的迹象,他在Zoan地上行过他的奇事。 人们记忆很短! 他们从红海走过才三天! 几周前他们才开始

articles.summary_zh: 费丝·库克（ Faith Cook ）的《麻烦之旅》（ Troubled Journey ）讲述了她作为OMF中国传教士的女儿的早期经历。为了表彰父母的信仰、勇气和自我牺牲，她还富有同情心地揭示了与父母长期分离所带来的家庭剥夺。下面的摘录是该书的第11章，其中[…]邮政父母：传教士儿童的经历首先出现在美国真理旗帜上。
articles.title_zh: 邮政父母：传教士儿童的经历
articles.content: Faith Cook’s Troubled Journey narrates her early experiences as the daughter of OMF missionaries to China. Honouring the faith, courage, and self-sacrifice of her parents, she also shines a compassionate light on the family deprivations brought about by long periods of separation from them. The excerpt below is Chapter 11 of the book in question, which cover Faith’s childhood between the ages of fourteen and eighteen. A passage on the P & O Carthage was booked for Stanley and Norah [Faith’s parents—Ed.] in early January 1952, only eight months after our family had first arrived back from China. It was a subdued Christmas we spent together that year, the last for some years to come. Frantic packing followed, purchasing school uniform and preparing for the long outward journey back to the Far East, this time by sea. A round of speaking engagements filled the days for my parents and seemingly eased the ache of the forthcoming separation. As the day of parting drew ever nearer, I noticed a new tenderness in their attitude towards me – a tenderness that only added to my distress. And at last came the day of departure. It would be four years before we would see them again. Photographs were taken on the steps of the mission headquarters, as all joined to wish the departing missionaries well. Norah’s expression told a story, as did fifteen-year-old Christopher’s forced smile, for in reality, the boy’s spirit was at breaking point. On we went to the station where our parents would board a train to Southampton. A large contingent of missionary personnel followed, for this departure was highly significant for the entire future of the mission, urgently seeking a new role for its operations now the door to China was closed. I found myself thrust to the back of the crowd as the train slowly moved off. Suddenly one more thoughtful friend spotted the irony of the situation and pushed me to the front to catch the last glimpse of my parents as they stood waving at the window of the train, my mother looking tense and tearful, and my father strained. Back at the mission home once more, we were at a loose end. No guardian had yet been appointed to care for us, although one or two kindly adults helped out if I asked for assistance. The Spring term would soon begin and I was glad. Some of my new clothes were too long and needed altering, and I discovered with alarm that the shoe repairer considered my school shoes beyond his skills to patch up. Never handy with a needle, I tried my best to turn up the hems myself. At last the third week of January arrived and I was on the train back to my well-loved school – a place I now regarded as home. Although soon immersed once more in all the trivia of boarding school life, I found time each week to write a letter to my parents. The first few letters were addressed to ports en route for Malaysia where the P & O Carthage would call: Aden, Penang and then to Singapore to await their arrival. Stanley and Norah treasured these schoolgirl epistles, storing them all up, until at last my father would present his married daughter with a shoe box crammed with letters dating from January 1952 until the time that he and my mother finally retired from missionary service in Malaysia more than twenty years later. These letters form a unique commentary on the development of a postal relationship with my parents that would form the bedrock of my security and development from a young teenager to womanhood and beyond. Faithfully my parents replied to each letter, commenting on my progress, chiding when they could sense my behaviour was becoming erratic, and offering advice as well as they were able. Not long after arriving back at the mission headquarters in London at the end of the spring school term, I discovered that a middle-aged couple had been appointed as guardians for the children of the missionaries: Louis and Nancy Gaussen. Understanding and kindly, they were well-suited to care for the children. ‘Mr and Mrs Gaussen
articles.content_zh: Faith Cook的"麻烦之旅"讲述了她作为OMF传教士去中国的女儿的早期经历. 她以对父母的信仰、勇气和自我牺牲的敬意,也为长期与父母分离所带来的家庭贫困而发出同情之光。 下面的节录是该书第11章,其中涵盖了费斯14至18岁的童年. 1952年1月初,我们一家刚从中国回来才八个月,为斯坦利和诺拉(Faith的父母——Ed.)预订了P & O迦太基号上的一段。 那年是我们一起度过的圣诞 几年来的最后一天 紧随其后的弗朗克包装,购买了校服并准备了远东的漫长出行旅程,这次是海上出行. 一轮的演讲为我父母提供了时间,似乎缓解了即将到来的分居的痛苦。 随着离别日的临近,我注意到他们对我的态度出现了新的温柔,这种温柔只会使我更加痛苦。 终于到了出发之日 四年后我们才能再见到他们 对特派团总部的步骤进行了拍照,因为所有人都希望离开的传教士们一切顺利。 Norah的言论讲述了一个故事,15岁的Christopher被迫微笑也讲述了一个故事,因为实际上,这名男孩的精神正在崩溃。 我们去了车站 在那里,我们的父母 会登上火车到南安普顿。 随即派出了大批传教人员,因为这次出走对传教团的整个未来都具有重大意义,因此紧急寻求为传教团的行动起新的作用,现在中国的大门已经关闭了。 我发现自己被推倒 在人群的后部 当火车慢慢地离开。 突然又有一位深思熟虑的朋友发现情况具有讽刺意味,把我推到前面,以抓住我父母站在火车窗前挥手的最后一眼,我母亲看起来紧张而泪流满面,而我父亲也感到紧张. 回到了任务之家, 我们处在一个松散的结局。 目前还没有指定监护人来照顾我们,不过,如果我想得到帮助,一两个成年人会帮助我们。 春季学期即将开始 我很高兴 一些我的新衣服太长,需要更换,我惊恐地发现,修鞋者认为我的校鞋超出了他的能力来补补补. 我从不用针指手画脚,我尽力自己把螺丝弄大 终于在一月的第三个星期抵达, 我坐上火车回到我深爱的学校, 虽然我很快再次沉浸在寄宿学校生活的三难之中,但我发现每周都有时间写信给我的父母。 最初的几封信是寄给前往马来西亚的港口,P&O迦太基会称这些港口为:亚丁,槟城,再到新加坡等他们到达. 斯坦利和诺拉珍藏了这些女学生的表皮, 把它们全部储存起来, 直到最后我父亲会向他的已婚女儿展示一个鞋盒, 里面塞有1952年1月的信件, 直到他和我妈妈20多年后终于从马来西亚的传教士退休。 这些信件构成了关于与我父母发展邮政关系的独特评论,这将构成我从青少年到妇女时代及以后的安全和发展的基石。 诚然,我的父母每一封信都回信,评论我的进展,当他们能感觉到我的行为变得不规则时,他们就会发号施令,并尽可能地提供建议。 在春季学期结束回到伦敦的使团总部不久后,我发现一对中年夫妇被指定为传教士子女监护人:路易和南希·高森. 理解和友善,他们很适合照顾孩子。 高森夫妇

articles.summary_zh: 六个帖子中的第四个帖子包含了阿尔伯特· N ·马丁（ Albert N. Martin ）在1984年旗帜青年大会（ Banner Youth Conference ）上给出的教学内容，展示了基督教生活的基本圣经神学。在基督徒的生活中，没有承诺或命令的危机经历是必不可少的元素。一些关于基督徒生活的教导断言， […]《基督徒生活中没有必要的危机经历》一文首先出现在《美国真理旗帜》上。
articles.title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有必要的危机经历
articles.content: The fourth of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. There is no crisis experience promised or commanded as an essential element in living the Christian life. Some teaching on the Christian life asserts that only a low level of Christian experience can be realized by the person who has not had a crisis experience subsequent to regeneration, or at least subsequent to conversion and to the beginning of conscious Christian experience. Furthermore, it is asserted that the crisis experience is both commanded and promised by God as the entrance into a qualitatively new dimension or level of spiritual experience, reality and power. Throughout the history of the Christian church there have been many different strands of this crisis teaching. There is what we might call ‘classic Wesleyan perfectionism,’ which concentrated particularly upon sanctification and spoke of a baptism of purifying fire, or of coming into a state of perfect love. It concentrated not so much on power for service or upon inward feelings, but on a crisis experience in which the power of indwelling sin was to all intents and purposes negated. I have read enough of classic Wesleyan theology to know that there are different opinions as to what John Wesley himself taught on the subject. But in a general descriptive manner this, I believe, is an accurate representation of old-style classic Wesleyan perfectionism. Then, too, there is ‘the old Pentecostalism’ in which the emphasis was upon a baptism in the Holy Spirit, generally subsequent to conversion, and invariably manifested by speaking in tongues: the way you knew that you had this baptism of power was that, when it came to you, you spoke in tongues. The primary focus in old classic Pentecostalism was the matter of power for service. Thirdly, there is the modern ‘charismatic movement.’ Like classic Pentecostalism, its teachers use many of the same passages in the Book of Acts to support their theory of this necessary crisis. So they emphasize that in most cases—although there are different schools among modern charismatics—it will be manifested by the speaking in tongues. Some are content to believe you have ‘got it’ if you have a season of holy laughter. Others, however, say that you have not spoken in tongues because you have some psychological hold-ups, and if these can be removed the tongues are there. You just have not given them utterance. Here the emphasis is not so much on a baptism of purifying fire (as in the case of old classic Wesleyan perfectionism), or the baptism of power (as in the case of old classic Pentecostalism), but more upon a baptism of joyful praise-filled experience. I have been speaking of generalities, but I believe they are accurate. Fourthly, there are the various forms of ‘higher life’ teaching. What they have in common is this: you are simply converted, simply united to Christ, simply regenerated, and then you come to a crisis of surrender and faith, in which ‘you let go and let God’ and appropriate the indwelling life of Christ. The common denominator is that it is a crisis without any external manifestation of tongues or holy laughter or shouting or jumping, but the end result will be new power to live a holy life—the emphasis falls upon the ability to be more efficient in the path of holiness. Fifthly, there is a kind of teaching which has both old and modern proponents. It focuses on assurance, and has been expressed in terms of the biblical language of a ‘sealing of the Holy Spirit.’ Some of the Puritans—Thomas Goodwin, for example—taught this. There have been certain preachers in our own day who have believed this very strongly and emphasized it repeatedly. The basic concern in this teaching is that, subsequent to regeneration and conversion, there is a crisis experience in which the believer enters into a qualitatively new dimension of assurance by
articles.content_zh: 阿尔伯特·N·马丁在1984年班纳青年会议上发表的包含教学内容的六篇文章中的第四篇,介绍了基督教生活的基本圣经神学. 没有任何危机经历作为过上基督教生活的一项基本要素得到承诺或接受。 一些关于基督教生活的教义主张,在再生后,或至少是在皈依后,以及自觉的基督教经历开始后,没有危机经历的人,只有低水平的基督教经验才能实现. 此外,有人断言,危机经历既是上帝的旨意,也是上帝的允诺,是精神经历、现实和力量进入一个全新的层面或层次的。 在基督教会的历史上,这种危机教育有许多不同的内容。 我们可能称之为“经典的卫斯理完美主义 ” , 它不是把精力集中在服务或内在感情上,而是集中在一种危机经历上,在这种经历中,罪恶的威力是所有意图和目的所否定的。 我读了足够多的经典的卫斯理神学,知道对于约翰·卫斯理自己教授的这个主题,有不同的看法. 但从一般的描述方式来看,我认为,这是对老式经典的卫斯理主义的准确表述. 也存在“五旬节派”的旧现象, 重点是圣灵中的洗礼, 通常是在皈依之后, 古老的经典五旬节主义的主要焦点是服务的权力问题. 第三,有现代`魅力运动'。 和经典的五旬节主义一样,它的老师们也用"行动书"中的许多同名段落来支持他们对这个必要危机的理论. 所以他们强调,在多数情况下,尽管现代魅力中存在着不同的学校,但用舌头说话将表明这一点。 如果你有一个圣笑的季节, 然而,其他人说,你没有说出舌头,因为你有一些心理障碍,如果这些障碍可以取出,舌头就在那里。 你只是没说 这里强调的不是净化火的洗礼(如旧经典的卫斯理完美主义),也不是权力的洗礼(如旧经典的五旬节主义),而是更强调充满欢乐的赞美经验的洗礼. 我一直在谈论泛泛而谈,但我认为它们是正确的。 第四,有各种形式的 " 更高的生活 " 教学。 他们的共同点是:你们只是皈依正教,只是与基督联合,只是再生,然后你们遭遇了投降和信仰的危机,你们在危机中“放手,放任真主出征”,而顺从基督永生。 共同的分母是,这是一场没有外在表现出舌头或圣笑或叫喊或跳跃的危机,但最终结果将是新的力量来过上圣生活——强调在圣道上更有效率的能力. 第五,有一种教学既有老的也有现代的支持者。 它侧重于保证,并用圣经中的"封圣"来表述. 一些清教徒——例如托马斯·古德温——教授了这个。 在我们这一天里,有一些传道者非常强烈地相信并反复强调这一点。 该教学的基本关注是,在再生和转生之后,存在着一种危机经历,信仰者通过下列方式进入了保证的质的新层面:
