articles.content: May the Lord be with you and bless you today, my friends. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include a couple of Christmas devotionals, a Greg Koukl classic, and Seth Lewis’s Dream Small , among others. In case it’s of interest, Audible continues to offer a great deal—three months of service plus a $20 bonus for $0.99/month. You can unsubscribe at any time. Recommended Reading A Manifesto for Phone-Free Church. This article offers a lot to think about when it comes to the consequences of using our phones in church. “Distractions in worship will be with us always, but that does not mean we ought to go out into the highways and the hedges and invite as many distractions as possible. And here, we should note that there are good distractions in church—I am thinking of those babies that cry and fuss and laugh at all the wrong moments. Good distractions remind us that church is more than our personal ‘alone time’ with God. We are part of a family.” The Missing Piece in John Mark Comer’s Quiet Time. I think Matthew Bingham’s review of John Mark Comer’s book is bang on in both what it praises and what it criticizes. “Though Comer identifies as a Protestant, he relies on numerous quotations from ‘desert fathers and mothers,’ medieval mystics, and modern Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox theologians to justify his cafeteria approach to spirituality. As in his previous work, he engages with few heirs of the Reformation. Comer insists that Scripture is essential, but, for him, it doesn’t stand alone. Consistent with this non-Protestant mystical tradition, the book strongly emphasizes subjective, immediate communication from God apart from God’s inspired words in Scripture.” Free Chick-fil-A For a Year. Did you know that Midwestern Seminary is home to Spurgeon College, which is an undergraduate school that exists to equip students for the Kingdom? This November, they’re giving away a year’s supply of Chick-fil-A! Head over here to enter to win and discover other opportunities to grow deeper in Christ this month! (Sponsored) The Pull of Rome and the Promise of Grace. Chris Castaldo writes about those who are drawn to Rome. “A member of your small group confesses, seemingly out of the blue, that he’s been attending Mass. Next, you hear a deacon wonder aloud if we really needed to break with Rome. Then a family member announces that she has ‘crossed the Tiber,’ meaning she has converted to Roman Catholicism. Such conversations seem to be happening with greater frequency in Protestant circles. But why?” 4 Misconceptions About Spiritual Warfare. Costi Hinn outlines four fairly common misconceptions about spiritual warfare. “There is a short list of Christian beliefs that have as much mystery as spiritual warfare. While some things are really clear in the Bible regarding demons and demonic activity, there is a supernatural element to the unseen realm that humbles even the most educated theological student! At the same time, it seems that many people have a variety of opinions based on their experiences, which is not necessarily a negative thing, but it can lead to a lot of misconceptions.” Slouching Toward Narnia. Personally I’ve been enjoying reading all the different perspectives on the growing information we have about the forthcoming Narnia film(s). I think Nicholas McDonald’s article is one of the best so far. He explains his formula for a successful film adaptation (Faithfulness to Theme + Thoughtful Innovations = Great Film Adaptation) and tells whether he’s feeling hopeful as he considers The Magician’s Nephew in that way. Four Corrections to Make When You Feel Guilty About Your Giving. I think most people feel guilty about their giving from time to time. When that’s true of you, here are some ways you can correct the way you think and act. What I’m Enjoying Every week I ask the readers of this site to tell me what they are enjoying and, therefore, what they recommend to others. Sometimes I like to give my own perspective on it. A Retr

愿主与你同在,今天祝福你,我的朋友们. 销售与交易今日的Kindle交易包括几个圣诞奉献,一个是格雷格·克克(Greg Koukl)经典,以及赛斯·刘易斯的"梦想之小"等. 如果有兴趣,Audible继续提供大量服务——3个月服务,再加上0.99美元的20美元奖金。 随时可以取消订阅.

推荐阅读无电话教会宣言. 这篇文章对于在教堂使用我们的电话的后果,提供了很多思考的机会. “崇拜中的分裂将永远与我们同在,但这并不意味着我们应当走进高速公路和树篱并尽可能多地分散注意力。

在这里,我们应当注意到,教会中有一些良好的分心——我想到那些婴儿哭出大惊小怪并嘲笑所有错误的时刻。 良好分心提醒我们,教会不仅仅是我们与上帝的"单独时间"。 我们是家庭的一部分。” 约翰·马克·科默尔的"安静时间"中的"失踪的碎片".

我认为马修·宾汉姆对约翰·马克·科梅尔(John Mark Comer)书的评论, 无论是赞美还是批评, 都令人振奋。 “尽管科默确定自己是一位新教徒,但他依靠许多来自`沙漠之父和母亲'、中世纪神秘论以及现代罗马天主教和东方东正教神学家的引文来证明他对精神的食堂方法是合理的。

和他之前的作品一样,他与改革派的少数继承人交往. 但对于他来说, 这并非孤立无援。 这本书与这种非抗议性的神秘传统一致,除了《圣经》中上帝所启示的文字外,大力强调主观的、与上帝的直接沟通。 一年免费小鸡

你知道中西部神学院是斯普琴学院的所在地吗? 斯普琴学院是一所为王国培养学生的本科学校。 今年十一月, 头到这里进入赢 并发现其他机会 在基督这个月更深了! (赞助)罗马的拉动和恩典的承诺.

克里斯·卡斯塔多(Chris Castaldo)写道那些被引向罗马的人. “你们小团体的一名成员承认, 接下来,你听到一个执事 大声问我们是否真的需要 与罗马决裂。 她已经皈依了罗马天主教。

这种对话似乎在新教圈子里更加频繁地发生。 为什么?” Costi Hinn概述了对精神战争的四个相当普遍的错误认识。 “有一份基督教信仰的简短清单,其神秘之处与精神战一样多。

虽然《圣经》中有些关于恶魔和恶魔活动的内容是十分清楚的,但是在幽灵世界中却有一种超自然的元素,即使最受过教育的神学学生也是谦卑的!

同时,看来许多人根据自己的经历有各种观点,这不一定是负面的东西,但会导致许多误解". 向纳尼亚走去 我个人一直喜欢阅读关于纳尼亚电影的不断增长的信息,

我认为Nicholas McDonald的文章是目前为止最好的一篇文章。 他解释了自己成功改编电影的公式(Faithinity to the Electric + Thought Innoversations = Great Film Refect),并说明了他是否觉得自己对魔术师的侄女有希望。 4个惩罚 当你觉得有罪 为你付出。

我认为大多数人对不时的奉献感到内疚. 当你这样做的时候,你可以用一些方法纠正你的思想和行动方式。 我要求这个网站的读者告诉我他们喜欢什么, 有时候,我喜欢自己来看待它。 调试器

articles.title_zh: IMB传教士到位，准备鼓励塞内加尔教会开展青年奥运会外展活动
articles.content: A Senegalese Christian shares the gospel with event volunteers during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo As athletes and spectators from around the world fill the streets of Senegal for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, missionaries and local believers are praying the event will leave behind more than medals and memories. For Carson West, an International Mission Board missionary serving in Senegal, the Games represent a unique opportunity not only to engage visitors with the gospel but also to mobilize local churches to take a more active role in evangelism long after the Olympic flame is extinguished. “This is the first Olympic event ever held on the continent of Africa,” West said. “For us, it was an opportunity to ask, ‘What are we going to do with this?’” The Youth Olympic Games, which began Oct. 31 and end Nov. 13, are taking place across three host cities: Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. Event organizers expect nearly 2,700 athletes, ages 14-17, to participate in 35 sports and represent more than 200 delegations. The Games have drawn a million spectators, and West reported more than 6,000 event volunteers are staffing all the venues. With so many people gathering in Senegal, West and his team concentrated on preparing Senegalese churches for evangelistic opportunities. “We could run and hide, or we could do this thing,” West said, recalling an early conversation with teammates. “We decided we were going to do this thing.” The 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, is the first Olympic event held on the continent of Africa. IMB Photo West serves as team leader for IMB work in Senegal, where ministry efforts focus on three areas: gospel engagement, church advancement and community development. The Youth Olympic outreach naturally aligns with the first two priorities. “Our approach has been to mobilize the local church,” he said. “This is their backyard.” Instead of relying on a large influx of international volunteers, though there is one volunteer team from the United States serving, the strategy has centered on equipping local believers. Senegal has four Baptist churches in the greater Dakar area. Many leaders representing the congregations, as well as other ministry partners, participated in evangelism training designed specifically for the Games. Church leaders and ministry partners in Senegal participate in an evangelism training session specifically designed to share the gospel during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo A key outreach method involves trading commemorative pins, a familiar Olympic tradition. Volunteers use the exchange as a natural conversation starter before offering gospel-centered materials. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code connected to a digital engagement platform adapted from previous Olympic and World Cup outreaches. Visitors who scan the code are directed to online resources and can connect with trained digital responders. Experienced volunteers in the U.S. are helping provide follow-up conversations. “We’re building on strategies that have been used effectively in previous Olympic Games,” West said. “It’s an easy, non-intimidating way to start gospel conversations.” Trading commemorative pins is an Olympic tradition. Volunteers use these pins to start gospel-driven conversations during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code that connects people to trained digital responders. IMB Photo The effort extends beyond Dakar. IMB teams and church partners are positioned in each of the three host cities. An IMB team, which includes three global missionary partners, is helping coordinate outreach efforts in Diamniadio, and an IMB team along with a Baptist church is organizing efforts in Saly. West believes the greatest potential impact may be felt not among international visitors but among Senegalese believers themselves. Senegal is approximately 95% Muslim and 0.2% evangelical. 对在塞内加尔服务的国际传教委员会传教士卡森·韦斯特来说,奥运会是一个独特的机会,不仅可以让游客接受福音,而且可以动员当地教会在奥运会火焰被扑灭后很长一段时间里在传教中发挥更积极的作用。 “这是非洲大陆有史以来第一次举行的奥林匹克活动,”West说。

articles.title: African workshop equips communicators
articles.summary: Participants say it will help bring attention to Bible translation movements in their countries.
articles.summary_zh: 参与者表示，这将有助于引起人们对自己国家圣经翻译运动的关注。
articles.title_zh: 非洲工作坊为沟通者提供装备
articles.content: Mike Arthur (GILLBT, Ghana), Daisy Kilel (BTL, Kenya) and Hellen de Bruijn (Wycliffe South Africa) working together at the communication workshop. (Photo: Mike Arthur/GILLBT) Nairobi, Kenya — Participants in a communication workshop say the experience will have a big impact on their work to bring attention to Bible translation movements in their countries. “I believe that communication will bring about a revival in the Bible translation ministry upon my return”, said Adelphe Dogue Syssa, Director for Communication at ACATBA in the Central African Republic. Dogue Syssa was one of 10 participants from across Africa gathered here for a communication workshop from 2-6 November, 2026. The workshop was led by communication staff members serving with several different Alliance organisations in Africa. The site was the BTL’s Christian International Conference Centre near Nairobi. This was the first in-person communication training event in Africa hosted by the Wycliffe Global Alliance in eight years. The workshop’s goal was to equip communication staff, who often take on several roles in their organisations, with the basic skills to serve across different areas of communication. Sessions included communication strategy and planning, interviewing and writing stories, use of design tools, social media and photography. Evans Abade, a communications assistant at BTL East Africa, attended specifically to develop his skills. ‘I want to gain skills in matters of communications’, he said, ‘but I know communication is very broad and we can’t do it alone with the team that we have. So when I heard that we are going to have the team from different organisations […] I thought of this is the best platform for me to gain skills.’ Rather than a single trainer, the workshop brought together staff from the participating Alliance organisations to share their skills and experience. The result was not only new technical knowledge for participants, but also a growing sense of community. ‘Now when I’m interacting with these people, I’m getting to know new ideas’, Abade said. The skills gained and the relationships built during the workshop could have a lasting impact. Dogue Syssa feels motivated to take his newfound knowledge back to the people he serves. CAR has 142 people groups and languages, many of whom do not have full Scripture. ‘Without communication, we cannot appreciate the relevance of the Bible translation’ he said. ‘Communication with churches and communities is essential.’ Isaac Forchie (CABTAL, Cameroon) leads group discussions during the communication workshop (Photo: Mike Arthur/GILLBT) Evans Abade (BTL, Kenya) and Adelphe Dogue Syssa (ACATBA, Central African Republic) share a joke during a break in the sessions. (Photo: Mike Arthur/GILLBT)

中非共和国基督徒废除酷刑行动组织通信主任Adelphe Dogue Syssa说,“我认为,在我返回后,沟通将使圣经翻译部恢复活力”。 Dogue Syssa是2026年11月2日至6日,来自非洲各地的10名与会者之一。

讲习班由在非洲几个不同联盟组织服务的通信工作人员领导。 该地是BTL在内罗毕附近的基督教国际会议中心. 这是Wycliffe全球联盟8年来首次在非洲举办面对面的通信培训活动。

讲习班的目标是使经常在其组织中起若干作用的通讯工作人员具备在各种通讯领域服务的基本技能。 会议内容包括传播战略和规划、采访和撰写故事、使用设计工具、社交媒体和摄影。

在BTL东非的通信助理埃文斯·阿巴德(英语:Evans Abade (film))专门参加开发他的技能. 他说:「我想获得沟通技巧」,

所以当我听说我们将会有来自不同组织的团队... ... 我认为这是我获得技能的最佳平台。 该讲习班不是单一的培训员,而是汇集了参加讲习班的联盟各组织的工作人员,分享他们的技能和经验。

其结果不仅是参与者掌握了新的技术知识,而且社区意识日益增强。 Abade说, 当我与这些人互动时, 讲习班期间获得的技能和建立的关系可产生持久影响。 Dogue Syssa觉得有动机把他的新知识带回他所服务的人身边.

中非共和国有142个民族团体和语言,其中许多人没有完整的圣经。 他说,“没有沟通,我们就无法理解圣经译文的相关性”。

articles.title: Who Is the God of the Bible?
articles.summary: Contemplating God’s names provides a deeper understanding of his being and attributes and a firmer foundation for our faith and hope.
articles.summary_zh: 沉思神的名字可以更深入地了解祂的存在和属性，并为我们的信心和希望奠定更坚实的基础。
articles.title_zh: 谁是圣经中的神？
articles.content: According to the Belgic Confession , God reveals himself to us in two “books”: the book of nature (God’s world) and the book of Scripture (God’s written Word). The primary way God reveals himself in the book of Scripture is by proclaiming his name. In this first of two paired lectures from TGC25, Scott Swain considers several of the names whereby God reveals himself in the Bible. Contemplating God’s names provides a deeper understanding of his being and attributes and a firmer foundation for our faith and hope. It also helps us better appreciate the ways God reveals himself to us in Jesus Christ. 根据贝尔吉克的忏悔书,上帝在两个"书"中向我们揭示了自己:自然之书(真主的世界)和天经之书(真主所写的文字). 神在"通典"中主要揭示自己的方式是宣布自己的名字. 在TGC25的两次对口讲座中,斯科特·斯温(Scott Swain)首先考虑了上帝在"圣经"中揭示自己的几个名字.

质疑上帝的名声为人们更深入地了解他的存在和属性,并为我们的信仰和希望打下更坚实的基础。 这也帮助我们更好地理解上帝在耶稣基督中向我们揭示自己的方式.

articles.title: ‘I Play Rocky’ Finds New Inspiration in an Old Story
articles.summary: ‘I Play Rocky’ is the latest pop-culture celebration of storytelling as agency: telling your story in just the way you want it to be told.
articles.summary_zh: “I Play Rocky”是将讲故事作为代理的最新流行文化庆祝活动：以您希望的方式讲述您的故事。
articles.title_zh: 《我扮演洛基》在古老的故事中寻找新的灵感
articles.content: Rocky debuted in theaters 50 years ago, in 1976—a bicentennial-year release that underscored the movie’s profound American spirit. Immediately a blockbuster and critical darling (the highest-grossing movie of 1976 and winner of the Best Picture Oscar), it has since become a pantheon film in American cinema. Rocky ’s Philadelphia setting and underdog, rags-to-riches story captured a hardscrabble American optimism, something that gave needed inspiration in the mid-1970s and resonates still today. Now in 2026—America’s semiquincentennial— Rocky is getting a theatrical rerelease. And a new movie, I Play Rocky (out today in select theaters) is telling the story of the iconic movie’s development, which is an underdog epic of its own. The movie, directed by Peter Farrelly ( Green Book ) and starring Anthony Ippolito in a breakout turn as Sylvester Stallone, is a refreshingly feel-good crowd pleaser. It’s the sort of well-made, intelligent, but also inspiring movie for grown-ups that feels like a dying breed in Hollywood. Movies About Moviemaking I Play Rocky (rated PG-13 for language) follows a well-worn template of a movie about the making of a classic movie. Saving Mr. Banks (2013) was about Walt Disney and the making of Mary Poppins . Hitchcock (2012) was about Alfred Hitchcock and the making of Psycho . Last year’s Nouvelle Vague was about Jean-Luc Godard and the making of Breathless . I Play Rocky is about Stallone and the making of Rocky . Hollywood loves making movies about itself: stories about storytelling, movies about moviemaking, actors playing actors. Hollywood loves making movies about itself: stories about storytelling, movies about moviemaking, actors playing actors. Self-reflexive inspiration goes back more than a century in cinema, perhaps starting with Dziga Vertov’s Man with a Movie Camera (1929). The 1950s produced classics like Sunset Boulevard (1950) and Singin’ in the Rain (1952), but the trend really picked up in the postmodern era in the 1960s and beyond: 8 ½ (1963), Day for Night (1973), Mulholland Drive (2001), Adaptation (2002), The Artist (2011), and Once Upon a Time . . . in Hollywood (2019). The list is long. A hallmark of postmodernity is a metaposture of knowing awareness—storytellers who know they’re storytellers and want the audience to know that they know. As postmodernism has given way to metamodernism , the trend of “movies about moviemaking” has continued, but in a slightly different register. These sorts of films are no longer merely metaexercises in self-awareness. The cerebral, cynical detachment of “films about filmmaking” like Barton Fink (1991), Ed Wood (1994), or even Who Framed Roger Rabbit (1988) has given way to metamodern expressions that blend cynicism and sincerity, self-awareness with earnest escapism. Steven Spielberg’s The Fabelmans (2022) is a recent example of a movie in this vein, and I Play Rocky has a similar feel. Even as it lifts the veil on the Hollywood myth factory and mines many laughs out of the fundamentally profit-seeking, money-centric nature of the movie business, it’s full of heart and soul. It has a joyful, hopeful, sincere, perhaps idealistic spirit (“I’d rather be an optimist and be wrong, than a pessimist and be right,” one character says). Refreshing Celebration of Marriage I also like how I Play Rocky celebrates the empowering beauty of marriage. The film opens with Stallone as a broke actor in New York, sometimes sleeping on the streets and at one point accepting a role in an X-rated adult film just to earn some desperately needed money (a dark part of Stallone’s past that the film plays for awkward laughs). He’s a lost soul with bleak prospects. But then he meets Sasha (AnnaSophia Robb), with whom he works at a movie theater. They get married and move to Los Angeles, and things start to turn around for him. As a husband and soon a father, Stallone feels more urgency to provide. articles.title: How the Lord’s Supper Fuels Spiritual Growth
articles.summary: Calvin shows us that the Lord’s Supper is fuel for spiritual growth, so we should come to the table expectantly every time.
articles.summary_zh: 加尔文向我们表明，主的晚餐是灵性成长的燃料，所以我们每次都应该期待地来到餐桌前。
articles.title_zh: 主的晚餐如何促进灵性成长
articles.content: Recently, I (and my peers) have experienced a number of parishioners converting to Catholicism. As I’ve talked to these converts, they’ve consistently brought up the Lord’s Table. They find encouragement in identifying the bread and wine with Jesus’s body and blood. I’ve heard statements such as this: Pastor George, I like the idea that Jesus was talking about the Lord’s supper when he said, “Whoever feeds on my flesh and drinks my blood abides in me, and I in him” (John 6:56). My faith just feels more real if I’m literally bringing Jesus into my body on a daily basis. While this phenomenon seems to be happening with greater frequency, it’s not totally new. Years ago, I served alongside a man at an ordination service for another pastor in our city. I hadn’t met this man before; I only knew he had until recently been a professor at a Reformed and evangelical seminary. This man preached a solid message on Jesus’s call for ministers of the gospel, and I thanked him for it. Then, the next day, I saw him being interviewed on TV. I tuned in just as he explained, I needed more realism than my tradition provided, so during lunch I would walk down to the local Roman Catholic parish and take the Eucharist. To unite literally with Jesus’s body and blood was more deeply satisfying to me than the “mystery of union with Christ” my church taught. So, I resigned my post at the seminary and went home to Rome. I could relate other conversations with those who have left the Reformed faith and joined the Roman Catholic, Orthodox, or Anglo-Catholic traditions. A similar theme runs through them all: the desire for a more transformational, sensory reality than what the Reformed view of the Lord’s supper provides. Is this critique valid? How would John Calvin respond to the critique that if you follow the Reformed view of the supper, you’re missing out on its power? Transformed at the Table Sometimes, in an effort to have biblically faithful theology, Reformed Christians speak only of what the communion elements are not . I’m painfully aware of my of shortcomings in this regard. This can inadvertently drive some believers to seek out a more “real” experience in other traditions. We can get caught up in debating the exact nature of the bread and wine and forget to ask the more pressing question: How should this meal change me today? Let’s look back at Calvin’s teachings on communion. When we do, we’ll recover a renewed vision for the table, one that sees it as a divine encounter that motivates a transformed life of profound gratitude and obedience. In short, Calvin shows us that the Lord’s supper is fuel for spiritual growth, so we should come to the table expectantly every time. In Calvin’s “ Short Treatise on the Lord’s Supper ,” he writes that the supper fuels the believer’s spiritual growth in at least three ways. 1. The supper assures us of our inheritance in Christ. Calvin teaches that Jesus uses his table to assure us of our inheritance. He doesn’t merely mean that the supper gives us a psychological boost. He means that assurance comes by means of a real union between Christ and the believer, and he means that our experience of this union is expedited by faithfully partaking in the covenant meal. Calvin shows us that the Lord’s supper is fuel for spiritual growth, so we should come to the table expectantly every time. In his commentary on Ephesians, Calvin writes , “Paul says that we are members of his [Christ’s] flesh and of his bones. Do we wonder then, that in the Lord’s Supper he holds out his body to be enjoyed by us, and to nourish us unto eternal life?” Calvin insists that by faith, Christians are made members of Jesus’s fleshly human body, so at communion, we experience all the benefits of spiritual union with him. Christ took on flesh so that in his ascended state, he might be a channel of righteousness to the believer, pouring into him all that Christ’s human life accomplished. articles.content: Abstract : Jonathan Leeman highlights the corporate component of conversion, pointing out that God not only reconciles us to himself through Christ but also to one another. While our (vertical) reconciliation to God is foundational and primary, our (horizontal) reconciliation to others is necessarily bound up with our salvation. Conversion makes us part of God’s people, and this corporate aspect of our salvation should compel us to join a local church. Editor’s Note: This article is taken from Church Matters, the 9Marks journal for pastors, in the issue titled Conversion . If your doctrine of conversion is missing the corporate element, it’s missing something essential. Jesus died for a people (see Mark 10:45). He saves us as individuals, and he saves us into a people. Salvation includes a family. If you’re not convinced, jump straight to these parallel statements from Peter: Once you were not a people, but now you are God’s people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy. (1 Pet. 2:10) If someone asks you how you became a Christian, you probably emphasize the second line in your testimony. You say something like, “I was living in sin apart from God. A friend shared the gospel with me. I recognized who God is and what Christ did in dying and rising again. Therefore, I repented and believed. Praise God, he forgave me and I received his mercy!” What a wonderful testimony. Don’t stop saying that! Widen Your Perspective But notice that Peter widens the aperture of the camera and tells us a little more about what happened in that same moment. In addition to moving from not mercy to mercy, we simultaneously moved from not a people to a people. That means our testimonies could include a little bit more. Like this: “I was living in sin apart from God, and I wanted nothing to do with God’s family, the church. A friend shared the gospel with me. I recognized who God is and what Christ did in dying and rising again. Therefore, I repented and believed. Praise God, he forgave me and I received his mercy! I also realized that—wow!—I was part of a family now, the church.” Do you see what I mean by the “corporate” component of conversion? We’re saved into the universal church. That’s not to say we should put the corporate element out front. One might think of N. T. Wright’s well-known line about justification being “not so much about soteriology as about ecclesiology; not so much about salvation as about the church . ” N.T. Wright, What Saint Paul Really Said (Eerdmans, 20 1 4), 1 1 9. This is a clear example, in Douglas Moo’s almost-as-well-known line, of backgrounding what the New Testament foregrounds, and foregrounding what the New Testament backgrounds (as cited in D. A. Carson, “Faith and Faithfulness,” Ligonier, February 1 , 20 1 0, https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/faith-and-faithfulness). There can be no true reconciliation between humans until individual sinners are first reconciled to God. The horizontal necessarily follows the vertical. Ecclesiology necessarily follows soteriology. Which is to say, the corporate element must not come first, lest we lose salvation altogether. Vertical and Horizontal But it must come. Indeed, the corporate component must remain within the structure of the doctrine of conversion itself. Our corporate unity in Christ is not just an implication of conversion; it’s part of the very thing. Being reconciled to God’s people is distinct from but inseparable from being reconciled to God. These two elements of conversion are wonderfully put on display in Ephesians 2 with two instances of the word “but.” The first comes as Paul narrates man’s rescue from sin and death (vv. 1–10), which hinges on the words “ But God, being rich in mercy . . . ” (v. 4). Those words introduce God’s saving love and the fact that he has “raised us up with [Christ] and seated us with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus” (v. 6). articles.content: What marks Christians attuned to cross-cultural missions? They may not serve as full-time missionaries, but they embrace Great Commission responsibilities. The history of missions reveals little-known senders who used their vocations for strategic gospel advance around the world. Captain Benjamin Wickes (1746–1830) was one such man. ‘Old Captain Wickes’ We meet this early American captain of a merchant vessel unexpectedly at a prayer meeting in 1806. The missionaries in Serampore, India, had gathered to send Henry Martyn to a station on the Ganges River where he would begin his work of translation and evangelism. Martyn recorded that they “met at my pagoda this evening for the purpose of commending me to the grace of God before my departure. My soul never before had such divine enjoyment” ( The Letters of Henry Martyn , 194). I would love to have been there. The meeting included both Baptist missionaries — William Carey, Joshua Marshman, and William Ward — as well as evangelical Anglicans David Brown, Daniel Corrie, and Henry Martyn. It represented a substantial collaboration between these earliest English missionaries for the advance of the gospel in India. Since much of India was controlled by the British East India Company, only Anglican missionaries received official recognition and freedom to travel. Even they, however, could pursue missionary work only when not employed in chaplaincy duties to English people residing in India. Amid such challenges, this prayer meeting of gathered co-laborers was a high point for Martyn and a moment he remembered fondly. To the list of those present, Martyn added “old Captain Wickes.” He mentioned him again in another letter as “the good old Captain Wickes, who has brought out so many missionaries to India” ( Letters , 178). But who was this old American captain so well loved by the English missionaries in India? Missionaries as Risky Passengers Captain Wickes was born to a seafaring family in Maryland in 1746. His older brother, Captain Lambert Wickes, fought and died at sea during the American War for Independence. Benjamin first entered the missionary record in 1799, when the Baptist missionaries Joshua Marshman and William Ward sought passage to India from London. The situation was sensitive. The East India Company had forbidden full-time missionaries from entering, so no English ship would give Marshman and Ward passage. Carey had established his home in the Danish port of Serampore, not far from Calcutta, but no Danish ships were available. Wickes’s American ship, however, could take the risk of transporting missionaries. When he heard about the situation, Wickes wrote to Baptist leader Andrew Fuller, saying that “he had long cherished the hope of being privileged to convey the messengers of the Gospel to the heathen, and that his fondest wish was about to be gratified” ( The Life and Times of Carey, Marshman, and Ward , 110). The privilege came with difficulties. Although American ships were regularly received in East India Company ports, the presence of missionaries complicated their arrival. When Wickes arrived in Calcutta with Marshman and Ward, East India Company officials refused him permission to sail home unless he took the missionaries with him. By God’s grace, Wickes convinced the authorities of the missionaries’ good intentions. When similar circumstances occurred in 1806, he persuaded officials that detaining his American ship might cause an international incident. Each voyage involved protracted negotiations that certainly distracted from his primary trading business. Yet Wickes’s service proved invaluable. Every time the missionaries mentioned him, they affirmed their unbridled thanks for his efforts. William Carey wrote about him in 1805, “I, in common with my dear brethren and sisters here, feel much pleasure in hearing of the safe return to you of our much beloved brother in Christ, Capt. Wickes” ( Evangelical Intelligencer , 1:201). Marshman and Ward called him “th

威克船长 在1806年的一次祈祷会中,我们意外地遇到了这位早期的美国商船船长. 印度塞兰波尔的传教士们聚集一堂,将亨利·马蒂恩送往恒河上的一个站,在那里他将开始翻译和福音派的工作.

Martyn记录说,他们“今晚在我的佛塔相会,目的是在我离开之前赞扬我受到上帝的恩惠。 我的灵魂从未有过如此神圣的享受”(The Letters of Henry Martyn, 194). 我很想去过那里。

与会的有浸信会传教士威廉·凯里(William Carey),约书亚·马什曼(Joshua Marshman)和威廉·沃德(William Ward)等,还有福音派圣公会教徒大卫·布朗(David Brown),丹尼尔·科里(Daniel Corrie)和亨利·马蒂恩. 它代表了这些最早的英国传教士为在印度推进福音而进行的实质性合作。

由于印度大部分地区被英国东印度公司所控制,只有英国圣公会传教士才得到官方的承认并享有出行的自由. 然而,即使他们也只能在不受雇于居住在印度的英国人担任牧师职务时才能从事传教工作。

在这样的挑战中,这次聚集的同实验室的祈祷会是马蒂恩的高潮,也是他亲切回忆的一瞬. 在出席者名单中,马蒂恩加上了“威克船长”。 他在另一封信中再次提到他,称他为“威克船长,他把这么多传教士带到了印度”(信件,178)。

但这位老美国队长 在印度的英国传教士这么爱谁? 传教士作为"冒险乘客""威克船长"于1746年生于马里兰的一个航海家庭. 他的哥哥,船长兰伯特·威克斯(Lambert Wickes)在美国独立战争中出战并死于海上.

本杰明于1799年首次入传教记录,当时浸信会传教士约书亚·马什曼和威廉·沃德从伦敦寻求通向印度. 情况很敏感。 东印度公司曾禁止全职传教士入道,因此英国船只不会给马什曼和沃德通过.

凯里在离加尔各答不远的丹麦塞兰波尔港建立了他的家,但是没有丹麦船只可供使用. 但威克斯的美国船可能承担运送传教士的风险。

当Wickes听说情况时,他写信给浸信会领袖Andrew Fuller,称“他长期以来一直珍视着有幸将福音信使传达给异教徒的希望,而且他最亲切的愿望即将得到满足”(The Life and Times of Carey, Marshman, and Ward, 110.). 特权带来了困难。

虽然美国船只经常被接收到东印度公司港口,但传教士的到来使其更加复杂. 当威克斯与马什曼和沃德一起到达加尔各答后,东印度公司官员拒绝他出航回家,除非他带着传教士一起. 在上帝的恩典下,威克说服了传教士的善意权威.

当1806年发生类似情况时,他劝说官员们,扣留他的美国船只可能造成国际事件. 每次航行都涉及旷日持久的谈判,当然分散了他的初级贸易业务。 但威克斯的服务证明是宝贵的。 每逢传教士提到他,他们都申明他们无所顾忌地感谢他的努力.

articles.content: At one point, Joel Smallbone and his brother Ben went their separate ways. “You could argue we ended up on our own sort of opposite sides of life’s battlefield,” Smallbone says. What brought them back together was a movie about the same thing. “I remember saying, wouldn’t it be fascinating if two brothers who’ve had ideological differences and creative differences came back together behind the camera to tell a story about two brothers that end up on opposite sides of a literal war?” That movie is Drummer Boy , a Revolutionary War Christmas musical that opened in theaters Nov. 6. Joel and Ben co-directed it, and Joel plays Jeremiah Clem. The cast includes Ioan Gruffudd and Melora Hardin (Jan from The Office) . It took a while. Smallbone, who sings in for KING + COUNTRY with his brother Luke, pitched it to Lionsgate on March 10, 2020, and, by his account, the studio nearly greenlit it. “And then March the 13th happened and the world shut down,” he says. Unsung Hero came first and the musical waited. Someone eventually reminded him 2026 is America’s 250th birthday. “Well, maybe it was just always meant to be now.” The Movie That Wrote Him “Do you write the movie or does the movie write you?” Smallbone asks. “There’s never been a movie that’s written me more than Drummer Boy .” He lists the evidence. “We came up with this rendition of ‘The Little Drummer Boy’ at the beginning of our career. We’re called for KING + COUNTRY, which is a British mantra. We wore these revolutionary-type uniforms for many years. I’m in a band with my brother. This is a movie about brothers on opposite sides of the battlefield. I’m a musician. It’s a musical. You just see all of these breadcrumbs.” When he got stuck on the lead character, a director asked him who he was. “I’ve got a rescuer complex,” he says. “A bit of a savior complex. And so I just wrote all of it into the film.” Unsung Hero was literally about his family, so it’s fair to ask why this one feels more like him. His answer is allegory. “Jesus was the allegory guy,” Smallbone says. “He made up stories for a living, you know? I see myself more in it because it’s all allegorical about our life, and America, and me being an immigrant and in a mixed marriage, and brothers on other sides of the battlefield.” A Musical for People Who Hate Musicals “I need to clear up something to the musical haters,” he says. About 30 minutes of the film are musical moments, “very personal expressions of heartache or love or loss.” He calls it “ Hamilton meets The Patriot meets Pride and Prejudice .” His rule for when a character should sing is simple. “The best musicals put language to things that you couldn’t express through dialogue. The worst musicals just sing the whole time. And I’m like, just stop. That’s not life.” His example is Chris Martin writing “Fix You” after Gwyneth Paltrow’s father died. “You have to express yourself in grief, in pain, and a lot of times it comes through music.” The same logic runs through the film. One character, an enslaved woman, sings her way through being stuck. “She’s stuck and she’s enslaved and she needs to sing about it to understand it better,” he says. Two Brothers Behind the Camera The shoot gave the co-directing brothers plenty of challenges to overcome. The last day of filming was the big argument between Jeremiah and Emmaline on a hillside, in 40 mph winds. “She’s in this dress, almost getting blown off the hillside,” Smallbone says. “We were like, I don’t know if we’re gonna use any of this.” The wind made the cut. “The tragedy of the bad weather actually created a third layer to the scene.” The argument matters to the story. Jeremiah, Smallbone says, is “not practicing what he’s preached.” His father taught him “no boy or girl or slave or free, because all in one in Christ are we,” an echo of Galatians 3:28. Jeremiah is “chasing, basically, imperialism and hierarchy and climbing the ladder by who he’s gonna marry.” Heat was the opposite problem. On a day he puts

articles.title_zh: 想要帮助消除贫困吗？这里有五种方法可以开始
articles.content: In the mid-2000s, Ate Tina was working long hours at a factory in the Philippines and supporting her household alone. Ate is Tagalog for older sister, and it’s a title of respect. Seven months after her wedding, her husband developed a serious medical condition, which made her the only breadwinner. When she became pregnant, the factory’s demands stayed the same. “I ended up giving birth at home because I wasn’t allowed to leave work,” she recalls. Two months after her daughter was born, she was back on the factory floor and her daughter was in the care of others. Tina began to notice changes in her daughter’s behavior that worried her. She says she prayed in desperation for a livelihood that would let her provide for her family and be present with them. In 2008, she connected with the Center for Community Transformation, a partner of HOPE International in the Philippines. Her first loan was $80. She repaid it, kept meeting with staff and fellow borrowers, and by her third loan, $800, she bought three sewing machines and rented an apartment to start a sewing business. “Because of that trust, I was able to start a business I can call my own,” she says of the organization that lent to her. The business has since grown into an online clothing company with around 70 employees. Tina trains them, encourages them to save and points them toward the same support she found. The loan mattered. So did the parts of her story that cost nothing: people who trusted her, a group of borrowers who met with her, a prayer life she kept returning to and a skill she kept sharpening. If your budget has no room for a monthly gift, that list is still within reach. Here are five places to start: Watch the way you talk about poverty. Poverty is more than a shortage of money. Material need is real, and it sits inside a larger brokenness that reaches into relationships, communities and a person’s sense of who they are. Talking about poverty that way changes who is in the story. Everyone knows what a broken relationship feels like, so the distance between you and the person asking for help on the corner gets shorter. You make eye contact instead of looking away. You ask a name. You find out what the person actually needs before you decide what to offer. Protect the dignity of the people you want to help. Tina put the turning point in terms of trust. The lender believed she would repay, and she did, and the business that followed was hers. That makes a useful test for any help you offer: does it treat a person as someone with ideas and work of their own, or as someone to be rescued? Giving things away freely is the right call in a crisis. Outside a crisis, it can turn people into recipients in their own community. The better question is how to meet someone’s needs as a whole person while protecting their dignity. Do your job well. You don’t have to work for a nonprofit to fight poverty at work. Vocation is one of the main ways Christians answer the call to love their neighbors, which means many of us are already doing some of that work without noticing. Tina’s sewing business now supports around 70 employees, which is vocation doing exactly this. A barista pours coffee grown by farmers in developing countries. Someone in telecommunications works in an industry that provides cell-phone access in impoverished nations. A worker on an oil field produces fuel that keeps a stranger warm at night. A recruiter connects a person to a job that person badly needs. Pray about where you’ve been placed, do the work well, and think of it as a way to serve people you will probably never meet. Spend your time where the need already is. Poverty has an address close to home, too. Food pantries, tutoring programs and church benevolence ministries run on volunteers, and they tend to need people who show up on a schedule. A standing weeknight shift usually builds more trust than a one-time service day, because the people on the other side get to know your name as well. If you have
articles.content_zh:
2000年代中期,Ate Tina在菲律宾的一家工厂工作了很长的时间,独自养活她的家人. Ate是Tagalog的姐姐, 在她结婚七个月后,她的丈夫发展出严重的健康状况,这使她成为唯一的养家糊口的人. 她怀孕后,工厂的要求保持不变。

她回忆道, “我最后在家中分娩, 女儿出生后两个月,她回到了工厂地板上,她的女儿在别人的照顾下. 蒂娜开始注意到她女儿担心自己行为的变化. 她说,她绝望地祈求生计,使她能够养活家人,并与家人同在。

2008年,她与HOPE国际在菲律宾的合作伙伴社区转型中心建立了联系. 她第一次贷款是80美元。 她偿还了这笔钱,不断与员工和同僚借款人会面,通过第三次贷款800美元,她买了三台缝纫机并租了一套公寓来开办缝纫业务.

“由于这种信任,我得以开办一个我可以称为我自己的企业,”她说,是借给她的组织。 该行从此发展为一家有约70名员工的在线服装公司. 蒂娜训练他们,鼓励他们保存并指向她找到的同样支持. 贷款很重要。

她的故事中那些没有付出任何代价的部分也一样: 相信她的人, 一群与她相遇的借款人, 她不断回归的祈祷生活, 以及她不断磨炼的技能。 如果你的预算没有月度礼物的空间,那名单仍然可以拿到. 这里有五个开始的地方: 注意你谈论贫穷的方式。 贫穷不仅仅是缺乏资金。

物质需求是真实的,它存在于更大的断裂之中,这种断裂涉及到关系、社区和一个人对自身身份的感觉。 说到贫穷 那样会改变故事中是谁 每个人都知道一个破碎的关系是什么感觉,所以你和在角落寻求帮助的人之间的距离会缩短. 你用眼睛接触而不是看不见

你问个名. 在你决定要提供什么之前,先找出这个人实际需要什么. 保护你想要帮助的人的尊严。 蒂娜把转折点 以信任。 贷款人相信她会报答她,她会报答她,随后的生意是她的。

这对你提供的任何帮助都是一种有益的考验:它是把一个人当作有想法和工作的人,还是当作要被拯救的人? 在危机中,自由放弃事物是正确的号召。 在危机之外,它可以把人们变成自己社区的受援者。 更好的问题是,如何满足个人整体的需要,同时保护他们的尊严。 做好你们的工作

你不必为非营利组织工作, Vocation是基督徒响应爱邻居号召的主要方式之一,这意味着我们许多人已经在做一些没有注意的工作. 蒂娜的缝纫行业支持大约70名员工, 一个酒吧为发展中国家农民所种植的咖啡倒灌.

电信业的某个人在贫穷国家提供手机接入的行业工作。 油田上的工人生产出能让陌生人在晚上保持温暖的燃料. 招募者将一个人与他急需的工作联系起来。 祈祷自己被安置在何处, 做得很好,

articles.content: I regret to inform you, dear reader, that heaven tourism is back. The genre possibly never went away entirely, but it did at least disappear from the bestseller lists for several years. Sadly, it has returned in Gabe Poirot’s 18 Days in Heaven , which was one of the bestselling Christian books last month and even made its way to the New York Times list of bestsellers—a feat most authors can only dream of. Out of sheer magnanimity (and perhaps a morbid sense of curiosity), I read it so you don’t have to. 18 Days in Heaven Gabe Poirot Before I tell you what it’s all about, here’s a brief history of heaven tourism. Don Piper kicked off the genre in 2004 with 90 Minutes in Heaven , and it proved a surprise hit that quickly dominated the sales charts, eventually tallying upwards of 8 million copies sold. Todd Burpo’s Heaven Is for Real followed in 2010 with over 10 million copies sold. That same year brought Kevin and Alex Malarkey’s The Boy Who Came Back from Heaven , which sold more than a million copies before Alex recanted his story and the publisher pulled it. The genre went on to deliver many more heaven books and a handful of less-popular hell books like Bill Wiese’s 23 Minutes in Hell , though none ever reached the same heights as the first few—no pun intended. My contribution to the genre was little more than reviewing several of the books and coining the snarky phrase “heaven tourism,” which, much to my delight, soon caught on . The genre inevitably ran its course, but has now returned in Gabe Poirot’s 18 Days in Heaven: I Left My Body. I Met Jesus. What He Told Me Will Alter Your Eternity . Sadly, but not surprisingly, it is just as bad as its predecessors, mixing truth with errors and documented facts with spurious speculations until it is as confusing and unreliable as any of them. 18 Days in Heaven follows the standard pattern by beginning with an account of a terrible accident—in this case, a head injury that resulted from a skateboarding mishap. Poirot, a young evangelist with a sizable YouTube following, was rendered comatose and remained hovering between life and death for 18 days. But while his body was inert, his soul was transported to heaven, where it experienced heavenly wonders, not the least of which was spending time with Jesus. What did he see and experience there? Many things, of course, some of which he is able to describe and many of which he insists he cannot, either because God told him not to or because they defy description. What can he describe? Jesus’s eyes, in which “I saw all the colors that had ever existed or could exist, all in one. He was the deepest ocean of liquid love that had no end. A spectrum of intensity that only increased the longer I stared. His eyebrows, hair, jawline, arms, chest, heart, stature, ears, forehead, eyelashes, teeth, mouth, skin, and complexion all said the same thing: I love you, I love you, I love you.” He describes Jesus’s scars which “were like an ocean that had no floor,” and had the name “Gabriel” written immediately above them. He learned from them that Jesus has completely and eternally forgotten his sins so that he could no longer remember them even if he wanted to. He smelled Jesus and observed that his “fragrance wasn’t like the humidity of the Florida Everglades. No, this was something eternal—an everlasting fountain of fire, not just surrounding me but burning into me. Wrapping around me like a robe, like a living garment of pure, unending presence. It felt burning hot and freezing cold at the same time.” He heard Jesus say many words and noted that his “words were not just a separate entity that He ‘released.’ They were like the sharpest spears that went right into the core of my very being. But these spears were not separate from Him—they were Him.” Poirot even saw his own conception: “The light from Father God united with the earthly seed from my father and the egg of my mother in that moment, and I began my existence on earth. I was not born just on

不幸的是,它回到了Gabe Poirot的"天堂18天"中,这是上个月最畅销的基督教书籍之一,甚至走进了纽约时报畅销书榜,这是大多数作者只能梦想的功绩。 我读了这篇文章,

同年,凯文和亚历克丝·马拉克的"从天堂回来的男孩"(The Boy Who Came from Heaven)也带来了,后者在亚历克丝收回他的故事并被出版商拉出之前就售出超过一百万份. 虽然没有人能达到与前几本书相同的高度,

我对这个流派的贡献不过是回顾几本书, 但现在又回到了Gabe Poirot在天堂的18天:我离开了我的身体。 我遇见了耶稣。 他告诉我 Will 改变你的永恒

可悲但并不令人惊讶的是,它同其前身一样糟糕,把事实与错误相混淆,把有记录的事实同虚假的猜测相混淆,直到它同其中任何一个都一样令人困惑和不可靠。 18天的"天堂"遵循了标准模式,首先讲述了一起可怕的事故——在此情况下,由于滑板出事而造成头部受伤.

Poirot是一位年轻的福音传播者,他带着一个庞大的YouTube跟随,因此被昏迷并徘徊在生与死之间长达18天. 但虽然他的身体是惰性的,他的灵魂被运到了天堂,在那里它经历了天堂的奇事,其中最起碼是和耶稣一起度过. 他在那里看到了什么? 体验什么?

当然,许多事情,有些是他能够描述的,有些是他坚持不能描述的,要么是因为上帝告诉他不要描述,要么是因为他们藐视描述。 他能描述什么? 耶稣的眼睛,其中,“我看到了曾经存在或可能存在的所有颜色,都是一种颜色。 他是无尽的液体爱最深的海洋

他从他们那里得知,耶稣已经彻底地,永远地忘记了自己的罪过,这样即使他愿意也再也记不住了. 他闻到耶稣的气味并观察到他的"香气不像佛罗里达埃弗格拉德河的湿润. 不,这是永恒的东西, 一个永恒的火焰喷泉, 不仅包围着我,而且燃烧在我身上。

articles.content: Good morning. I’ve got A La Carte and a regretful book review for you today. Over the weekend you’ll find Saturday’s Weekend A La Carte plus Sunday’s Works & Wonders, which shares content that is just right for a Sunday morning. I hope you enjoy reading it all as much as I have enjoyed putting it together. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals are headlined by Joel Beeke’s A Radical, Comprehensive Call to Holiness . You may also be interested in a book about women who overcame a difficult past or a biography written for a younger audience. Recommended Reading Selfies Are Not the Self: Forming Embodied Youth in a Disembodied Age. This article from Harvest USA has some helpful insights about young people and their mobile devices. “Increasingly, research shows that teenagers know their technology is making them miserable. They don’t love their phones, but they hate missing out. They know the noise is making them sick, but they’re terrified of the silence. When teenagers are so thirsty for connection and validation that they’ll go to a well they know is poisoned just to get a drink, what an amazing opportunity we have as the church to offer something better, something truly beautiful. We don’t want our youth ministries to be known for what they lack. We want them to be known for their abundance.” Can’t You Just Love Everyone? Jeremy Walker addresses churches that think their calling is to “just love everyone.” “Why not just love one another? Why build walls, make distinctions, establish boundaries, and draw lines? Why confront sins? Why not welcome all equally? Can’t you just love everyone?” 4 Applications for the Order of Love—From the Home to the Ends of the Earth. Speaking of love, Alex Kocman addresses the necessity of rightly ordering our love. “Augustine’s idea of ordo amoris —the ‘order of love’—reflects the Scriptural pattern of directing our affections to first love God, then to love our families, and then to extend that love outward to others. This theme of ordered love has wide-ranging implications—from the home to the ends of the earth. But just as preaching without application is lifeless, so too is a study of love without practical exhortation. Here are four admonitions…” Effective Altruists and the Spreadsheet Gospel. Writing for TGC, Nathan Leamer addresses the effective altruism ideology that is so influential in Silicon Valley. “Over the past decade, an emergent secular philosophy has taken root in Silicon Valley. It now drives many conversations around politics and technology, particularly as its ideas shape how our society approaches artificial intelligence. Known as ‘effective altruism,’ this worldview is having a moment. The Economist recently called the philosophy ‘this century’s biggest idea’ and labeled the movement as ‘admirable, but dangerous.'” Your Thoughts Are Shaping Your Life. “Your thoughts are shaping your life.” That might sound like the kind of thing Joel Osteen or a New Age practitioner would say, but there is truth to it. “Our thought life matters more than we often realize. The conversations we replay in our minds, the offenses we revisit, and the fears we entertain can shape how we see our circumstances and respond to the people around us. I know how easily my thoughts can become consumed by something that has happened or something I fear might happen. Before long, I find myself responding to the present through the lens of thoughts I have been rehearsing.” Don’t Despise the Red Flags. Katie Laitkep writes to those who are dating, and to young women specifically, to warn them not to ignore or despise the red flags. “When we see signs marking a dangerous road, we respond immediately, knowing we need to find a different path. But when it comes to red flags in dating relationships, we don’t always view the warning signs as clearly.” Reviews I like to share the occasional reminder that it is tremendously helpful to authors if you post even brief reviews of their books at Amazon. articles.title: Editor’s Pick: New Children’s Picture Books
articles.summary: Let these stories remind you to enjoy the goodness of the moment and, even as it changes to something new, that God’s goodness is everlasting.
articles.summary_zh: 让这些故事提醒你享受当下的美好，即使它变成了新的东西，神的美好是永恒的。
articles.title_zh: 编辑精选：全新儿童图画书
articles.content: Autumn is a season of changes. At our home, as the leaves yellowed and the days shortened, my youngest child started middle school. That means picture books have me feeling a little nostalgia for the past these days, right alongside a lot of excitement for new things to come. Many of these books are about big changes and adjusting to them, like living with a new baby, moving to a new place, or finding a new heart in Christ’s kingdom. But some are also about the little changes happening around us every day, like laughter over a fleeting moment of childhood imagination or settling down to sleep to prepare for a new day. With all these experiences arriving on the horizon and then flying past like interstate billboards, it’s sweet to remember that “every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow due to change” (James 1:17). As you hand one of these brand-new books to a young reader or curl up to enjoy it together, let these stories remind you to enjoy the goodness of the moment, even as it is changing to something new, and that God’s goodness is everlasting. 1. God Gives Sleep by Betsy Childs Howard, illustrated by Bethan Welby ( TGC Store | Amazon) When our family was exhausted and planning a big move with four children ages 6 and under, I really could have used this little book from Betsy Childs Howard. God Gives Sleep is a rhyming board book with illustrations of adorable animals (sleeping ladybugs!) and two simple refrains that even very young listeners can repeat or “read” for themselves: “God gives sleep” and “God will keep.” Both reflect promises from God that feel vital to the early days of parenting filled with sweet, sleepy snuggles and long, sleepless nights. The last picture shows the entire family asleep and includes Isaiah 40:31 (“Those who hope in the LORD will renew their strength,” NIV). God Gives Sleep is engaging, gentle, funny, and wise, and I’ve already given it to parents of new babies. 2. Winnie-the-Pooh: The Graphic Novel by A. A. Milne, adapted by Kevan Chandler and Joe Sutphin ( Amazon ) Full disclosure: I’m a huge Pooh fan. I’ve probably read the original Milne book dozens of times, and I can be a little sniffy about adaptations. But I loved this one. While I missed Milne’s distinctive narration in parts of the storytelling, this graphic novel retains enough of the original language and has such beautiful artwork that it easily justifies its existence. Parents of young independent readers often ask me for recommendations for books complex enough to be engaging but with content and formatting suitable for early elementary school. This version perfectly fits that space where 6-to-9-year-olds can track the story through the pictures but also enjoy the challenge of some complex vocabulary (“Sudden and Temporary Immersion”) and jokes that reward context research (“An ambush is a sort of Surprise.” “So is a gorse-bush sometimes.”). Winnie-the-Pooh: The Graphic Novel is a sweet and worthy tribute to this classic celebration of early childhood in all its imaginative wonder. 3. The Upside-Down, Inside-Out, Can’t-Believe-It Kingdom by Jonathan Landry Cruse, illustrated by Joe Hox ( Amazon ) The adventure begins with a son begging his father to tell him an exciting bedtime story with dragons and knights. The result is this retelling of the gospel as a quest with a king and a prince and a reminder of our humble place in the kingdom. Joe Hox’s illustrations stand out for being traditional and bright, with a dragon that isn’t too fierce for younger readers but also enough detail within the pictures to engage older readers. The story tells us that the good King will “make us be strong with the strength of His might,” a powerful message for young knights who want to do great things for the kingdom. 4. articles.content_zh:
秋为一季之变. 在家中,随着叶子被黄了,日子被缩短,我最小的孩子开始上中学. 这意味着图书让我觉得过去有些怀旧, 与很多刺激 来的新事物。

这些书中很多是关于大变化并适应它们,比如与新婴儿一起生活,搬到新地方,或者在基督的王国中找到新的心. 但有些人也谈到我们周围每天发生的小变化,比如在童年短暂的想象中欢笑,或者沉睡以准备新的一天。

随着所有这些经历的到来,然后像州际告示牌一样飞过,令人欣慰的是,“每一个好的礼物和完美的礼物都是来自上面,来自灯之父,与他一起没有变化或阴影。” (詹姆斯1:17)。

当你把这些全新的书交给一个年轻的读者 或整理起来一起欣赏的时候, 让这些故事提醒你享受这一刻的美好, 即使它正在变成新的事物, 上帝的善良是永恒的。 1. 联合国

由Bethan Welby(TGC Store QQ Amazon)所展示, 当家庭精疲力竭,计划一个大动作 四个孩子6岁和6岁以下, 我真的可以用这本小书 从贝茜 Childs Howard。

上帝赐予睡眠(God Gives Sleep)是一本配有可爱动物(sleeping ladybugs!)插图的韵律板书,还有两个简单的节奏,即使非常年轻的听众也能为自己重复或“阅读 ” : “ 上帝赐予睡眠 ” 和“上帝会保留 ” 。 两者都反映了上帝的诺言,这些诺言对养育孩子的早期至关重要,充满了甜蜜的,沉睡的和漫长的,无眠的夜晚.

最后一张图片显示整个家庭都睡了,包括以赛亚40:31(“那些希望被耶和华唤起力量的人”,NIV)。 上帝赐予睡眠的热情、温和、幽默和智慧, 由Kevan Chandler和Joe Sutphin(亚马逊)改编 全面披露:我是一个巨大的维尼粉丝。

我可能读过Milne的原作数十次, 但我爱这个 虽然我错过了Milne在故事部分的突出叙事,

年轻独立读者的家长经常向我征求关于书本复杂到足以参与,但内容和格式适合初等学校的建议。

这一版本完全适合6至9岁的人通过图片追踪故事的空间,但也享受一些复杂词汇的挑战(“突然和暂时的印象”)和奖励上下文研究的笑话(“埋伏是一种惊喜”)。 “有时粗鲁也是。 ”

Winnie-the-Pooh:"图形小说"(The Graphic Newvel)是对这一经典的幼儿期庆祝活动的甜美而值得称道的赞誉,在其所有富有想象力的奇迹中. 3. 乔纳森·兰德里·克鲁斯(Jonathan Landry Cruse)的《上下、内出、不能相信的王国》。 冒险从一个乞求父亲的儿子开始,告诉他一个令人兴奋的与龙和骑士同床共枕的故事.

结果是福音的重现 与国王和王子一起探索 并提醒我们在王国的卑微地位 乔·霍克斯的插画突出表现为传统和明亮, 龙对年轻读者来说不是太凶猛,

故事告诉我们,好国王将“以他的力量使我们强大起来”,这是希望为王国做大事的年轻骑士的有力信息。 Mitali Perkins的《为开端祈祷》, Andrés Landazábal(亚马逊) 所描述,

articles.title: How Memorizing the Sermon on the Mount Reorders My Heart
articles.summary: In a world where algorithms capture our affections and lure us online via our cravings, one of the most effective resistance strategies we can employ is to study and memorize Scripture—especially the Sermon on the Mount.
articles.summary_zh: 在一个算法捕捉我们的感情并通过我们的渴望在网上引诱我们的世界里，我们可以使用的最有效的抵抗策略之一是学习和背诵圣经，尤其是登山宝训。
articles.title_zh: 背诵登山宝训如何重塑我的心
articles.content: A couple of years ago, two college students challenged me—a woman in her 50s—to memorize the Sermon on the Mount (Matt. 5–7). Inwardly, I balked, but now I know that few things in my 35 years of following Jesus have been more transformative than committing Jesus’s most famous sermon to memory. John Stott wrote that the Sermon on the Mount is “the nearest thing to a manifesto that [Jesus] ever uttered, for it is his own description of what he wanted his followers to be and to do.” After spending the last few years memorizing it, I see with increasing clarity that I need Jesus’s help to live out what he taught. In a world where algorithms capture our affections and lure us online via our cravings, one of the most effective resistance strategies we can employ is to study and memorize Scripture—especially the Sermon on the Mount. Create a New Algorithm The algorithm often knows us better than we know ourselves. Every time we buy something on Amazon or pause to watch a reel on social media, the algorithm chronicles our activities and builds a profile of us. This profile shows our real interests (not just the ones we list in our social media bios) and some of our most private behaviors (the ones we thank God aren’t live streamed). In milliseconds, companies use what the algorithm knows about us to discover the most effective way to get us to buy their products. In the same way that the algorithm learns about us with each post we like and each reel we watch, God’s Word comes alive in us with every command we learn and put into practice, with every verse we ponder, and with every teaching we adopt as a way of life. By absorbing and obeying Jesus’s Sermon on the Mount, we can create a feedback loop that enlarges his kingdom rule over our lives. Let Scripture Reorder Your Heart Before I started my memorization project, I’d heard many Christians tout Scripture memory as one of the most potent tools for conforming to Jesus, but I didn’t take it seriously. All that changed when I realized algorithms had more access to my life than God’s Word did. By absorbing and obeying Jesus’s Sermon on the Mount, we can create a feedback loop that enlarges his kingdom rule over our lives. Like many Americans, I was averaging more than two hours daily scrolling social media and shopping online, and much less time reading the Bible. I’d thought lack of time was my biggest obstacle to memorizing Scripture. But in reality, my affections and priorities were the obstacle. Memorizing and studying the Sermon on the Mount has provided a powerful reset. I’ve noticed two significant changes in my life. 1. My thoughts are increasingly populated by Jesus’s desires for me. Previously, I was easily shaped by what internet influencers said I should be doing and what my heart really wanted to do. Now, Scripture tenderly draws me to Christ’s transforming grace. For example, a few months ago, someone wrote harsh words to me. I couldn’t sidestep what I’d memorized: Pray for those who hurt you (Mt. 5:44) In those difficult interactions, Jesus’s teaching gave me wisdom to stop reacting and start praying for the one lashing out. Pausing to pray breaks down my self-protective stance so I can consider what the log in my eye might be (Mt. 7:5). 2. I see how vastly different God’s kingdom is from the world we live in. I no longer feel as drawn to the shallow version of perfection the algorithm offers me—the beautiful home, the perfectly fit woman charmingly dressed, or the promise of perpetual travel. When I stop to linger over another picture-perfect kitchen, the Sermon on the Mount prompts me to consider where my treasure really is. These chapters have given me a robust lens through which I can view all of God’s Word. After drinking so deeply of Jesus’s sermon , I see it as the hinge on which both the Old Testament and the New Testament hang. 几年前,两个大学生挑战我——一个50多岁的女性——要记住山上赛门(Matt. 5-7). 但现在我知道,在我追随耶稣的35年里, 没有什么事情比把耶稣最出名的布道当作记忆更具有变革性。

约翰·斯托特(John Stott)写道:"山上赛蒙是[耶稣]曾经发表的宣言中最接近的东西,因为这是他自己对追随者所希望的和所要做的事的描述". 我越来越清楚地看到,我需要耶稣的帮助来维持他所教的。

在一个算法捕捉到我们感情并通过我们的渴望来引诱我们上线的世界中,我们可以采用的最有效的抵抗策略之一是学习并记住"圣经"——特别是"山上"的"塞尔门". 创建新算法 算法常常比我们自己更了解我们.

每次我们购买亚马逊或暂停观看社交媒体的片段, 算法记录我们的活动, 以及一些最私人的行为(我们感谢上帝的人不是活生生的)。

在毫秒内,公司利用算法了解我们的情况,发现最有效的方法让我们购买他们的产品. 正如算法用我们所喜欢的每一个帖子和我们所看的每一卷片子来了解我们一样,上帝的言语以我们所学习和运用的每一个命令、我们所思考的每一个诗句和我们所采纳的作为生活方式的每一个教义,在我们中充满活力。

通过吸收和服从耶稣在"山上"的赛蒙,我们可以建立一个反馈回路,扩大他的王国对我们生活的统治. 在开始我的回忆计划之前, 我听到许多基督徒将圣经记忆说成是符合耶稣的最有力工具之一,

我本以为没有时间是我记起圣经的最大障碍。 但实际上,我的爱和优先考虑是障碍。 纪念并研究了"山上"的"塞尔门"提供了强大的重置. 我注意到我生命中有两个重大的变化。 1. 耶稣对我的渴望使我的思想日益丰富。

之前,我很容易被网络影响者 说我应该做什么 和我的心真正想要做什么。 现在,《圣经》轻而易举地吸引我走向基督的恩典。 例如,几个月前,有人给我写了严厉的话. 我无法回避我所记住的:为伤害你的人祈祷(Mt.

5:44 在困难的交往中,耶稣的教导给了我智慧,让我停止反应,开始为那一次狂欢祈祷. 暂停祈祷 打破自我保护的姿势 这样我就可以考虑我的眼中可能是什么(7:5山) 2. 我看到上帝的王国与我们生活的世界大相径庭。

我不再觉得算法能吸引到我的 浅薄的完美版本, 当我停止停留 停留在另一个图片完美的厨房, 山上赛门 促使我考虑 我的宝藏到底在哪里。

articles.content: I’m excited to tell you the story of how God used a simple verse, from a complicated passage, to change the life of a man named Charles Spurgeon. His story is for everyone, but it may have a special word to speak to a few groups in the room. One is laymen — that is, people who work for a living in normal jobs, outside of Christian ministry. People without a seminary education, people who aren’t pastors or have ministry jobs. We recognize that this series has profiled four men who were preachers. Now, there is an interesting flow to our series: - first, Saint Augustine, - then, Luther, who was an Augustinian monk, - then, John Bunyan, whose favorite book outside the Bible was Luther’s commentary on Galatians, - now, Charles Spurgeon, whose favorite book outside the Bible was Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress. We’ve moved from one convert to another, each building in some way on the previous one, but a weakness of our series (in some sense) is that they all became preachers. And we don’t expect you all to become preachers; we’d like a few, but most will be laymen, and that’s good. Now, Spurgeon is known as “the Prince of Preachers.” But the hero, under God, in Spurgeon’s story is not Spurgeon, and not a trained, paid preacher, but a layman. So, Spurgeon’s story has a special word for laymen who are willing to open their mouths and say what they know about Jesus. Spurgeon’s story also has a special word for teens and young adults. Spurgeon came to faith at age fifteen, which in his day was far more like young adulthood. Still, his story offers a challenge to those who are no longer children and not yet established adults: teens, college students, grad students, even young professionals. Don’t let the world (or the church) lower your standards of what’s possible in being deeply converted and dedicated to Jesus — and how God can make his Son thrilling to a young soul. My prayer is that God might be pleased to give some their own engine. So often, parents, college workers, and pastors help young adults along and give them pushes. And then sometimes, God is pleased in the life of teenagers to give them their own engine, and they don’t need any more pushing. They say, “Get out of my way! I am going to follow Jesus. You can’t keep me from him and worship, my Bible, and prayer!” That’s what God did for Spurgeon at age fifteen — he gave him his own engine. And I pray he might be pleased to do that even here this morning. Spurgeon’s story speaks to one more group: those in the room who are willing to admit, “I’m here but I’m not saved.” For two thousand years, unsaved people have shown up at churches for all sorts of reasons. That’s Spurgeon’s story. He was searching. He was unsaved and in a church on a Sunday morning when God broke through. So, if you’d say this morning, “I haven’t settled the issue of my sin and rebellion against God,” or “I haven’t ‘been saved,’” or “if I died on the drive home today, I wouldn’t be at peace with my Maker,” this story has a special word for you. So, let me tell you about Charlie Spurgeon. His Early and Whole Life He was born in 1834, about 40 miles northeast of London, into a Christian family. In fact, both his father and grandfather were pastors. But his father met financial troubles and sent the young Charles to live with his grandparents from ages one to six. I don’t think this is an insignificant part of the story; don’t underestimate the effects of a good grandma and grandpa in the lives of our children. From their influence he emerged as “precocious,” learned to read, and first found Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress (which he would read more than a hundred times). From his earliest days, he was unusually sharp, ahead of his age level, “always reading books” (Spurgeon: A Biography, 8). He returned home at age six and excelled at school in both math and reading. He was noticed for “his unusual mental ability and his rare clarity of speech” (10), including “his native audacity” (11), that is, his courage to say

我非常兴奋地向大家讲述上帝如何用一段简单的诗句, 从一段复杂的段落中, 他的故事是针对每个人的,但可能有一个特别的单词,可以和房间里的几个团体交谈. 一个是外行者,也就是在基督教部之外从事正常工作谋生的人。

没有神学院教育的人, 我们承认,这一系列的描述 4人谁是传道者。

现在,我们的系列有一个有趣的流传:首先,圣奥古斯丁, 然后,路德,他是一个奥古斯丁的修道士, 然后,约翰·邦扬,他最喜欢的书是路德对加拉提安的评论, 现在,查尔斯·斯普吉翁,他最喜欢的书是"邦扬朝圣者的进步"。

但我们系列的一个弱点(某种意义上的)就是他们都成了传教士。 我们并不期望你们都成为传教士;我们想做几个,但多数是外行,这很好。

现在,斯普吉翁被称为"道教的王子". 但是,在上帝的统治下,在斯普吉翁的故事里,英雄不是斯普吉翁,也不是一个受过训练,有报酬的传教士,而是一名外行人. 因此,斯普吉恩的故事有一个特别的词来形容那些愿意张开口子,说出自己对耶稣所了解的. Spurgeon的故事中也有一个针对青少年和年轻成年人的特殊词.

斯普吉安在15岁时开始信仰,在他这一天,这更像是年轻的成年. 然而,他的故事给那些已经不是孩子和还没有成年的人带来了挑战:青少年,大学生,研究生,甚至年轻专业人员.

不要让世界(或教会)降低你对于什么是可能的, 我的祷告是 上帝可能很乐意 给一些自己的引擎。 父母、大学员工和牧师经常帮助年轻的成年人并给予他们推动。

有时,上帝在青少年生活中很高兴给他们自己的引擎,他们不需要再再推了. 他们说:你们离我远点! 我要跟随耶稣。 你无法阻止我远离他, 这是上帝在15岁时为斯波克森所做的——他给了他自己的引擎. 我祈求他今天上午也乐意这么做

Spurgeon的故事又讲述了一个群体:那些在房间里愿意承认“我在这里,但我没有被拯救。 ” 两千年来,无所救护的人出于各种原因都出现在了教堂. 这是斯普吉恩的故事。 他在寻找。 周日早上,上帝破门而入时,他被解剖,在教堂里。

所以,如果你今天上午说,“我还没有解决我的罪恶和反抗上帝的问题,”或者“我还没有`拯救',或者“如果我今天在回家的路上死了,我也不会与我的造物主和睦相处,”这个故事有一个特别的词给你。 让我告诉你查理·斯波克森的事 他于1834年生于伦敦东北约40英里处,进入基督教家庭.

事实上,他的父亲和祖父都是牧师。 但是他的父亲遇到了财政上的困难,并派年轻的查尔斯从一到六岁就和外祖父母住在一起. 我并不认为这是故事的次要部分,

从他们的影响力中,他出现了“珍贵的,”学会了阅读,并首先发现了邦扬的"朝圣者进步"(他将读一百多遍)。 从他最初的年代起,他就异常尖锐地领先于他的年龄,"总是阅读书籍"("外科医生:一部传记",8). 他六岁回家,在学校数学和阅读方面都非常出色。

articles.title_zh: 五个辅导失误和圣灵的帮助
articles.content: As we were finishing a counseling session, Jill looked at me with concern, her eyebrows furrowed. “You got distracted,” she bluntly stated. Unfortunately, Jill was right. Just outside my workspace, several pastors gathered in the church office lobby, talking and laughing. I’d gotten sidetracked by the commotion. About 70 percent of me was attending to Jill, but 30 percent of my headspace had shifted to the lobby: What are they doing? What’s so funny? We live in a distractible culture. Between YouTube shorts and checking our email inboxes every hour, our minds wander quickly. Staying focused is a skill few truly master. But it’s essential if we’re going to care well for God’s people. Whether formally or informally, counseling another soul is a distinct privilege. Yet, too often, mistakes plague our conversations. Fortunately, getting distracted is one of several common mistakes that are correctable. After Jill’s jarring comment, I closed the window blinds (simple fix), talked to the staff about keeping the commotion down (another simple fix), recommitted to staying focused (possible, though it would be work), and prayed the Lord would renew my love for his sheep. What counseling mistakes are you prone to make? Take a quick check. Mistake 1: Fear of Man Charlotte shares about her struggles with her job. She dislikes her boss, and she’s weary of her work. Unfortunately, she often responds to her difficulties with sinful choices. This time, she lied to her boss to get out of an assignment. You sympathize with her frustrations but feel convinced you’ve got to speak up about her lying. Charlotte’s a Christian, and Scripture makes clear that because God never lies, Christ’s followers shouldn’t either (Colossians 3:9–10; Titus 1:2). Yet you hesitate. You know Charlotte will get angry, and your fears kick in. Why bother bringing it up? Lying is between her and God. Right now, she needs a friend. But you know if you don’t say something, Charlotte will eventually lie to her boss again. What should you do? Repent of your fear that causes you to avoid a difficult word. Confess your worry about speaking up to the Lord (Psalm 34:4). If you struggle with people-pleasing, then saying a difficult word will feel painful. Reframe your situation by putting the fear of God at the center of your thinking (Proverbs 29:25; Luke 12:4–5). If we fear God more than Charlotte, we won’t let Charlotte’s potential anger get in the way. My friend Jonathan Leeman calls the helper in this situation a “sin-absorber.” A true friend willingly absorbs the cost of another person’s sin for the sake of honoring Christ. Would you be willing to absorb Charlotte’s anger if it helps her address her lie? Mistake 2: Assumed Insight Angela and John have been married for 31 years. Sometimes John gets frustrated with Angela because she assumes what he’s thinking. “I know I’m not supposed to assume,” Angela would think, “but we’ve been together for a long time.” The more familiar you are with someone, the more you’re likely to get in trouble. Familiarity breeds assumptions . Think about your last conflict. How many assumptions did you make? Probably a few. Assumptions can create problems. Sometimes our assumptions are true, but often they’re not. If you’re prone to making assumptions, here’s how to stay away from trouble: Don’t overestimate your ability to size up a situation. Pride makes you think, “I know what’s going on.” Humility tells you, “Ask God for wisdom.” The humble recognize they’re not as smart as they think and must depend on the Lord for insight (James 1:5). After you’ve asked the Lord for help, test your assumptions. Don’t tolerate any of them. Check the validity of your assumptions by asking thoughtful, careful, and loving questions. Genuine curiosity will lead you to ask rather than assume. At the encouragement of a friend, Angela asked more questions during marital conflict, and that built more understanding between her and John. The apostle Paul tells us that

articles.title_zh: 周末单点菜肴（ 11月7日）
articles.content: Welcome to Weekend A La Carte. I hope you find something here, whether a longform article, a reader recommendation, or something else entirely, that makes your weekend just a little bit better. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several newer and older books that are all worth at least thinking about. If you’re interested in doing some theological reading, Westminster Books is offering up to 57% off the three-volume set of Warfield’s works. Also, I haven’t reviewed it yet, but did want to briefly recommend the new graphic novel adaptation of Pilgrim’s Progress . It seems to be priced just about equally at Westminster Books and Amazon (for me, at least). Recommended Reading Canada’s Maclean’s magazine has an interesting article about the Hutterites and their caution when it comes to modern technologies. The author, like so many of us, is alarmed by the ways technology overtakes our lives, and sees that the Hutterites may have a healthier relationship to it. Most of us—including me—are worried that we’ve all become desensitized to the manifold and multiplying ways technology is negatively affecting our lives. Social media has been blamed for rising rates of political polarization and radicalization, damaging young people’s ability to form relationships and eroding mental health. And we’re all trying to figure out what to do about it. Slick startups sell devices you tap with your phone to “brick” it (that is, blocking distracting social media, apps and internet access). There are apps to remove short-form videos from social media feeds. There are now social media bans in place for youth in Australia, in parts of Europe and Asia and, this June, proposed in Canada. Sales of dumbphones and flip phones have grown in the past few years. Even landlines are trendy again. But this is like pushing back the tide with a broom. For most of us, technology feels like a force of nature that will wash over us whether we want it to or not. The Hutterites are more optimistic. They think if they can keep their distance from the wider world, and adopt the right set of rules around technology, they can hold onto its positive features and simply seal out what they don’t like. Read: The Hutterites’ Guide to Technology. The New York Times was in touch with many Gen Zers and explains how their entry into the job market is much different from previous generations. I think it’s easy for those of us who are older to act as if Gen Z is lazy or otherwise not putting in much effort, but this article ought to give us some compassion. They described a process that is lonely, opaque and impersonal, in which it is hard to tell whether one is being rejected by a hiring manager or an A.I. screener. The problem is not just that hiring has slowed across the labor market, or that the specter of A.I. is threatening entry-level positions, they said. It was that they could not get a real, live human being to speak to them. Ever. About anything. The same language came up over and over in their responses: They felt as if they were throwing their applications into “the void.” Some of them opted for slightly different terminology — a “black hole” or an “abyss” — but they painted a similar picture of the application process as a swirling vortex where aspirations and cover letters vanish, unlikely to be retrieved. One part that jumped out to me was the person who insists on they/them pronouns. I would imagine that is a huge red flag for people in charge of hiring! Read: Searching for Jobs, Gen Z Feels Like It’s Staring Into ‘The Void’. The Verge has a lengthy article that describes the bizarre and heterodox gospel according to Peter Thiel. It’s a time of apocalyptic worldviews in Silicon Valley. The latest AI doom cycle is driven by effective altruism (EA), a philosophy that has lurked around the fringes for years but recently burst into the mainstream because its adherents are embedded across the AI industry, from Anthropic to newly appointed AI safety watchdog METR. E

加拿大的Maclean杂志有一篇有趣的文章, 作者和我们许多人一样,对科技超越我们生活的方式感到震惊,并看到胡特人可能与其有更健康的关系.

我们多数人,包括我在内,都担心我们都对技术的多重和倍增方式失去敏感认识,对我们的生活产生不利影响。 社会媒体被指责为政治两极化和激进化率上升,破坏了年轻人建立关系的能力并侵蚀了心理健康。 我们都在想办法解决它。

Slick startups将你用手机窃听的装置卖掉, 有应用从社交媒体的种子中去除短式视频. 澳大利亚、欧洲和亚洲部分地区以及今年6月加拿大提议禁止青年使用社交媒体。

过去几年来,哑电话和翻接电话的销售量有所增加。 连地上线也是潮流 但是这就像用扫帚把潮流推倒 对我们大多数人来说,技术就像一股自然的力量,它会冲过我们,不管我们是否愿意。 胡特人比较乐观.

他们认为,如果他们能与更广阔的世界保持距离,并围绕技术采取一套正确的规则,他们就可以坚持其积极特征,简单地封杀他们不喜欢的东西。 参见:《胡特人技术指南》。 "纽约时报"曾与多位"Gen Zers"保持联系,并解释了他们进入就业市场与前几代人有何不同.

我认为我们这些年纪较大的人, 他们描述了一个孤独、不透明、不讲人性的过程,在这个过程中,很难知道是被雇用经理还是人工智能筛选员拒绝。

他们说,问题不仅仅是整个劳动力市场的雇用速度放慢,或者A.I.的侧面正在威胁起职职位。 他们无法找到一个真正的活人与他们交谈。 从来没有。 什么都说

在他们的答复中,同样的语言反复出现: 他们觉得好像把申请扔入了“空白”。 其中一些人选择了略为不同的术语——“黑洞”或“旁观者”,但他们将申请过程描绘成一幅相去甚远的漩涡,其中愿望和封面字母消失,不可能取回。

跳出来给我看的就是坚持他们/他们的代名词的人. 我想这是一面巨大的红旗 对于负责雇佣的人! 读取:寻找工作,Gen Z感觉像是"星入"(The Void). Verge有一篇长篇报道 描述Peter Thiel所说的奇异异和异形福音 在硅谷,
