articles.title_zh: IMB传教士在服务之旅中分享首尔的愿景
articles.content: Ask most people what comes to mind when they think of South Korea, and they’ll likely mention K-pop, skincare, cutting-edge technology, or bustling city streets filled with young professionals. Hun and Eunjoo Sol see those things too. But after more than a decade serving as International Mission Board missionaries in Seoul, they also see something many visitors never notice. “Many people think that Korea is exciting and successful,” Hun said. “They think about the K-pop, the K-culture, K-technology, K-cosmetics. Yes, good things… But many Korean people are struggling right now.” The Sols, who were featured in the 2025 Week of Prayer for International Missions , continue to rely on the prayers of faithful Southern Baptists. Prayers sustain them and help to push back the darkness they confront in their home culture. Hun often describes that hidden struggle with a Korean word: han. There is no simple English translation. It speaks to a deep sorrow shaped by generations of war, division, loss, and the quiet resolve to endure. Hun sees it in the young adults he meets every week—people navigating loneliness and relentless expectations, quietly asking what their lives are for beneath a veneer of success. Han is heavy. For many young adults, that weight can feel unbearable. Suicide is one of the leading causes of death among teenagers and young adults in South Korean. Hun and Eunjoo see the effects of that reality every day, and it’s one reason they believe they have no time to waste. That understanding shaped the week of Serve Tour Seoul this summer. There were no construction sites, no paintbrushes, no tools or work gloves. Instead, the team stepped into ministries local churches had been faithfully building long before the volunteers arrived. In May, 27 volunteers from seven churches across the United States came alongside local churches already serving their communities in Seoul, Paju, and Gwangju. They taught English classes, ran children’s camps, walked neighborhoods in prayer, distributed food, and sat down with college students, one conversation at a time. For Nick Holst of Sandals Church in Riverside, California, the goal was simple enough to say in a sentence: “We came to meet people,” Holst said. “We want to hear their stories, and that leads to some very meaningful connections as you get past the surface into something deeper.” That’s where the week actually lived: past the surface and past the small talk, where the quiet weight of han is often carried without words. On college campuses, volunteers played games, asked questions and mostly just listened. Some conversations lasted a few minutes and ended there. Others kept going long past the point where either person expected them to. One morning, after asking his church back home to pray, Holst sat down with a university student named Intec. They talked about culture first, the way strangers do, and then the conversation turned somewhere neither of them planned. “I got to ask him, ‘What do Koreans believe?’” Holst recalled. Intec said he didn’t believe in God. Then he recited John 3:16 from memory, word for word, a verse he’d heard somewhere along the way and never forgotten. Before they parted, Holst asked if he could pray that God would keep drawing Intec toward Himself. “He said yes.” In a city where many conversations never move beyond the surface, the exchange was a reminder of why the team had come. Not to win an argument, but to listen, to ask questions, and to trust God with what happens next. The same pattern unfolded elsewhere, beginning in classrooms and ending on city streets. Jeremy Doyle, missions pastor at Valley Baptist Church in Bakersfield, California, watched an English conversation club grow from two students on its first night to eight by the second. Nobody advertised it as anything more than a place to practice English, but the room kept filling, and so did the conversations. The team’s work with students didn’t stop there. articles.title: God’s mission in Africa: ‘There is still much to do’
articles.summary: For both the African and global audiences at the Yaoundé gathering, panel members underscored a fundamental truth: Bible translation is not an isolated academic exercise.
articles.summary_zh: 在雅温得会议上，小组成员向非洲和全球观众强调了一个基本事实：圣经翻译并不是一项孤立的学术活动。
articles.title_zh: 神在非洲的使命： “还有很多事情要做”
articles.content: YAOUNDÉ, CAMEROON — During the Wycliffe Global Alliance Africa Area Gathering, a question was put before delegates: Is the African Church awake? A three-person panel, moderated by Dr. Zac Manyim, Director of the Department of Church and Scripture Engagement at CABTAL (Cameroon Association for Bible Translation and Literacy), delved into the continent’s strategic mission challenges and local breakthroughs. A Call from the Pulpit to Action ‘Yes, the African Church is awake, but it is not active,’ said Rev. Abel Chebe Ngah of the Apostolic Church in Cameroon. He noted a disparity in how modern ministry resources are being spent. ‘Some churches are focused on building megachurches, while only a few are focused on spreading the Word of God. The African church should have been doing exploits, but it is not yet doing so. There are still many areas in Africa not reached by the gospel.’ For the landscape to shift, Ngah argued that mission cannot be treated lightly; the local church must intentionally send missionaries. Demonstrating local ownership, his own denomination dedicates a specific Sunday every year entirely to Bible translation, using it to mobilise believers and raise financial support for CABTAL’s fieldwork. Though some local churches might lack the required financial resources, they offer abundant human and material resources needed in Bible translation. The Lifelong Impact of Mother-Tongue Literacy Pastor Alphonse Gamaldak, president of the Mofu Gudur Inter-Church Committee, said Bible translation reshaped his entire life trajectory. Before receiving any formal education, he learned to read and write in his mother tongue. This linguistic foundation gave him the leeway to master French, eventually leading him to seminary. ‘Yes, the church is awake in Mofu Gudur (a language community of northern Cameroon) because many kids have now grown and seen their lives transformed by the Bible translated into our language,’ he said. The impact extends far beyond the sanctuary. Through mother-tongue functional literacy programmes overseen by the translation project, community members have developed income-generating activities, drastically improving local livelihoods. Today, over 250 literacy teachers are actively instructing inside churches and surrounding villages. Yet, Pastor Gamaldak warned that sustainability requires ongoing investment. ‘There is still much to do,’ he said, ‘like continuing to build the capacity of and support these 250 literacy teachers.’ In 2008, when the Mofu Gudur New Testament was dedicated, the church and the community came together to facilitate the distribution. Five thousand copies were printed, and they were all sold out in the following months. A second run of 4,000 copies was printed. A few years later, it was still hard to obtain a copy. This motivated CABTAL to begin work on the Old Testament, which was dedicated in May 2026. Thanks to the commitment of the local church, the Mofu Gudur people now have a complete Bible. The Takeaway for the Global Alliance For both the African and global audiences at the Yaoundé gathering, panel members underscored a fundamental truth: Bible translation is not an isolated academic exercise. When local churches move from being merely ‘awake’ to being actively engaged, Scripture access unlocks deep spiritual maturity, local resource mobilisation and holistic community development. Story and Photos: Isaac Forchie
articles.content_zh: 在威克里夫全球联盟非洲地区集会期间,向代表们提出了一个问题: 非洲教会醒了吗? 一个三人小组,由CABTAL(喀麦隆圣经翻译和识字协会)教会和圣经参与部主任Zac Manyim博士主持,探讨了非洲大陆的战略任务挑战和地方突破。 喀麦隆使徒教会的Abel Chebe Ngah牧师说, 他指出,在现代部委资源如何使用方面存在差距。 :"有些教堂专注于建造特大教堂,而只有少数教堂专注于传播"上帝之道". 非洲教会本应在进行剥削,但尚未这样做。 非洲仍有许多地区没有获得福音。 为了改变地貌,Ngarh认为不能轻视任务;当地教会必须故意派遣传教士. 他自己的教派每年专门用一个礼拜天翻译圣经, 尽管一些地方教会可能缺乏所需的财政资源,但它们提供了圣经翻译所需的大量人力和物力资源。 Mofu Gudur教会间委员会主席Alphonse Gamaldak教授的《母亲-通格识字牧师终身影响》说,《圣经》翻译重塑了他的整个人生轨迹。 在接受任何正规教育之前,他学会用母语读写. 这个语言学基础给了他掌握法语的回旋余地,最终引导他进入神学院. 他说 : “ 是的, 教堂在Mofu Gudur(喀麦隆北部的一个语言社区)醒了, 因为许多孩子已经长大, 影响远远超出避难所。 通过翻译项目监督的母语实用识字方案,社区成员开展了创收活动,大大改善了当地生计。 今天,250多名扫盲教师正在教会内部和周围的村庄积极进行教学。 然而,Gamaldak牧师警告说,可持续性需要持续投资。 他说,“还有许多事情要做,就像继续建设和支持这250名扫盲教师的能力。” 2008年,当"莫福古都尔新约"被奉献时,教会与社区聚集一堂来为发行提供便利. 印出五千本,后数月全部被卖出. 第二次印制了4000册. 几年后,仍难以获得副本. 这激励了CABTAL开始"旧约"的工作,该"旧约"于2026年5月被专门化. 由于当地教会的承诺,莫福古都尔人现在有了完整的"圣经". 小组成员强调了一个基本真理:圣经翻译不是孤立的学术活动。 当当地教会从仅仅是`觉醒'走向积极参与时,《圣经》的获取将释放出深刻的精神成熟、地方资源动员和整体社区发展。 故事与相片:以撒·福奇

articles.title: ‘Mosquito Bowl’: Football Stars on the Front Lines
articles.summary: Peter Berg’s ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ is essentially ‘Friday Night Lights’ meets ‘Hacksaw Ridge.’
articles.summary_zh: Peter Berg的“The Mosquito Bowl”本质上是“周五夜灯”与“Hacksaw Ridge”相遇。
articles.title_zh: “蚊子碗” ：前线的足球明星
articles.content: Peter Berg’s The Mosquito Bowl is essentially Friday Night Lights meets Hacksaw Ridge . It’s a movie with the same creative vibe as Friday Night Lights (gritty handheld camera, muted color palette, Explosions in the Sky post-rock soundtrack) but applied to a brutally violent true story of WWII’s Battle of Okinawa, one of the single bloodiest battles of the 20th century. Also like Berg’s Friday Night Lights , The Mosquito Bowl ( out now in theaters ; coming to Netflix November 25) is based on a book by Pulitzer Prize–winning journalist Buzz Bissinger . The 2022 book—subtitled A Game of Life and Death in World War II —only has one chapter (of 41) devoted to the actual 1944 football game dubbed “The Mosquito Bowl.” Most of the book is about the war, and the young men who left wives, kids, and promising NFL careers to fight it. Likewise, Berg’s film adaptation is mostly a somber, unflinching WWII film, with a brief reprieve of joy in the form of a football game on Guadalcanal between the 4th and 29th regiments of the 6th Marine Division. Just as in Friday Night Lights , where the drama of high school football parallels the struggles and triumphs of life off the field, the football game in The Mosquito Bowl parallels the “game of life and death” that surrounds the men at war. Sports are interesting in this way: They provide escape from real life but also training for it, an arena of danger and high stakes but not ultimate stakes. Sports often map onto life—we draw up plans and plays but have to improvise; we get hurt but can heal; we thrive individually through teamwork; sometimes we win and sometimes we lose. Yet sports are unlike real life too. Winning or losing on the field is a matter of trophies and glory, but off the field, it can be a matter of life and death. Young Men Willing to Fight and Die The Mosquito Bowl (rated R for graphic war violence and language), opens with a well-known epigraph from Herbert Hoover : Older men declare war. But it is youth that must fight and die. And it is youth who must inherit the tribulation, the sorrow, and the triumphs that are the aftermath of war. This is a movie about youth—or rather, the passage from youth into adulthood that war accelerates. This is a movie about youth—or rather, the passage from youth into adulthood that war accelerates. The movie opens with muddy college football scenes in the fall of 1941, as the four central characters are introduced: John McLaughry (Nicholas Galitzine), Brown quarterback; Bob Baumann (Bill Skarsgård), University of Wisconsin tackle; Tony Butkovich (Ray Nicholson), Purdue fullback; and Dave Schreiner (Tom Francis), Wisconsin end. They were all-star athletes with promising futures. Many of them were collegiate All-Americans and drafted by NFL teams. Yet December 7, 1941, happened, and their futures were all changed. Once bound together by football skill, friendly rivalry, and fierce competition on the gridiron, these men soon bonded in a different setting: as marines in WWII’s savage Pacific theater. Instead of fighting for yards on the field, they fought for ground in a war of attrition on Okinawa. Instead of a football in hand, they carried guns and bayonets. Instead of tackling their opponents, they wrestled them to the death in hand-to-hand combat. Like many in the Greatest Generation, these men volunteered to enlist and fight. The Mosquito Bowl celebrates their duty and sacrifice. In one scene, Baumann’s younger brother says, “You don’t have to go,” to which Baumann replies, “I do. I’m needed.” It’s hard to imagine star athletes, whether collegiate or professional, volunteering to go to war in 2026. But in 1943, it was normal. Okinawa, Bissinger writes in the book, was “by far the largest collection of athletes ever to die in a single battle.” And in the entirety of WWII, 21 NFL players died in combat, as well as two players from Major League Baseball. Why were they so willing to lay down their lives? Perhaps back then, men had the bigger hori

articles.title: Pastor, Be Opportunistic
articles.summary: Pastor, you cannot afford to coast. You cannot afford autopilot. Be a gospel entrepreneur. Eternity is at stake.
articles.summary_zh: 牧师，您负担不起海岸。您买不起自动驾驶仪。成为一名福音企业家。永恒岌岌可危。
articles.title_zh: 牧师，抓住机会
articles.content: My coffee had gone cold as the church planter mourned that his church felt stagnant. Worse than not growing—a thick malaise had settled over the congregation. The first three years were exciting; the community was intrigued by a new church plant, genuinely curious about what it was all about. But everything had plateaued. Leaders grew complacent. Sundays—even with strong preaching—felt cold and passionless. The church’s reason for existing had shrunk to feeding and caring for the Christians who already called it home. The church planter couldn’t see how it was still transforming the community. An older mentor at the table cleared his throat. “I’m sorry to hear that. Let me ask you—what is one risky, hard thing the Lord is inviting your church to do that you’re hesitant to do?” The planter scratched his head. “I don’t know. I’ve never been asked that before.” The older man shrugged. “Every pastor should be ready to answer that question. If he can’t, he needs to spend some time praying and fasting until he can. Comfort and complacency are incredibly dangerous.” I’ve sat in enough of these conversations to know that wise, healthy risks are vital to the life of the church. Without them, the church atrophies. Its reason for existing collapses into self-care and, after a few years, into self-preservation. Risky and hard things keep gospel blood flowing through the body. Pastor, you cannot afford to coast. You cannot afford autopilot. You owe it to Jesus and to your church to make the most of opportunities in your city—which means that alongside preaching, teaching, praying, and developing leaders, you need to prioritize seeking new avenues for ministry. Be a gospel entrepreneur. Church-planting networks have long understood that entrepreneurial aptitude is essential for planters. But what about established churches—do their pastors need to be entrepreneurial too? What Is a Gospel Entrepreneur? There’s still hesitancy around saying pastors need entrepreneurial aptitude. Maybe it’s because we picture someone who constantly starts new things he can’t sustain—a person with a billion ideas who follows through on none of them. If this is what we mean, then no, we don’t want our pastors to be entrepreneurial. Comfort and complacency are incredibly dangerous. But a gospel entrepreneur is something different. He doesn’t pile up harebrained ideas. He stays awake and sober-minded about the opportunities the Lord is opening in the community. He sees the wooden frames of a new development and prays about how the gospel will reach those families once they move in. He looks at neighborhoods where existing churches can’t possibly reach everyone—and plants a church there. He saves, scrimps, and sacrifices to move a growing church plant into a more strategic location. He keeps his eyes open, his mind sharp, and his hands ready for the moment God opens a door. Biblical Call When this topic comes up, someone usually asks, “Where do you see the need for a pastor to be an entrepreneur in the Bible?” My answer often surprises people: Jesus’s parable of the dishonest manager. In Luke 16:1–9, a rich man discovers his property manager has been wasting his possessions and tells him to settle accounts—he’s about to be fired. The manager realizes losing his job means either digging or begging, so he immediately goes to work cutting deals to gain favor with other wealthy employers. When his employer finds out, he commends the manager for his shrewdness. Ethical or not, it was a genius move. At this point, we should ask, Why is Jesus telling this story? Maybe he’s about to indict people like the manager. But the manager’s dishonesty has nothing to do with Jesus’s point. The twist is that Jesus holds up the dishonest manager as an example of what he wants his disciples to be. “The master commended the dishonest manager for his shrewdness,” Jesus says. “For the sons of this world are more shrewd in dealing with their own generation than the sons of light” (Luke 16:

articles.title_zh: Packers的Josh Jacobs说，他的达阵庆祝活动是对福音歌曲“打破每一条链条”的颂歌，而不是他最近的逮捕
articles.content: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs says the celebration that set off social media after his latest touchdown was a tribute to a gospel song, not a joke about his recent arrest. In the second quarter of the Packers’ 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers, Jacobs scored on a 1-yard run and briefly put his hands behind his back while teammates congratulated him. Some viewers watching on television thought he was pretending to be handcuffed. Jacobs said he was modeling the moment after a gospel song called “Break Every Chain.” “The guys did it with me,” he said. “I didn’t think it was going to be a thing that can be perceived a certain type of way. But it’s 2026, and it is what it is.” It was Jacobs’ second game of the season. He had spent time on the NFL’s commissioner’s exempt list after charges were filed against him in August over a May altercation with his then-girlfriend, who said he threw her to the ground. Last month he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property. He was taken off the list last week and returned to the field, though the league’s investigation is still ongoing. Jacobs said he talked with receiver Savion Williams and other teammates before his season debut, and they planned two celebrations. After his first touchdown of the season, in a 20-17 loss at Detroit, he went to his knees and raised his arms to thank God. The “Break Every Chain” moment was meant for the next one. He also said the broadcast cut away early. “It was more to it than that,” Jacobs said. “They stopped showing the celebration after that.” The NFL’s investigation of Jacobs remains open.
articles.content_zh: Green Bay Packers跑回Josh Jacobs说, 上次触地得分后引发社交媒体的庆典, 在打包员27-19战胜卡罗来纳黑豹队的第二季中,雅各布斯在一码跑道上打入了分数,并短暂地将手放在了背后而队友们向他表示祝贺. 一些在电视上观看的观众认为他假装被铐了. articles.summary: If you’re 25, the Gen Z church revival you keep hearing about may not describe you. Pew Research Center’s newest report on American religion finds that adults ages 23 to 26 are actually the least religious age group in the country on the core measures it tracks, including how often they pray, how much religion…
articles.summary_zh: 如果你25岁，你一直听到的Z世代教会复兴可能无法形容你。皮尤研究中心（ Pew Research Center ）关于美国宗教的最新报告发现， 23至26岁的成年人实际上是该国宗教信仰最少的年龄组，其追踪的核心指标包括他们祈祷的频率、宗教信仰……
articles.title_zh: 皮尤： 23至26岁的美国人是该国宗教信仰最少的成年人，而18至22岁的人参加教会的比率高于任何人
articles.content: If you’re 25, the Gen Z church revival you keep hearing about may not describe you. Pew Research Center’s newest report on American religion finds that adults ages 23 to 26 are actually the least religious age group in the country on the core measures it tracks, including how often they pray, how much religion matters to them and whether they identify with a religion. But the group just below them looks very different. Among adults 18 to 22, 41% say they attend a church, synagogue, mosque or other house of worship at least once or twice a month. That is higher than the 33% for the U.S. public as a whole, and higher than adults born in the 1990s, 1980s, 1970s and 1960s. Among adults 23 to 26, the number is 27%, one of the lowest of any age group. Pew calls the overall picture “complicated,” and the report is careful about what the younger figure can carry. Outside of attendance, the youngest adults are less distinctive. They pray and identify with a religion at lower rates than many older groups. They are no more religious than people that age were in 2014, and by Pew’s measures of prayer, religion’s importance and religious identification, both young groups are significantly less religious than their counterparts in 2007. That said, Pew’s sample is small. The 18-to-22 findings rest on 443 respondents from Pew’s 2025 and 2026 surveys, with a margin of error of plus or minus 5.7 percentage points. Applied to the 41% figure, that is a range of roughly 35% to 47%. Split the group by gender or party and the margins widen further. Pew also notes that this has happened before. In its 2014 Religious Landscape Study, 18-to-22-year-olds attended services at a rate 6 points higher than 23-to-26-year-olds. What is new is that the 2025 and 2026 surveys are the first in which the youngest group is significantly more religious than the next group up on all four of Pew’s core indicators. When the youngest adults have looked more religious in the past, Pew says, the effect has tended to fade with time. It adds that the bump may partly reflect a rebound from the pandemic, and that scholars of religion tend to study change over decades. Some of the details cut against the usual storyline about who is showing up. Young men now attend more often than young women, which Pew says it has not seen before, but 35% of the youngest women attend at least monthly, about the same as women born from the 1950s through the 1980s. Among the youngest Republicans, 55% attend monthly. The youngest Democrats also attend at relatively high rates compared with other Democrats, so Pew says it cannot call this an exclusively Republican phenomenon. Across all ages, Pew finds religion holding steady. The shares who identify with a religion, pray daily, call religion very important and attend monthly have been flat since 2020, and 34% of U.S. adults said in a June survey that they had attended services in person in the previous month, the highest since Pew began asking in 2020. Pew says it has no way of knowing whether the youngest adults will follow the old pattern or break it, and describes the open question as “a turning point or a blip.” If it is a revival, it belongs so far to the very youngest adults in the survey.
articles.content_zh: 若你25岁, 皮尤研究中心关于美国宗教的最新报告发现,23-26岁的成年人实际上是该国在追踪的核心衡量标准上最不信奉宗教的年龄组,包括他们的祈祷次数、宗教对他们的重要性以及他们是否认同某一宗教。 但是他们下面的人群看起来很不一样。 在18至22岁的成年人中,41%的人说,他们每月至少去一次或两次教堂、犹太会堂、清真寺或其他礼拜场所。 这比整个美国公众的33%高,也比1990年代,1980年代,1970年代和1960年代出生的成年人高. 在23至26岁的成年人中,这一数字为27%,是任何年龄组中最低的。 皮尤称总体情况“复杂”,报告对年轻人物能够携带什么十分谨慎。 除了出勤外,最年轻的成年人也不太特别. 他们祈祷和认同宗教的比例低于许多老年群体。 他们的宗教程度不比2014年那个年龄的人多,根据皮尤的祈祷、宗教的重要性和宗教认同措施,2007年,这两个青年群体的宗教程度明显低于同龄人。 皮尤的样本很小。 18至22分的调查结果取自皮尤2025年和2026年调查的443个答卷人,误差幅度为上下5.7个百分点。 适用于41%的数字,约为35%至47%。 按性别或政党划分,差额进一步扩大。 Pew也指出,这以前发生过。 在其2014年的"宗教景观研究"中,18至22岁的青少年参加服务,比23至26岁的青少年高6分. 新情况是,2025年和2026年的调查是第一次最年轻的群体比皮尤所有四个核心指标的下一批群体宗教程度高得多。 当最年轻的成年人在过去看起来更加宗教化时,皮尤说,这种效果往往随着时间逐渐消退. 它还说,这一起伏可能部分反映了该流行病的反弹,宗教学者往往研究几十年来的变化。 一些细节与通常的故事情节相对应, 青年男子现在比青年妇女更经常参加,皮尤说以前从未见过这种活动,但最小的妇女中35%至少每月参加,大约与1950年代至1980年代出生的妇女相同。 在最年轻的共和党人中,有55%每月参加. 与其他民主党人相比,最年轻的民主党人也以相对较高的比率参加,因此皮尤称这不能称之为纯粹的共和党现象. 在所有年龄,皮尤发现宗教是稳定的。 认同某种宗教,每日祷告,呼唤宗教非常重要并每月出席的股份自2020年以来一直是平平的,34%的美国成年人在6月的调查中表示,他们上个月曾亲自参加过各种服务,是皮尤自2020年开始询问以来最高的. Pew说,它无法知道最年轻的成年人是否会遵循旧模式或打破旧模式,并形容这个尚未解决的问题是“一个转折点或一滴一滴地”。 如果是复兴,它迄今为止属于调查中最年轻的成年人。

articles.title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有“万能钥匙”
articles.content: The first of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. A question of major importance is ‘How am I to live as a Christian’? It is one thing to be certain on biblical grounds that I have life from Christ, now I must be clear as to how I am to live the life of Christ. My purpose in setting before you some of the major principles of living the Christian life is three-fold: —I wish to sketch in a biblical theology of the Christian life. My purpose is unashamedly one of indoctrination. I wish by God’s help, by Spirit and word, to indoctrinate you in a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. —I wish to inoculate you and to immunize you against the major false views of the Christian life. Some of us desperately wish we had received such an inoculation early in our Christian experience. We spent many years chasing rabbits that we could never catch. We went after experiences and states of mind and heart in the hope that somehow in so doing we would find what it really meant to live as a Christian. —I wish to purge you of any existing misconceptions which you may presently have. It may not be pleasant but it is in your own best interests. We now examine these major principles of the Christian life. Principle 1: There is No One ‘Master Key’ to Living the Christian Life The kind of teaching I am purposing to focus upon in this principle goes something like this: There is a Christian who for many years has found himself in the doldrums. He has had his sails hoisted but he goes nowhere. It seems that he knows little of the wind of the Spirit filling his sails and carrying him anywhere. Or, to change the analogy, he may have his sails hoisted but they seem for ever to be full of holes, and while all around him have hoisted sails and appear to be making progress he seems to be going nowhere. And then one day at a conference or while reading a book or in his own devotions he comes across a passage of Scripture, say John chapter 15, and there he reads in the words of our Lord Jesus that beautiful analogy of the Christian’s relationship to Christ as the relationship of a branch to a vine. This so ignites his own spiritual life that he is almost overnight lifted to an entirely new plateau of spiritual vitality. Either the holes in his sails get mended or it is as though a mighty zephyr from God himself fills his sails, causing them to billow out to the full. He makes more substantial progress in the Christian life in six months than he has made in the previous six years. This man says that the master key to the Christian life is understanding John 15 and if others will only come to understand the concept of Christ’s relationship to his people as the branch and the vine are related they too will come to an entirely new plateau of spiritual vitality and reality in their Christian walk. Another example could be someone who has been struggling with a certain besetting sin which leaves him continually bowed down and crippled with guilt. Here is a young Christian struggling with a certain area of besetting sin, unknown to others, and he is constantly bogged down. His wheels are up to the hub-caps in mud, and no matter how much he changes the gears and pushes down on the accelerator he is spinning his wheels and all he is doing is using up petrol and making a mess. He is in that position for weeks and months perhaps, and then one day at a conference or reading a book or in his own devotions he comes to Romans, chapter 6, and he reads the glorious truth that in union with Jesus Christ all that he was as old man has been put to death, and in union with Jesus Christ the totality of the old life has been buried in Christ’s tomb and he is now a new man in Jesus Christ and he sees that he is called upon to reckon it so, and in the light of that, present himself as alive from the dead. articles.content_zh:
阿尔伯特·N·马丁在1984年班纳青年大会上发表的六篇包含教学内容的文章中的一篇文章,介绍了基督教生活的基本圣经神学. 一个非常重要的问题是:我如何作为一个基督徒活下来? 从圣经上确定我的生命来自基督是一回事,现在我必须明白我如何活基督的生命.
在你们面前,我提出一些关于基督教生活的主要原则,目的有三个方面:——我想在圣经中描绘基督教生活的神学. 我的目的就是毫不羞愧地教化别人 我希望通过上帝的帮助,通过精神和文字,将你灌输到基督教生活的基本圣经神学中去.
我希望为你们接种疫苗,并为你们接种疫苗,反对基督教生活中的重大错误观点。 我们当中有些人非常希望我们早期在基督教经验中得到这样的接种。 我们花了很多年 追赶我们永远抓不到的兔子
我们追寻经验 和精神状态和心境, 希望能找到作为基督徒生活的真正意义。 我希望清除你目前可能存在的任何误解。 这也许不愉快,但符合你的最佳利益。 我们现在审查基督教生活的这些主要原则。
然后有一天,在会议中,或者在读到一本书时,或者在自己的奉献中,他穿过了圣经的一行,如约翰·第15章,他用我们的主耶稣的话来读到,把基督教与基督的关系比作树枝与藤条的关系。
这如此点燃了他自己的精神生活,以至于几乎一夜之间被抬到一个全新的精神活力高地. 要么他的帆上有洞被修补好 要么就好像上帝亲自放出一个强大的快活器 来灌入他的帆上 让他们满地找牙 他在6个月里在基督教生活中取得了比前6年更大的实质性进步.
这个人说,基督教生活的主要关键在于理解约翰·15,如果其他人只了解基督与其人民的关系概念,因为树枝和藤蔓是相连的,他们也会在基督教行走中来到一个精神活力和现实的全新的高地。
另一个例子是,有人一直在为某种困扰他的罪行而挣扎,使他不断屈从并因罪恶而致残。 这里有一个年轻的基督教徒在挣扎着 某些困扰的罪恶领域, 其他人不知道, 他经常陷入困境。
他的车轮在泥地上被吊起,无论他如何改变齿轮并推倒了加速器,他正在旋转他的车轮,他所做的就是用上汽油并制造一团糟。
赫里斯特和他看到,他被召唤去 如此估计, 并据此, 现身 活着 从死亡。 他读了这段话,

articles.title: Peace for Second-Guessers
articles.summary: How do we know when we’ve worked hard enough? Pastor John offers six ways to fight anxiety and rest in the grace of Christ. Listen Now
articles.summary_zh: 我们如何知道我们已经足够努力了？约翰牧师提供了在基督的恩典中战胜焦虑和安息的六种方法。现在聆听
articles.title_zh: Peace for Second-Guessers
articles.content: Audio Transcript Last week, we looked at whether Pastor John was trained well enough to be a pastor when he became one in 1980. We live in a world where you can get a lot of formal training, and it can be very helpful. But all the training in the world will not alleviate the anxiety we can feel over whether we are serving people adequately. “Imposter syndrome,” some call it, or “perfectionism.” We all want to excel at our callings. We want to be capable. We want to succeed. And we want to bless others and truly impact the world for good. So, how do we learn to leave off the anxiety that says we could do everything better? That’s today on Ask Pastor John: peace for second-guessers. An anonymous man, a surgeon, writes with our question today: “Pastor John, thank you for this podcast, and for sharing your own experience as an aspiring medical professional in college, which I have heard you mention in APJ episodes 1373, 1382, 1730, and 1916 at least. I relate to that part of your story as a surgeon currently struggling with anxiety and stress related to my job. Many nights, I lie awake, worrying about my patients, whether I could have made better decisions, how I could improve my skills, or stressing over unresolved issues. “This constant drive to do more and be better makes me less present with my family, and sometimes I even yearn for early retirement. While I understand that God is sovereign over my patients and their outcomes, I also know that my own effort and diligence directly impact their care. My question is: How do I find the proper balance between resting in God’s providence and being diligent in my job, without becoming so consumed by my work that it pulls me away from my family when I’m off the clock? These competing forces are causing me inner turmoil, and I’m struggling to navigate them well.” Faith-Filled Effort That question is absolutely basic to living the Christian life, and it’s not unique to the pressures of being a surgeon. It’s an issue for teachers who want to have good lessons for their students, and for the handyman who wants his repair job not to break down the day after he leaves. So, did he do a good enough job? Did he spend enough time on it? For pastors who wonder if they’ve made enough house calls, done enough evangelism, prepared long enough on the sermon. For moms who wonder, Have I spent enough time with my kids? For consultants who wonder if they’ve put in enough hours to be worthy of the fees they’re collecting, and on and on and on. In other words, everybody who is a serious Christian faces the question, “In view of God’s sovereignty and wisdom and goodness in my life, have I done enough, or have I done too much? Am I exerting faith-filled effort to do the best job I can? Too much or too little?” Everybody faces this question. It’s a wonderful, so-important question. Our surgeon friend says, “I worry whether I could have made better decisions and how I could improve my skills.” He knows something’s off because he’s often not really present with his family when he’s present with his family. He asks, “How can I find the right balance . . . resting in God’s providence and being diligent in my job?” In the end, what I would say to start with is this: Peace of mind like that is a gift of God. It’s a fruit of the Holy Spirit. It goes beyond human rationality and figuring out. We know that because Paul says that in Philippians 4:7: “the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding.” That’s amazing. He knows you can’t figure this out. You can’t make peace happen by your rational computations. That peace will guard your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus, though it comes from him directly through means but is not entirely quantifiable with your reason. It goes beyond human rationality. So, I pray now that this gift will be given to this surgeon, and everybody else who’s listening who struggles with this — like all of us. 上星期,我们研究了约翰牧师是否受过足够好的训练,在1980年成为牧师时,他是否成为牧师. 我们生活在一个你可以接受很多正式训练的世界,这可以很有帮助. 但是,世界上的所有培训都无法减轻我们对我们是否在为人民充分服务感到的焦虑。

“冒牌综合症,”有人称之为“完美症”。 我们都想出色地履行我们的使命。 我们希望有能力。 我们希望取得成功。 我们想祝福他人,真正地影响世界。 那么,我们如何学会摆脱那些 说我们可以做得更好的焦虑? 今天,

一位匿名人士,一位外科医生,今天用我们的问题写道:“约翰神父,谢谢你的播客,感谢你把自己作为大学有抱负的医学专业人员的经验分享给大家,我听到你在APJ第1373、1382、1730和1916集至少提到了这一点。 我指的是你作为外科医生的那部分 与我的工作有关的焦虑和压力

很多晚上,我睡着, 担心我的病人, 是否我能做出更好的决定, 如何提高我的技能, “这种不断努力做更多的事情,做更好的事情,使我更不愿意与家人在一起,有时甚至渴望提前退休。

虽然我知道上帝对我病人及其结果拥有主权,但我也知道,我自己的努力和勤奋直接影响到他们的护理。 我的问题是:我如何在安息于上帝的保佑和勤奋地工作之间找到适当的平衡,而不会因为我的工作而变得如此消耗,以至于我下班时会远离家人?

这些相互竞争的力量正在引起我内心的动荡, 充满信仰的努力 这个问题对于基督教生活来说是绝对最基本的,

这对想为学生上好课的老师来说, 那么,他做得够好吗? 他花足够的时间吗? 在布道上准备了足够长的时间。

给那些好奇的妈妈们 我和孩子们在一起的时间够多了吗? 这些顾问想知道他们是否投入了足够的时间, 换句话说,每个认真的基督徒都面对一个问题,“鉴于我生命中上帝的主权、智慧和善良,我做得够不够,还是做了太多?

articles.title_zh: 世俗与神的友谊
articles.content: If you’re a faithful follower of Jesus today, try this experiment: Imagine that in five years you have completely walked away from Jesus. You’re not questioning or struggling or arguing anymore. You’re not wrestling with whether to stay or leave the church. You never open the Bible. You have almost no impulse to pray. You’re shutting out anyone and everyone who wants to talk about God. You’re just gone. All the way gone . I hope it feels horrible, even unimaginable. I’m not exaggerating when I say nothing worse could happen to you (Revelation 14:11). If you’re honest in this hypothetical horror, what do you suspect might have led you away? What could have possibly drowned your once-strong love for Jesus? You might immediately assume some stubborn sin, or an especially painful relationship, or something in the Bible that never sat right with you. Sadly, souls discard Jesus every day for all kinds of awful reasons. If you forced yourself to list a dozen serious threats to your faith, would you think to list the risk of worldliness ? Do you ever fear that you would love this world too much to keep loving Jesus? Too few of us fear enough. Could You Be Demas? We know how dangerous worldliness can be because God gave us Demas. He inspired the apostle Paul to report, “Demas, in love with this present world, has deserted me” (2 Timothy 4:10). Demas once seemed to be an unusually strong, devoted, and fruitful lover of Jesus (Colossians 4:14) — a bold and effective minister of the gospel! — but he kept nibbling at the wrong buffets. And as he nibbled, an unholy hunger grew and grew until he spat Jesus out of his mouth. Paul watched his once-close friend die by short-lived pleasure. Worldliness is loving what the world loves at the expense of what God loves. Sometimes, worldliness is a love for something bad — drunkenness, gossip, violence, pornography. Often, it’s a distorted and disproportionate love for something good — family, food, career, sex. The unbelieving world loves those things, but in ways that defy God and deface all he loves — his word, his Son, his church. Do you love any calling, hobby, or relationship in such a way that it has started to erode the most important loves? Do you see hints of Demas’s descent anywhere in your life? Do you find your thought life being devoured by work? Do you spend hours and hours with your family and rarely talk about Jesus? Do you never miss your favorite show, but you struggle to find time to pray? Do you drag your feet to get to church and rush home to catch the game? Jesus warns us about the seed that falls among the thorns of worldliness: “They are those who hear the word, but the cares of the world and the deceitfulness of riches and the desires for other things enter in and choke the word, and it proves unfruitful” (Mark 4:18–19). He’s describing soul suffocation — the sharp tentacles of worldliness slowly wrapping themselves around a heart and strangling out hope, joy, and love. It’s horrifying. Why would anyone ever let that happen? Because Satan knows all too well how to make worldly anxieties seem bigger than God (Matthew 4:2–3), and he schemes to make earthly pleasures seem sweeter than God (Genesis 3:4–5). “This world is all that really matters,” he whispers. And if we believe him, we end up wanting the world God made — but hold the God, please. Four Dangers of Worldliness When this temptation comes — and it will come — will we cave and run like Demas, or will we fight for the only love that will truly satisfy? God arms us to face the deadly thorns: Do not love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that is in the world — the desires of the flesh and the desires of the eyes and pride of life — is not from the Father but is from the world. And the world is passing away along with its desires, but whoever does the will of God abides forever. (1 John 2:15–17) Do not love the world. Worldliness, these verses tea
articles.content_zh:
如果你今天是耶稣的忠实追随者,请尝试这个实验: 想象五年后你完全离开了耶稣 你不再质疑或争吵。 你们不是在争先恐后, 你从来没有打开圣经。 你几乎没有祈祷的冲动。 任何想谈论上帝的人,

你刚刚走了。 一直不见了。 我希望这感觉可怕,甚至难以想象。 我并没有夸张, 如果你在这种假想的恐怖中诚实, 还有什么能淹没你曾经对耶稣的爱?

你可能立即承担一些固执的罪过, 或一种特别痛苦的关系, 或者圣经中从未与你同在的东西。 可悲的是,灵魂每天都以各种可怕的理由抛弃耶稣. 如果你强迫自己 列出十几个严重的威胁 你的信仰, 你会考虑 列出 世界的风险?

你是否曾担心过你会太爱这个世界 不再爱耶稣? 我们中恐惧的人太少了 你能成为德马斯吗? 我们知道世界有多危险 因为上帝给了我们德马斯 他激励使徒保罗报告说,“德马斯爱上了这个现在的世界,抛弃了我”(Timothy 4:10)。

德马斯曾经似乎是耶稣的异常强壮,执着,富有成果的爱人(Colosians 4:14)——一位勇敢而有效的福音大臣! ——但他却不停地在错误的自助餐上抱怨. 当他吞咽时,不祥的饥饿逐渐增长,直到他吐出耶稣的嘴. 保罗看着他曾经亲密的朋友死于短暂的快乐.

世界是爱世界所爱 牺牲上帝所爱 有时,世界性是对一些坏东西的热爱——醉酒,八卦,暴力,色情. 这往往是一种扭曲和不相称的对美好事物的爱——家庭、食物、职业、性。 不信世的人们喜欢那些东西,但是却以藐视上帝和诋毁他所爱的一切的方式——他的话,他的儿子,他的教堂.

你是否喜欢任何电话、爱好或关系 以至于它开始侵蚀最重要的爱? Demas在一生中, 你发现你的思想生活被工作吞噬了吗? 你和家人一起呆上好几个小时 很少谈论耶稣? 你从来没有错过你最喜欢的节目, 但你努力寻找时间祈祷?

你拖着脚去教堂 赶回家接球吗? 耶稣警告我们,世界的荆棘中落下的种子是:“他们就是那些听话的人,但世界的关心和财富的欺骗性以及对其他事物的欲望进入并扼杀这个词,这证明是不果实的”(Mark 4:18-19)。

他描述灵魂窒息 — — 世界的尖锐触角慢慢地包围着心,扼杀希望、喜悦和爱。 这太可怕了。 为什么有人会让这种事发生? 因为撒旦非常了解如何使世界的焦虑看起来比上帝大(Matthew 4:2–3),他计划使地球的快乐看起来比上帝更甜(Genesis 3:4–5).

“这个世界才是真正重要的。” 如果我们相信他,我们最终希望得到上帝创造的世界——但请抓住上帝。 世界的四种危险 当这种诱惑到来时——它将到来时——我们是否会像德马斯那样洞穴和奔跑,还是我们将为真正满足的唯一爱而斗争? 上帝让我们面对致命的刺: 不爱世间或世间物.

若有人爱世间,则父之爱不在他. 因为世上的一切——肉体的欲望和眼睛的欲望和生命的骄傲——不是来自父亲,而是来自世界. 世界正在随其欲望而逝去,但谁遵循真主的旨意,谁将永居其中。 (约翰: 2:15-17) 不爱世间. 世界,这些诗歌茶

articles.title: The Dangers of Getting Advice from the Internet
articles.summary: Melissa and Courtney discuss how to cultivate discernment when seeking advice online and recognize the danger of letting AI or influencers replace wise counsel from the body of Christ.
articles.summary_zh: Melissa和Courtney讨论了如何在网上寻求建议时培养洞察力，并认识到让人工智能或影响者取代基督身体的明智建议的危险。
articles.title_zh: 从互联网上获取建议的危险
articles.content: Melissa and Courtney discuss how to cultivate discernment when seeking advice. They talk about how sometimes we think we need information when what we really need is relationship. They discuss what kind of advice they like to get from the internet or ChatGPT, why they don’t recommend it for wisdom issues such as marriage and parenting, and why we shouldn’t let advice from AI or influencers replace wise counsel from the body of Christ. Resource Mentioned: Kitchen-Table Counseling Within Your Local Church Related Resources: Let’s Talk: Finding a Mentor and Being a Mentor Want to Grow in Wisdom? You Need Gospel Friends. Why AI Parenting Advice Falls Short Don’t Treat AI as Your Pastor Discussion Questions: 1. When you face a difficult decision or struggle, where do you typically turn for advice? 2. How do you discern whether online advice is helpful or unwise? 3. What makes advice offered within a personal relationship different from advice taken from an online blog or influencer or generated by AI? 4. How might repeated exposure to ideas about marriage, parenting, or relationships on social media influence our thinking without us being aware of it? 5. What do we lose when we turn to online sources for counsel instead of investing in relationships with people who know and love us? 6. Who in your life knows you well enough to speak honestly into your decisions and loves you enough to do so? How can you cultivate those kinds of relationships? 7. How would you like to grow in your ability to offer wise counsel to others?
articles.content_zh: Melissa和Courtney讨论如何在寻求建议时培养辨识力. 他们谈论我们有时认为我们需要信息, 当我们真正需要的是关系。 他们讨论他们喜欢从网络或ChatGPT获得什么样的建议, 为何不推荐给婚姻及养育等智慧问题, 资源参考:在您当地教会的相关资源中提供厨房-餐桌咨询:让我们谈谈:寻找导师和成为导师想要在智慧中成长? 你需要福音的朋友。 为何AI的家长建议会落下, 2. 你如何辨别在线建议是否有益或不明智? 3. 个人关系中提供的建议与在线博客或影响者或大赦国际提供的建议有何不同? 4. 在社交媒体上反复接触关于婚姻、养育子女或关系的想法会如何影响我们的思想,而我们却不知道这一点? 5. 当我们转向在线律师来源而不是投资于与了解和热爱我们的人的关系时,我们会失去什么? 6. 在你的生活中,谁足够了解你 诚实地谈论你的决定, 并爱你 足够这样做? 你怎么能养成那种关系? 7. 如何提高你向他人提供明智建议的能力?

articles.title: Beware Making Mental Illness an Identity
articles.summary: ‘All in Your Head’ is a concrete and compelling remapping of mental health culture with impressive explanatory power.
articles.summary_zh: “All in Your Head”是对心理健康文化的具体而引人注目的重新映射，具有令人印象深刻的解释力。
articles.title_zh: 小心让精神疾病成为一种身份
articles.content: In the years since he was involuntarily committed to a mental health institution for bipolar disorder, Frederik deBoer has wrestled with both profound gratitude for a system that saved his life and also palpable frustration that his experience of healing has become so rare. All in Your Head: Illness as Identity, Trauma as Fashion, and the Desire to Be Disordered is the latest broadside from one of the internet’s most heterodox thinkers and writers. As an “old school” Marxist best known for writing The Cult of Smart , deBoer takes aim at how the cultural drift within his own tribe is responsible for making mental health care so elusive for those who need it most: “The tendency to treat mental illness as an exciting adventure, the endless romanticization of lunacy in popular culture, is one of many aggravations I have nursed for years” (8). The root of his aggravation—the treatment of mental illness and disability as an identity to be celebrated rather than a disability that needs treatment —isn’t all in his head. The use of talk therapy rose 47 percent between 2019 and 2024 . A 2025 LifeStance survey found around 29 percent of U.S. adults have self-diagnosed their mental health condition after consuming online content, rising to 50 percent among Gen Z (versus 9 percent of boomers). Of the people who self-diagnose symptoms, almost a quarter (24 percent) “rarely” or “never” feel the need to take the next step to discuss them with a qualified clinician. DeBoer argues that rather than reducing the stigma surrounding mental illness, the inordinate attention given to the mildly and dubiously afflicted is a dangerous distraction crowding out help for the severely ill. Accelerated by social media, this “gentrification of disability” has become a full-blown social contagion, compromising even the experts and institutions responsible for mental health care (153–54). DeBoer is largely right, and the cultural shift he identifies has real-world implications both inside and outside the church. But the same ideological priors that so sharpen deBoer’s critique also suffer from two significant blind spots that, were they addressed, would make All in Your Head the more courageous, more constructive, and, therefore, more widely read manifesto we need. General Bipartisan Ire If you picked up All in Your Head to understand how modern therapy culture spread like wildfire across social media over the last several years, it’s not immediately obvious why deBoer starts his argument with an in-depth analysis of the anti-psychiatry movement’s influence in late 20th century politics and academia. But, if you can forgive me the pun, there’s a method to his madness. After a blistering critique of “rightwing libertarian” policies that neglected mental illness, he cashes in on the subsequent trust he earns with left-leaning readers to launch a series of absolute haymakers toward “a species of thought that sometimes amounts to a kind of leftist pseudo-radicalism or a libertarian fantasy” (198) that drives the “destabilizing . . . move from mental illness as reality to mental illness as symbol” (8). American individualism and anti-institutional bias aren’t new, but the painstakingly specific way deBoer traces their spread through the culture surrounding mental health and therapy is refreshing and instructive. Our “apolitical romanticism of resistance to modern society” fuels two opposite errors: On the right, mental illness is sometimes seen as either imagined or a symptom of weak character. But on the left, the same romanticism often describes mental disability as more en abling than dis abling, as if neurodivergent minorities don’t need society’s help—society needs theirs. Gentrification of Disability DeBoer’s emphatic rejection of this predominantly progressive error— of “making a medical disorder an identity”—is the “overarching principle of [his] book” (165). This is never more clear in what he labels “the gentrification of disability,” where “diagnoses bec
articles.content_zh: 在他非自愿地被送入精神病院治疗两极分化后的几年里,弗雷德里克·德·博尔带着对挽救他生命的系统深表感谢和明显的沮丧,因为他的治愈经验变得如此罕见. 在你的脑海中:作为身份的疾病,作为时尚的创伤,以及希望陷入混乱,是互联网上最异形的思想家和作家之一的最新一面。 作为一位最以写作"聪明的邪教"而出名的"老派"马克思主义者,德博尔以自己的部落内部的文化漂移为目的,让那些最需要的人如此难以接受精神保健:"将精神疾病视为激动人心的冒险的倾向,在流行文化中无休止地浪漫化的放荡,是多年来我所照顾的诸多恶化之一"(8). 他的病情恶化的根源——将精神疾病和残疾视为一种值得庆贺的身份,而不是需要治疗的残疾——并不是他脑子里所有的东西。 2019年至2024年间,谈话疗法的使用率上升了47%. 2025年生活稳定调查发现,约29%的美国成年人在消费了在线内容后自行诊断出自己的心理健康状况,在Gen Z中上升到了50%(相对于9%的繁荣者). 在自我诊断的人群中,近四分之一(24%)的人“勉强”或“从未”感到有必要采取下一步措施,与合格的临床医生讨论这些症状。 DeBoer认为,对受轻度和可疑折磨的人的过度关注,与其减少精神疾病的污名化,不如说是一种危险的分心,挤出对重病患者的帮助。 社交媒体加速了这种 " 残疾意识化 " ,已成为一种全面的社会传染,甚至损害负责精神保健的专家和机构(153-54)。 DeBoer基本上是正确的,他所认定的文化转变在教堂内外都具有现实世界的影响. 但德布尔批评如此尖锐的意识形态前科也遭遇了两个重大盲点,如果这些盲点得到解决,将使你的头脑更加勇敢,更具建设性,因此,我们需要更广泛地阅读宣言。 一般两党爱尔兰人 如果你在脑海中看到现代治疗文化在过去几年里如何像野火一样在社交媒体上传播,那么DeBoer为什么以深入分析20世纪后期反精神病运动在政治和学术界的影响为出发点,这并不明显。 但是,如果你能原谅我的双关语,他疯狂是有办法的。 在对忽视了精神疾病的“右翼自由派”政策猛烈批评后,他依靠后来与左翼读者获得的信任,发动了一系列绝对的干草人,走向“有时相当于一种左翼伪激进主义或自由派幻想的思想”(198年),这种思想驱使“从精神疾病变成现实,转变为精神疾病作为象征”(8)。 美国的个人主义和反机构偏见并非新事物, 但DeBoer通过精神卫生与治疗的文化, 我们“反对现代社会的政治浪漫主义”助长了两个相反的错误: 在右边,精神疾病有时被视为一种想象或一种弱性症状. 但是在左边,同样的浪漫主义常常将精神残疾描述为比分身更困难,仿佛神经分身的少数民族不需要社会的帮助——社会需要他们的帮助。 对DeBoer残疾人的强烈反对,即 " 使医疗障碍成为身份 " 这一主要进步的错误,是 " 书中的首要原则 " (165)。 这在他所称的“残疾的基因化”中再清楚不过了。

articles.title: How a Former Prisoner in Iran Wants You to Pray for Christians in Chains
articles.summary: Pray not only for what God might do for Christian prisoners in Iran but for what God might do through them, for his glory.
articles.summary_zh: 不仅祈求神可以为伊朗的基督徒囚犯做些什么，而且祈求神可以通过他们为祂的荣耀做些什么。
articles.title_zh: 伊朗前囚犯如何希望你为被锁的基督徒祈祷
articles.content: Not long ago, I had a surreal phone call with two young Christian men serving prison sentences in one of Iran’s hardest prisons. They’re there because they refuse to stop preaching about Jesus. When I asked how I could pray for them, their answer wasn’t what you might expect. “Pray that we would not be released until our job here is finished,” they said. They had led numerous fellow prisoners to faith. Now, their chief concern was to remain inside long enough to disciple them. The call took me straight back to the five years I spent in prison for my faith. Now, these dear brothers (let’s call them Vahid and Reza) were behind bars, and I was outside. As we spoke, I pictured the wards and corridors, imagined the sounds and smells, and remembered how hard it was not to know how many years I would be there. But it was also an encouraging call. Vahid and Reza were in high spirits, talking about Bible passages that were sustaining them and how the Lord was at work. They didn’t see themselves in a miserable, dark place. They saw themselves in a different mission field. Their focus was the same as Paul’s in Colossians 4:3: “Pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to declare the mystery of Christ, on account of which I am in prison.” Paul’s request wasn’t for an open prison door but for an open door for the gospel. Pray for Gospel Fruit Vahid and Reza’s request resonated with me. I remember being unable to pray for my own release. I tried on a few occasions, but I couldn’t open my mouth to ask the Lord to release me. If I’m following Christ, I cannot choose the path. I cannot choose the location. I should follow him wherever he goes. And as I followed him to prison, he brought beautiful fruit. They didn’t see themselves in a miserable, dark place. They saw themselves in a different mission field. I think of one prisoner, a devout Muslim, who was wrongly accused of spying for Iran’s enemies. He was praying he would be released and was frustrated to get no answer. He approached me one day, saying, “Farshid, our God is dead. But I’ve heard yours is alive. Will you pray for me?” Fearing it might be a trap, I took him quietly aside and prayed briefly in the name of Jesus: “Lord, you know this man. Please hear his prayer.” The very next day, the man rushed over excitedly and gave me a huge hug. That morning, he had learned his name had been cleared. He was released two weeks later. Our God is indeed alive. The Lord was also at work softening my parents’ hearts toward Christ during those years. I always say that even if only for the salvation of my parents, my time in prison was worth it. So, when you pray for persecuted believers, pray not only for what God might do for them but—as Vahid and Reza requested—for what God might do through them, for his glory. Pray for gospel fruit. Pray for Comfort and Endurance I don’t want to make prison sound easier than it was. The suffering was real. So pray also for comfort and endurance. They beat me; they broke my toe. But the prolonged separation from my two children was the hardest burden to bear. The day I went to prison, my son was 2 years old and my daughter was 7. Missing their childhoods was an unspeakable loss. Yet I know others who have suffered much more than I did. I think of a brother currently in prison who has been tortured. I think of a sister who was sexually assaulted when she was arrested. Even the apostle Paul was at times “so utterly burdened beyond [his] strength that [he] despaired of life itself.” And his request to the church was simple: “You also must help us by prayer” (2 Cor. 1:8, 11). Brothers and sisters like these need us to pray for them with love. Whatever the situation, we can pray that God would grant the suffering believer comfort, peace, and endurance. The more specific the prayers, the better. While in prison, I received letters from people around the world who were praying for me. One wrote, “I am praying for your sleep. May the Lord give you
articles.content_zh: 不久前,我和两名基督教青年在伊朗最困难的监狱之一服刑。 因为他们拒绝停止宣扬耶稣。 我问自己如何为他们祈祷, 他们说,“祈祷我们在这里的工作结束前不会被释放。” 他们带领许多同狱囚犯信仰。 现在,他们最关心的是 留在里面的时间足够长 让他们入门。 那通电话把我带回我为信仰在监狱里度过的五年。 现在,这些亲爱的兄弟(让我们叫他们Vahid和Reza)在监狱里,我在外面。 就在我们发言的时候,我想象了病房和走廊,想象了声音和气味,并想起了不知道我会在那里呆了多少年是多么困难。 但这也是一个令人鼓舞的呼吁。 瓦希德和礼萨精神高尚,谈论着支撑着他们的圣经段落,以及上帝是如何工作的. 他们并没有看到自己在一个悲惨而黑暗的地方。 他们看到自己在另一个任务领域。 他们的重心与保罗在Colosisans 4:3中的重心相同 : “ 也为我们祈祷,以便上帝为我们打开一个话语之门,宣告基督之谜,我为此而入狱。 ” 保罗的要求并不是打开监狱的门, 祈求福音果实Vahid, 我还记得我无法为自己的自由祈祷 我尝试过几次, 我无法选择道路。 我无法选择位置 我该跟着他 不管他去哪 当我跟着他进监狱时 他带来了美丽的水果 他们并没有看到自己在一个悲惨而黑暗的地方。 他们看到自己在另一个任务领域。 我想到一个囚犯, 一个虔诚的穆斯林, 他祈祷自己会被释放,并因得不到答复而感到沮丧。 有一天,他靠近我说,“法尔希德,我们的神死了。 但我听说你还活着。 你会为我祈祷吗?” 我担心那可能是一个陷阱,悄悄地把他放在一旁,以耶稣的名义简短地祈祷道:"主啊,你认识这个人。 请听他的祈祷。” 第二天,那个男人激动地冲过来,给了我一个巨大的拥抱。 那天早晨,他得知自己的名字已被清除。 他两周后被释放。 我们的神确实还活着。 在那些年中,上帝也在努力使我父母对基督的心软化。 我总是说,即使只是为了拯救我的父母, 我在监狱的时间是值得的。 当你们祈祷受迫害的信士们的时候,你们应当祈祷真主所意欲者,犹如瓦希德和里萨所意欲者那样,祈祷真主所意欲者。 祈取福音果实. 祈祷舒适与耐力, 苦难是真实的。 因此也祈求安慰和耐力. 他们打我,把我的脚趾弄断了 但是,与我的两个孩子长期分离是最难承受的负担。 我入狱那天,我的儿子2岁,女儿7岁。 失去童年是一个难以形容的损失。 然而,我认识其他人,他们遭受的痛苦比我多得多。 我想到目前在监狱里的一个兄弟 曾遭受酷刑 我想到一个妹妹在被捕时曾被性侵犯. 甚至使徒保罗,有时也“承受了超过他力量的沉重负担,以致于他对生命本身绝望”。 他向教堂提出的要求很简单:“你还必须通过祈祷帮助我们”(第1:8、11节)。 这样的兄弟姐妹需要我们用爱为他们祈祷. 无论情况如何,我们可以祈祷上帝会给予受苦受难的信徒以安慰、和平和耐力。 祈祷越具体越好 在狱中,我收到了世界各地为我祈祷的人的来信。 有人写道:“我在为你的睡眠祈祷。 愿主赐予你

articles.content: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include books about the Old Testament, Proverbs, faithful presence, the life and influence of Tim Keller, and a whole lot more. Westminster Books is continuing their Reformation sale by offering discounts on ESV Bibles as well as the tremendous new 500th anniversary edition of Tyndale’s New Testament. Recommended Reading How the Mainstream Recruits for the Manosphere. Aaron Renn explains how “asymmetric blame, hectoring lectures, and selectively revived norms are driving young men to the influencers the mainstream condemns.” How Mental Illness Became an Identity. Myles Werntz has an interesting review of a new book by Fredrik deBoer that explains how mental illness became an identity. “Mental illness in the 21st century is an expanding category—and one increasingly dominated by its most functional and therefore visible members. That displacement—in our collective imagination and public discourse—of the profoundly mentally ill by my college students didn’t happen all at once. And how did it happen? Was it because of the closure of traditional mental hospitals, like those of One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest ? Was it because of the internet-driven phenomenon of self-diagnosis by very functional influencers? The marginalization of psychiatry as a profession? Or denial, romanticization, and politics?” It Can Happen Here, Too. “As numerous countries in Europe experience riots, many in America are asking, ‘What on earth is happening on the continent that was, in many ways, the cradle of Western civilization?’ As historic buildings, places of worship, and commercial properties combust before our eyes on the nightly news, how are we to make sense of this?” Carl Trueman warns that what’s happening in Europe could also happen in the United States. 8 Ways to Help Your Kids Love the Church. Shiphrah Lakka offers a series of ways to help your kids learn to love the church. “While discipleship at home is extremely important and something every Christian parent should pursue, it can never replace the church. Reading Scripture together, praying as a family, and teaching our children about God within our homes are vital practices. Yet God’s design for believers extends beyond the walls of our homes. He calls us to belong to a community of believers who worship, serve, and do life together.” I Hate Your Halloween Decorations. Marc Sims writes about the reality of Halloween today. “The next time I am out, we will really slow down to take in the diorama you set up of black hooded figures encircling a pentagram-alter with a fake infant set in the middle of it, that way he can become familiar with Satanic rituals and child sacrifice. I mean, where else is he going to get this important cultural experience? Apparently, you are under the impression that becoming desensitized to violence and death is an important step for our whole neighborhood to take in—to celebrate, even. Here, frumpy old Marc ( boooo! ) was worried about why our culture seems ever more eager to relish death and the demonic—but you have shown me that this is really just fun! Save a fake a corpse for me!” Why Paper Books Endure. Daniel Darling explains his ongoing love for paper books (even while he’s not entirely opposed to electronic ones). “When I began my writing career in the early 2,000s, every single writing conference I attended featured speakers who issued grave warnings. E-books would eventually take over. Paper books would be a thing of the past. Libraries are nice relics of another era. Except that didn’t happen.” Something Worth Doing These words by Maltbie Davenport Babcock have often been a challenge to me, and I wouldn’t be surprised if they challenge you as well. We often think that if we had that man’s means or that man’s ability or that man’s opportunity, we could do something worth doing; but, as we are, there is no possibility of any great thing. Yet God does n

articles.title: Is It a Sin to Use AI Porn?
articles.summary: What happens when the people in porn are not real exist, but are merely generated by AI? articles.content: Over the past two decades, I have written a great deal about pornography . At many different times and in many different forms, I have urged people to consider a long list of arguments against it. I’m thankful to have interacted with many people who have come to see pornography as evil and who have committed themselves to sexual purity. Some of the strongest and most effective arguments against using pornography are based upon the humanity of the people who are involved in it. So, for example, in “ 7 Good Reasons To Stop Looking at Porn Right Now ,” I wrote that we need to consider the cost to those who make it. “Pornography exacts a high cost of those who create it—the cost to their bodies, to their souls, to their mental well-being, to their dignity, to their future. A vast amount of the pornography you enjoy is created by people against their wills. The simple fact is, by watching porn, you are watching rape and deriving pleasure from it. You become a willing participant in sexual violence and you allow that actor on the screen to suffer for your pleasure.” Even if some pornography is consensual, a great deal of pornography is not, and the viewer cannot know which is which. Similarly, in “ 8 Sins You Commit Whenever You Look at Porn ,” I said that those who watch it are guilty of sexual assault. “A person who drives a getaway car for a band of bank robbers will rightly be charged with murder for anyone who is killed in committing that crime. The person who voluntarily watches sexual assault for purposes of titillation is rightly guilty of that sexual assault. And a nauseating quantity of pornography is violent in nature, displaying men taking advantage of women. Sometimes these women have volunteered for such degradation and sometimes they are forced or raped into it. To watch such horrifying smut is to be a participant in it and to bear the moral blemish of it.” While these are far from the only arguments against pornography, I believe they are especially effective ones. But what happens when the characters involved in pornography are no longer people? What happens when they no longer exist at all, but are merely generated by AI? Could AI allow us to create “ethical pornography” that solves one of the foremost concerns that come with “real” pornography? In other words, is it a sin to look at AI-generated porn ? (For our purposes, we will assume that we are already rejecting deepfake porn—using the likeness of an existing person—as morally repugnant and both immoral and illegal. Instead, we are considering images of people who are generated entirely by AI.) The simple answer is yes: it is as sinful to look at AI-generated porn as it is to look at human-created porn. While some of the arguments may not be as relevant, the majority are unchanged. Before I explain how and why, I want you to listen to a warning: we are all experts at circumventing the spirit of the law by abiding within the strict letter of the law. There is something deep within us that wants to defy the rules that are given to us, and we become skilled at justifying the ways we do this. Often this involves reducing morality to a strict binary, then convincing ourselves that because we have not blatantly broken the law, we have abided by it. This was exactly the sin of the Pharisees of Jesus’s day who would strictly tithe the spices they grew in their gardens, yet fail to live according to the higher principles of justice, mercy, and faithfulness. There is something of the Pharisee in each one of us. With that in mind, here are reasons why it is a sin to use pornography that has been generated by AI. You are still lusting , even if you are lusting after a person who exists only on a screen. To lust is to long for an illicit sexual pleasure, and to long for an illicit sexual pleasure is to find satisfaction in what God has forbidden. articles.title: How Ordinary Christians Can Help Others Follow Jesus
articles.summary: Salvador Blanco-Perello shows how everyday activities can become opportunities to help others follow Jesus.
articles.summary_zh: Salvador Blanco-Perello展示了日常活动如何成为帮助他人跟随耶稣的机会。
articles.title_zh: 普通基督徒如何帮助他人跟随耶稣
articles.content: Ask a handful of Christians to define “discipling,” and you’ll probably get a handful of different answers . Some may mention meeting with another follower of Jesus for an hour each week. Another might say it means attending the weekly Sunday school class on discipleship. Someone else says it involves teaching another Christian how to make disciples who disciple others . But ultimately, discipling others means giving someone access to your life. That’s how Jesus did it. Jesus’ whole life was a teaching moment for his disciples. Not only the miraculous parts of his life, but the ordinary ones too. The times in between: walking, talking, eating. This approach is often inconvenient, but it was the key ingredient to Jesus’ discipleship plan. I want to propose a simple principle for discipling: bring someone with you. Sure, there’s more to discipling, but you won’t disciple anyone if you don’t bring anyone along to what you’re already doing as a follower of Jesus. Call it discipling as double-duty. Imagine what it could look like. By doing something as simple as sitting in worship with someone, you may learn how to serve your own family better. Perhaps you’ll see how a young father serves his wife by taking the baby out so his wife can focus on the sermon or prayers. Perhaps you’ll be able to model your own worship habits. Corporate worship is a form of discipling. In fact, it’s the center from which all discipling flows . We learn to worship Jesus privately as we learn from other Christians publicly. Don’t miss on what you can teach or learn by observing Christians around you before, during, and after worship services. Or perhaps you can bring someone along to a community group to sing, pray, bear each other’s burdens, and apply the sermon more deeply to their lives. By bringing a person you’re discipling or being discipled by, perhaps you both learn new forms of hospitality . Maybe you learn how to disagree more lovingly and patiently. You learn to rejoice with those who rejoice and weep with those who weep. You could also bring someone along as you evangelize . Often, Christians don’t know how to evangelize because they’ve simply never seen another Christian do it. Does the person you disciple have a chance to see how you might share the gospel with someone? Even if you do all these things, someone you’re discipling must be able to see your walk with Jesus in order to replicate what they see in everyday life. The disciples didn’t just see Jesus preach the Sermon on the Mount . They saw the moments in between. They saw not only how he taught, but what he did after he taught. Jesus did say: “Therefore whoever relaxes one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven, but whoever does them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven” (Matt. 5:19). Discipling as double-duty will mean bringing someone along with you to the most ordinary moments of life. It will involve both teaching and doing what Christ commands. On the grocery run. The walk around the neighborhood. The car ride when you’d rather listen to music. As you bring other followers of Jesus with you into your existing rhythms of following Jesus, don’t underestimate what God might be teaching others. All of life following Jesus can be an opportunity to disciple others. Maybe the question shouldn’t be: “How can I make more time to disciple others?” But instead: “How can I use the time I have to disciple others?” Everybody does not have time for everybody, but everybody has time for somebody.
articles.content_zh:
让少数基督徒定义“纪律”, 有些人可能提到每周会和另一个耶稣的追随者会面一小时. 另一种说法可能表示,这意味着参加每周一次的"周日"学校的门徒会. 有人说,这涉及到教另一个基督徒 如何使门徒谁门徒。
但归根结底,管教别人意味着 给别人进入你的生活。 耶稣就是这样做的。 耶稣一生都是他的门徒们的教诲时刻. 不仅是他生命中的奇迹 也是普通的 中间的时代:行走,说话,吃. 这种做法往往不方便,但它是耶稣的门徒计划的关键要素。
我想提出一个简单的纪律原则:带一个人来。 当然,还有更多的纪律约束,但如果你不把任何人带到你作为耶稣的追随者已经在做的事情上,你就不会门徒。 称其为"纪律"为"双重义务". 想象一下它会是什么样子。
通过做一些简单的事情, 和别人一起礼拜, 你可以学习如何更好地为自己的家庭服务。 可能你会看到年轻父亲如何为妻子服务, 或许你可以模仿自己的崇拜习惯。 企业崇拜是纪律约束的一种. 事实上,这是所有纪律都来自的中心。
我们在公开学习其他基督徒时,学会私下崇拜耶稣. 在礼拜活动之前、期间和之后, 或许你可以带一个人到一个社区团体去唱歌、祈祷、相互承担负担,
基督教徒通常不会传福音, 门徒们有没有机会 看看你如何和别人分享福音? 即使你做了这些事,你纪律严明的人 也必须能看到你和耶稣的行走, 以复制他们在日常生活中看到的。
门徒们不只看到耶稣在山上宣扬赛门教。 他们看到了中间的瞬间 他们不仅看到了他如何教书,还看到了他在教书后的所作所为.
耶稣确实说过:“因此,凡放松这些最最次要的诫命之一并教别人做同样的事情的人,在天国中称为最少的;凡这样做并教他们的人,在天国中称为伟大”(Matt. 5:19)。 分离为双重义务 将意味着带人 与你一起生活 最普通的时刻。
它既包括教学,也包括执行基督的命令。 在杂货跑。 绕行相邻. 你宁愿听音乐, 当你把其他的耶稣追随者带入你跟随耶稣的节奏时, 追随耶稣的所有生命都可以成为门徒他人的机会.
也许问题不应该是:我怎样才能让更多的时间给别人? 却取而代之:"我如何能用我的时间去门徒? 每个人都没有时间为每个人, 但每个人都有时间为某人。

articles.title: 从敬拜领袖到杀妻凶手
articles.summary: 贪婪不只是贪钱，也可能是贪恋地位、名声，以及掌控一切的感觉。一桩令人震惊的杀妻案提醒我们：当人既想满足私欲，又不肯承担后果，就可能亲手毁掉自己原本拥有的幸福。
articles.content: 他看上去是个好基督徒。事实上，他还是一位带领敬拜的平信徒长老。俄亥俄州二月的夜晚寒气逼人，他那不起眼的家却温暖而寻常，两个年幼的女儿还在屋里熟睡。然而，警方执法记录仪拍下的画面，与这一切形成了强烈反差。他惊慌失措，泣不成声，身穿印有“与神的大能相称的异象”（God-Sized Vision）字样的卫衣，告诉警察：窃贼闯进家里，开枪打死了躺在床上的妻子，然后逃走了。 但这套说辞经不起查证。曾参加《美国偶像》（American Idol）的凯勒布·弗林（Caleb Flynn），于 9 月 29 日被判谋杀妻子罪成立。大量证据表明，他一心想除掉妻子，好与婚外情对象在一起；对方也是他所在教会的一名领唱歌手。 庭审视频显示，律师宣读了弗林与情人之间的短信，其中流露出盼着他妻子死去的念头。弗林坐在那里，始终面无表情。在他被判终身监禁、不得假释前几分钟，妻子的家人 向他宣读了女儿们写来的信 。 那一刻，弗林仿佛尝到了一点真实的地狱滋味：那些曾经爱他的人，用自己的话提醒他，他永远失去了什么。这些话，也成了对他所作所为的公正审判。 一个带领敬拜的人，怎么会走到这一步？ 从贪婪走向谋杀 有人会说，是情欲。他们没说错。任何基督徒都不该低估不正当幻想的力量。我们任由想象沉溺其中，迟早就会想要付诸行动。奸淫会带来毁灭性的后果。难怪所罗门要儿子想一想：“人若怀里搋火，衣服岂能不烧呢？”（ 箴 6:27 ） 但如果只看见情欲，就漏掉了其他问题。情欲可以解释他为什么背弃婚约，却未必能解释他为什么扣下扳机。这个身穿“与神的大能相称的异象”卫衣的男人，将在监狱里度过余生，不只是因为情欲，也是因为贪婪。 在美国，对婚姻不满的人几乎可以出于任何理由提出离婚。无论从法律、政治还是现实条件来看，都没有什么使弗林不能与情人在一起，而必须留在妻子身边。即使离婚，他也极有可能仍能与妻子共同享有女儿的监护权。 那么，为什么阿什莉·弗林（Ashley Flynn）“非死不可”？因为发起离婚意味着他必须承认自己的奸淫，不仅向妻子承认，也要向周围所有人承认。他必须离开主日敬拜的聚光灯，也会失去在岳父手下那份收入丰厚的工作。 我们无法看透弗林的内心，也无法完全了解他复杂的动机。但我怀疑，他想要的是婚外情，却不愿付出婚外情的代价。 贪婪不易察觉 许多人都知道，情欲多么善于欺骗人。但对不少福音派信徒来说，贪婪却是一条更难揪出来的蛇。一个原因是，贪婪不像情欲，贪婪可以披上美德的外衣。一个基督徒若被教会里的弟兄姊妹看见自己的色情浏览记录，会感到羞耻；但如果他为了事业野心不顾一切，却很可能期待大家支持、肯定他。 贪婪有时藏得很深。一听到这个词，我们很容易只想到守财奴埃比尼泽·斯克鲁奇（Ebenezer Scrooge，《圣诞颂歌》主角）：办公室冷得像冰窖，他却不许鲍勃·克拉奇特（Bob Cratchit）添火取暖。但贪婪不只是贪钱，也包括紧抓着自己的身份和成就不放。 一位知名牧师犯下足以使他失去牧职资格的罪，起初也表达了懊悔，为什么却不能在余生中安静、谦卑地悔改，不再追求出头露面？很多时候，是因为他贪恋领袖和讲道人受人敬重的身份。他无法想象，失去牧职带来的地位与待遇，自己还能怎样生活；就像斯克鲁奇无法想象，自己怎么能多拿出一点钱帮助穷人。 也有另一种可能：至今仍未认罪的弗林以为，只要控制住后果，就能让罪显得没那么严重。我不知道，他是否曾这样说服自己：杀死妻子，就能让她免受背叛与离婚之苦。也许，他甚至荒谬地把自己看成了英雄，宁可让自己的良心背上污点，也不让妻子承受被抛弃的痛苦。 如果真是这样，那也是贪婪：他贪求掌控一切，不愿承受自己的选择所带来的后果。如果弗林任由奸淫带来的后果显露，哪怕最终婚姻破裂，他也可能在其中遇见恩典，回转悔改。浪子本不该离家，但落到与猪争食的境地，却使他回了头。相比之下，犹大没有给自己机会，去知道彼得也曾背叛主。如果他愿意承受羞耻和耻辱，而不是以自杀逃避，也许他也会听见主问：“你爱我吗？” 掌控和金钱一样，都是我们急于得到的东西；一旦觉得自己有了一点，就又想得到更多。德国哲学家哈特穆特·罗萨（Hartmut Rosa）认为，现代社会追逐金钱与追求掌控的方式十分相似。但当我们接受 世界并不尽在掌握之中 ，就会发现，那些让生活充满不安的事，也恰恰使生活有了意义。无法掌控一切固然令人害怕，却也让我们有机会被触动、被改变，并从中蒙福。 贪婪最大的谎言 贪婪最大的谎言就是让人相信，唯有牢牢抓住，才能真正拥有。因此，我们需要不断提醒自己两件事：我们无法掌控一切；而那位掌管一切的主，虽然悉心照料祂所造的世界，却更加顾念我们。 贪婪的谎言终究会被揭穿。对弗林而言，揭穿谎言的是 女儿们的话 。其中一个女儿在信中写道： 妈妈是个完美的人，真的完美极了。她究竟做错了什么，让你那么恨她？ 她爱你，关心你，照顾你。她全心全意地爱着你。 她是我最好的朋友。可你却选择杀死我唯一的妈妈。我真的好想她，好想、好想、好想她。你根本不知道我有多想她。 女儿看得明白：父亲不是太渴望幸福，而是他所追求的幸福太狭小了。贪婪不只扭曲了他的心，毒害了他的行为，也蒙蔽了他的眼睛。 但女儿仍不肯放弃他。她在信的结尾写道：“记住，你还有机会。你总还有选择。我希望你能重新让耶稣住进你的心里。” 如今，凯勒布·弗林已失去一切掌控，余生都将在监狱中度过。然而，只要他还不肯悔改、认罪、领受神的恩典，就仍是贪婪的囚徒。 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： Caleb Flynn and the Deadly Sin of Greed .

articles.title: Best Practices from Evangelistically Effective Churches
articles.summary: While thousands of Americans are dechurching, some churches are baptizing many new members. Here’s how the country’s most evangelistically effective churches are sharing the gospel.
articles.summary_zh: 虽然成千上万的美国人正在脱离教会，但一些教会正在为许多新成员施洗。以下是这个国家最有效传福音的教会分享福音的方式。
articles.title_zh: 传福音有效教会的最佳实践
articles.content: https://media.thegospelcoalition.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/23102213/effective-evangelism.mp3 In the summer of 2021, pastor Luke Peterson moved to Columbus, Ohio, to look for lost people. To find them, he joined a gym. He started building friendships. And then he began asking those friends if they wanted to come over. “Word started getting around—‘You’re not going to believe this, but Luke’s a pastor,’” he said. ‘It created some intrigue, and people started coming. I used to have a note in my phone of how many people came to our church because I went to CrossFit Grandview. It was up to like 60 or 70 before I stopped counting because it was impossible.” Peterson’s good at evangelism, and his church is too—last year, they welcomed around 500 first-time visitors. When he preaches, he knows about half his audience is probably unchurched. Pastor Luke Peterson (right) chats with Capital Church attendees / Courtesy of Capital Church Facebook This is unusual in a country where 40 million adults have stopped attending church over the last 30 years, and where 76 percent of pastors said “fostering connections with unchurched people” is a need in their church. Much has changed since the Billy Graham rallies of the ’60s, the door-knocking of the ’80s, and seeker-sensitive church billboards of the ’90s. In the past, “you could randomly walk up to the person pumping gas next to you and say, ‘Do you know Jesus?’” said Perimeter Church pastor Jeff Norris. “Could that still work? Sure. But more and more, we tell people to invite neighbors into their home. The reality is that evangelism is much slower, and more relational, than it used to be.” Today, people aren’t as likely to read the Bible, think it’s the Word of God, or go to church . But they’re also less hostile to Christianity than they were five years ago. And while they read the Bible less—especially in Gen Z—the trajectory is moving up . “We’re not past ‘my truth, your truth,’” said Rob Warren, pastor of Doxa Church in Madison, Wisconsin. “But people aren’t as sure that their truth is actually true.” These days, evangelistically effective churches are keeping evangelism front of mind in the way they preach, train, and encourage their congregations. They’re celebrating small wins. And they’re leading with a high view of Scripture, prayer, and God’s sovereignty. “We’ve seen all of our ministries grow—from kids to youth to college ministry to Doxa Church as a whole,” Warren said. “It’s not just one demographic of people who are getting saved. God’s doing something.” Times Have Changed Thirty years ago, evangelical churches leaned on programs like Evangelism Explosion or Continuous Witness Training to deliver evangelistic focus and training, church leader Thom Rainer said . Those structured initiatives fit well in a culture that was more Christian and more institutionalized—it took an average of 20 church members to reach one person for Christ per year. Today, it takes 50, Rainer said . “Evangelism efficacy, evangelism effectiveness, has definitely diminished.” That trend is likely to continue. As social media and AI fill our time and increase our social anxiety, even relational evangelism is growing more difficult. As social media and AI fill our time and increase our social anxiety, even relational evangelism is growing more difficult. “I’ve got a new couple that moved into my neighborhood a while ago, and I haven’t even seen them yet,” said Daniel Simmons, executive pastor of campuses and central discipleship at The Summit Church. This means equipping the congregation is more challenging—and important—than ever before. “Evangelism can be this thing that is so burdensome and guilt-driven,” said pastor Christian Gracia. He planted King’s City Church in Las Vegas in 2024 with around 80 people and has seen the church grow to more than 400. “People can feel like they’re not ready or not good enough at evangelism,” Gracia said. “They don’t always know what to say, and can feel like a terri

articles.title: We Need to Know Our Reformed Roots
articles.summary: This volume is an invitation to rediscover that heritage and to find fresh encouragement in the faithfulness of God, who has sustained his church through the centuries.
articles.summary_zh: 这本书邀请我们重新发现这一遗产，并在神的信实中找到新的鼓励，神几个世纪以来一直支持他的教会。
articles.title_zh: 我们需要了解我们的改革根源
articles.content: What does it mean to be Reformed? The label is used frequently but not always carefully. For some, it simply refers to a particular view of salvation. For others, it evokes a tradition, a culture, or even an aesthetic. Yet historically, to be Reformed has meant something much richer. While no single sentence can capture the fullness of the Reformed tradition, at minimum it means three things: to be biblical, to be covenantal, and to be confessional. The authority of Scripture governs our theology, covenant theology provides Scripture’s redemptive framework, and the historic confessions summarize and safeguard the church’s doctrinal convictions. Remove any one of those pillars, and something essential to the Reformed tradition is lost. With “Reformed” in its name, it’s hardly surprising that Reformed Theological Seminary has long sought to equip pastors and church members in all three areas. In recent years, members of its faculty have produced substantial volumes on the Old and New Testaments and on covenant theology. Now, with The Westminster Confession of Faith: A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application , they turn their attention to the confessional foundation of the Reformed tradition. The result is a volume that seeks not only to explain what the confession teaches but also to demonstrate why confessional theology remains vital for the church today. What Is the Westminster Confession of Faith? The Westminster Confession of Faith takes its name from the Westminster Assembly, a gathering of more than 100 ministers and theologians convened by the English Parliament in 1643 at a time of profound political and ecclesiastical upheaval. The assembly was tasked with recommending reforms to the doctrine, worship, government, and discipline of the Church of England. After more than five years of careful biblical study and theological deliberation, the assembly produced the Westminster Confession of Faith along with the Larger and Shorter Catechisms. Together, these documents have served as the doctrinal foundation of Presbyterian churches throughout the world for nearly four centuries. The assembly’s influence, however, extends far beyond Presbyterianism. The confession has helped shape the broader Reformed tradition, providing the framework for later confessional statements. As a result, its theological influence shaped generations of Congregationalists, Baptists, and other evangelical Christians. The editors of this volume rightly observe, The confession is also ecumenical because it found wide acceptance among Congregationalists and Particular Baptists in the seventeenth century, as two different groups of theologians adapted the confession according to their theological convictions, producing the Savoy Declaration (1658) and the Second London Confession (1689). Thus the Westminster Confession is relevant to Presbyterians, Congregationalists, and Baptists. (xx) Why Another Commentary? The Westminster Confession has never lacked commentators. From the 17th century onward, pastors and theologians have written to explain its theology. Quality works by A. A. Hodge , G. I. Williamson, R. C. Sproul, and more recently Chad Van Dixhoorn have each served the church well in different ways. So why do we need another commentary on the confession, and what makes this one useful? The Westminster Confession has helped shape the broader Reformed tradition, providing the framework for later confessional statements. First, this isn’t the work of a single author but a collaborative effort by scholars whose expertise spans several areas of theology. That breadth allows the volume to approach the confession from different perspectives while maintaining a clear unity of purpose. Each contributor brings particular expertise to the section he addresses, but the volume as a whole is concerned with helping readers understand the confession and its significance for the church. Second, the commentary is consciously pastoral. Rath
articles.content_zh: 改革意味着什么? 标签经常使用,但并不总是谨慎。 对某些人来说,它只是提到救赎的特定观点. 对其他人来说,它引起一种传统、一种文化,甚至一种美学。 然而,从历史上看,改革意味着更加富有的东西。 虽然没有一句话能捕捉到被改造后的传统的全部,但至少它意味着三件事:是圣经,是盟约,是忏悔. 圣经的权威支配着我们的神学,盟约神学提供了圣经的红发框架,历史的忏悔总结并捍卫了教会的教义信念。 移除其中任何一根支柱,失去对改革后的传统至关重要的东西。 改革神学院长期试图在所有三个领域为牧师和教会成员提供教具, 近年来,该校院士编写了大量关于"旧约"和"新约"和"盟约神学"等著作. 现在,随着《威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔:对其历史、神学和适用的综合评论》,他们把注意力转向改革后传统的忏悔基础。 结果的一卷不仅试图解释忏悔的教义,还试图表明为什么忏悔神学在今天仍然对教会至关重要. 韦斯敏斯特对信仰的忏悔是什么? 威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔会取而代之的是威斯敏斯特大会(Westminster Assembly),这是1643年英国议会在政治与教会剧变深刻的时期召开的由100多位部长和神学家组成的集会. 大会的任务是建议对英格兰教会的学说,崇拜,政府和纪律进行改革. 经过五年多的认真的圣经研究和神学审议后,大会产生了"威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔"(Westminster Confession of Faith)和"更大规模和更短的卡特克主义". 近四个世纪以来,这些文件共同成为全世界长老会教会的理论基础。 然而,议会的影响远远超出长老会。 忏悔有助于形成更广泛的改革后传统,为后来的忏悔声明提供了框架。 因此,它的神学影响塑造了几代基督教会,浸信会等福音派基督徒. 这本书的编辑们正确地指出,《忏悔书》也具有普世性,因为它在17世纪被基督教会和特定浸信会广泛接受,因为两个不同的神学家群体根据他们的神学信念修改了供词,产生了"萨伏依宣言"(1658年)和"第二次伦敦忏悔书"(1689年). 因此,威斯敏斯特忏悔与长老会、基督教会和浸信会有关。 (二十) 为什么另作一评注? 威斯敏斯特的"忏悔"从未缺少评论家. 从17世纪起,牧师和神学家都撰文解释其神学. A. A. Hodge、G. I. Williamson、R. C. Sproul和最近的Chad Van Dixhoorn以不同方式为教堂服务。 因此,我们为什么需要关于供词的另一条评论,是什么使得这一条有用呢? 威斯敏斯特忏悔有助于形成更广泛的改革后传统,为后来的忏悔声明提供了框架. 首先,这不是一位作者的工作,而是学者的合作努力,他们的专业知识跨越了神学的几个领域。 这种宽度允许量从不同的角度对待供词,同时保持明确的目的一致。 每个贡献者都会为他所讲的一节带来特殊的专门知识,但该卷整体关注的是帮助读者理解忏悔及其对教会的意义. 第二,评注是自觉的放肆。 拉斯语Name
