articles.title: If the Church Did Its Job, Would the Parachurch Exist?
articles.summary: Do pregnancy centers, food pantries, or campus ministries exist because the church is failing to do her work?
articles.summary_zh: 是否存在怀孕中心、食品储藏室或校园事工，因为教会未能完成她的工作？
articles.title_zh: 如果教会做了它的工作，教堂会存在吗？
articles.content: I’ve heard it said more than once: “If the church did its job, the parachurch wouldn’t have to exist.” For instance, I was consulting with a local pastor who wanted to see the church serve people in poverty in his community. It was important to him that the church do it, not a nonprofit. Since he understood that God’s kingdom is bigger than his congregation, he wanted to engage multiple churches in the project. I suggested he consider forming a council of pastors and collectively hiring a staff member to manage the operations of the combined program. He thought that could work well for his context. I’m not sure he was aware of the irony. I certainly was: We’d just reinvented a variant of the 501(c)(3) nonprofit that he so keenly wanted to avoid in the first place. While the allergy to faith-based nonprofits was especially strong in his case, many people accept the premise at a basic level. In my experience, this sentiment is just as likely to come from someone who works in nonchurch ministry as from a pastor. If we understand the church is the core institution created by Christ to advance the kingdom of heaven, has it failed so badly that we need an army of auxiliaries to prop it up? Clarifying Terms and Roles I answer that the parachurch doesn’t exist because the church has failed. It exists because God’s commands naturally generate institutions beyond family, church, and state. Proving that starts with clarifying terms. The parachurch exists because God’s commands naturally generate institutions beyond family, church, and state. “Church” has more than one use in Scripture. In some contexts, it describes the people of God universally (Matt. 16:15–18; Eph. 1:22–23; Col. 1:18). In others, it’s a local congregational institution with the parameters God has placed around its operation (1 Thess. 1:1; 1 Tim. 3:1–5; Philem. 1:2; James 5:14). “Parachurch” typically refers to faith-based nonprofits who serve people in need or provide evangelistic and discipleship resources. Certainly, as part of the universal church, all God’s people hold equal status in advancing God’s mission, whether they labor as nurses, students, pastors, or tentmakers (see Acts 18:1–3). Just as surely, all God’s people shouldn’t merely attend but be accountable to a local congregation that enables their spiritual formation. When not assembled, God’s people are charged with many tasks—everything from stewarding creation to seeking justice for the oppressed. We can fulfill these tasks as individuals, but it often makes sense to create or join institutions dedicated to fulfilling them. Which brings us to a crucial point: God ordained some institutions specifically, and some emerged organically from God’s commands. Ordained or Emergent Institutions The family, the local church, and the government are ordained institutions. The Bible gives each ordained institution some guidance but also leaves a lot open to interpretation. While these ordained institutions are necessary for all people, they aren’t sufficient to fulfill God’s myriad commands to their fullest extent. Thus, some institutions emerge from the commands, rather than from a revealed institutional structure: The command to work led to the formation of businesses. The command to pass knowledge to subsequent generations led to the formation of schools. The command to care for the sick caused Christians to form the first hospitals. The command to care for the poor, widows, orphans, and strangers led to the formation of charities . The command to make disciples of all nations led to mission boards, publishing houses, and Bible-translation ministries. This ordained-emergent distinction parallels Abraham Kuyper’s “ sphere sovereignty ” in its recognition of institutions not explicitly outlined in Scripture. Many of these commands can be fulfilled to some lesser degree by the ordained institutions, but there are limitations. A family may work without forming a business, but they’ll never raise a skyscraper. Most be

articles.title: Ministry Lessons from the Puritans (with Joel Beeke)
articles.summary: Joel Beeke joins Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan to explore what the Puritans can teach today’s pastors about prayer, preaching, personal holiness, shepherding souls, handling criticism, and persevering in ministry.
articles.summary_zh: 乔尔·比克（ Joel Beeke ）与马特·斯梅瑟斯特（ Matt Smethurst ）和利贡·邓肯（ Ligon Duncan ）一起探索清教徒可以教导今天的牧师关于祈祷、讲道、个人圣洁、牧养灵魂、处理批评和坚持传道。
articles.title_zh: 清教徒的教训（与Joel Beeke一起）
articles.content: What can pastors today learn from the Puritans? Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan welcome Joel Beeke to discuss the lasting wisdom of Puritan pastors and theologians. Drawing from decades of studying and teaching the Puritans, Beeke explains why they placed such a high priority on prayer, personal holiness, and applying Scripture to the hearts and lives of their congregations. articles.summary_zh: 由于黎巴嫩目前受到战争、难民危机等的影响，美丽的故事可能很难被理解。对于在黎巴嫩活跃的事工，满足精神，物质...
articles.title_zh: 黎巴嫩的艺术项目将美丽带入危机
articles.content: With Lebanon currently being impacted by war, a refugee crisis, and more, stories of beauty can be hard to come across. For ministries active in Lebanon, meeting the spiritual, physical and emotional needs of a country just trying to survive can take its toll. Horizons International’s Pierre Houssney said that despite the trauma the country faces due to the fallenness of man in a sinful world, God has still created a world that contains beauty. “And I think that beauty speaks to people’s hearts about God, especially when it’s not just beauty, you know, for beauty’s sake, but when it’s beauty in the name of Christ,” Houssney said. “In the midst of the trauma, in the midst of the poverty, we’re trying to give opportunities for believers, who have artistic gifts, to have a prophetic voice through their art to the society, so that we can be calling out for Christ in the midst of the crisis.” Some of these opportunities for creating beauty are fine art classes offered by Horizons International. Horizons International has had up to 35 students at one time participating in these classes revolving around painting or drawing. Students in visual arts classes had the opportunity to participate in an exhibition in Beirut called “His Touch.” People from the community were invited to see the work of beginner students as well as 10 different Christian artists. Graphic design classes offer a more practical element, allowing students to learn a skill they could use in their everyday lives. On the worship side of things, music theory and classes in instruments are helping raise up worship leaders for local churches. One unit teaching guitar, piano, and drums to beginners looking to lead worship at their church had 70 people participate. “And so this new generation needs training, and they need, you know, they need mentoring, and they need to have those skills so that they can, they can lead their congregations in worship,” Houssney said. Though some may have more trouble connecting visual arts directly with ministry, Houssney says social media helps make that connection more clear. Beautiful videos that contain scripture messages alongside visual art tend to get a higher viewership. When posts like that get more views, they can potentially bring more people to Christ. “And so it needs to be beautiful. It needs to be excellent, it needs to be well done. And that’s what our Lord deserves,” Houssney said. “That’s not just what social media deserves.” Currently, Horizons International has to spread resources between humanitarian aid like food and medicine and projects that glorify God through the arts. In the midst of the crisis in Lebanon, pray for God to provide the resources for canvases, studio spaces, art instructors and more. Houssney also says what an organization like Horizons International is here for is to see God open more and more hearts to the Gospel. “So I’m not praying that the church would have less hardship. I’m not praying for you know, for less, you know, political chaos. What I’m praying for is that, through it all, people would continue to open their hearts, and that God will be glorified.” Learn more about the work of Horizons International in Lebanon by visiting https://www.horizonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis .
articles.content_zh: 黎巴嫩目前受到战争、难民危机等影响, 对活跃在黎巴嫩的各部来说,满足一个国家的精神、身体和情感需求,只是为了生存而努力,这可能会造成损失。 Horizons International的Pierre Houssney说,尽管由于人类在罪恶世界中的堕落,国家仍然面临创伤,但上帝仍然创造了一个包含美丽的世界。 “我认为,美丽对人们的心来说是关于上帝的,特别是当它不仅仅是为美丽着想,而是以基督为名的美丽时,”Houssney说。 “在创伤中,在贫困中,我们试图给那些拥有艺术天赋的信徒机会,通过他们的艺术向社会发出先知的声音,以便在危机中呼唤基督。” 其中一些创造美貌的机会是地平线国际提供的精美艺术课. 地平线国际曾经有多达35名学生参加这些围绕绘画或绘画而旋转的课. 视觉艺术课的学生有机会在贝鲁特参加一个名为“他的触摸”的展览。 社区人士被邀请观看初学者和10名不同的基督教艺术家的作品. 图形设计课程提供了更实用的元素,让学生学习在日常生活中可以使用的技能. 在事物的崇拜方面,乐器中的音乐理论和课程正在帮助培养地方教会的崇拜领袖. 一个教吉他,钢琴,和鼓的单位在他们的教堂里为初学者寻找引领崇拜,有70人参加. “因此,这新一代需要培训,他们需要,你知道,他们需要指导,他们需要这些技能,以便他们能够领导他们的教会进行礼拜。” 虽然有些人可能更难直接将视觉艺术与部委联系起来, 包含经文信息与视觉艺术的美丽视频往往获得更高的收视率. 当这样的帖子获得更多的观点时,它们有可能将更多的人带入基督. “因此,它必须是美丽的。 它需要出色,需要做得很好。 这才是我们的主应得的。 这不仅仅是社交媒体应得的。 目前,地平线国际必须在食品和医药等人道主义援助和通过艺术来赞美上帝的项目之间分配资源。 在黎巴嫩危机中,祈求上帝为画布、工作室空间、艺术教员等提供资源。 霍斯尼还说,像地平线国际这样的组织在这里是为了看到上帝对"福音"越来越开放的心. 我并不祈祷教会会减少困难。 我并不是为你们祈祷, 我所祈祷的是,通过这一切,人们将继续敞开心扉,而上帝将受到赞美。” 透过访问https://www.horisonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis,

articles.summary_zh: 这件事发生在15年前，但我记得很清楚。在日常生活的嗡嗡声中，很容易陷入粗心大意……
articles.title_zh: v.容忍
articles.content: This incident took place over 15 years ago, and yet, I remember it clearly.  In the buzz of daily life, it is easy to get caught up in the carelessness of the checklists, and forget the intentionality of abiding in Him. I remember how frantic I was once at or late deadline and how frustrated I was at all the problems we were having in getting the program together.  We’d all kinds of equipment failure throughout the day and I was going to have to drive the program across town to get it uploaded to the satellite.  It was already 7 pm and the babysitter was calling me every 10 minutes. Then, I got a call from a lady with a gentle Creole accent. She told me, “I felt led to call you and pray with you.”  I SO didn’t want to talk to this lady, wasn’t interested in being prayed over, and really just wanted to leave to get this program fed and pick my 2-year old up.  I was impatient when I responded to her.  Rather than take insult from what was probably a curt rebuff,  she just said , “Wow. You REALLY need the peace of our heavenly Father on your heart right now.” And…she burst out in song.   Now I’m wondering why I’m on the phone with this crazy lady, and then she prayed through the worship song and then rolled right into praying for me, for my distress, for the things I thought I needed to do…and prayed that I would be still and listen, that my heart would be quiet long enough to remember the awe of God, and that the joy would come back to my heart as we produced MNN… The more she prayed, the more convicted I grew and I realized I was caught up in the ‘do’ and not the ‘be’…and THEN she pulled out the big guns: the story of Mary and Martha. Luke 10:38-42 New International Version (NIV) At the Home of Martha and Mary 38 As Jesus and his disciples were on their way, he came to a village where a woman named Martha opened her home to him. 39 She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to what he said. 40 But Martha was distracted by all the preparations that had to be made. She came to him and asked, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister has left me to do the work by myself? Tell her to help me!” 41 “Martha, Martha,” the Lord answered, “you are worried and upset about many things, 42 but few things are needed—or indeed only one. [ a ] Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her.” She ended our conversation with, “Sometimes, it’s ok to be Mary and sit at the feet of Jesus.  Stuff will still be there to do. It will eventually get done.  But the lasting investment is remembering to sit and BE at the feet of Jesus.” It was a much needed gentle rebuke along with a little encouragement from an unknown sister in Christ that I still remember to this day…thousands of productions later.   What we do is important…but not at the risk of forgetting to abide in Christ.
articles.content_zh: 这一事件发生在15多年前,然而,我清楚地记得。 在日常生活中,很容易陷入清单的粗心大意之中,而忘记遵守他的意向。 我记得我曾经在最后期限或晚到的时候 多么疯狂 以及我对我们把节目整理好时遇到的所有问题 感到多么沮丧 我将不得不把程序推向全城, 已经七点了 保姆每十分钟给我打电话 然后,我接到一个女士的电话 带着温柔的克里奥尔口音。 她对我说:我的确猜想,我曾与你一起祈祷。 我本不想和这位女士交谈, 我对她的反应很不耐烦 她没有从可能是一种曲折的反驳中取出侮辱,而是说,“哇。 你现在真的需要我们天父的和平。” 然后... 她唱出歌来 她透过崇拜之歌祈祷, 然后转而为我祈祷, 为我的痛苦祈祷, 祈祷我需要做的事情. 她越是祈祷, 我越是被定罪, Luke 10:38-42 新国际版 (NIV) 在玛莎和玛丽38的家,由于耶稣和他的门徒们在路上,他来到一个村庄,一个叫玛莎的女人向他打开了她的家. 39 她有一个叫玛丽的姐姐,她坐在主的脚下,听他说的话。 40,但玛莎被所有必须做的准备所分心. 她来到他身边问道,“主啊,你难道不关心我姐姐离开我一个人做这个工作吗? " 41 " Martha, Martha, " 主回答说, " 你对许多事情感到担心和不安,42件,但需要的东西很少,甚至只有一件。 [a] 玛利亚已选择了更好的事物,它不会被夺走。 她结束我们的谈话时, 事情还会在那里做。 它最终会完成。 但持久的投资是记得坐在耶稣的脚下。” 这是非常需要的温柔的回斥 以及基督中一个未知的妹妹的一点鼓励 我至今仍然记得... 我们所做的是重要的... 但不会冒着忘记遵守基督的风险

articles.title_zh: Koinonia
articles.content: Koinonia (Koy-no-nee’-ah) is a Greek word, occurring 20 times in the Bible, which means “fellowship” or “brotherly love.” It carries with it the meaning of a committed, trustworthy, and dependable relationship. Such a relationship can be experienced through participation, sharing, giving, and contributing. The first occurrence of koinonia is Acts 2:42 “They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.” But the rest of the passage reads:  “ 43 Everyone was filled with awe at the many wonders and signs performed by the apostles. 44 All the believers were together and had everything in common. 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. 46 Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, 47 praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.” Christian fellowship is a key aspect of the Christian life. Believers in Christ are to come together in love, faith, and encouragement. The essence of koinonia: “one another”. Scripture commands us to be devoted to one another (Romans 12:10), honor one another (Romans 12:10), live in harmony with one another (Romans 12:16; 1 Peter 3:8), accept one another (Romans 15:7), serve one another in love (Galatians 5:13), be kind and compassionate to one another (Ephesians 4:32), admonish one another (Colossians 3:16), encourage one another (1 Thessalonians 5:11; Hebrews 3:13), spur one another on toward love and good deeds (Hebrews 10:24), offer hospitality (1 Peter 4:9), and love one another (1 Peter 1:22; 1 John 3:11; 3:23; 4:7; 4:11-12). Koinonia is translated many different ways in English Bibles: -fellowship (koinonia), to the breaking of bread and the prayers.” -contribution (koinonia) for them and for all others.” Paul writes to the believers in Philippi: “That I may know him and the power of his resurrection, and may share (koinonia) his sufferings, becoming like him in his death” (Phil 3:10). – Christian living– the dynamic whole of it. It describes an interactive relationship between God and believers who are sharing new life through Christ.  It captures the entirety of this relationship. It involves active participation in Christian community: sharing in spiritual blessings and giving material blessings. How does this idea fit into the theology of ‘And’? Acts 1:8—it empowers us with the chisomo—the grace to DO—the all-inclusive– “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.” And they will know you by your love.  (John 13:35)   “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”

articles.title_zh: 契  约
articles.content: Isaiah 54:10  Though the mountains be shaken and the hills be removed, yet my unfailing love for you will not be shaken nor my covenant of peace be removed,” says the LORD, who has compassion on you. There is something of music in the very sound of these words. The thought that lies below them, sweeping as it does through the whole creation, and parting all things into the transient and eternal, the mortal and immortal, is still greater than the music of the words. ‘These’ are removed; ‘this’ abides. The thing in God which abides is all-gentle tenderness, that strange love mightier than all the powers of Deity beside, permanent with the permanence of His changeless heart. ‘My loving kindness and the covenant of My peace,’ outlast everything else. The antithesis of what passes and what abides is mind-boggling. ‘all things are in a state of flux’—it’s a basic tenant of physical science…and yet it seems as unchanging as anything we know…it’s the shape of the box…and yet,  if we had nothing abiding beyond this universe, what would be the point? There’s an unspoken  ‘But’  here–  in that vacuum, the Great Spirit moves all the material universe, Himself unmoved, undiminished by creation, or by said vacuum.  The Unknowable whose name means ‘breath’ is YHWH—who comes to us in man-form to help the created move toward and abide in this presence. I’m sort of blown away by how big this passage paints God…and blown away that we are His children…and that we able to abide because of Christ…that our part in glorifying Him and enjoying Him forever comes in walking alongside a global family and telling their stories.  Insignificant, by itself, but being used as a tool to help others abide and recognize the mercy and grace of this big Abba. We can touch the face of God…because He calls us to Himself.

articles.content: The Scriptures Ephesians 6:10-18 (NIV) 10 Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. 11 Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. 12 For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. 13 Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand. 14 Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, 15 and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. 16 In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. 17 Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit,which is the word of God. 18 And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people. Matthew 10:16-20 16 “I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves. 17 Be on your guard; you will be handed over to the local councils and be flogged in the synagogues. 18 On my account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.19 But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given what to say, 20 for it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.” Today, it’s just been on my mind to bring our attention back to the armor of God and the fact we need to be wise like serpents, innocent as doves. I want to speak to the first part, being wise like serpents. Going to Malta helped bring to my attention how much I don’t know about my own country’s politics, the refugee crisis, trusting God, and even God’s word. I feel like I’m doing “better than the average U.S. citizen.” But, in reality, I don’t know very much. And I’ve realized when it comes to engaging in conversation with others, it’s important to have a handle on topics like these. I.e., talking with my dad about refugees. Having facts and knowing the what the constitution says helps me to better articulate and defend my stance culturally and based by our country’s laws. Knowing about the situation with refugees abroad also helps and is a tool in dispelling the fear which the current administration seems to use to get support to make the calls it’s trying to make both about refugees and immigrants in general. The second part, being innocent like doves…that’s a hard one for me because I’ve thought in the past it means to be naive. I don’t want to be naïve. But being innocent doesn’t mean you’re naïve. I think it means we guard our hearts and take our thoughts captive. What we put into our minds affects the lens through which we see the world and view the Bible—and it has the power to jade us. I.e., rape. I know rape is in the world. I know it is destructive. I’ve seen it damage lives. And I’ve seen God redeem. But, what I don’t need to do is read the part of a book or watch a TV series which details a situation of rape. I don’t need to invite that in my mind to “know” about rape. I’m thinking of a book one of my youth group girls was reading. I haven’t read it, but I see how she struggles with her sexuality, her relationship with God, and for a period even suicide. I also see how her parents are okay with exposing her to things that are a bit mature for her age. Compared to another one of our girls who is aware of what happens in the world, but her parents are careful to protect her from exposure to things which are dark, damaging, fracture her relationship with God. She’s being taught to be innocent, not naïve (or judgmental), and to take her thoughts captive. Both of these
articles.content_zh: 圣经以弗所书: 6: 10-18(NIV) 10 最后,要坚固于主和他强大的力量. 11 穿上上帝的全盔甲,以便你能够采取立场对抗魔鬼的阴谋. 12,因为我们的斗争不是反对血肉之争,而是反对统治者,反对当局,反对这个黑暗世界的力量,反对天界邪恶的精神力量. 13 因此穿上神的全甲,使出恶事之日到来后能站起地来,在做了一切后能站起地来. 14 站稳了, 真理带系住你的腰部, 胸罩是正义的, 15 和你的脚 与来自和平的福音的准备。 16,除此外,取起信道之盾,用之能灭一切恶道所发之火箭. 17取出救生之盔和"灵剑",这是"神之道". 18,并随各种祷告和请求,在"精神"中作各种祈祷. 考虑到这一点,保持警惕,并始终为主的所有人民祈祷。 Matthew 10:16-20 16 “我把你像羊一样放出狼群。 因此要像蛇一样精明,像鸽子一样无辜. 17 个 人 守 住 ; 交给 地方 议会 、 在 犹太会堂 被 鞭打 . 18,就我而言,你们将被带见总督和国王,作为他们和外邦人的见证。 19,但当他们逮捕你时,不要担心该说什么或怎么说. 在那日,你们得享受你们所应当享受的,20个是你们所应当享受的,只有你们父亲的精神。 今天,我刚刚想到让我们重新关注上帝的盔甲, 以及我们需要像蛇一样聪明, 我想谈谈第一部分,像蛇一样聪明。 前往马耳他让我注意到我对本国政治、难民危机、信任上帝甚至上帝之言一无所知。 我觉得自己比普通美国公民做得更好。 但事实上, 我意识到在与他人对话时, 和我爸谈难民的事 了解事实、了解宪法内容, 有助于我更好地表达和捍卫我的立场, 了解国外难民的情况,也有助于消除现政府似乎用来获得支持的恐惧, 第二部分是像鸽子一样无辜, 我不想天真。 但无辜并不意味着你天真。 我认为这意味着我们保护我们的心 并抓住我们的思想。 我们脑中的东西影响着我们通过这个镜头看到世界并看到圣经——它有制玉的力量。 强奸 我知道强奸在世界上。 我知道这是破坏性的。 我见过它会伤害生命。 我见过上帝赎回。 但我不需要阅读一本书或看一部电视连续剧, 我并不需要邀请她「知道」强奸事件。 我想到一本我的青年团体女孩正在阅读的书。 我还没读过, 但我看到她如何与性、与上帝的关系相抗争, 我也明白她的父母 让她面对一些对她的年龄来说有点成熟的事情是怎样的 和另外一位我们的女孩相比,她知道世界发生的事情,但她的父母很小心地保护她免受那些黑暗,有破坏力,断裂她与上帝关系的东西的暴露. 她被教导自己是无辜的, 两者

articles.title_zh: 亚伯拉罕和洛特
articles.content: Genesis 13 So Abram left Egypt and traveled north into the Negev, along with his wife and Lot and all that they owned. 2 (Abram was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold.) 3 From the Negev, they continued traveling by stages toward Bethel, and they pitched their tents between Bethel and Ai, where they had camped before. 4 This was the same place where Abram had built the altar, and there he worshiped the Lord again. 5 Lot, who was traveling with Abram, had also become very wealthy with flocks of sheep and goats, herds of cattle, and many tents. 6 But the land could not support both Abram and Lot with all their flocks and herds living so close together. 7 So disputes broke out between the herdsmen of Abram and Lot. (At that time Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land.) 8 Finally Abram said to Lot, “Let’s not allow this conflict to come between us or our herdsmen. After all, we are close relatives! 9 The whole countryside is open to you. Take your choice of any section of the land you want, and we will separate. If you want the land to the left, then I’ll take the land on the right. If you prefer the land on the right, then I’ll go to the left.” 10 Lot took a long look at the fertile plains of the Jordan Valley in the direction of Zoar. The whole area was well watered everywhere, like the garden of the Lord or the beautiful land of Egypt. (This was before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.) 11 Lot chose for himself the whole Jordan Valley to the east of them. He went there with his flocks and servants and parted company with his uncle Abram. 12 So Abram settled in the land of Canaan, and Lot moved his tents to a place near Sodom and settled among the cities of the plain. 13 But the people of this area were extremely wicked and constantly sinned against the Lord. 14 After Lot had gone, the Lord said to Abram, “Look as far as you can see in every direction—north and south, east and west. 15 I am giving all this land, as far as you can see, to you and your descendants[a] as a permanent possession. 16 And I will give you so many descendants that, like the dust of the earth, they cannot be counted! 17 Go and walk through the land in every direction, for I am giving it to you.” 18 So Abram moved his camp to Hebron and settled near the oak grove belonging to Mamre. There he built another altar to the Lord. At this point in the story, God’s promise to Abraham of the promised land hasn’t come true yet, but good land is part of the promise We’ve seen Abraham have faithful triumphs and failures, but this is a time when Abraham showed great faith once again because there are SEVERAL reasons why Abraham could have taken the better land 1. movement towards God’s promise of good land anyway 2. and this is probably a more striking one to me, but culturally speaking, the older would NEVER defer to the younger. Lot, as the younger, should have deferred to Abraham the older – both in going to him to resolve the disagreement between their herdsmen and in giving him the better pick of land But Abraham wasn’t fixated on culture and on manipulating God’s promises Abraham’s dealings are not in seniority, but in brotherly love and that’s what faith does. Faith resolves tension with generous self-sacrifice Christians often say in tense situations, “Well, I’m not a doormat! I deserve not to be walked all over!” But my pastor said something very striking to me. “Aren’t we glad Christ never said that?” A faithful and generous person doesn’t need to manipulate or control the situation because they are resting in the promises and sovereignty of God Faith leads to trust leads to generosity and self-sacrifice with others.
articles.content_zh: 创世记13 索·阿布拉姆从埃及出走,向北走入了内盖夫河,与他的妻子和洛特以及他们所拥有的一切. 2 (Abram有非常丰富的牲畜,白银和黄金. 3 他们从内盖夫出发,继续分步向贝瑟尔出行,在贝瑟尔和艾之间搭起帐篷,他们以前在那里扎营. 页:1 这是阿布拉姆建造祭坛的地方,在那里他再次崇拜了主. 5,当时正与阿布拉姆一起出行的洛特也变得非常富有了有羊羊群,牛群和许多帐篷. 6个 但土地无法支撑阿布拉姆和洛特 他们所有的羊群和群 生活如此相近。 第7条 亞伯蘭和魯特的牧民,互相爭論; (當時,迦南人和比瑞斯人同住), 8 最后,Abram对Lot说: " 让我们不要让这场冲突发生在我们和牧民之间。 我们毕竟是近亲! 第9条 整个农村都对你开放. 你选择你想要的土地的任何部分 我们就会分开 如果你想让土地在左边,那我就让土地在右边。 如果你喜欢右边的土地,那么我就往左边去。 10 洛特对约旦河谷向左尔方向的肥沃平原进行了长时间的考察. 整个地区到处都有良好的取水,如主的花园或埃及美丽的地. (这是在主毁灭了索多玛和戈莫拉之前) 11 洛特自己选择了他们以东的整个约旦河谷. 他带着他的羊群和仆人去那儿,和他叔叔Abram分道扬镳。 12日,阿布拉姆在迦南地定居,洛特将帐篷搬到了索多姆附近的一个地方,并定居于平地的城市中. 13,但此地之人,极恶而常犯主. 14 在洛特离开后,主对Abram说: " 请你看看每一个方向,即北和南、东和西。 15,我把所有的土地,就你所看到的,作为永久财产,交给你和你的子孙。 十六,我给你这么多的后人,像地上的尘土一样,他们不能被统计! 17 出行,走遍地上,各行各业,我把它赏赐你们。” 18日,阿布拉姆将营地迁至希伯伦并定居在属于马姆雷的橡树林附近. 在那里他又为主建造了一座祭坛. 在故事的这一刻,上帝对亚伯拉罕的允诺还没有实现,但好地是我们所见到的亚伯拉罕有忠实的胜利和失败的诺言的一部分,但此时亚伯拉罕再次表现出了极大的信心,因为有SEVERAL的理由,亚伯拉罕可以夺取更好的地一. 但从文化上讲, 年长者决不会屈从于年轻人。 作为年轻人,洛特应该把年长者留给亚伯拉罕 — — 既去他解决牧民之间的分歧,又让他选择更好的土地 — — 但亚伯拉罕并不热衷于文化和操纵上帝对亚伯拉罕的诺言 — — 亚伯拉罕的交往不是在资历上,而是在兄弟般的爱心上,而这正是信仰的作用。 信仰用慷慨自救的基督徒解决了紧张局势, 我不应该到处走! 但我的牧师对我说了一些非常引人注目的话。 “难道我们不庆幸基督从未这么说吗?” 一个忠诚而慷慨的人不需要操控或控制局势,因为他们沉浸在上帝信仰的承诺中,而主权导致信任导致与他人的慷慨和自我牺牲。

articles.title: Carried Through
articles.summary: Lillie Cunningham is 110 years old, yet she isn’t reliant on a cane or walker. She does rely on Scripture, however, which she reads every morning and night—and attends church every Sunday. When she considers her life, she states, “I just always had faith and trust in God that he was going to carry us through.”

articles.content: Good morning. May the Lord be with you and bless you today, my friends. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include lots of good books from New Growth Press and other publishers. Among them you’ll find several good options from Jared Wilson. Recommended Reading Goodbye, ‘Sam’s Club’ Megachurch. Hello, Stained Glass. Christianity Today reports on what I consider a welcome trend: church buildings that look like churches instead of warehouses. It begins this way: “Trinity Presbyterian finally has a church building of its own. That building has arches. And carved hammerbeams that tell the story of the Bible.” 3 Reasons Why Christians Should Lay “R.I.P.” to Rest. Nick Batzig thinks it would be best for Christians to lay R.I.P. to rest. “I’ve noticed something of a concerning trend over the past several years. It is the way in which believers speak about culture-impacting individuals at their deaths. Instead of simply expressing appreciation for their life and achievements, it has become commonplace for Christians to use the shorthand ‘R.I.P.’ (rest in peace) on social media when speaking of individuals in whose lives there was no evidence of saving grace at their death. At the risk of sounding ill-tempered, I wish to set out several reasons why I am troubled by this occurrence.” Go Deeper with Ligonier’s Grow App. Looking to put down roots in God’s Word? The Grow app from Ligonier Ministries gives you clear Bible teaching and guides your daily study for a deeper walk with Christ. Ministry Partners can also access the verse-by-verse notes from the Reformation Study Bible directly in the app and get reliable answers to their theological questions with the Ask Ligonier intelligent assistant. Not a Ligonier Ministry Partner yet? Try these features for 30 days when you download Grow and sign in. (Sponsored) Beauty Demands to Be Noticed. Michael Jensen is right: beauty demands to be noticed. He tells about people who understand the connection between beauty and transcendence and says, “Clearly, the reductive and polemical explanation of the atheists isn’t proving to be compelling. People can’t square their deeply felt experience of the world with that. To the people I’ve been speaking with, at least, the world simply cannot be reduced to its material components, nor can its coherence be explained by resorting to chance.” Aslan Sane: The Bowiefication of Narnia. I’ve got a pair of articles to share that comment on the forthcoming Narnia movies, each taking a different perspective. In the first, the writer remembers the old Narnia series from her childhood and bridges from there to what we know of the new one. She’s not impressed with it. Aslan and the Christians Who Can’t Be Enchanted. In the second, the author rebukes people like me (and the previous author) who have expressed concerns. He reminds us that it’s a movie for kids and that we don’t really know much about it yet. (I’d say he writes with some degree of exaggeration when he accuses me of losing my mind, but I’m glad to consider what he says nonetheless.) The Day of Pioneer Missions Is Not Over. Writing for Desiring God, my friend Tim Keesee wants us to know that the day of pioneer missions is not over. “Pioneer missionaries are still needed today because there are vast territories and high-rise megacities where the gospel message has yet to reach.” Videos Worth Watching Here are several brief videos that are worth your time. 5 Signs Your Church Might Be Too Seeker Sensitive. Adriel Sanchez explains seeker sensitivity and offers signs your church might lean too much in that direction and become seeker driven. How to Leave a Church Well. Hershael York speaks specifically to pastors to explain how and when to leave a church well. The Enduring Word. This short film from Crossway celebrates God’s providence through the history of Bible translation. Flashback What’s The Point Of Family Devotions? articles.content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. This week brings a substantial new commentary on the Westminster Confession of Faith from a whole team of Reformed scholars, an updated edition of a well-known apologetics book, a couple of books for kids, and a new edition of the ESV. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. (This is a new feature I trialed last week. The response was positive, so I’m going to keep it going. I have tried to improve the format and layout to make it easier to read.) Books for Everyone Crossway The Westminster Confession of Faith A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application Edited by J. V. Fesko, John R. Muether, and D. Blair Smith Endorsed by: Joel R. Beeke, Michael Horton, Keith A. Mathison, Robert Letham, and Jonathan L. Master Publisher’s description What is Reformed theology? In 1646, a group of theologians composed what is arguably the most comprehensive statement of faith, the Westminster Confession. Their efforts to preserve Protestant theology against opposing beliefs endured. Today, amid growing interest in Reformed Christianity, the Westminster Confession remains an indispensable guide for living out doctrine, worship, and church governance sola Scriptura, “by Scripture alone.” This essential collection of essays presents an accessible guide to the Westminster Confession of Faith for 21st-century readers. Each chapter is devoted to a section of the historic document, carefully studying its context, its significance to the faith, and its application, as well as any controversies. Clear, thorough explanations of principles, including the Trinity, creation, providence, baptism, last judgment, and more, make this the definitive guide on Reformed Christian doctrine. The essays are written by faculty from Reformed Theological Seminary in their areas of expertise, ensuring a trustworthy and high-quality text for church leaders, teachers and students of theology, and laypeople. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . Crossway I Don’t Have Enough Faith to Be an Atheist Updated Edition Norman L. Geisler and Frank Turek Endorsed by: Gavin Ortlund, Sean McDowell, Gregory Koukl, Alisa Childers, and Josh Howerton Publisher’s description To some, the concept of having faith in a higher power or a set of religious beliefs is nonsensical. Indeed, many view religion in general, and Christianity in particular, as unfounded and unreasonable. Frank Turek and Norman Geisler argue, however, that Christianity is not only more reasonable than all other belief systems but is indeed more rational than unbelief itself. With conviction and clear thinking, Turek and Geisler guide readers through some of the traditional, tested arguments for the existence of a creator God. They move into an examination of the source of morality and the reliability of the New Testament accounts concerning Jesus. The final section of the book deals with a detailed investigation of the claims of Christ. This updated volume with fresh arguments will be an interesting read for those skeptical about Christianity, as well as a helpful resource for Christians seeking to articulate a more sophisticated defense of their faith. Buy it at Amazon . Baker Books Giver of All Good God as the Beginning and End of Ethics Chase R. Kuhn Publisher’s description Where do our ethics come from? Are they based on unchanging realities or subject to revision as human culture develops and changes? What distinguishes Christian ethics from other moral claims? And how can Christians engage these questions with clarity and confidence—without either abandoning their convictions or abandoning the conversation? In Giver of All Good , Chase R. Kuhn argues that the answer begins not with ourselves—our feelings, our culture, our moral intuitions—but with God. What we believe about God shapes how we live. Our theology guides
articles.content_zh: 星期二是大多数出版商发行新书的一天,所以每周我都会告诉你,我最密切地关注的出版商刚刚给我们带来了什么。 本周来自整群改革派学者对"威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔"(Westminster Confession of Faith)提出了实质性的新评论,并更新了一出名作"通俗小说"(Apologetics Book),一出给孩子们的几本书和一出"ESV"的新版本. 每一次,我都包括出版商的描述。 (这是上星期我试演的新节目) 回应是积极的, 我努力改进格式和布局,使其更容易阅读。 ) 由J. V. Fesko、John R. Muether和D. Blair Smith编辑, 乔尔·R·比克、Michael Horton、Keith A. Mathison、Robert Letham和Jonathan L. Master Publishers对改革神学的描述。 1646年,一群神学家组成了可以说是最全面的信仰声明"威斯敏斯特忏悔". 他们努力保护新教神学,反对对立的信仰。 如今,在对改革后的基督教越来越感兴趣的情况下,威斯敏斯特忏悔仍然是“仅靠圣经”活出学说、崇拜和教会治理的不可或缺的指南。 这份重要的散文集为21世纪的读者提供了威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔的可获取指南. 每一章都专门讨论历史文件的一节,仔细研究其背景、其对信仰的意义、其应用以及任何争议。 对原则,包括"三一","创造","天赐","受洗","最后的判断"等进行明确,彻底的解释,使这成为"改革后基督教学说"的决定性指南. 论文由改革神学院的教师在其专业领域撰写,确保教会领导人、神学教师和学生以及外行者能够获得可靠和高质量的文本。 在亚马逊或威斯敏斯特书店买的 Crossway I don't have enough Faith to be an Atheist 更新版 Norman L. Geisler and Frank Turek 由加文·奥尔特伦德,肖恩·麦克道威尔,格雷戈里·库克尔,艾莉莎·柴尔德斯和乔什·豪尔顿出版商的描述认可 对一些人来说,对更高权力或一套宗教信仰有信仰的概念是没有意识的. 事实上,许多人认为,一般宗教,特别是基督教,是毫无根据和不合理的。 然而,弗兰克·图雷克和诺曼·盖斯勒(Norman Geisler)认为,基督教不仅比所有其他信仰体系更合理,而且确实比不信本身更合理. 以信念和清晰的思考,图雷克和盖斯勒指导读者通过一些传统的,经过考验的关于创造出神存在的论点. 他们开始研究道德渊源和"新约"中有关耶稣的叙述的可靠性. 该书的最后一节详细论述对基督的主张的调查. 这本附有新论点的增订本,对于那些对基督教持怀疑态度的人来说,将是一个有趣的读物,也是基督教徒寻求更尖端地捍卫其信仰的有用资源。 在亚马逊买的 Baker Books of All Good God的出品人作为伦理学的开始和结束 Chase R. Kuhn出版社的描述 我们的道德从何而来? 它们是建立在不断变化的现实基础上,还是随着人类文化的发展和变化而需要加以修改? 基督教道德与其他道德主张有什么区别? 基督徒如何以明确和自信的方式处理这些问题,而不放弃他们的信念或放弃对话? Chase R. Kuhn指出,答案不是从我们自己开始的——我们的感情、我们的文化和我们的道德直觉——而是从上帝开始的。 我们对上帝的信仰 塑造了我们的生活 我们的神学指南

articles.summary_zh: 我经常被问及与三名被性贩运者剥削的年轻女孩一起在东南亚监狱度过的夜晚。但主要的问题不是我为什么入狱。相反，为什么这三个女孩一开始就被关在监狱里？为什么是他们，而不是抓走……的人贩子……
articles.title_zh: 破碎的系统保护贩运者，而不是女孩
articles.content: I’m often asked about the night I spent in a Southeast Asian jail alongside three young girls who had been exploited by sex traffickers. But the primary question isn’t about why I was in jail. Rather, why were those three girls in jail to begin with? Why them, and not the traffickers who had taken them from their families and sold them repeatedly for sex, turning their lives into a brutal nightmare? Why not the woman who had put tape over the mouth of the young girl so that the man who was raping her would not be disturbed by her screams. The system failed them. The brothel keeper was tipped off about their rescue operation, allowed to hide her crime, and told to dump the girls at a nearby bus stop. The police who should have rescued them instead arrested them on immigration charges. The trafficker walked free, while the girls were treated as criminals. As I sat with them that night, I longed for those girls to have never been taken to jail, much less a brothel. I wanted them to have always been at home with their families, going to school, and playing with their friends. I wanted them to have never been harmed in the first place. But the reality is, like millions of women and girls in our world today, they suffered the consequences of a broken justice system. And so, the reason I stayed with the girls is simply that the alternative was just too horrible. I preferred to be arrested myself rather than leave them vulnerable to further assault. But there’s an important detail to clarify: in the end, I did not need to stay the full night. Once it was clear I was not going away, the jailer himself took on the responsibility of assuring their safety. In a broken system, when even just one agent uses their authority for good, the door to justice begins to open. Shifting Power The very next day, my colleagues at International Justice Mission (IJM) and I were able to bring the girls to safety and long-term holistic aftercare. I continued to visit the girls for years, witnessing their healing as they moved into new lives of freedom. But nearly 25 years after that night in jail, the fight remains the same; we must not leave until those with governing power wield their power to protect the most vulnerable. If we fail to intervene for the women and girls being brutalized by violent criminals, including intimate partners and family members, the alternative is unconscionable. But when we do show up, we get to be part of shifting the levers of power. Entire systems – even the most corrupt and unjust – begin to change for good. In the 21st century, we must reckon with the reality that millions of women and girls are still not any more safe from violence than they have been in any previous era. It is still true, as it has been for decades, that one in three women will experience physical or sexual violence in their lifetime. Today, and in fact, every day, 140 women will be killed by their partners or family members. But far too often, law enforcement and other government actors appear to be on the side of violent perpetrators and other abusers, rather than those who are suffering violence. Whether it’s taking bribes to protect traffickers, criminalizing women and children who are being exploited, or allowing them to be intimidated into not reporting the abuse, agents of the law bear tremendous responsibility and opportunity to change the systemic violence they have enabled to perpetuate. Violent crime thrives on opportunity, and the argument for countering this could not be more clear: strengthening justice systems deters violence. When laws are enforced and traffickers and other abusers are held accountable, other perpetrators of violence are discouraged from committing similar crimes. I think of this as flipping the fear equation. When violent abusers begin to fear the consequences of law, women and children begin to live free from fear. In my work with IJM, I’ve helped build a model that has proved this theory of change. We’ve meticulously m
articles.content_zh: 我经常被问及在东南亚监狱度过的夜晚, 但首要问题并不在于我为何入狱。 相反,为什么这三个女孩要入狱? 为什么是他们,而不是那些从家人那里夺走他们,并反复出卖他们的性生活,把他们的生活变成残酷的噩梦的人? 为什么不让那个把录音带放入年轻女孩口中的女人 让强奸她的男人不会被她尖叫所打扰 系统失败了 妓院老板被告知他们的营救行动,允许她隐瞒罪行,并说要把女孩们扔到附近的一个公交站。 本应救出他们的警察却以移民指控逮捕了他们。 贩卖者走得自由,而女孩则被当作罪犯对待. 当晚我和她们坐在一起时,我渴望那些女孩从来没有被关进监狱,更不用说妓院了。 我希望他们总是和家人一起在家,上学,和朋友一起玩. 我希望他们从一开始就没有受到伤害。 但是,现实是,同我们当今世界上数百万妇女和女童一样,她们遭受了司法制度被打破所造成的后果。 所以,我和女孩们在一起的原因 就是另一种选择太可怕了。 我宁愿自己被捕,而不是让他们受到进一步的攻击。 但有一个重要的细节需要澄清:最后,我不需要过夜。 一旦我明白我不会离开, 看守自己承担了保证他们安全的责任。 在一个破碎的体系中,即使只有一个特工善用权威,正义之门也开始打开. 正在移动电源 第二天,我在国际司法特派团(正义团)的同事和我得以使这些女孩安全地得到长期的全面照顾。 多年来,我继续探访这些女孩,目睹她们进入自由新生活时愈合。 但是,在狱中当晚近25年之后,这场战斗依然如故;我们决不能离开,直到那些拥有统治权的人行使权力保护最脆弱群体。 如果我们不能干预暴力罪犯,包括亲密伴侣和家庭成员对妇女和女孩的残暴行为,那么,另一种选择是不合理的。 但是,当我们出现时, 我们就会成为改变权力杠杆的一部分。 整个系统 — — 甚至最腐败和最不公正的系统 — — 开始永远改变。 在21世纪,我们必须考虑这样一个现实:数百万妇女和女童仍然比以往任何时代都更无法免遭暴力。 几十年来,每3个妇女中就有1个在一生中遭受身体或性暴力。 今天,事实上,每天都有140名妇女被其伴侣或家庭成员杀害。 但是,执法部门和其他政府行为者似乎往往站在暴力肇事者和其他施虐者一边,而不是那些遭受暴力的人一边。 无论是收受贿赂来保护被剥削的妇女和儿童,还是让他们受到恐吓来不报告虐待,法律工作者都肩负着巨大的责任和机会来改变他们得以延续的系统性暴力。 暴力犯罪依靠机会而兴起,打击暴力的论据再清楚不过了:加强司法系统可以阻止暴力。 当法律得到实施,贩运者和其他施虐者被追究责任时,其他暴力行为的犯罪人就被劝阻不犯下类似的罪行。 我认为这是在改变恐惧的等式。 当暴力虐待者开始害怕法律的后果时,妇女和儿童开始免于恐惧地生活。 在与IJM的合作中, 我帮助建立了一个模型, 我们非常谨慎

articles.summary_zh: 一名在土耳其东部船形编队工作的雷达科学家说，他的扫描显示里面有组织的图案、腔室和走廊，这些特征不是天然岩石。根据该项目的说法，科学家Khosrow Bakhtar是一位资深的美国国防科学家，也是现场使用的BakhtarRadar系统的发明者。
articles.title_zh: 研究人员说，雷达显示土耳其船形编队内的房间和走廊，有些人认为是诺亚方舟
articles.content: A radar scientist working at a boat-shaped formation in eastern Turkey says his scans show organized patterns, chambers and corridors inside it, and that those features are not natural rock. The scientist, Khosrow Bakhtar, is a veteran U.S. defense scientist and the inventor of the BakhtarRadar system used at the site, according to the project’s release. He reported the preliminary results from inside the Durupınar Formation, a roughly 515-foot structure near Mount Ararat that Ark hunters have studied since 1959. Bakhtar said the radar was set to mask natural geological signals, so a purely natural anomaly would not have shown up in the processed images. He called it “the most significant finding of 45 years of my career.” Prof. Cenker Atila of Sivas Cumhuriyet University, who oversees the permitted project, reviewed and confirmed the preliminary results, the release says. He added that the radar also shows a structure with three levels, which he compared to the three levels of the Ark in “our Holy Books.” The findings were presented at a symposium in Turkey, and the group, Noah’s Ark Scans, announced them this week. The group also reports recovering charred wood from almost 30 feet down inside the formation, and says the condition of the wood is what makes it interesting. Genesis describes the Ark coated in pitch, which burns easily, so the release suggests someone may have tried to set the Ark on fire long ago. Charring slows decomposition in soil, often to well under 1% a year, so “what was meant to destroy it may have actually preserved it,” the release says. The group also says the wood is not recent surface debris and was not carried in by mudflow, because it came from deep within the formation. The release allows other explanations for the charring, including lightning or volcanic activity. Founder Andrew Jones said the wood could be the charred remains of the Ark or the remains of a campfire a shepherd lit while using it for shelter centuries ago. The wood has been sent for carbon-14 dating and species identification, and the team says no firm conclusions should be drawn until the results are published. Dating would give the wood’s age and identification would show what kind of tree it came from, but neither result would by itself show that it came from a boat. Everything here comes from the group itself. The radar results are preliminary, the masking is the team’s own processing, and none of it has been through independent peer review. A 1996 study by geologist Lorence Collins and Ark hunter David Fasold concluded that Durupınar is a natural rock formation. Noah’s Ark Scans also sells guided tours and merchandise, is running a GiveSendGo fundraiser for more core drilling, and its release asks for donations and points readers to a gold dealer and a preparedness retailer. More radar processing and reporting is expected in the coming months, and Jones has said initial lab results are expected over the winter. Atila has said photos of the wood will be released in the near future.
articles.content_zh: 一位在土耳其东部的船形编队工作的雷达科学家说,他的扫描显示它内部有条理的图案,室室和走廊,这些特征不是天然岩石. 科学家Khosrow Bakhtar是一位美国资深国防科学家, 他报告了Durupınar Formation公司内部的初步结果,这是Ararat山附近一个约515英尺高的结构,由Ark猎人自1959年以来研究。 巴赫塔尔说,雷达是用来遮掩自然地质信号的,因此在经过处理的图像中不会出现纯粹的自然异常. 他称之为“我45年职业生涯中最重要的发现”。 师曰. Sivas Cumhuriyet大学的Cenker Atila监督了许可的项目,审查并确认了初步结果。 他补充说,雷达还显示一个具有三个级别的结构,他与方舟子在“我们的圣书”中的三个级别相比。 调查结论在土耳其的一次研讨会上发表, 剧组还报告从形成地近30英尺下方取出烧焦的木头,并说木头的状况使得它很有趣. "创世记"描述了被涂入花筒的"方舟",这很容易被烧伤,因此发行表明有人可能早就想放出"方舟"了. 碳化物在土壤中的分解速度慢了,每年的分解率往往不到1%,因此“破坏它的意图可能是实际保存下来的”。 剧组还称该木不是近代地表出土出土的地表出土出土后被泥流所承载,因为它出土出土了形成地深. 释放后可以对焦炭进行其他解释,包括闪电或火山活性. 创始人安德鲁·琼斯(Andrew Jones)说,木头可能是"方舟"被烧焦的遗骨,也可能是数百年前在使用时被牧羊人点燃了的营火的遗骨. 该木被送去进行碳-14约会和物种鉴定,队伍表示在结果公布之前不应得出确定的结论. 约会可以说明木材的年代, 这里的一切来自团体本身. 雷达结果初步,口罩是团队自己的处理方式,没有经过独立的同行评审. 1996年由地质学家洛伦斯·柯林斯和方克猎人大卫·法拉尔德进行的一项研究得出结论,杜鲁普纳尔是天然岩层. 诺亚方舟扫描公司也出售导游和商品, 预计未来几个月会有更多的雷达处理和报告,琼斯表示预计冬季会有初步的实验室结果. Atila表示, 木头的照片将在不久的将来发布。

articles.summary_zh: 至少根据他们自己的说法， 2026年25岁的人开始的成年生活比2010年25岁的人更糟糕。盖洛普最新的幸福感报告发现，今年到目前为止， 18至29岁的美国成年人中有44% “茁壮成长” ，低于2010年的64%。盖洛普认为某人正在茁壮成长……
articles.title_zh: 盖洛普： 30岁以下美国人的生活水平比2010年低20个百分点
articles.content: A 25-year-old in 2026 is starting adult life in worse shape than a 25-year-old in 2010, at least by their own account. Gallup’s newest wellbeing report finds that 44% of U.S. adults ages 18 to 29 are “thriving” so far this year, down from a high of 64% in 2010. Gallup counts someone as thriving if they rate their current life a 7 or higher on a zero-to-10 ladder and expect to rate their life an 8 or higher five years from now. Most of the drop came recently. About two-thirds of the total decline has happened since 2019. Gallup is careful about causes, saying a set of factors “may explain” the decline among young adults. It points to a rise in depression, weaker close relationships, less daily enjoyment and less feeling active and productive each day. It also lists lower satisfaction with living standards, with leaders who create enthusiasm about the future and with progress toward personal goals. Among adults 30 to 44, it says the share currently having or being treated for depression is up 15 points since 2019, to 37%. Beyond those measures, Gallup names loneliness, which it says has been particularly acute among younger men, along with housing affordability and fear of losing jobs to AI. About half of adults 18 to 49 doubt Medicare and Social Security will be available in 10 years, far more than other age groups. Just 14% of adults 18 to 34 say they are “extremely proud” to be American, down 10 points since 2025. The numbers follow people as they age. Adults now 34 to 46 are at 46%, compared with 64% when they were the 18-to-29 group in 2010, so their ratings fell as they got older while the young adults behind them are starting from a lower place. Adults 30 to 44 are at 45%, down from a high of 62% in 2016 and 2017. Adults 45 to 64 are at 46%, which matches their low from 2008. The estimates come from three Gallup Panel surveys in February, May and August 2026 with 15,156 U.S. adults in total.
articles.content_zh: 2026年出道的25岁少年开始的成人生活状况比2010年出道的25岁少年更糟糕,至少是靠他们自己的说法. 盖洛普最新的福利报告发现,今年到目前为止,美国44%的18至29岁的成年人在“抢走”,低于2010年的64%。 盖洛普认为,如果把目前的寿命定在7至10个梯子上,并期望从现在起将生命定在8至10个梯子上,那么,盖洛普就认为某人是繁荣的。 大部分的货最近才来 约三分之二的总下降发生在2019年以来. 盖洛普对原因很谨慎,说一系列因素“可以解释”年轻人的下降。 这表明抑郁症的上升,亲密的关系更弱,日常的享受减少,每天的活跃和生产的感觉也更差. 它还列出了对生活水平、对未来产生热情的领导人以及在实现个人目标方面取得进展的低满意度。 在30至44个成年人中,它说,目前接受或正在接受抑郁治疗的比例自2019年以来上升了15分,达到37%. 除了这些措施外,Gallup还称孤独,这在年轻男子中尤其严重,而且住房负担不起,担心会失去AI的工作。 大约一半的18至49个成年人怀疑在10年内将可获得医疗保健和社会保障,远远多于其他年龄组。 18至34岁的成年人中只有14%说,他们“非常自豪”是美国人,自2025年以来下降了10分。 数字跟随人们老去。 成人目前为34至46人,占46%,而2010年是18至29人组的64%,因此他们的收视率随着年龄的增长而下降,而背后的青壮年则从更低的地方开始。 成年人30至44人占45%,低于2016年和2017年的62%。 成年人45至64人的比例为46%,与2008年的水平相匹配。 估计数来自2026年2月,5月和8月的三起盖洛普小组调查,共计15,156名美国成年人.

articles.content: The search bar in a Bible app works like any other, which means it shows what people are worried about before they’ve said it out loud to anyone. YouVersion says “Psalm 91” was the single most-searched term in the app this year. In its newest release , the company also says “anxiety,” “hope” and “healing” were among the year’s most searched terms. YouVersion describes Psalm 91 as a psalm that encourages readers to turn to God for refuge and comfort in difficult times. The psalm runs 16 verses. Together, YouVersion says, the searches offer a glimpse into the personal questions and hopes people are bringing to Scripture. Daily use of the Bible App grew by more than 13% compared with 2025, reaching 18.5 million people a day. It also says it added more than 160 million new installs across its family of apps in 2026, after celebrating one billion installs last November. Daily engagement grew faster than installs, which the company reads as a sign that people are returning to the app and not only downloading it. Some of the highest engagement is outside the U.S. YouVersion says it sees some of the highest levels of Bible App engagement in Sub-Saharan Africa, the Middle East and Southeast Asia, and it is building regional hubs in places including the United Kingdom, Brazil, Kenya and Mexico. Its apps offer 3,800 versions of the Bible in 2,400 languages, and it works with a network of more than 45,000 churches and partners. Bobby Gruenewald, YouVersion’s founder and CEO, said in the release that the company has been encouraged by “how many people are turning to Scripture for answers to their questions.”

YouVersion指出, 搜索可以窥见个人问题, 希望人们能带来圣经。 与2025年相比,"圣经App"的日常使用量增长了13%多,每天达到1850万人. 去年11月庆祝了十亿个安装, 日常参与比安装增长得快,公司读到这表示人们正在回归应用,而不仅仅是下载. 在美国YouVersion以外, 一些最高的接触者表示, 在撒哈拉以南非洲、中东和东南亚, 其应用软件以2400种语言提供3800个版本的"圣经",它与超过45000个教堂和合作伙伴的网络合作. articles.title: Fear Itself
articles.summary: Widow's Bay  and the Trolley Problem of Life   The post  Fear Itself  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
articles.summary_zh: 寡妇湾和生活的手推车问题帖子Fear Itself首先出现在Mockingbird上。
articles.title_zh: 恐惧自身
articles.content: W hat is your biggest fear? Spiders? That’s a classic. Deranged clowns? Sure! Maybe you prefer the more existential variety? How about never fully realizing your potential or dying alone? All of the above? Similar to the What superpower would you choose? question, it is hard for me to select only one. I am a fearful person. I have a way of collecting fears as I go about my life. Alpha-gal, something I did not know existed until two days ago, is the flavor of the week. But my fear of dying alone is more like a longtime, trusted companion. The world is a scary place. At any moment, our identities could be hacked. Our phones could ring with dreadful news. Our brains could suffer an aneurysm. Swimming in a bottomless sea of insecurity, we are meagerly equipped with our basic survival instincts: fight, flight, freeze, and appease. These impulses may help keep us safe from spiders and clowns (answer for both: flight!), but what do we make of the dangers that are harder to pin down? What if the dangers are not only without but within? Leave it to this year’s hit TV series to explore these questions. If you’re looking for a spooky show to get into this weekend, it’s Widow’s Bay. The Emmy-sweeping, genre-bending, horror-comedic series is a triumph for a number of reasons. For starters, it muddles the black-and-white worlds Hollywood has created (e.g., horror movies without humor, comedies without any depth), reminding us that life can be both scary and funny. The show has all the irresistible horror tropes (the harbinger who warns everyone of impending doom, the suspenseful music, the jump scares) but, along with its crowd-pleasing antics, it dives deeper than surface-level fears. Its anthropology is refreshingly low. This is not a match between good people and evil monsters. Yes, sometimes the enemy is a chainsaw-wielding fiend. Much scarier, however, is when the enemy is yourself. Take Tom Loftis, for instance, the ambitious new mayor who wants to transform the cursed island town of Widow’s Bay into the next Martha’s Vineyard. He is, from every angle, a secular man. For Tom, God is no more real than ghosts. The only higher power that exists is the one you achieve by climbing the ladder. He resents how the locals tolerate the town’s haunted reputation. For too long, people have been resigned to the rumors that the hotel is haunted, the church is cursed, and the bay isn’t safe for a swim. For Tom, the only thing to fear is fear itself. Like any mayor with a messiah complex, he sets out to do something about it. As Loftis sees things, the real problem with the place is not that it is demonically possessed. The real problem is bad branding . In his eyes, Widow’s Bay is simply misunderstood. When visiting Widow’s Bay to write a piece for the New York Times travel section, a reporter asks Loftis about a framed article in the historical society titled “Cannibalism in God’s House.” Loftis tries to water it down. “These stories get so exaggerated over time,” he says. “Was there a deadly storm in 1786? Yes. Did a group of people get trapped inside a church? Apparently so. Did they immediately turn to cannibalism? No, that took four days !” See? That’s not so bad, right? Loftis’ PR campaign is like slapping new siding on a haunted mansion. He is convinced that the plight of Widow’s Bay can be solved by installing a proper cappuccino machine in the local coffee shop. Cappuccino machines are great at making a proper latte but pretty useless when up against the occult. Before long, Loftis’ denial of the curse over the island town is just as dangerous as the curse itself. The first step to keeping the forces at bay is to admit they exist. There is a scene in which Loftis speaks to another character about the Trolley Problem, an ethical thought experiment in which there is a runaway trolley barreling down the tracks toward a crowd of people. In this hypothetical setup, there is a lever that would switch the trolley to a different track with only one
articles.content_zh: 帽子是你最大的恐惧? 蜘蛛吗? 这是经典。 疯狂的小丑? 当然! 也许你更喜欢生存的品种? 永远不能充分发挥你的潜力 或孤独地死去怎么样? 所有这一切? 类似于你选择的超级大国? 问,我很难只选一个 我是一个害怕的人。 我有办法收集恐惧 当我去我的生活。 Alpha -gal,我两天前才知道的东西 是这个星期的口味 但我害怕孤独地死去 更像是长期 值得信赖的同伴 世界是个可怕的地方。 我们的身份随时可能被黑入 我们的电话可能会传出可怕的消息 我们的大脑可能会有动脉瘤 在一个不安全的无底海中游来游去,我们装备了我们的基本生存本能:战斗、出逃、冻结和安抚。 这些冲动也许可以帮助我们远离蜘蛛和小丑(回答:飞行!),但我们如何应对那些更难消除的危险? 如果危险不仅是没有危险,而且是内部危险呢? 让今年的电视连续剧来探讨这些问题。 如果你想要一个恐怖的节目进入这个周末, "艾美扫地"(英語:Emmy-sweating, genre-bending),"恐怖喜剧"(英語:Description-comed)系列,由于多种原因,是一场胜利. 首先,它搅乱了好莱坞所创造的黑白世界(例如没有幽默感的恐怖电影,没有任何深度的喜剧),提醒我们生活既会恐怖又会搞笑. 该节目拥有所有不可抗拒的恐怖颤抖(预告会警告所有人即将来临的末日,悬疑的音乐,跳跃的惊吓等),但连同其人群取悦的焦虑,其潜入比地表恐惧更深. 它的人类学水平低得惊人 这不是好人和邪恶怪物的对决 是的,有时敌人是一个 链锯的恶魔。 然而,更可怕的是当敌人是你自己的时候。 以汤姆·洛夫蒂斯(Tom Loftis)为例, 他,从每个角度来说,都是世俗的人. 对汤姆来说,上帝不比鬼更真实. 唯一高的电能是通过攀登梯子实现的. 当地民众如何容忍镇上闹事的名声? 久而久之,人们对旅馆闹鬼、教堂被诅咒、海湾游泳不安全等谣言辞职。 对汤姆来说,唯一害怕的是恐惧本身. 像任何拥有救世主建筑群的市长一样,他开始对此有所行动. 正如洛夫提斯所见 这个地方真正的问题不是 它被恶魔附身 真正的问题是品牌不好 在他眼中,寡妇湾只是被误解了。 当一位记者访问寡妇湾为纽约时报旅行部写出一篇作品时,他问洛夫蒂斯关于历史社会中一篇被设定为“神殿中的食人狂”的文章。 洛夫提斯试图给它浇水 他说,“这些故事随着时间的推移变得如此夸张。” “1786年是否有致命的风暴? 对 一群人被困在教堂里了吗? 显然如此。 他们有没有立即转向吃人? 不,那需要四天时间!” 这还不算太糟吧? Loftis的公关活动就像在闹鬼的豪宅上再拍一拍。 他相信寡妇湾的困境可以通过在当地咖啡店安装适当的卡布奇诺机器来解决。 卡布奇诺机器很擅长做一个正宗的拿铁 但和神秘主义作对时却很没用 不久之后,洛夫蒂斯否认对岛屿城镇的诅咒,与诅咒本身同样危险。 阻止势力存在的第一步是承认它们的存在. 有个场景让洛夫蒂斯向另一个角色讲述了"特罗莱问题"(Trolley Problem),这是一场道德思想实验,其中有一个跑跑的推车管向一行人冲去. 在这个假想的设定中,有一个杠杆,可以把推车换到只有一跑道的另一跑道.

articles.title: A Crazy Train Crying in the Wilderness
articles.summary: Ozzy Osbourne's Plea to Be Heard   The post  A Crazy Train Crying in the Wilderness  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
articles.summary_zh: Ozzy Osbourne的《Pleas to Be Heard》《A Crazy Train Crying in the Wilderness》一文首次出现在《知更鸟》上。
articles.title_zh: 疯狂的火车在荒野中哭泣
articles.content: No matter who won or lost the last big game you attended, chances are, Ozzy Osbourne was there in electronic chains, locked inside a brain-rattling sound system, unnoticed, unnamed, misunderstood, a voice crying in the wilderness of crowded rows of fans desperate for a win, cheering for their heroes while jeering at their opponents, paying too much for unnecessary carbs and calories, possibly on the sabbath day. When Ozzy cried, “All aboard!” you stood with hundreds or thousands of tangential warriors singing along with the fatalistic chorus, air guitaring with the riffs, nodding with the rhythm, but you weren’t there for music. You were there to shout, thump your chest, flex, thrust hands with fingers contorted into symbols of specific allegiance, or claim you’re #1, convinced that the song, the battle cry, and the power behind it all were on your side. The words didn’t matter. Your heroes were fighting for you, to give you hope. You’d fight for them if you could, if you had to, against whoever stands in your way, to win at all costs. But what if that’s not what Ozzy wanted? How do we know what he wanted? He screams, “You’ve got to listen to my words!” Below is a paraphrase of the “Crazy Train” lyrics: “It’s crazy, but it’s always been like this — we’re all living as enemies. But maybe it’s not too late to learn how to love and forget how to hate. We’ve all got mental wounds that aren’t healing. I’m losing it. I’ve listened to everyone — fools, preachers, anarchists. Nothing helps. There’s always a system run by someone who’s a product of the system and has been conditioned to run the system, which is sold to us by rich people who get richer by keeping the system alive. And we buy it, screaming in pain from our open mental wounds. It’s messed up. I’m messed up. We’re all messed up. We inherit each other’s trouble. We’re heirs of unresolved conflict. I keep saying it, but no one listens. You’ve got to listen to my words. I can’t figure out how to feel. The mental wounds don’t heal. I don’t know who to blame, but I know it’s not fair.” I wrote the above paraphrase to read to my senior literature class last Monday morning. Nearly half of the students in the class are varsity football starters chasing championships and full-rides. I prefaced the reading with a white lie, “I got this message from someone you all know over the weekend. I won’t tell you who it is, but I want you to help me think through how to respond.” The starting quarterback, worried, tried to interrupt me. I didn’t look up, held my hand out to pause questions, and continued reading. When I finished, there was a chorus of concern from several voices: That’s a cry for help! Is it from a boy or a girl? You said we know them? Who is it? Did they email you? What did you say? They need help. Who are you going to talk to? Still in character, I said, “I can’t tell you a name, but I’ll play this song.” A few seconds into “Crazy Train,” the students realized what was going on, looked relieved, but then became uncomfortable when I turned down the volume and read out the actual lyrics. In confused silence, their faces said, We weren’t listening . I felt bad. I smiled and apologized for manipulating their emotions, and the air lightened. Someone started singing the chorus, and we moved on. But I’m not sure we should have. “Crazy Train” is the most popular song from the most recognizable sex, drugs, and rock-n-roll villain to ever bite the head off a bat, but it’s also a cry for help from a struggling human admitting personal weakness and claiming no superiority. While suggesting that love is better than hate, he’s doing more than just asking us to love. He’s asking us to LEARN HOW TO. French philosopher and mystic, Simone Weil, who died during World War II in solidarity with residents of German-occupied France, didn’t write how-to books, but she couldn’t stop talking about attention. Her bumper sticker quote, “Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity,” is clippe

articles.title: East Coker and the Cure for Human Inability
articles.summary: "... to be restored, our sickness must grow worse."   The post  East Coker and the Cure for Human Inability  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
articles.summary_zh: “......要恢复，我们的疾病必须变得更糟。“《East Coker and the Cure for Human Inability》一文首次出现在《知更鸟》上。
articles.title_zh: East Coker和治疗人类残疾的方法
articles.content: H ow strange that one can read the same poems countless times and discover new things with each visit, like a traveler coming home for Christmas only to find it slightly altered! It is the same for me revisiting T. S. Eliot’s Four Quartets : the end is different than I imagined in the beginning when I first read these words, imagined these places, and attempted to grasp the author’s meaning. Eliot had the same experience. The meaning of the Four Quartets was one thing when he originally envisioned them, another when he wrote them, and still another when the public began analyzing them. He never believed they would be forever linked with the world’s most destructive war. He had not even known there would be four. In the beginning, there was only “Burnt Norton,” written in 1936 and intended to be a one-off. It was generally well received by critics, and the whole business could have been over then. But three years passed, and Eliot found himself with that most common of authorly ailments: not knowing what to write or fearing that he no longer knew how to write properly. Specifically, he had gone for some time without constructing new poems. The world had changed since “Burnt Norton” was published. A growing menace once possible to ignore had exploded into a firestorm of destructive force sweeping through the nations of Europe, consuming all in its path. The bonds that had knit together what remained of Western Christian civilization were snapping with wild abandon, supplanted by ideologies of extermination. Faced with such a crisis, Eliot searched for the one fixed point amid the whirling chaos. He settled on the village of East Coker in Somerset, England. His ancestor Andrew Eliot had left there in 1669, abandoning the historic family home and immigrating to New England. Nearly three centuries later, Thomas Stearns Eliot had become the first member of the family to move back to the motherland, and the family connection held spiritual significance for him. In 1937, he visited St. Michael and All Angels’ Church in East Coker, where his ashes would one day be placed. I know something of Eliot’s experience. I too am the descendant of Englishmen and women whose bones lie buried in every corner of that land, some in tombs I have visited. I too was the first person in my family to return and live in England, if only for a year. It did feel in a sense like returning to my beginning, which is probably why I connect so strongly with the Four Quartets . The secret Eliot discovered at East Coker is one that has transformed my own life as well: we do not possess the power to redeem ourselves or the world and are utterly dependent on the gift of grace. Of all the Four Quartets , this is the most law and gospel poem. The Four Quartets are commonly associated with the four traditional elements of the physical world: air, earth, water, and fire. But as I have noted, Eliot did not begin with a grand plan, so the elemental symbolism becomes stronger in the later poems. Yes, we see the movement of air in “Burnt Norton” disturbing a bowl of rose leaves and carrying the laughter of children, but you would not conclude “This is an air poem” unless you had the other three Quartets to guide you. Likewise, the earth theme is not obvious after the first section of “East Coker,” but once we get to “The Dry Salvages,” we will be drowned in water imagery, and “Little Gidding” will pelt us with fire from beginning to end. Thus, Eliot begins “East Coker” rooted in the earth, in time and place and home. But immediately, the earth is overturned by the machinations of human societies succeeding and supplanting one another, building up to heaven and returning to dust. In my beginning is my end. In succession Houses rise and fall, crumble, are extended, Are removed, destroyed, restored, or in their place Is an open field, or a factory, or a by-pass. If you have visited the ancient monument of Stonehenge on Salisbury Plain, you know it sits at a motorway intersecti
articles.content_zh: 奇怪的是,人们可以阅读同名诗作无数次,每次拜访都会发现新的事物,就像一个旅行者回家过圣诞节,只为了发现它略有改变! 我同样重温了T. S. Eliot的四重奏:结局和我最初读到这些话、想象这些地方并试图理解作者含义时所想象的不一样。 Eliot也有同样的经历. 四重奏的意义是他最初设想它们的时候是一回事,他写它们的时候是另一回事,当公众开始分析它们的时候仍然是另一回事. 他从未相信它们会永远与世界上最具破坏性的战争联系在一起。 他甚至不知道会有四个。 一开始只有"伯恩特·诺顿"(Burnt Norton,作于1936年)一作一作一作一想. 它普遍受到批评者的好评,整个业务本来可以到那时结束. 但三年过去了,艾略特发现自己与最常见的作者病症相伴:不知道该写什么,或担心自己不再知道如何正确写作. 具体地说,他已经走了一段时间,没有创作出新诗. 自“Burnt Norton”出版以来,世界发生了变化。 日益严重的威胁一旦可能被忽视,就已演变成一股由毁灭性力量横扫欧洲各国并吞噬其道路的火焰。 将西方基督教文明遗留下来的东西联系起来的纽带,被被灭绝思想所取代而疯狂地抛弃了。 面对这样的危机,埃利奥特在旋转的混乱中寻找一个固定点. 他定居于英格兰萨默塞特的东科克村. 他的祖先安德鲁·埃利奥特于1669年离开那里,放弃了有历史意义的家族家园并移民到新英格兰. 近3个世纪后,托马斯·斯蒂恩斯·埃利奥特成为了第一个搬回祖国的家庭成员,家庭联系对他具有了精神意义. 1937年,他参观了东科克的圣迈克尔和All Angels教堂,在那里有一天他的骨灰会被放置. 我知道Eliot的经验。 我也是英国男人和女人的后人 他们的骨头埋在这片土地的每一个角落, 一些在我的访问过的坟墓。 我也是我家里第一个回到英国生活的人 哪怕只有一年 我确实感觉回到我的开始, 这可能是为什么我如此紧密地与四重奏联系起来。 Eliot在东科克发现的秘密 也改变了我自己的生活: 我们没有拯救自己或世界的能力, 完全依赖恩赐。 在所有四重奏中,这是最有法律和福音的诗. 四重奏通常与物理世界的四大传统元素相通:空气,地,水,火. 但正如我所指出,艾略特并没有从一个宏伟的计划入手,因此元素符号主义在后期诗作中变得更加强大. 是的,我们看到“Burnt Norton”中的空气运动扰乱了一碗玫瑰叶并带了孩子们的笑声,但除非有另外三个四方来指导你,否则你不会得出“这是一首空气诗”的结论。 同样地,在第一部分“东科克”之后,地球主题并不明显,但一旦我们到达“干涸的盐水”,我们将被水上图像所淹没,而“小吉丁”将从头到尾向我们开火。 因此,Eliot开始“东科克”扎根于地球、时间、地点和家园。 但是,立即,人类社会的成功和取而代之的诡计推翻了地球,使地球升入天堂并回到了尘土中。 在我开始的时候,就是我的结局。 房屋的起伏、倒塌、被延长、被拆除、被摧毁、被恢复或取代,都是空地、工厂或旁道。 如果你曾参观过萨利斯伯里平原上古老的巨石阵纪念碑 你知道它坐落在一条相交的公路上
articles.author: Amy Mantravadi

articles.title: A Few Thoughts on 300 Episodes of Grace (and Its Absence)
articles.summary: Fun, Forgiveness, and Death   The post  A Few Thoughts on 300 Episodes of Grace (and Its Absence)  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
articles.summary_zh: 乐趣、宽恕和死亡《A Few Thoughts on 300 Episodes of Grace (and Its Absence)》一文首次出现在《知更鸟》上。
articles.title_zh: 300集恩典（及其缺席）的几点思考
articles.content: Listeners will have a better idea of why The Mockingcast works (or doesn’t) and why they keep tuning in, 11 years later. We included a few such stories at the beginning of the 300 th episode , and the tears I shed were real. But I thought take the opportunity to offer a few observations from behind the curtain about what I personally appreciate about our podcast, what I’m most proud of, and what’s been challenging. No doubt my co-hosts would have other aspects they’d highlight. First, the longevity. It’s worth celebrating, even if it’s both a blessing and a curse. The time has allowed us to develop some pretty priceless chemistry. When I’m picking articles for us to talk about, I know that even if the material falls flat, I can rely on our dynamic to take up the slack. I trust my co-hosts, and it’s been very gratifying to watch us gel in a non-contrived way over the years. We’ve been through a lot together, and it shows, I think. Being around so long (in internet years) means we’ve had the benefit of watching things come and go. Sarah mentioned this recently in relation to the moralization of food in our society. It was super acute about eight years ago, then it retreated a bit with the body-positivity moment, now it’s back again under the guise of #maxxing. But that’s just one example. I could mention radical atheism, or gospel-centered this and that, or mindfulness. We’ve seen cultural fixations take hold and then recede, specific anxieties bubble up and dissipate. The longer view allows for a measure of perspective that I believe lends the show added depth. Longevity can also be a curse. The ebb and flow can foster a degree of detachment that masquerades as superiority. For example, it’s hard to take the latest rebranding of medieval monasticism (or justification by works) seriously when you’ve seen it happen four times under four different (best-selling) names already. Discipline becomes application becomes virtue becomes formation and so on. It’s a challenge to keep listening and paying attention, but a challenge that I’m proud of us for at least trying to live up to. Because beneath every one of the trends we’ve observed are real people with real hopes and dreams and disappointments. The second longevity-related challenge is the same one that afflicts anyone in a public role, especially those in ministry or thought life. It’s the danger of impersonating yourself. Whenever I detect in my voice any sense of “the grace guy needs to say a grace thing now” — it makes my skin crawl. Autopilot is the enemy, along with its cousin repetition. I remember a trusted listener once warning me that we were becoming a podcast about social media. Another said we were talking too much about parenting. These grooves are understandable, but to keep things fresh, especially over the long haul, you have to always be finding fresh vistas, not just in the culture but in yourself. It’s not easy. This leads me to the next observation: over ten years, it’s become notably more difficult to find suitable material for The Mockingcast . One of the things that I hold sacred about our show is its role as a refuge from culture wars. I want listeners to be confident that when they press play, we’re not going to trigger them about the same headlines that trigger them the rest of the day. We haven’t done this perfectly, I realize, but it remains a guiding principle. When the occasional how-dare-you emails come in, folks are usually surprised to hear that they come just as frequently from both sides of the aisle. If they didn’t, I’d try to course correct. Finding stuff that threads the needle of interesting and substantial but not pre-narrativized has gotten more challenging over our tenure. It’s like the ledge we walk has gotten narrower. Not nonexistent, mind you, just narrower. I’m so proud we’ve reached this milestone without, at least in my view, falling into an ideological ditch or becoming (too) predictable. articles.content_zh: 听众会更清楚为何《嘲笑者》在11年后(或不是)工作, 在三百集的开头, 我们包含了一些这样的故事, 我个人对播客的欣赏、我最自豪的以及挑战性。 无疑我的联合主办方还会有他们强调的其他方面。 首先,长寿。 这值得庆祝, 时间允许我们开发一些 相当无价的化学。 当我挑选文章让我们讨论时, 我知道,即使材料平平了, 我也可以依靠我们的动力来消遣。 我信任我的同座主持人, 我们一起经历了很多事情, 在网路上呆了这么久, 莎拉最近提到这个问题,谈到我们社会中食品的道德化。 大约八年前,它非常急性, 随身体接触的瞬间, 但这只是一个例子。 我可以提到激进的无神论, 或以福音为中心的这个和那个,或注意。 我们已看到文化定型逐渐稳固, 较长的视野允许某种角度的视角,我认为这可以使节目更深入。 长生亦能作一咒. ebb和流能培养出某种程度的离散,以伪装为优越. 例如,当你在四个不同的(畅销的)名称下看到中世纪修道院(或以作品为理由)的最新重塑很难认真对待。 纪律变成应用,美德变成形成等等。 继续倾听和关注是一项挑战,但我为我们至少努力做到这一点而感到自豪。 因为在我们所看到的每一个趋势之下,都是真正有希望、梦想和失望的人。 与长寿有关的第二个挑战也是影响任何公共角色,特别是部会或思想生活角色的挑战。 这是冒充自己的危险。 每当我从我的声音中察觉到任何“恩人现在需要说一件恩事”的感觉时,这让我的皮肤爬行。 自动驾驶是敌人,还有它的表弟重复. 我记得一位值得信赖的听众曾警告我,我们正成为社交媒体的播客。 另一个人说,我们谈论太多关于养育子女的问题。 这些凹槽是可以理解的, 但为了保持新鲜, 特别是从长远来看, 你必须总是找到新鲜的外观, 不仅仅是在文化中, 还是在你自己。 这不容易。 更难为《嘲笑者》找到合适的材料。 我对我们的表演持神圣态度之一 就是它作为文化战争的避难所的作用 我希望听众们有信心, 当他们按下播放时, 我们不会引发同样的头条新闻, 我们并没有完美完成这项工作, 人们通常会惊讶地听到, 如果不是,我会试着正确行事。 寻找一些能勾结到 有趣和实质性但并非预述的东西, 在我们的任期内变得更具挑战性。 我们走过的窗帘越来越窄了。 不是不存在的,你介意,只是狭小。 我感到非常骄傲的是, 我们达到了这个里程碑, 至少在我看来, 我认为,

articles.summary: What Mbird Has Been for Me   The post  Rumors of Grace  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
articles.summary_zh: Mbird对我来说是什么恩典的帖子谣言首先出现在知更鸟上。
articles.title_zh: 恩典的谣言
articles.content: “You only work on Sundays, anyway.” One of the go-to jokes of a group of guys I hang out with. I laugh because, well, I just like to please people. But every time the boys say it, I think to myself, “If you only knew what being a pastor feels like sometimes.” An impromptu funeral at the clinic for veterinarians whose colleague committed suicide, scrolling to find an angry email about last week’s sermon or the changing of the carpet color in the narthex, begging financial generosity from people who pay your salary, lunch with a lonely man going through a brutal divorce, restocking the youth fridge with 7,000 Cheerwines, hearing that they’re gossiping about you again, failing yet again to prepare a sermon that marries TikTok and TED Talk, off to the shelter to serve dinner, did I even eat lunch? Did I mention that this was last Tuesday? Ministry is often pure gift. The highs are as high as they get. Pastors bear witness to the most intimate, most raw, most human, most beautiful and terrifying moments of people’s lives. We play at the level of the soul. We get paid to read and write and pray. We have a front-row seat to miracles: the bound freed, the sinner forgiven, the debts paid, the dead resurrected. It’s not lost on me that having a job rife with meaning is a privilege and honor. This is what God has chosen to make of my life, and I am truly grateful. And yet, there’s no way to get away from the fact that ministry is a burden too. Its shape is a cross. Its form is death and resurrection. People bring all their junk to church — and they should. Sunday mornings are not an assembly of the righteous, they are a sanctuary for sinners — hypocrites anonymous, I like to call it. One of the chief problems that has arisen in my ministry is that I find it so hard to be ministered to. Ministers minister, preachers preach, consolers console, but if you’re not careful, a pastor will find herself without a pastor, a preacher will find himself without a preacher. Everyone needs both. Not long ago I burnt out. Years after, I realize the burnout was not the product of overwork. The fire in my soul was extinguished because for years I had offered relief to others without finding ways to receive it myself. What becomes of a healer who forsakes his own wounds? Pay attention when your soul stops singing. And I did. I prayed for God to bring relief, somehow, someway. And then, to quote Morgan Freeman in The Shawshank Redemption , “a beautiful little bird flew into my drab little cage.” That beautiful bird was Mockingbird Ministries. And now for six years I have done what Michael Gershon calls “staking one’s life on the rumors of grace.” As the 300th of the Mockingcast draws near, I thought it fitting to say what Mbird has been for me: My theological home: Pastors in the mainline will tell you that our denominations are fracturing. It’s tempting to give in to extremes and to weaponize politics toward ecclesial ends. This has made me feel like I don’t belong anywhere politically, theologically, or pastorally. I know many fellow pastor Mbirders agree because we’ve talked about it. Pastors in the mainline who long for a ministry rooted only in the gospel are like an island of misfit toys. Mbird has become for us a gracious home and a place to be reminded again and again of the gospel of grace. My Preacher: I listen to the Mockingcast on Monday mornings. You pastors out there know Monday’s malaise. Dizzied and frenzied from all of Sunday’s work and pressured by a million regrets about the sermon or the attendance, I find sweet relief in the words of RJ, Sarah, and Dave. “That’s right,” I think. “This is what ministry about.” God may not speak to us all through an audible voice in our heads, but God does speak through the words of a sermon.
