articles.title: How Can I Find the Motivation to Use My Time Better at Work?
articles.summary: Let’s start by counting the cost.
articles.summary_zh: 让我们从计算成本开始。
articles.title_zh: 如何找到更好地利用工作时间的动力？
articles.content: I work for a property management company that oversees retail space. I haven’t been doing this very long, but I’m finding that I’m not as productive as I’d like to be. Often, entertainment and fear of failure keep me from working. How can I get motivated to use my time better? Given that we’re to submit to our earthly masters with sincere hearts as unto Christ (Eph. 6:5), our productivity at work isn’t ultimately about our advancement or our employer’s success—it’s about our gospel witness. From before the fall, God ordained our work for keeping, cultivating, subduing, and exercising dominion over his creation. We’re still called to that today in any work to which we set our hand—including the property management of retail space. As believers, all work invites us to leverage our God-given talents and strength to bless and bring order to God’s creation in order to glorify him. When alluring distractions or a fear of failure hinder our labor, we can turn to him who calls us for the truth that will rightly spur us on. Distraction of Entertainment When entertainment distracts us from working, we should start by counting the cost. If we’re spending work hours on entertainment and then have to finish our tasks in what should be our free time, what else is this keeping us from stewarding well? It may be infringing on our time for relationships, spiritual disciplines, or true rest. On the other hand, if our working hours are fixed regardless of how on (or off) task we are, such as a job we clock in and out of with responsibilities only while we’re present, why are we willing to steal from our employer by accepting their payment without exchanging it for the labor we promised? Maybe we need to “cut off” what’s tempting us by blocking entertainment apps on our phone and computer during the workday (Matt. 5:30). If we’re spending work hours on entertainment, what else is this keeping us from stewarding well? Once we do, how might we instead faithfully devote that time to our employer’s good, even being willing to go a mile beyond what’s expected of us (v. 41)? Maybe we provide the talking points requested for a presentation—but also organize them into slides to save someone else from having to do so. Maybe we address the three issues our leader ask us to correct—but also address two more we discovered in the process. Perhaps if we worked with this level of diligence and care, like Joseph with Potiphar, we’d be given increased responsibility and influence that could be leveraged for the kingdom. Those who can be trusted with little can also be trusted with much (Gen. 39:1–6; Luke 16:10). Certainly, God would be glorified as we work with all our heart as to the Lord and not to man (Col. 3:23). Fear of Failure When a fear of failure keeps us from working altogether, we can start by digging out the root of that fear. Do you fear that your limitations and propensity to error will keep you from succeeding? Acknowledge that inaction guarantees you won’t succeed, but attempts to succeed in the work God has entrusted to you allow the opportunity for his power to be made perfect in your weakness (2 Cor. 12:9). When you feel discouraged by your insufficiencies, trust God to provide the wisdom and strength necessary for the work to which he’s called you—by prayer (James 1:5), the edification of his Word, and your humble pursuit of correction and growth through helpful resources and the example of others. Do you fear others’ judgment when you fail? Remember that your purpose is ultimately to please God, not man, and that there’s no condemnation for those in Christ (Rom. 8:1; Gal. 1:10). When you make a mistake or fall short of what’s expected of you, admit your error, seek understanding about what to do differently, and move forward with the humility and resolve that may make others respect you even more than they did before. Trust God to provide the wisdom and strength necessary for the work to which he’s called you. Do you fear your identity being
articles.content_zh: 我为一家监管零售空间的物业管理公司工作 但我发现自己没有自己想要的那么有生产力。 通常,娱乐和对失败的恐惧使我无法工作. 我怎么能有积极性 更好地利用我的时间? 我们的工作效率最终不是关于我们的进步或雇主的成功, 而是关于我们的福音见证。 从秋天之前开始,上帝就规定我们的工作是保持、培育、征服和支配他的创造。 包括零售空间的物业管理。 作为信徒,一切工作都邀请我们利用上帝赐予我们的才华和力量来祝福并给上帝的创造带来秩序来赞美他. 当引人注意或担心失败会阻碍我们的工作时,我们可以求助于他,他呼唤我们寻求正确激励我们的事实。 娱乐的分心 当娱乐干扰我们工作时,我们应该从计算成本入手。 如果我们在娱乐上花工时, 然后必须在什么是空闲时间完成我们的任务, 它可能侵犯我们的时间 关系,精神学科,或真正的休息。 另一方面,如果我们的工作时间是固定的,不管我们是如何完成(或关闭)任务的,比如我们只是在在场时就负责地工作,那么我们为什么愿意接受雇主的付款而不以我们承诺的劳动来换取呢? 也许我们需要在工作日(Matt. 如果我们在娱乐上花工时, 一旦我们这样做了,我们如何忠实地把时间用于雇主的利益,甚至愿意超越我们的期望(v.41)? 也许我们提供了演讲所要求的谈话要点,但也把它们组织成幻灯片,以拯救别人不必这样做。 我们或许可以解决我们领导人要求我们纠正的三个问题, 也许如果我们像约瑟夫和波提乏那样勤奋谨慎, 能够被很少信任的人也可以被很多信任(Gen. 39:1-6;Luke 16:10). 当然,当我们全心全意地为主而不是为人工作时,上帝将受到赞美(第3:23上校)。 对失败的恐惧 当对失败的恐惧使我们无法完全工作时,我们可以首先挖掘出这种恐惧的根源。 难道你怕自己的限制和偏执使你无法成功吗? 承认这种无所作为保证了你不会成功,但为了在上帝委托给你的工作上取得成功而作的尝试,允许他的机会在你的弱点中完美地发挥出他的力量(2 Cor. 12:9). 当你们因自己的不足而感到沮丧时,请相信上帝为他所说的你们的工作提供必要的智慧和力量——通过祈祷(詹姆斯1:5),将他的话化,并通过有益的资源和他人的榜样谦卑地追求纠正和成长。 难道你不怕别人的判断吗? 记住你的目的最终是为了取悦上帝,而不是取悦人类,对基督中的人没有谴责(8:1;Gal:1:10). 当你们犯错误或者没有达到预期时,你们承认自己的错误,寻求了解应该如何采取不同的做法,并以谦卑和决心前进,这可能会使别人比以前更加尊重你们。 相信上帝为他所说的你的工作提供必要的智慧和力量。 你怕你的身份吗?
articles.author: Kaitlin Febles

articles.title: God’s comfort
articles.summary: My family still wrestles with what feels like very fresh grief over my dad’s passing last September. There are moments where things hit us and we feel this ache of...
articles.summary_zh: 我的家人仍然在为父亲去年9月的逝世感到非常新鲜的悲伤而挣扎。在某些时刻，事情触动了我们，我们感到这种痛苦......
articles.title_zh: 神的安慰
articles.content: My family still wrestles with what feels like very fresh grief over my dad’s passing last September. There are moments where things hit us and we feel this ache of his absence. We know that he has gone to be with his Heavenly Father and no longer suffers from the limitations of this mortal coil. It’s just that sometimes, we miss him. It’s at those times when something happens that reminds us of the hope that we have in Christ our Savior, of our purpose here as followers of Christ, as co-laborers in the Kingdom of Heaven. These reminders serve as encouragement to fight the good fight, keeping our eyes on the prize. I was thinking of my dad today and decided to read some of the devotionals he used to write for the ministry to which he dedicated his remaining years, Transport for Christ. When his health could no longer allow him to serve onsite as a chaplain, he wrote encouragement to the truck drivers and the chaplains in service. I can hear his voice in these words. There’s great comfort in his reminder. I share his words with you so that you may also take comfort in a greater plan, and in the hope that comes from trusting God is in control: “Most of the time, when we grieve, we grieve over something that’s happened in our lives. But there are also times when we grieve over something that hasn’t happened or “what might have been.” Unrealized expectations and dashed hopes can paralyze us with sadness. We mourn for what we could have had, could have done or could have experienced. We live in a fog as we struggle with our unmet goals and dreams. Are you wrestling with accepting something in your life? Mourning a shattered dream? Instead of focusing on what might have been, try focusing on what is and what could still be. Revising your dreams isn’t bad. It’s realistic. And the sooner you do, the sooner the weight of grief will let go. The fog will lift. Hope will return.”
articles.content_zh: 我父亲去年九月去世, 有些时候 事情袭击了我们 我们感到他缺席很痛苦 我们知道他和他天父在一起 不再受到这个凡人圈子的限制 只是有时候,我们想念他。 我们的救世主, 我们作为基督的追随者, 这些提醒有助于鼓励我们打好这场好仗,使我们继续关注这一奖项。 我今天想到我爸,决定读一些他以前为他剩下的岁月所奉献的部会而作的奉献,"为基督而运输". 当他的健康不能再允许他当上牧师时,他写信给正在服役的卡车司机和牧师。 这些话我都能听到他的声音。 他提醒大家, 我和你们分享他的话,以便你们也能在更大的计划中得到安慰,希望来自信任上帝的希望是控制着:“多数时候,当我们悲伤的时候,我们对生活中发生的事情感到悲伤。 但有时我们也为一些没有发生的事情而悲伤, 未实现的期望和破灭的希望会使我们感到悲哀。 我们对本可以、本可以或本可以经历的事情表示哀悼。 当我们与未实现的目标和梦想相抗争时,我们生活在雾中。 你是在拼命接受你生活中的东西吗? 打破了梦想? 与其专注于可能已经发生的事情,不如专注于现在和可能仍然可能发生的事情。 改变你的梦想并不坏。 这是现实的。 你越早做, 悲伤的重量会越快松开。 雾会升起 希望将回归。”
articles.author: R.B. Klama

articles.title: A chance meeting?
articles.summary: You’ve probably heard someone say ‘There is no such thing as a coincidence’. Usually people nod their heads and murmur agreement, but the real question is “Do you believe it?“...
articles.summary_zh: 您可能听说过有人说“没有所谓的巧合”。通常人们会点头低语，但真正的问题是“你相信吗？” ……
articles.title_zh: 一相逢
articles.content: You’ve probably heard someone say ‘There is no such thing as a coincidence’. Usually people nod their heads and murmur agreement, but the real question is “Do you believe it?“ Are people just wishful thinkers, or is God really so intimately involved in our daily lives that He orchestrate events on our behalf? What will a chance meeting turn into later? The idea of seeds, planting and harvest is a theme resonant throughout Scripture. Aside from the overt nature of sharing the hope of Christ, there are times we don’t recognize an opportunity at the time, but hindsight has a way of revealing it to us. On my last day in Cairo, I was sitting in the hotel lobby waiting for the rest of the team to come down for checkout. I opened my laptop, and began weeding through emails, and getting pictures uploaded for post, and checking through Facebook. An older gentleman (whom I’d seen at different times all week) came over and said ‘You work too much’. I told him I was just killing time and not really working at all. He began asking me questions about my visit to Cairo. Given the upset of the country, I was still guarding my words very carefully so as not to endanger people who live and minister in Cairo. He began asking more pointed questions like “What do you think of this revolution?” Alarm bells were ringing in my head, so I trod very carefully as I answered. I told him that it was a very exciting time in Egypt’s history. Nothing would ever be the same for the country again. To be here during this growth period was both exhilarating and a little scary. He then asked what my friends thought of the goings on. Now, here I had to be very careful. I asked God for wisdom and told him that depended on who I spoke with. There were some who were very optimistic about the outcome, although they knew there would be a hard period to get there. Others were very pessimistic and a little fearful about what lay ahead for them. Still others were moving forward in confidence. He nodded a few times as I responded to his question, then said, “You should come to Lebanon.” I responded “I would LOVE to come to Lebanon!” So he handed me his business card and said, “E-mail me when you come.” He wrote his email address on the bottom of the card. Initially, I was wary about taking some stranger’s e-mail, but I figured I would not necessarily use it and I did not have to respond by giving him my e-mail. We stood, shook hands and parted. I noted that as he left, he entered a diplomat’s vehicle. Only then did I read his business card. It read “Mahmoud Hammoud, Lebanese Ambassador”. He’s the former Foreign Minister of Lebanon, currently serving as an ambassador. I have no idea why our paths crossed. However, God orchestrated it for some reason. There are no coincidences…just opportunities. I wonder what comes next.
articles.content_zh: 你可能已经听到有人说“没有巧合”了。 通常人们点头并含糊其辞,但真正的问题是“你相信吗?” 难道人们只是希望的思想家,还是上帝真的如此亲密地参与我们的日常生活,以至于他代表我们组织各种活动? 机会会议以后会变成什么? 种子、种植和收割的理念是贯穿整个圣经的主题。 除了分享基督希望的公开性质外, 有时我们并不认同当时的机会, 在开罗的最后一天,我坐在酒店大厅里,等待队伍的其他人下来看病。 我打开了笔记本电脑, 开始通过电子邮件去除草, 一位年长的绅士(我整个星期在不同时间见过他)过来说道:你工作太忙了。 我告诉他我只是在浪费时间 完全没有工作 他开始问我关于我访问开罗的问题。 鉴于这个国家的不安,我仍在非常谨慎地捍卫我的话,以免危及在开罗生活和担任部长的人。 他开始提出更尖锐的问题,如“你对这场革命的看法如何?” 警钟在我脑中响起,所以我回答时非常小心。 我告诉他,这是埃及历史上一个非常激动人心的时刻。 对这个国家来说,一切都不会变了 在这个成长时期来到这里既令人振奋,又有些吓人。 他接着问我的朋友们对事情的看法如何。 现在,我必须非常小心。 我向上帝求取智慧 告诉他这取决于我和谁说话 有些人对结果非常乐观,尽管他们知道要到达那里会有一段困难的时期。 其他人则非常悲观,有些担心未来会如何。 还有一些国家正在以信任的态度向前迈进。 当我回答他的问题时,他点了几次头,然后说:“你应该来黎巴嫩。” 我回应说, 他把他的名片递给我,然后说:“你来了就给我电子邮件。” 他写了他的电子邮件地址 在卡底。 起初,我对收取陌生人的电子邮件很担心,但我想我不一定会使用,我不必通过把电子邮件给他来回应。 我们站了起来,握起手来分开。 我注意到,当他离开时,他进入一名外交官的车辆。 那时我才看他的名片 原文为“黎巴嫩大使马哈穆德·哈穆德”。 现任大使。 我不知道我们为什么要过路 然而,上帝出于某种原因安排了它。 没有巧合 只是机会 不知道接下来会怎样
articles.author: R.B. Klama

articles.title: What comes first: chicken or the egg?
articles.summary: One thing I am noticing here is how different the context of ministry is from country to country. You can sometimes THINK you understand the concept of the vehicle, like...
articles.summary_zh: 我在这里注意到的一件事是，不同国家的事工背景是多么的不同。有时您可能会认为自己了解车辆的概念，例如...
articles.title_zh: 先吃鸡还是先吃鸡蛋？
articles.content: One thing I am noticing here is how different the context of ministry is from country to country. MNN's Ruth Kramer on assignment. You can sometimes THINK you understand the concept of the vehicle, like micro-enterprise, but once you hear how things are put into practice, what works and what doesn’t, you begin to see the subtleties emerge. For example, we met with a partner yesterday who assists community development. They are unashamedly Christian, because the Gospel is part of everything they do…however, they know that dealing with poverty is a ‘must’, as well. So, which came first, the chicken (community development) or the egg (Gospel)? Can they be done simultaneously and be effective? Do you really just have two eggs or two chickens? The clear answer on that was: ‘We have an egg, it becomes a chicken’. Folks, that’s the answer to the question of questions. The hope of Christ changes the outlook for the poor in this context. The other big question was how the community development works in the Egyptian Muslim context in the rural areas. It is in these places where it’s likely opposition will rise up and equate physical attacks. The mindset is quite different. Micro-enterprise comes up at this point. In some Asian countries, the structure of a micro-enterprise program works like this: church committee sees community member in need (often a believer under the discipleship of the pastor), they provide a loan so this person can start a small business–i.e.—buy a sewing machine to make clothes, or a couple of goats to make cheese and sell milk…from the profits, the person tithes to the church, enabling the support of the pastor…and the person is more able to support him/herself. However, when I asked about the structure of the micro-enterprise, it can’t work that way in the Egyptian context. There are lots of things that can really be misinterpreted within the social structure (and Islam) and this is one of them. The set up of the program is similar, but different because it’s tailor-made to fit the need of the people and the mission of the group. That just struck me. I had made an assumption that all micro-enterprise was the same. I made similar assumptions about vocational training programs, literacy programs, etc (thinking I adjusting for a different context, language, etc). I think it’s kind of a colonialistic thinking that we slip into. It’s kind of like providing someone a loaf of bread (mission field)…from the grocery store (missionary). They need the food to stay alive, but the plastic around the bread is giving them indigestion. They need to prepare the bread the way they now how and all we need to do is supply the ingredients (resources) and the recipe (training). Yes, I know you might be thinking ‘well, duh’. It is one thing to say it and to think you might even understand it, it is another thing entirely to actually see it with my own eyes, hear what works and what doesn’t from the guys implementing helps. By the way, because they do this work well, they have just come under scrutiny. One of this ministry’s main offices was raided by the Egyptian government this week, and the hard drive with the database was taken. All of their records on every program were on it. Everything is exposed. Their face is an NGO and they are well-known. With the events that have occurred in Egypt over the last month, it’s no surprise they’re looking at all NGO’s. Please pray for this team. They are careful, and they are smart. Most of all, they want to share the hope of Christ with those they encounter. That love for people permeates everything they touch…including the chickens in the coop…and eggs in the community. Works for me…
articles.content_zh: 我在这里注意到的一件事是,部委的背景因国而异。 MNN的Ruth Kramer在执行任务 你有时可以认为你理解汽车的概念, 比如微型企业, 但一旦你听到事情是如何付诸实践的, 什么可行什么不可行, 你就会开始看到微妙之处的出现。 例如,我们昨天会见了一个协助社区发展的伙伴。 他们毫不羞愧地信奉基督教, 因为福音书是他们所做的一切的一部分. 那么,什么是第一位的, 鸡(社区发展)还是蛋(Gospel)? 它们能否同时进行并有效? 你真的有两只蛋还是两只鸡? 答案是:我们有一个鸡蛋,它变成了一只鸡。 各位,这就是问题答案。 基督的希望改变了穷人在这方面的前景。 另一个大问题是社区发展如何在农村地区埃及穆斯林背景下运作。 这些地方很可能会有人反对, 心态完全不同。 此时小微企业也出现了. 在一些亚洲国家,微型企业计划的结构是这样运作的:教会委员会看到社区成员有需要(常常是牧师门徒下的信徒),他们提供贷款,以便此人能够创办小企业,即购买缝纫机来做衣服,或买一对山羊来做起司和卖牛奶. 从利润中,一个人一分之一到教堂,使牧师能够支持.这个人更有能力支持自己。 然而,当我问到微型企业的结构时,在埃及不可能如此。 在社会结构(和伊斯兰教)中, 有许多事情可以真正被误解, 节目的设置类似,但因适合人民的需要和团体的使命而有所不同. 这让我很吃惊 我假设所有微型企业都是一样的 我对职业培训计划,扫盲计划等做出了类似的假设(认为我适应不同的环境,语言等). 我认为我们滑入的是一种殖民主义思想。 像是从杂货店(Missionary)提供面包。 他们需要食物才能活下来 但面包周围的塑料 让他们消化不良 他们需要用他们现在的方式准备面包,我们需要做的就是提供原料(资源)和食谱(培训)。 是的,我知道你可能在想,“好,好” 并且认为你可能甚至能理解, 以我自己的眼光亲眼目睹, 顺便说一句,因为他们做得很好,他们刚刚受到审查。 埃及政府本周突袭了该部的一个主要办公室, 他们在每个程序上的所有记录都在上面。 一切众生被所出. 他们的外表是非政府组织,是众所周知的。 在埃及上个月发生的事件中, 请为这支队伍祈祷. 他们很小心,很聪明。 最重要的是,他们想与所遭遇的人分享基督的希望. 这种对人的爱贯穿了他们所接触的一切... 包括笼子里的鸡... 和社区的鸡蛋. 为我工作...
articles.author: R.B. Klama

articles.title: The power of prayer unleashed
articles.summary: Last night, I attended a prayer meeting at a church in downtown Cairo, near Tahrir Square. The church was gathering to cry out to God in their distress over the...
articles.summary_zh: 昨晚，我在开罗市中心解放广场附近的一个教堂参加了一次祈祷会。教会聚集在一起，在他们的痛苦中向上帝呼求……
articles.title_zh: 释放祈祷的力量
articles.content: Last night, I attended a prayer meeting at a church in downtown Cairo, near Tahrir Square. MNN in Egypt The church was gathering to cry out to God in their distress over the recent events in the country, and cry out, they did. As we sang together, worshiped together, and encouraged one another, I experienced something I have never experienced before. I’m a fairly reserved person and I am even more so in prayer. It is in times of great distress that I get out of my own way and fall before the Lord prostrate. Last night, although everyone around me was praying in Arabic, I found myself humbled before the Lord and joining in that chorus of crying out. The pastor was beyond ‘crying out’….he was screaming and sobbing before the Lord, as was much of this nearly 1,000 person gathering. Here they were, in prayer before God, confessing, repenting, requesting and rejoicing…even as tear gas seeped into the courtyard from Tahrir Square. All of a sudden, I found myself reminding God of His promises, and asking Him to give comfort to His bride in Egypt, to give them hope and wisdom and to be asking with a fierceness I had not ever before encountered…and moments later, the pastor or worship leader would be saying the same thing, or using the same verse, or introducing the song on the same topic…that happened over and over last night. An immediate confirmation of God’s response left me stunned. Much of what I have heard from Egypt’s Christians that I have encountered has been this is a year of prophecy coming true. There is a GREAT confidence in many of the church leaders and congregations in forging ahead… The other thing that we’re often hearing is that Egypt’s Church is not ‘persecuted’ so much as it is a church under pressure. The boldness of this family is so encouraging, and such a reminder of the presence of the Holy Spirit…especially as they go out with joy to tend to the wounded people coming into the field hospital set up in their courtyard. The confirmation of God’s answers to prayer gives a great boldness to those on the frontlines of the missional movement in Egypt. While bombings, riots and general chaos looks really bad in the headlines (and it is happening), fear is not the response of this emboldened Body. Church leaders we have met with all over the city have said the same thing ‘The wall of fear is broken’. Change is coming. Egypt will have her Revolution…and its face is the Church.
articles.content_zh: 昨晚,我参加了在开罗市中心的一座教堂举行的祈祷会,该教堂靠近塔里尔广场. 埃及的MNN 教会正在集会 向上帝呼喊 在他们的痛苦 最近的国内事件, 当我们一起唱歌,一起崇拜,互相鼓励时,我经历了一些我从未经历过的事情. 我是一个相当有保留的人, 是在大难之时,我走出了自己的道路,倒向了主的叩头. 昨晚,虽然我周围的每个人都用阿拉伯语祈祷,但我发现自己在主面前谦卑并加入了那场叫喊的合唱. 牧师已经超越了“哭出声来”的范围, 他们在这里向上帝祈祷,忏悔、悔改、请求并欢欣鼓舞, 突然间,我发现自己提醒了上帝他的承诺,要求他安慰他的埃及新娘,给他们以希望和智慧,并以我从未遇到过的激烈要求. . . 立即确认上帝的反应,使我感到震惊。 我从埃及基督徒那里听到的大多是今年的预言。 许多教会领袖和会众对前进充满信心... 我们经常听到的另外一件事是,埃及的教会并没有像压力下的一个教会那样被 " 迫害 " 。 这个家庭的胆量是如此鼓舞人心,如此地提醒着圣灵的存在...... 特别是当他们欢快地出门去照顾受伤的人进入他们院子里建立的野外医院时. 在埃及传教运动的前线, 虽然爆炸、暴动和普遍混乱在头条新闻上看起来非常糟糕(而且正在发生), 我们与全市的教会领袖都说过同样的话:恐惧之墙被打破了。 变化即将到来。 埃及将会有她的革命... 它的脸是教会。

articles.summary: Can you imagine sprinting as hard as you can possibly run . . . without being able to see? That’s what happens in Paralympic guide running. Blind runners compete with a guide, someone who runs alongside them step by step, connected by a short tether.
articles.summary_zh: 你能想象在看不到的情况下尽你所能地跑步吗？这就是残奥会向导跑步的方式。盲人跑步者与向导竞争，向导通过短绳一步一步地与他们并肩奔跑。

articles.title_zh: 九十五条论点是什么？
articles.content: On October 31, 1517, Martin Luther, now in his mid-thirties, made his way to the Castle Church in Wittenberg and posted his Ninety-Five Theses on the church door. Originally intended as propositions for public debate, the theses were written in Latin—the language of the scholar, not of the street. Luther could have had no idea that they would echo around Europe and become the catalyst for a spiritual revolution. Many of those who saw the papers on the Castle Church door—which seems to have served as a public notice board—would not have been able to read Latin. But soon the theses were translated into German and thereafter spread throughout Europe like wildfire—indeed, like an “act of God.” What were the Ninety-Five Theses? They were statements aimed directly at specific corruptions in the church of Luther’s day, many of them related to issues of pardon, purgatory, and the power of the pope. The first of them was particularly startling: By saying “Repent,” our Lord and Master Jesus Christ willed that the whole of the life of believers should be repentance. (Dominus et magister noster Iesus Christus dicendo “Poenitentiam agite etc.” omnem vitam fidelium poenitentiam esse voluit.) Luther had grasped that the Vulgate translation of “Repent” ( poenitentiam agite ) was open to the misinterpretation “Do penitence (or penance).” And he had also grasped a principle that John Calvin would later expound with great clarity: penitence or repentance is not the action of a moment; it is the turning around of a life—the rejection of sin effected by the gracious work of the Holy Spirit. It cannot therefore be a single act completed in a moment; it is a style of life that lasts until glory. Luther led a full and adventurous life that only an extensive biography can well describe. He was a remarkable man with enormous God-given energy. His speech was direct and plain and not infrequently earthy. He was a teacher of theology, a preacher of the gospel, and an author of some of the most important books in the Reformation period. Notable among his early publications was his On the Babylonian Captivity of the Church , which exposed the church’s failures, while in On the Freedom of a Christian he explained how in Jesus Christ believers are set free both to love God and to serve their neighbor. Thus he wrote in a beautifully crafted sentence that captures the paradox of the gospel-centered life: “A Christian man is the most free lord of all, and subject to none; a Christian man is the most dutiful servant of all, and subject to everyone.” By his preaching, by writing, and especially by his influence in the explanation of salvation by grace through faith in Christ, Luther was used by God to transform the Christian church. The leading Reformers in England and Scotland were influenced by his writings, often smuggled in by merchant sailors. In Scotland in particular, the martyrs of St. Andrews, Patrick Hamilton and George Wishart (whose bodyguard John Knox had been), were disciples of Luther’s teaching. Likewise in England, the heroic William Tyndale left a legacy not only in his English translation of the Bible but in an entire body of literature that echoed the German Reformer’s work. But what did Luther teach? His chief emphases are aptly summarized in the well-known Reformation solas: (1) sola Scriptura : we come to know God through Scripture alone, not through the traditions of the church as such; (2) sola gratia : we come to receive forgiveness by God’s grace alone, not because we are able to earn merit; (3) sola fide: we receive justification by faith alone, and not by faith plus something else; (4) solus Christus : all of God’s riches are given to us in Christ alone; (5) soli Deo gloria: the goal of all of life is the glory of God alone. These principles simply underlined the emphases Luther found in Scripture. But in context, what is most significant about them is not only what they stressed but what they bypassed. articles.content_zh: 1517年10月31日,现在已30多岁的马丁·路德(Martin Luther)前往维滕贝格的城堡教堂并把他的"九十五部曲"张贴到教堂门上. 这些论文最初是打算作为公众辩论的命题,是用拉丁文写的——学者的语言,而不是街上的语言。 路德根本不知道他们会在欧洲周围呼应,成为精神革命的催化剂. 许多人在城堡教堂门上看到报纸, 但很快,这些论文被翻译成德文,然后像野火一样传遍了欧洲,事实上,就像“上帝的行为 ” 。 "九五传"是什么? 这些言论直接针对路德节教堂的具体腐败,其中许多涉及赦免、炼狱和教宗权力等问题。 其中第一个特别令人吃惊:我们的主和耶稣基督大师说“忏悔”,希望信士们的一生都能悔过。 (Dominus et magister noster Iesus Christus dicendo “Poenitentiam angite等”。 Poenitiam intentium sese voluit。) 路德已经明白,“悔改”的Vulgate译文(poenitentiam angite)对“悔改(或忏悔)”的错误解释持开放态度。 他还理解了约翰·卡尔文后来将非常明确地阐明的原则:忏悔或忏悔不是一瞬间的行动;而是生命的转折——圣灵的慷慨工作对罪恶的拒绝。 因此,它不能是一个在一瞬间完成的单一行为;它是一种直到荣耀的生活方式。 路德过着充实而冒险的生活,只有广泛的传记才能很好地描述. 他是一个了不起的人 拥有巨大的上帝赐予的能量。 他的演讲是直截了当的,而且并非经常是土生土长的。 曾任神学教师,"福音"传道人等职,并出自"改革时期一些最重要的著作". 在他早期的著作中,著名的是他的《关于教会的巴比伦式控制》,该书揭露了教会的失败,而在《基督教自由》中,他解释了耶稣基督信徒如何获得自由,既爱上帝,又为邻居服务。 因此,他用一个精心设计的句子写道:“一个基督教徒是所有人中最自由的领主,不受任何人支配;一个基督教徒是所有人中最忠诚的仆人,服从每一个人。” 通过他的传道,写作,特别是他通过对基督的信仰,对恩典解释救赎的影响,路德被上帝用来改造基督教会. 英格兰和苏格兰的主要改革者受到他所著作的影响,经常被商船水手偷运入去. 特别是在苏格兰,圣安德鲁斯,帕特里克·汉密尔顿和乔治·怀克特(他的保镖约翰·诺克斯曾是)的烈士是路德教的门徒. 同样,在英国,英勇的威廉·廷达勒不仅在圣经的英文译本中留下了遗产,而且在与德国改革者著作相呼应的整个文献中也留下了遗产. 但路德教的是什么? 他的主要重心在著名的"改革"(Reformation solas)中得到了恰当的总结:(1) sola Scriptura:我们通过《圣经》,而不是通过教会的传统来了解上帝;(2) sola 惠给:我们通过上帝的恩惠来获得宽恕,而不是因为我们能够获得功绩;(3)  sola 敬畏:我们通过信仰获得理由,而不是信仰获得其他的东西;(4) Solus Christus:神的所有财富都只由基督给予我们;(5) Soli Deo Gloria:所有生命的目标都是上帝的光荣. 这些原则只是强调《圣经》中路德的强调。 但就背景而言,它们最重要的不仅是它们强调的内容,而且是它们所绕过的内容。 无论是路德还是其他的弹匣

articles.title_zh: 退休人员为教会服务的5种方式
articles.content: “Retirement at last! Now I can sleep as late as I want to. Now I get to do nothing all day.” Such is a popular description of how retirement looks to many people. I know some who would even add, “Now I get to play golf every day.” Obviously, this does not reflect the Christian perspective of someone who understands that his chief end is “to glorify God and enjoy Him forever” (see Westminster Shorter Catechism 1; 1 Cor. 10:31; Rom. 11:36). This is not to say that sleeping later and playing golf are anti-Christian. However, there are some significant ways that retirees can still serve the church. 1. Be a volunteer. Retirees have valuable practical and professional experience that can be used in service to others. For example, some of you may have skill sets and expertise that enable you to erect a building or a cabin at a camp from the ground up in very little time. One organization I’m familiar with travels to camps and other locations, bringing their own living accommodations, tools, and know-how to be a blessing to other ministries. Some may volunteer in maintenance of a church’s lawns and gardens to keep them looking tidy. Volunteers can save churches and various ministries a great deal of money and provide much encouragement to them. The church where I attend has many volunteers (both retired and pre-retired) who help at the annual church youth camps. They serve in the kitchen and dining hall, as cabin staff and counselors, as camp nurses and in technical positions, and pay their own way to camp. While not everyone can serve in such physical ways, everyone can volunteer in some way according to their abilities and gifts: “As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another . . . in order that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ” (1 Peter 4:10–11). 2. Show the younger generations a model of an older person who still walks with the Lord. The youth in our churches need models of older believers who are faithful in their daily walk with the Lord. What might this example look like? We can show that we have not waned in faithfulness in our older years, that we are active and unashamed to belong to God’s people, and that we continue to radiate joy in our relationship with the Lord. We can model what it looks like to have no hesitation to speak about Christ in the doctor’s office, store, or when traveling, and that we are not reluctant to share Scripture with other people. Paul wrote to the saints in Philippi: “Brothers, join in imitating me, and keep your eyes on those who walk according to the example you have in us” (Phil. 3:17). Note these words from the psalmist: O God, from my youth you have taught me, and I still proclaim your wondrous deeds. So even to old age and gray hairs, O God, do not forsake me, until I proclaim your might to another generation. (Ps. 71:17–18) 3. Regularly attend worship services and wholeheartedly participate. Not only should retirees maintain a faithful walk with the Lord, but they ought to remain consistent in their attendance at the regular worship services of the church. It is a testament to the Lord’s faithfulness when they are seen in the pews, not just taking up space or putting in their time, but wholeheartedly and enthusiastically singing, listening, and note-taking. This is important because it seems that many young people today view church as optional rather than a joyful habit. Granted, this should begin with the influence of godly parents, but it is reinforced and aided when the testimony of the older generation displays undiminished love for corporate worship, viewing it not as drudgery but delight. Hebrews 10:23–25 instructs us in this way: Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who promised is faithful. And let us consider how to stir up one another to love and good works, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day drawing near. 4. Teach or assist thos
articles.content_zh: “终于退休了! 瞷и何眔边 现在我整天什么都不做。” 这是许多人对退休的看法的流行描述。 我知道有些人甚至会说,“现在我每天都要打高尔夫。” 显然,这并没有反映基督教的观点,即有人理解,他的主要目的就是“颂扬上帝,永远享受他”(见Westminster Shorter Catechism 1; 1 Cor. 10:31; Rom. 11:36)。 这不是说睡觉后打高尔夫是反基督教的。 然而,退休人员仍然可以有一些重要的方式为教会服务. 1. 志愿工作。 退休人员具有宝贵的实践和专业经验,可用于为他人服务. 例如,你们中有些人可能拥有技能和专门知识,能够在极短的时间内从地上建起一座建筑物或一个小木屋。 我熟悉一个组织前往营地及其他地点, 有些人会自愿维护教堂的草坪和花园, 志愿者可以挽救教会和各部一大笔钱,并为它们提供很大的鼓励. 我所在的教堂有许多志愿者(既有退休的,也有退休前的),他们在每年的教堂青年营中提供帮助. 他们在厨房和餐厅服务,担任木屋工作人员和咨询员,担任营地护士和技术职务,并支付自己去营地的方式。 虽然并非每个人都能以这样的身体方式服务,但每个人都能根据自己的能力和天赋以某种方式自愿: " 由于每个人都收到礼物,利用礼物互相服务,以使上帝在一切事情上都能被耶稣基督所赞美" (1 Peter 4:10-11). 2. 向年轻一代展示仍然与主同道的老年人的模范. 我们教会中的青年需要老信徒的模范,他们在每天与上帝一起行走时是忠实的。 这个例子会是什么样子? 我们可以表明,我们年事已高,在忠诚中并不衰弱,我们积极而且毫不羞愧地属于上帝的子民,而且我们继续在与上帝的关系中放出欢乐。 我们可以在医生的办公室、商店或旅行时, 以毫不犹豫的方式谈论基督, 保罗在Philippi给圣徒们写了一封信:“兄弟们,一起模仿我,并注意那些按照你们在我们身上的榜样行走的人”(Phil. 3:17)。 请注意,这些话来自诗人:上帝啊,你从我的青春中教我的,我仍然宣布你的奇事。 所以,上帝啊,即使老去和灰发,也不要抛弃我,直到我向另一代人宣告你的力量。 3. 定期参加礼拜仪式并全心全意地参加。 退休人员不仅应当与主保持忠实的行走,而且他们应当始终如一地参加教会的定期礼拜服务. 这证明了上帝的忠诚,当人们看到他们出现在树上时,他们不仅占据了空间或投入了时间,而且全心全意地歌唱、聆听和记事。 这一点很重要,因为今天许多年轻人似乎将教堂视为可选的习惯,而不是令人高兴的习惯. 当然,这应该从上帝父母的影响入手,但是当年长者的证词显示对企业崇拜的爱不减时,它得到了加强和帮助,认为它不是劳累,而是快乐。 希伯来人10:23-25这样教导我们:让我们不动摇地坚持我们的希望的忏悔,因为承诺的人是忠实的。 让我们考虑一下如何相互激起爱和善行,而不是像有些人的习惯那样忽视相会,而是相互鼓励,正如你们看到的日子临近的时候一样。 4. 教育或援助托斯人

articles.title_zh: 这五个唯独对今天的教会仍然重要吗？
articles.content: The five solas (Latin for “alone”) of the Reformation—Scripture alone, grace alone, faith alone, Christ alone, to the glory of God alone—are indispensable for the church in any era. They will always be relevant because they summarize the biblical gospel, which is the church’s lifeblood in every age. They are particularly significant today because even professing evangelicals, to say nothing of the culture around us, are being tempted to abandon the gospel. Therefore, the church must recognize the dire need of not only defending the five solas but also celebrating them. The five solas are important for us today for at least three reasons. 1. The five solas set apart the true gospel from every other religion, worldview, or philosophy. Every day, the world calls out its siren song of spiritual compromise. Satan loves to negotiate the nonnegotiables of biblical truth. He whispers the lie that we don’t need to have strong convictions about the Bible as our only standard of truth or hold firm to the teaching that only those who trust Christ alone for salvation are right with God. The temptation to downplay doctrine is unceasing. A winsome but unyielding grasp of the five solas can help us resist these attractive lies. 2. The five solas provide us with unspeakable comfort in a chaotic world. The pace of modern life is unsustainable. It colors our understanding of “the normal Christian life.” We tend to equate busyness in ministry with productiveness for Jesus. But the two must not be confused. Knowing that we are saved by God’s grace alone through faith alone gives us rest from an exhausting world. We leave behind a performance mindset in our relationship with God and embrace a life of trusting, resting grace. Safe in the arms of our Savior, we are set free to let go of trying to earn what God freely gives us—Christ Himself. 3. The five solas remind us that our salvation is secure. Only when we are assured of the love of God will we live out the commands of God. The five solas enable us to say with David, “Oh how I love your law! It is my meditation all the day” (Ps. 119:97). Following Jesus, obeying Him by the Spirit, and killing sin become our joy. So many Christians drift, unconsciously most of the time, to the belief that God loves them when they obey. But the true gospel of the five solas pulls us back to the bedrock scriptural truth that God loves us and therefore we obey. The difference is subtle, but it makes all the difference in our daily lives. Your Father loves you! He is pleased with you in Christ. When those realities come home, John’s words become our delightful creed: “For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments. And his commandments are not burdensome” (1 John 5:3). In sum, nothing is more urgent for the church than protecting, propagating, and passing on the true gospel encapsulated by the five solas . It is our only hope, our greatest comfort, and our supreme joy. Most of all, these biblical teachings will always be important because they bring us to Christ, who is our life. 1 Footnotes Editor's Note: This article was originally published January 19, 2022. ↩
articles.content_zh: 改革的五所索拉斯(拉丁语为“单独”)——光是文字、光是恩典、光是信仰、光是基督、光是上帝的光荣——在任何时代,对教会都是不可或缺的。 因为他们总结了圣经福音, 它们今天特别重要,因为甚至宣称福音派教徒 -- -- 更不用说我们周围的文化 -- -- 被诱惑放弃福音。 因此,教会必须认识到,不仅迫切需要捍卫五个独奏会,而且迫切需要庆祝它们。 五个索拉斯今天对我们很重要,至少有三个原因。 1. 这五所索拉斯将真正的福音与所有其他宗教、世界观或哲学分开。 世界每天都在呼唤着它的精神妥协之歌。 撒旦喜欢商议圣经中不可谈判的真理. 他低语地说,我们不需要对《圣经》作为我们唯一的真理标准抱有坚定的信念,也不要坚持这样的教导,即只有那些只相信基督的人才能与上帝同在。 轻描淡写理论的诱惑是不停的。 能够帮助我们抵制这些有吸引力的谎言。 2. 在一个混乱的世界中,这五相声给我们带来了难以形容的安慰。 现代生活的步伐是不可持续的。 它体现了我们对“正常的基督教生活”的理解。 我们往往把部长的繁忙与耶稣的生产力等同起来。 但两者不可混淆. 仅凭信仰,我们就能从一个疲惫的世界中安息。 在与上帝的关系中,我们留下了一种表现的心态,并拥抱一种信任和安息的恩典的生活。 在我们的救世主的怀抱中,我们被放任去试图获得上帝给我们的自由——基督。 3. 五相声提醒我们,我们的救赎是安全的。 只有当我们得到上帝的爱的保证时,我们才会遵守上帝的命令。 这五相相声使我们能够和大卫说:“我多么爱你的律法! 我一整天都在冥想”(临119:97)。 顺从耶稣,顺从他的精神,杀戮罪孽成为了我们的喜悦. 如此多的基督徒在无意识中大部分时间漂移到相信上帝在他们服从时爱他们. 但是,五相声的真正福音让我们回到上帝爱我们,因此我们服从的基础性文字真理. 区别是微妙的,但它使我们日常生活中的一切不同。 你父亲爱你! 他在基督里对你感到高兴 当这些现实回到故乡时,约翰的话成了我们令人愉快的信念:“这是上帝的爱,我们遵守他的戒律。 他的戒律不是累赘的"(1 John 5:3). 总而言之,对教会来说,最紧迫的莫过于保护、宣传、传递由五所索拉斯所封印的真正福音。 这是我们唯一的希望,我们最大的慰藉,和我们最大的快乐。 最重要的是,这些圣经教义将永远是重要的,因为它们把我们带到基督那里,而基督是我们的生命. 1 脚注编辑注:本文章最初于2022年1月19日发表. .

articles.title_zh: 黑暗之后，光明
articles.content: In the old city of Geneva, Switzerland, there is a large park on the grounds of the University of Geneva that commemorates the Reformation. That park is adorned with a huge wall, called the International Monument to the Reformation or simply the Reformation Wall. In statues and bas-reliefs, the wall depicts figures from the Reformation including John Calvin, John Knox, William Farel, and Theodore Beza. Surrounding these and other statues, the motto of the Reformation is inscribed on each side: post tenebras lux —after darkness, light. This phrase refers not only to the unveiling and liberation of the Scriptures—which were made available to the common people during the Reformation—but also to the loss and recovery of the most important biblical doctrine there is: the doctrine of justification by faith alone. This was the primary and central issue of the Protestant Reformation. During the dispute between the Protestants and the Roman Catholics, both sides saw that justification was so important that no compromise was possible. Both sides were convinced that what was at stake in the doctrine of justification was the very essence of the biblical gospel. When the gospel is at stake, everything is at stake, because the gospel tells us how we can be right with God. In Galatians 1:6–9, Paul writes about the importance of getting the gospel right: I am astonished that you are so quickly deserting him who called you in the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel—not that there is another one, but there are some who trouble you and want to distort the gospel of Christ. But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach to you a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be accursed. As we have said before, so now I say again: If anyone is preaching to you a gospel contrary to the one you received, let him be accursed. This Apostle was a man who was constantly extolling the virtues of patience, gentleness, meekness, charity, and tolerance; who, conversely, constantly rebuked the sins of contentiousness, divisiveness, quarrelsome spirits, belligerence, and so on. This man said that we ought to strive as much as we possibly can to live at peace with all men; he was known as the Apostle of peace and unity. Yet suddenly he came to a point over a doctrine where he said, “There can be no toleration here. To tolerate the distortion of the gospel into another gospel is to tolerate the intolerable.” The first thing that Paul did was express his amazement—not that the people had left the gospel that he had preached to them, but that they had done it so quickly. He was hardly gone from their midst before they wanted to listen to the teachings of the Judaizers, who insisted that one cannot be saved by faith in Christ alone but must also have good works and obedience to the law in order to be saved. This “other gospel” was no gospel at all—there is only one gospel, the gospel of God, revealed in and through Christ and proclaimed and expounded by the Apostles. The stakes are so high when it comes to this point that Paul pronounced a curse on anyone who teaches otherwise. The Greek work translated “accursed” is anathema —damned. The Apostle understood that the issue of justification was no mere academic issue, but one that touches every person’s life ultimately. It can be summed up in one question: How are we saved? It is a life-and-death matter, an eternal life matter. The New Testament makes it clear that each of us will be called into account before God, and that God is righteous while we’re not. The doctrine of justification addresses the solution to that problem, declaring how we, as unjust people, can be reconciled to a just and holy God. So if there’s anything in the essence of the Christian faith, of the good news of the gospel, it’s this doctrine. Martin Luther, building on Paul’s assessment, called the doctrine of justification the article on which the church stands or falls. Luther understood that theology is syste
articles.content_zh: 在瑞士日内瓦老城区,日内瓦大学地上有一座大型公园来纪念"改革". 那个公园的装饰有一堵巨大的墙,被称作"改革国际纪念碑"或"改革墙". 在雕像和堡垒救济中,墙上描绘了来自改革派的人物,包括约翰·卡尔文,约翰·诺克斯,威廉·法雷尔和西奥多·贝扎. 围绕这些和其他雕像,"改革"的座右铭被刻在了每一边:后倒行奢侈——在黑暗后,光辉. 这一短语不仅指《圣经》的揭幕和解放(在改革期间提供给普通人民),而且还指最重要的圣经学说 -- -- 仅以信仰为理由的学说 -- -- 的丧失和复苏。 这是新教改革的首要和核心问题。 在新教徒和罗马天主教徒之间的纠纷中,双方认为这种辩解非常重要,不可能妥协. 双方都相信,辩护理论的关键在于圣经福音的精髓。 当福音受到威胁时,一切都处于危险之中,因为福音告诉我们,我们如何能够与上帝对齐。 在加拉提亚1:6-9中,保罗写道正确福音的重要性:我感到惊讶的是,你如此快地抛弃了以基督之恩召唤你并转向另一个福音的人,而不是另一个福音,但有些人烦恼你并想歪曲基督的福音。 即使我们或从天上降下的天神,为你们传福音,与我们所传教你们的福音相悖,教他受诅咒。 正如我们以前说过的,现在我再说一遍: 如果有人向你们宣扬与你们所接受的福音相悖的福音,你们就应当诅咒他。 这名使徒是一个不断赞颂耐心、温和、温柔、慈善和宽容等美德的人;相反,他不断斥责争议、分裂、争吵、好战等罪恶。 这位先生说,我们应该尽我们所能地同所有人和平相处;他被称为和平与团结的使者。 然而,他突然想到一个理论,他说,“在这里是不能容忍的。 容忍将福音歪曲为又一福音就是容忍不能容忍的福音。” 保罗做的第一件事是表达他的惊叹——不是说人民已经离开了他向他们所宣扬的福音,而是他们如此快地做到了. 在他们想听犹太教的教义之前,他几乎没有离开他们中间,犹太教坚持一个人不能只靠信仰基督而得到救赎,为了得到救赎,他还必须有善行并服从法律. 这种 " 其他福音 " 根本不是福音 -- -- 只有一种福音,即上帝的福音,在基督中和通过基督揭示,并由使徒们宣布和阐述。 此时此刻,利害攸关,以致于保罗对教别的人发出诅咒. 希腊翻译的作品“被诅咒了”是令人厌恶的。 使徒们明白,理由问题不仅仅是学术问题,而是一个最终触及每个人生活的问题。 它可以概括为一个问题:我们如何得到拯救? 这是生死攸关的 永生攸关的 《新约》明确指出,在上帝面前,我们每一个人都将受到重视,上帝是善良的,而我们不是正义的。 辩解的理论涉及这个问题的解决,宣布我们作为不公正的人民如何能够与一个公正和神圣的上帝相协调。 因此,如果有基督教信仰的本质,福音的好消息,那就是这个学说。 马丁·路德(Martin Luther)根据保罗的评估,称教会所立足或倒下的文章为辩解理论. 路德知道神学是循环的

articles.summary_zh: 西奥多·贝扎（ Theodore Beza ）今天在福音派世界中是一个陌生的人物。他受到许多历史学家和神学家的诽谤，他们创造了一个严肃的人的形象，他将加尔文的神学变成了一个干旱的学术体系。这张照片实际上与事实相去甚远。那么西奥多·贝扎到底是谁？他于1519年出生于法国韦泽莱，是一个富裕的法国小贵族家庭。他的一生几乎跨越了整个十六世纪，他于1605年去世，享年八十多岁。
articles.title_zh: 西奥多·贝扎是谁？
articles.content: Theodore Beza is an unfamiliar figure today in the evangelical world. He has been much maligned by many historians and theologians who created the image of an austere man who turned Calvin’s theology into an arid scholastic system. This image is actually very far from the truth. So who was Theodore Beza really? He was born in Vézelay, France, in 1519 in an affluent family of the minor French nobility. His life spanned almost the whole sixteenth century, and he died in 1605 at the age of eighty-six. By God’s providence, there were two clear turning points in his life. The first occurred at the age of nine when he was placed as a lodger with a Lutheran scholar, Melchior Wolmar, who became his preceptor. He spent seven years with Wolmar, who taught him law, Latin, and Greek. Interestingly, one of Wolmar’s other students during that time was none other than Calvin, who was just ten years older than Beza. Wolmar gave Beza a first-rate education, and, like Calvin, Beza was likely more fluent in Latin than in French. More importantly, Wolmar was instrumental in his journey toward the new Reformed faith. It was through Wolmar that, sometime around 1535, Beza read a book by the Swiss Reformer Heinrich Bullinger and was converted. Years later, Beza wrote to Bullinger: “You made known to me true piety, and its purest source: The Word of God.” 1 However, Beza had a lot to lose if he disclosed his newfound faith. He received substantial ecclesiastical incomes through one of his uncles, who was an abbot, and this allowed him to enjoy a life of pleasure in Paris, dedicating himself to poetry and humanistic studies. For several years, he kept his faith secret, and he secretly married Claudine Denosse, the daughter of a Parisian Protestant merchant. Beza promised he would marry her publicly whenever they could find a truly Reformed church. The second turning point of his life came in 1548 when he contracted the plague and came close to death. He took it as a clear warning from God and came out openly about his faith. Shortly after, he fled to Geneva. Theodore and Claudine were publicly married by Calvin himself, and they remained devoted to each other and to the cause of Christ until Claudine’s death in 1588. After teaching Greek in Lausanne for a few years, Beza settled in Geneva permanently in 1558, mainly because of his admiration for Calvin. He lived there until his death, faithfully serving alongside Calvin and assuming his mantle as leader of the French Reformed church after Calvin’s death in 1564. Beza’s legacy is immense and multifaceted, and it is difficult to summarize it in a few words. He was first and foremost a man of letters. One of his first tasks in Geneva was to complete the translation of the Psalms from Hebrew into French for the Huguenot psalter, a translation left unfinished by another Reformed poet at his death. Beza also published a critical edition of the Greek New Testament that was influential on the Textus Receptus, from which the King James Bible was translated. In fact, the 1565 edition was dedicated to Queen Elizabeth I. In many ways, this was Beza’s lifetime project. He tirelessly corrected and improved the text and published several editions, with the last major revision appearing in 1598. In 1559, he published a “Confession of the Christian Faith,” addressed to his father, to explain why he had embraced the Reformed faith. Although it was penned in a few days, it was hugely popular, as it was published at least thirty-five times during his lifetime and translated into Latin, English, German, and Dutch. He consolidated Calvin’s legacy in Geneva by preaching regularly and teaching theology for forty years. We know from several sources that his teaching was greatly appreciated. For example, an alumnus wrote in 1578: We listened to you with so much admiration and pleasure. Apart from your own personality traits, you combined Melanchthon’s penetrating insights, Calvin’s solid and direct common sense, and Vermigli’s
articles.content_zh: 西奥多·贝扎是今天福音世界中不熟悉的人物. 他深受许多历史学家和神学家的污蔑,他们创造了一个把加尔文神学变成干旱学术体系的紧缩人的形象。 这个形象实际上与事实相去甚远. 谁是西奥多·贝萨? 他于1519年生于法国韦泽莱的一个小法国贵族富裕家庭. 他的生平几乎跨越了整个16世纪,他于1605年以86岁之多去世. 上帝保佑,他的人生有两个明显的转折点。 第一个发生在9岁时,他被安置在路德会学者梅尔奇奥尔·沃尔马尔(Melchior Wolmar)的住处,他成为他的受体. 他与沃尔玛共事了七年,沃尔玛教他法律,拉丁语,希腊语. 有趣的是,当时沃尔玛的其他学生中只有一个是加尔文,他刚刚比贝扎大了十多岁. 沃尔玛给予贝扎一流的教育,而同加尔文一样,贝扎在拉丁语中可能比法语更流利. 更重要的是,沃尔玛在走向新的改革后信仰的旅程中起到了推动作用. 正是通过沃尔玛,在1535年左右的某个时候,贝扎阅读了由瑞士改革者海因里希·布林格所著的一出书并被皈依. 多年后,贝扎写信给布林格:"你让我知道真正的虔诚,以及它最纯洁的来源:上帝之道". 1 然而,贝扎如果透露出他新发现的信仰,就会损失很多. 他通过他的一位叔父获得了大量的教会收入,他是一位方丈,这使得他能够在巴黎享受快乐的生活,专心于诗歌和人文研究. 几年来,他保守了信仰的秘密,他秘密地嫁给了一位巴黎新教商人的女儿克洛丁·德诺塞. 贝扎答应他只要找到真正改革的教堂 就会公开娶她 他生命的第二个转折点是1548年他感染了瘟疫并接近死亡. 他认为这是从真主发出的明确的警告,并且公开地阐明他的信仰。 不久,他逃到日内瓦. 西奥多和克洛丁由加尔文本人公开出嫁,两人始终致力于彼此和基督的事业,直到克洛丁于1588年去世. 在洛桑教希腊语几年后,贝扎于1558年在日内瓦永久定居,这主要是因为他对加尔文的钦佩. 他在那里一直活到去世,忠实地与加尔文并肩服役,并在加尔文于1564年去世后担任法国改革会会长. 贝萨的遗产是巨大的和多方面的,很难用几句话概括一下。 他最先是写信的人 他在日内瓦的最初任务之一是完成将"诗经"从希伯来语翻译成法语,为"胡盖诺特诗人"(Huguenot psalter)所翻译,这是另一位改革诗人死后留下的未完成的译作. 贝扎还出版了"希腊新约"的批判版,该版对"特特鲁斯受体"有影响,从中翻译出"国王詹姆斯圣经". 事实上,1565年版是献给伊丽莎白一世女王. 在很多方面,这是贝扎的一生项目. 他不懈地纠正并改进了文本,并出版了多本版本,最后一出重大修订于1598年. 1559年,他发表了一份致其父亲的“基督教信仰的承认”,以解释他为什么接受改革后的信仰。 虽然短短几天就被收录了,但极受欢迎,因为在他的生平中至少出版了35次并被翻译成了拉丁语,英语,德语和荷兰语. 他通过定期传教和教授神学四十年,巩固了加尔文在日内瓦的遗产. 我们从几个来源知道,他的教学受到极大的赞赏。 例如,一位校友在1578年写道:我们非常钦佩和愉快地聆听了你们的发言. 除了你自己的个性特征,你结合了梅兰希通的洞察力,加尔文的坚实而直接的常识,和弗米利的常识.

articles.content: Kirk Franklin did not walk through The Jennifer Hudson Show’s spirit tunnel. He worked it. The Jennifer Hudson Show posted the walk to Instagram with one caption: “Show off those moves @kirkfranklin!” View this post on Instagram A post shared by The Jennifer Hudson Show (@jenniferhudsonshow) He was there to promote his new album, I Am What I Am , which comes out Friday, Oct. 30. It’s his 14th solo album, and he’s a 20-time Grammy winner. His song with Karen Clark Sheard, “Thank You For Everything,” is already out. It made its live TV debut at the 41st Stellar Gospel Music Awards. At a listening party in Atlanta on Oct. 12, according to Hot 100.9, Franklin said, “I’ve never done a double album before.” He described the TobyMac collaboration “It Gets Better” as “my attempt to find a space to talk about mental health,” and added, “I’ve had my own journey with anxiety and depression.” He also talked about changes in the Black church. “The Black church culture changed,” he said. “The church got rid of their choirs and the music was in a space that was not my strength.” He had advice for emerging artists, too. “Start off very true and build your audience slow,” he said. “Don’t ride the trends because you don’t know when they’re coming.”

articles.title_zh: 马刺新秀Tarris Reed Jr.受洗： “我从不想与主无关，到现在渴望为他而活”
articles.content: San Antonio Spurs rookie Tarris Reed Jr. got baptized days after making his NBA debut, and he posted the video to Instagram under two words: “Jesus Saves.” Reed, a 23-year-old center, was the No. 26 pick in this year’s draft out of UConn. Denver took him, and San Antonio acquired him in a trade. He debuted on Tuesday, Oct. 20, in a 116-104 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder. In the caption, Reed wrote that he got home late after his first NBA back-to-back and “got my first real glimpse of just how grueling the 82-game NBA season can be.” On the plane ride, he remembered it was Baptism Sunday at his church. “I texted Pastor Ed, and the rest was history LOL.” “It’s been on my heart for a while now to be baptized,” Reed wrote. “I wanted to publicly signify my union with Christ and what it means to walk in His grace, mercy, and NEWNESS OF LIFE!” He quoted Romans 6:4: “We were therefore buried with him through baptism into death in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may live a new life.” He also wrote about what he sees coming next. “The Lord has placed me in a unique position to help others come to know Christ and experience His life changing power,” he wrote. “To think that I went from wanting nothing to do with the Lord to now desiring to live for Him is something I never could have imagined. I never would have thought my life would look like this.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by TRJ (@iamtarrisreed) Reed is a St. Louis native who started his college career at Michigan, transferred to UConn after his sophomore year and was the Big East Sixth Man of the Year as a junior. In April, UConn lost the national title game to Michigan, and Reed went to Instagram afterward. “I’ve been wrestling with God about this all day” , he wrote in a post that week. “Losing the biggest game of my entire basketball career hurts,” he said. “I tend to be a perfectionist, but only Jesus was perfect.” He wrote that he felt Jesus put it on his heart to go to an Athletes in Action meeting and speak, even though he didn’t want to. He barely had time to prepare, so he told himself he would let the Holy Spirit speak through him. “That night, two of the women’s basketball players got baptized,” he wrote. “It’s not my will, it’s His.” His October post ended with “All glory to God!”
articles.content_zh: 圣安东尼奥·斯普斯新手塔里斯·里德(英语:San Antonio Spurs newers Tarris Reed Jr.)在做了他的NBA出道后几天被洗礼,他把视频贴到Instagram上,上面有两个词:“耶稣拯救了”. Reed是一个23岁的中心, 是今年UCON的26号选手。 丹佛把他带走了,圣安东尼奥在一次交易中收购了他. 他在10月20日星期二以116-104输给俄克拉荷马城雷霆的比赛中出道. 在标题中,里德写道,他在第一次NBA后背后回家很晚,并“第一次真正地看到82赛事NBA赛季的惨痛情况。” 在飞机上,他记得那是他教堂的洗礼周日. 我给Ed牧师发了短信, Reed写道, “我心中已经有一段时间要受洗了。 “我想公开表示我与基督的结合, 他引用了罗马人6:4:“因此,我们通过受洗被埋葬而与他同葬于死地,以便像基督通过父的荣耀从死地复活一样,我们也能够过上新的生活。” 他还写了自己接下来所看到的 他写道,“上帝使我处于独特的地位,帮助他人了解基督并体验他改变生活的力量。” “认为我从不想与上帝有任何关系到现在渴望为他而活,是我无法想象的。 我从来没有想过我的生活会是这样的。” 在由TRJ(@iamtarrisreed)分享的Instagram A上查看这篇文章, Reed是一位圣路易斯本地人,在密歇根州开始了大学生涯,他大二后转到了UCON,并且是当年的"大东方第六人",当年是少年. 4月,UConn输给密歇根州的国名赛事,里德继而出战Instagram. 他在文章中写道, 他说,“失去我整个篮球生涯中最大的一场比赛是痛苦的。” “我往往是一个完美主义者,但只有耶稣是完美的。” 他写道,他觉得耶稣是用心去参加Athletes行动会议并讲话的,尽管他不愿意。 他几乎没有时间准备,于是他告诉自己,他会让圣灵通过他说话. " 那天晚上,两名女子篮球运动员受了洗礼, " 他写道: “这不是我的意志,而是他的意志。” 他的"十月"文章以"上帝的光荣!

articles.title_zh: 点菜（ 10月27日）
articles.content: Good morning from somewhere in rural Colorado. I’m here for the next few days for meetings and training, as well as a bit of hiking and photography and, best of all, some quiet times of writing. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include O. Palmer Robertson’s two-part Christ of the Consummation , which was commended by, among others, D.A. Carson, Sinclair Ferguson, and Joel Beeke. You’ll also find lots of great deals from Zondervan from books that are related to Protestant theology. Recommended Reading Can a Christian Be Demon-Possessed? I know there are many people who are concerned that, even though they are Christians, they may still be possessed by demons. Anthony Faggiano explains why that is not a legitimate fear. “Desire entices us; yielding gives birth to sin; sin grows toward death. Satan can tempt us, but we remain responsible for our desires and decisions. We cannot blame an indwelling demon for what Scripture traces to our sinful hearts. Yet God hasn’t left believers powerless. Through his Holy Spirit, we can begin to put sin to death and walk in obedience.” 7 Keys for Thriving in Lifelong Ministry. I enjoyed reading Joel Beeke’s keys for thriving in pastoral ministry. “Looking back over my ministry over the long term is much more encouraging than looking at it in the short term. A long-term perspective helps me see those who have been saved by the Spirit through my sermons, those marriages that have been strengthened, and even the fruitfulness of elders and deacons who were unsaved when I arrived at my church 40 years ago but have since come to know the Lord personally, vibrantly, and experientially.” Why Does Everyone Else’s Life Seem Better Than Mine? There are some good insights in Zachary Conover’s article on comparison and envy. “Comparison has a way of making us dissatisfied with things we once received with gratitude. We can be thankful for our homes, our families, our work, and the opportunities God has given us. But then we see someone else’s life. We scroll through reel after reel, and suddenly our own begins to feel inadequate. Their opportunities seem greater. Their accomplishments seem more significant. Their circumstances seem more desirable. Am I the only one who doesn’t have it all together? Why don’t I have what they have? And without realizing it, we begin to measure the goodness of God toward us against what He has given to someone else.” Put the Destination in the Frame. John Seel has a guest piece on Aaron Renn’s Substack that offers some helpful points on the way we talk about young men. “We are talking about men incorrectly. We frame discussions of men in terms of problems – the ‘crisis of boys and men’ or ‘failure to launch’ – rather than the destination we want men to arrive at. If we want a different outcome, we need to change the frame of our discussions about men to center on the new reality we want to create. We need a frame that naturally leads us to answer the key question: What kind of men do we want our boys to become?” Welcome to the Valley of Pain. This article from The Atlantic points out, correctly, that the “safe internet” is shrinking and that we need to be more vigilant than ever. “For the next year or two, if not longer, the internet is going to feel a bit touch and go, and more dangerous than we’ve come to expect. ‘It’s going to feel like the sky is falling’ for a while, Prince said. There’s a decades-long backlog of bugs in software written without much review or scrutiny—which was more or less fine so long as there was a very small number of skilled hackers. Over the past two decades, companies, governments, and individuals have been lulled into a false sense of security: Most people don’t think twice about punching credit-card numbers into the website of a local restaurant or gift shop, or forking over a home address and phone number in just about any customer survey. But the internet was always a dangerous place. We’re just waking up from a trance.” Adoption Is Not a T

articles.title_zh: 在婚姻中培养亲密感
articles.content: I recently spent a couple of weeks preparing a great deal of fresh material for a weekend-long marriage seminar. Along the way, I often found myself convicted by the content I was preparing. As I readied myself to teach others, I had to consider the ways in which I needed to be a student before I should be a teacher. One area this proved true was intimacy in marriage—but a kind of intimacy I think many of us seldom consider. There is no doubt that marriage is meant to involve a husband and wife baring their bodies before one another, so that marriage is the context in which a man and woman can experience what it is to be naked and unashamed—to be fully bared, yet fully accepted. And because marriage is meant to be the deepest kind of unity two human beings can experience, it makes sense that there is a physical component to it through which two bodies are literally joined together. This is usually what we mean when we discuss intimacy in marriage. It is my understanding that this kind of intimacy, while real, is also in a way representative or symbolic. It is a demonstration of a unity between two people that is not merely body-deep , but fully soul-deep. Physical intimacy is both significant and essential to marriage, but it is not meant to be the sum total of the intimacy shared between a husband and wife. Yet as Aileen and I have interacted with other couples, we have observed that many husbands and wives find it easier to bare their bodies than their souls. Even as they routinely give themselves to one another physically, they can withhold a great deal relationally and emotionally. Even as they give themselves in free and joyful lovemaking, they can stop short of a greater baring, which is the baring of their souls and the revealing of the deep recesses of their hearts. As Aileen and I discussed this together, we had to conclude that this is something we are prone to as well. It’s not that we hold back shocking secrets or scandalous sins that would cause the other to recoil in dismay or disgust. It’s that we are both reserved people who find it hard to let another person in. We are both wounded people who have been hurt by those who have misused information we have revealed to them. And then I suppose we are both prideful or distrustful people who hold back the pieces of ourselves that we think might cause the other person to lower their respect for us. But by holding back, we are failing to live with full transparency and, therefore, failing to live with full intimacy. The baring of our bodies exceeds the baring of our souls. There is an irony to this, because I am convinced there is a deep longing within each of us to be known. We want someone else to know us as we truly are and to still love us and give us their approval. But even while we want it on one level, we resist it on another, because we wonder what that other person will think of us if they know our deep thoughts, our secret longings, and our hidden fears. We wonder if they will still respect us if they know what causes us to feel shame or express remorse. Perhaps we doubt they’ll still love us if they know who we are far beneath the surface. Still, there is this longing to be known, to be as bare emotionally as we can be physically—and still to be loved and accepted. It is this longing that we never address when we hold back from revealing who and what we truly are, when we refuse to foster a deep soul intimacy—an intimacy that is then represented by, rather than superseded by, sexual intimacy. So how can we foster this kind of baring? By letting our spouse really know us, which may mean creating times and contexts for lengthy, deep, and uninterrupted conversation. This will involve asking good questions and then listening attentively so we can come to a correct rather than trite or hasty understanding of what is being communicated. To really know and be known is the work of a lifetime. It is work, but work worth committing to. By assuring one another that no
articles.content_zh: 我最近花了几周时间 准备了大量的新材料 为周末的婚姻研讨会。 一路走来,我常常发现自己被我准备的内容定罪. 当我准备去教别人时,我不得不在做教师之前考虑我需要成为学生的方式。 婚姻中的亲密关系是事实, 毫无疑问,婚姻意味着丈夫和妻子在彼此面前禁止其身体,因此,婚姻是男女能够体验裸体和无羞无耻——被完全禁止,但却被完全接受的背景。 因为婚姻是两个人类能够经历的最深层次的团结,所以它有一个物理成分,通过它,两个身体可以真正结合在一起。 这通常是我们讨论婚姻亲密关系时的意思. 我的理解是,这种亲密关系虽然是真实的,但在某种程度上也是有代表性的或象征性的。 它表明两个人之间的团结 不仅仅是身体深处,而且是灵魂深处 肉体亲密关系对婚姻既重要又重要,但并非夫妻共有亲密关系的总和。 然而,随着艾琳和我与其他夫妇的互动,我们观察到,许多丈夫和妻子发现露出自己的身体比灵魂更容易. 即使在他们习惯上互相施舍的时候,他们也可以在感情上和感情上保持相当的克制。 即使在他们自由而欢快地做爱时,他们也可以停止更大的禁酒,这就是他们的灵魂被束缚,以及他们内心深处的沉睡。 正如我和艾琳一起讨论的那样,我们不得不得出结论,这也是我们容易看到的。 并不是我们隐瞒令人震惊的秘密或可耻的罪恶, 我们都是有保留的人, 我们都是被滥用我们所透露的信息的人所伤害的受伤者。 然后我想,我们都是骄傲或不信任的人,他们屏蔽着我们自己的碎片,我们认为这可能会使他人降低对我们的尊重. 但是,通过阻挠,我们没有完全透明地生活,因此,没有完全亲密地生活。 身体的阻断 超过了灵魂的阻断 这一点具有讽刺意味,因为我相信,我们每个人都有很深的渴望要知道。 我们希望其他人了解我们的真实身份,仍然爱我们,并给予我们批准。 但是,即使我们希望在一个层次上,我们抵制另一个层次,因为我们想知道,如果其他人知道我们的深思熟虑,我们的秘密渴望,以及我们隐藏的恐惧,我们会怎么想。 我们想知道,如果他们知道是什么使我们感到羞愧或表示悔恨,他们是否仍然尊重我们。 也许我们怀疑如果他们知道我们是谁, 然而,人们仍渴望知道这一点,希望我们能像身体上那样裸露出情感——仍然希望得到爱和接受。 正是这种渴望,当我们不愿透露我们真正是谁和什么时,当我们拒绝培养一种深厚的灵魂亲密关系时,我们从未谈到这种渴望——这种亲密关系由性亲密关系而不是取而代之。 那么,我们如何促进这种酒吧? 通过让我们的配偶真正了解我们,这可能意味着为冗长、深入和不间断的对话创造时间和背景。 这将涉及提出好的问题,然后认真倾听,以便我们能够对所传达的内容有一个正确而不是老练或仓促的理解。 真正知道和被了解是一生的工作。 这是工作,但值得致力于工作。 互相保证不会

articles.content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals If all goes well, today’s Kindle deals should include several important books that deal with a Christian understanding of science. Westminster Books is offering a deal this week on the two-part John Calvin’s Illustrated Institutes , which drives the price as low as 50% off. Recommended Reading This Is Roman Catholicism. Here’s a tremendous new project from the Reformanda Initiative—a free documentary series that “offers a firsthand look at often-overlooked yet integral aspects of Roman Catholic theology and practice, challenging idealized perceptions of Rome and encouraging informed, biblical discernment—particularly among those drawn to it. This docuseries is made primarily for Protestant Christians who want to understand what Rome teaches and practices. Featuring: Leonardo De Chirico, Mark Dever, Kevin DeYoung, Albert Mohler, Lauren Montenegro, and Michael Reeves.” Three Ways to Walk With Those Who Grieve. Kirsten Black outlines three ways that any of us can walk faithfully and compassionately with those who are in a time of deep grief. “Often, we do not know how to step into spaces of loss. There is a beautiful and godly desire to bring comfort, yet when facing the reality of walking with the grieving, we are also confronted with the limits of the comfort we can actually offer. This holy work often brings with it an acute awareness of how easy it is to say the wrong thing and unintentionally add more pain to the one who is already suffering.” Explore the Reformation in Ligonier’s Grow App . The Protestant Reformation was not a minor theological dispute—it was a recovery of the biblical gospel. With Reformation Day coming this Saturday, you can explore a variety of free Reformation-themed teaching series with R.C. Sproul in the Grow app from Ligonier Ministries. Download the app and study the five solas , the life of Martin Luther, and much more. (Sponsored) 5 Ways Men Can Serve the Church & 5 Ways Women Can Serve the Church. A pair of articles from Ligonier Ministries offers distinct and meaningful ways that both men and women can serve within the local church. Christian Universalism Is Alive (Just Go to a Funeral). Yes, I have observed as well that funerals are the events where we are most likely to see evidence of Christian universalism. “I’ve been to many funerals and memorial services in my life, and through the years, I’ve encountered religious people who give off the impression that they believe everyone goes to heaven. Culture gives the same impression. Words reveal worldviews. The deceased person may not have received Christ by faith, may not have gone to church, may have even lived an unrepentant and selfish life, and some people still seem to assume they went to a ‘better place’ or went to heaven. Might Christian Universalism be more prevalent than we think?” Stinginess and the Generosity of God. Randy Alcorn contrasts the stinginess of human beings—and even Christian human beings—with the generosity of God. “A life characterized by greed and stinginess is neither Spirit-filled nor Christlike — nor is it happy. If we know Jesus, we will become more and more like our generous God.” Unclear Evangelism Leads to Unclear (And False) Conversions. Writing for 9Marks, John Lee explains how unclear evangelism can lead to false conversions. “When we are unclear about the urgency of conversion, the cost of conversion, or the accountability that should accompany conversion, we risk leaving people deceived about their eternal state. Ultimately, our job is simply to proclaim the gospel clearly, trust God to open people’s hearts to the truth, and provide ongoing discipleship to those who respond in repentance and faith.” Reader Recommendations Once a week, I like to ask what you enjoy and recommend. What books, products, videos, sites, or other experiences do you recommend to others who read this blog/newsletter? Let me know, and I’ll share a collection on Saturday. (If you’re
articles.content_zh: 早上好,你好吗? 格蕾丝和平安 销售和交易 如果一切顺利,今天的Kindle交易应该包括几本重要书籍,涉及基督教对科学的理解。 威斯敏斯特图书公司本周在约翰·加尔文两地的Illustrated Institutes提供一笔交易, 推荐阅读 这是罗马天主教。 以下是Reformanda倡议的一个巨大的新项目,这是一部免费的纪录片系列,“第一手看一看罗马天主教神学和实践中经常被高瞻远瞩但不可分割的方面,挑战对罗马理想化的看法,并鼓励知情的、圣经上的分辨——特别是在那些被吸引的人中。 这种道克系列主要为新教基督徒所制作,他们想了解罗马的教义和实践. 表演:莱昂纳多·德·奇里科、马克·德维尔、凯文·德杨、阿尔伯特·莫勒、劳伦·黑山和迈克尔·里夫斯。” 柯尔斯滕·布莱克概述了我们中任何人都能与那些处于极度悲痛的时代的人们忠实而富有同情心地行走的三种方式. “当然,我们不知道如何进入损失空间。 有一种美丽而神通地渴望带来舒适,然而当面对与悲伤相伴而行的现实时,我们也面临着我们实际所能提供的舒适的限度. 这种神圣的工作往往使人们敏锐地意识到说错话是多么容易,无意中给已经遭受痛苦的人增加了更多的痛苦。” 探索Ligonier Grow App的改造。 新教改革并不是一个小的神学纠纷——这是圣经福音的收复. 随着本周六的改造日的到来,你可以在利戈尼耶各部的"成长"应用中,与R.C.Sproul一起探索各种自由改造主题的教学系列. 下载应用程序并研究五索拉斯, 马丁路德的生活,还有更多。 (赞助) 5 道:男人可以为教会服务 5道:女人可以为教会服务. 利戈尼耶各部的一对文章提供了独特而有意义的方法,男女都可以在地方教会中服务。 基督教世界主义是活的(去葬礼吧). 是的,我也注意到,葬礼是我们最有可能看到基督教普遍主义证据的事件。 「我一生中参加过许多葬礼和追悼会, 文化也给人同样的印象。 语出出世相. 死者可能没有信仰接受基督,可能没有去教堂,甚至过着不悔改和自私的生活,有些人似乎仍然认为他们去了"更好的地方"或去天堂. 基督教世界主义会比我们想象的更盛行吗? 坚忍与神通相. Randy Alcorn将人类的吝啬——甚至基督教人类——与上帝的慷慨相提并论。 “一种以贪婪和吝啬为特点的生活既不是充满精神,也不是基督般的,也不是幸福的。 如果我们了解耶稣,我们将越来越像我们慷慨的上帝。” unclear Evangelism 引出unclear(和假)转换. 写作为9马克斯,约翰·李(John Lee)解释不清楚的福音会如何导致虚假的转换. “当我们不清楚转换的迫切性、转换的成本或与转换相关的问责制时,我们有可能让人们对其永恒状态受到欺骗。 归根结底,我们的工作只是明确宣示福音,相信上帝为人们打开真理的心扉,为那些以忏悔和信仰回应的人不断提供弟子之道". 读者建议 每周一次 我想问问你喜欢什么 推荐什么 你推荐哪些书籍、产品、视频、网站或其他经验给阅读博客/通讯的其他人? 让我知道, (如果你是的话)

articles.title_zh: 弗兰妮·卡什（ Franni Cash ）离开家族乐队，首次独唱并在邪教中成长
articles.content: Franni Cash was about 13 when she says the community her family belonged to officially became a cult. She was 17 when her family left it. She told RELEVANT that her parents joined after their marriage hit a rough patch and a friend suggested counseling. The therapist they saw, she said, was “dangerously smart” and used people’s vulnerabilities “to kind of tether loyalty to himself.” Counseling sessions became Bible studies with other families, and then she says they were told they no longer needed church. Eventually the leader declared himself their spiritual father and warned that anyone who broke covenant with him would be cut off, and women who disagreed with their husbands were said to have “the Jezebel spirit.” “It just became so far away from the truth,” Cash said. She kept a diary about how strange it all felt. The leader found it and burned it. She was 14. “From that place I pushed it down,” she said. “I can’t question it and can’t voice this anymore.” Her family left in the middle of her senior year of high school, after an article exposed years of alleged fraud and sexual allegations tied to the leader. She remembers her parents telling the kids in their bedroom. “It was like this weight flew off my shoulders,” she said. Then came a harder year, when she feared the curses and watched her brothers struggle. “I didn’t know if I was gonna make it. I really mean that.” Her parents put the family in therapy immediately. Talk therapy alone didn’t work for her, because she was still so brainwashed she didn’t know what she could say. EMDR and brainspotting did. She has been in consistent therapy for ten years now and says talking about the cult no longer stings. “I’ve had to grieve them being susceptible to something so harmful,” she said of her parents. “But right off the bat, they got themselves in therapy.” She describes her healing journey as medicine and scripture working together. “You can’t just slap a Bible verse on it,” she said. “Scripture is so powerful, but sometimes you don’t know how to absorb it until you can do some surgery.” The family’s first song came a year and a half after they left, and it became We the Kingdom. Cash said the band was a place where she felt understood, because her family were the only people who could laugh at the jokes instead of being horrified. She also says they were trauma bonded, and that she needed to learn who she was on her own. She left the band, and says she and her family are now the closest they’ve ever been, “from a health and respect” place that “doesn’t feel enmeshed.” Her solo debut, Here I Am , takes its title from a lyric she and her father, producer and songwriter Ed Cash, wrote together for the song “The Real Thing”: Here I am, I made it through. The page is burned, but this story is not over. Here I Am was also going to be the title of an album she planned at 16, in the middle of everything. “Now here I am, kind of on the other side of healing,” she said. Getting there meant relearning music. A friend, the writer Paul Duncan, told her she needed to “date music like you would your spouse,” meaning listen to records she loved as a kid with no goal. She was driving on the Pacific Coast Highway when U2’s “Where the Streets Have No Name” came on. “It was like I heard music for the first time,” she said. She has since been listening to Marvin Gaye’s What’s Going On , Al Green, Elton John, Casey Musgraves, John Mayer and Linkin Park’s Hybrid Theory . Her view of God changed too. “I just really thought that God was this angry man upstairs,” she said. She remembers being told to get off the worship stool because she wasn’t “anointed enough.” Then she met what she calls the real Jesus. “He was so loving. And gracious with me,” she said. “It changed everything.” When we asked what she’d say to someone inside a controlling church, her answer was short. “Leave. You’re free to. articles.content: “Who is God?” This is the most important question we can ask, yet many people in the United Kingdom are unsure of how to answer it. In this year’s State of Theology survey , 39% of UK adults responded “not sure” to the statement, “There is one true God in three persons: God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit.” The doctrine of the Trinity is fundamental to the Christian faith, because what we believe about God shapes our entire lives. This uncertainty extends beyond the Trinity. This year’s survey results reveal that many UK adults are also unsure about other core Christian beliefs: 39% are unsure of whether Jesus is God 46% are unsure if the Holy Spirit is a personal being 33% are unsure if the Bible is literally true These findings reveal a significant need for clear, faithful Bible teaching. Many people simply do not know what Scripture teaches about God and the Christian faith, and new believers need to be firmly grounded in the truth amid a society that has forgotten many of its biblical roots. articles.title_zh: 马丁·路德是谁？
articles.content: As a doctoral student, Martin Luther finally had access to the university library. Here, for the first time in his life, he held a complete Bible in his hands. The Bible was venerated in the medieval church, and portions of it were read from the lectionary used in worship services. But Bibles had to be copied by hand, so they were very expensive. Many churches did not even own one. And if they did, most people were illiterate, so they could not read it anyway. No wonder the church had drifted from the Word of God. Yes, the medieval church taught that Jesus died for our sins, a salvation applied at baptism. But if you sinned after that, you had to pay. Each sin that you confessed before a priest could be forgiven, as long as you performed some kind of penance. Even forgiven sins, though, required a temporal punishment, if not in this life, then in purgatory. In the meantime, to be saved, a Christian needed to accumulate enough merit through good works and acts of devotion in order to deserve God’s grace and to earn a place in heaven. Young Luther was no rebel. He took the church’s teaching seriously. Church vocations, with their vows of celibacy and other ascetic disciplines, were thought to be more spiritual and more likely to lead to heaven than the worldly lives of the laity. So Luther became a monk, then a priest. Still, he would agonize over his sins. Once he had access to a Bible, he read it voraciously, and a new picture of God, of Christ, and of salvation started to become clear. The University of Wittenberg was one of the new Renaissance schools that stressed going back to the original sources. The medieval universities taught theology through the method known as scholasticism , using authoritative textbooks and rationalistic disputations. But the original source for Christianity is the Bible. And since Renaissance-style, classical education also taught Greek and Hebrew, it became possible to study the Bible in its original languages, whereas previously it had only been available in a Latin translation. When Luther earned his doctorate, the university put him on faculty and gave him the responsibility of teaching the Bible. In preparing a lecture on the book of Romans, Luther struggled to understand this passage: “The righteous shall live by faith” (Rom. 1:17). Suddenly it hit him: We are justified by grace through faith in the atoning work of Jesus Christ! Luther said, “Here I felt that I was altogether born again and had entered paradise itself through open gates.” Meanwhile, it became clearer that the medieval church thought otherwise. It was sponsoring a sale, promising to release Christians from purgatory if they would buy a certificate called an indulgence . People had been taught that they would suffer in penitential fire for seven years for every sin they committed, including those that had been forgiven. Christians were expecting to be in purgatory for thousands of years before they could enter heaven. Of course, they gladly bought indulgences. For Luther, not only was this a cynical scam that exploited the poor (an indulgence cost workers about a week’s wages), it was a monstrous violation of God’s saving Word. On October 31, 1517, Luther nailed to the church door a list of Ninety-Five Theses against the sale of indulgences, which he was willing to debate. Someone, using the newly invented printing press, printed hundreds of copies. Someone else translated them from scholarly Latin into popular German, selling thousands. They soon spread through all of Germany. They were then translated into French, Italian, and English. The Ninety-Five Theses, as we would say today, went viral. The Vatican responded with treatises of its own, which Luther answered. The controversy escalated into other issues. Luther said that the Bible gives no support for indulgences. articles.content_zh: 作为博士生,马丁·路德终于可以进入大学图书馆. 在这里,他一生中第一次手持完整的"圣经". 中世纪的教堂中尊奉了"圣经",其中部分内容取自于礼拜服务中使用的词典. 但"圣经"必须用手抄取,所以非常昂贵. 许多教堂甚至没有一座教堂。 如果他们这样做,大多数人都是文盲,所以他们不能读它。 难怪教堂从上帝的言语里漂了出来 是的,中世纪的教会教诲耶稣为我们的罪而死,这是在受洗时应用的救赎. 但是,如果你有罪 之后,你必须支付。 你向牧师忏悔的每一起罪 都可以被赦免 只要你做了某种忏悔 即使赦免了罪过, 也需要暂时的处罚, 如果在今世没有, 然后在炼狱。 与此同时,为了得到拯救,一个基督教徒需要通过善行和献身行为来积累足够的功绩,以便获得上帝的恩惠和在天堂得到一席之地。 年轻的路德不是反叛者。 他认真对待教会的教义. 教会的教义,以独身和其他醋酸盐学科的誓言,被认为比贵族的世界生活更具有精神,更可能通向天堂. 于是路德成为了道士,后又成为了牧师. 但是,他会为自己的罪孽而痛苦。 一旦他有机会读出圣经,他就非常贪婪地阅读了它,对上帝,基督,救赎的新画面开始变得清晰. 维滕贝格大学是新文艺复兴时期的学校之一,强调要回到原来的来源. 中世纪的大学通过被称为学术主义的方法教授神学,使用权威的教科书和理性的争论. 但基督教的原始来源是"圣经". 而从文艺复兴风格起,古典教育也教授了希腊语和希伯来语,因此可以以原文来研究"圣经",而以前只有拉丁文译本. 当路德获得博士学位后,大学把他安排在教职员上,并赋予他教授"圣经"的责任. 在准备关于罗马人著作的讲座时,路德竭力想理解这一段:“正义者应当以信仰为生”(1:17). 它忽然袭击了他:我们凭着对耶稣基督所行的善行的信念,是被恩典证实的。 路德说,“我在这里感到,我再次出生,并通过开放的大门进入了天堂。” 同时,中世纪的教会也越来越清楚地认为并非如此. 它赞助了一次销售,承诺如果基督徒购买一份名为"宽恕"的证明,他们就会从炼狱中释放出. 人们被告知,他们因犯下的每一项罪行,包括那些被宽恕的罪行,将在忏悔火中受苦七年。 基督徒期望在炼狱中被囚禁了几千年,然后才能入天堂. 当然,他们很高兴 买了宽大。 对路德来说,这不仅是一个剥削穷人的玩世不恭的骗局(允许工人花一周的工资),而且是对上帝拯救言语的粗暴违反。 1517年10月31日,路德在教堂门上钉上一张反对出售放纵品的"九五通"名单,他愿意对此进行辩论. 有人利用新发明的印刷机印刷了上百份. 有人把它们从学术拉丁语翻译成了流行德语,卖出上千个. 它们很快会扩散到整个德国. 随后被翻译成了法语,意大利语和英语. 正如我们今天要说的那样,九十五部曲是病毒性的。 梵蒂冈以自己的论文回应,路德对此作出了回答. 争议升级为其他问题. 路德说圣经不支持宽恕 梵蒂冈回答说,他们得到了教皇的授权. 路德回应道"圣经"是比教皇更高的权威. 梵蒂冈问路德如何
