articles.title: Your People Need to Know the “Why” of Shifting to a Plurality of Elders
articles.summary: It seems the reason God gives pastors a job that is too big for one man is that he never intended for one man to do it alone!   The post  Your People Need to Know the “Why” of Shifting to a Plurality of Elders  appeared first on  9Marks .
articles.summary_zh: 看来，神之所以给牧师一份对一个人来说太大的工作，是因为他从来没有打算让一个人独自完成！ Your People Need to Know the “Why” of Shifting to a Plurality of Elders （你的人民需要知道转向多元长老的“原因” ）一文首先出现在9Marks上。
articles.title_zh: 你的人民需要知道转向多元长老的“原因”
articles.content: Abstract : Zach Kilpatrick encourages pastors to help their congregations see the need for a plurality of elders, first from Scripture and then from the various ways it can bless the church and its pastors. Many Christians aren’t aware of the Bible’s teaching about elders, nor do they recognize the strain that pastoral responsibilities can put on the pastor in a senior pastor model. In this second of three articles dealing with transitioning a church from a single-pastor model to a plurality of elders, Kilpatrick helps pastors think through educating their people on this important change. I never understood algebra until I took physics. Algebra was just abstract numbers until physics put those numbers to work. For instance, the quadratic formula helps determine how long a football can stay in the air and whether a receiver running at a certain speed could catch it. Now I’m interested. That’s what most people want—not just abstract theory but practical application. When leading a church through a major change, you should put both on offer. This article is the second in a three-part series on leading a church from a single-pastor polity to a plurality-of-elders model. As in the previous article, I’m using the terms “pastor” and “elder” interchangeably. In the first article , we saw the importance of evaluating your church’s history to help predict hazards you will likely encounter. In this article, we will see the importance of education in the transition process. Help Them See the Need from Scripture On the day of Pentecost, Peter told the gathered crowd to “Repent and be baptized . . .” (Acts 2:38). However, before he gave this command, he preached a sermon full of reasons why they should eagerly do so. In a similar way, we shouldn’t urge a change in polity until we’ve explained why that change needs to be made. Help your church see how a plurality of elders fits better with the teaching and example we find in the New Testament. Once they grasp the Bible’s model, adorn it with practical blessings that will come from adopting it—more on this in a minute. I’m convinced many Christians would be surprised to learn what Scripture actually says about polity. It’s simply too often assumed rather than understood. Therefore, we need to help our members locate the ecclesial prescriptions in their Bibles. Consider Paul’s example and instructions in Acts 20:17–35: elders should teach publicly and privately; teach believers and evangelize unbelievers; proclaim the “whole counsel of God”; know and care for all members of the flock; and protect the church against false teaching. According to Ephesians 4:11–12, elders are among those whom Christ has given to the church to “equip the saints for the work of ministry.” And when Paul tells Timothy the qualifications for being an elder, he says that elders should “manage [their] own household well,” “care for God’s church,” and be “above reproach” (1 Tim. 3:1–7). Given the breadth of these pastoral responsibilities, it’s not surprising that the New Testament repeatedly underlines there being multiple elders for each local church (Acts 14:23; Titus 1:5; Jas. 5:14). Even on a practical level, a plurality of elders appears to be a more sustainable model for pastoral ministry. But if you don’t educate the congregation on these things, many will never see it. Help Them Feel the Need Once members understand the scope and difficulty of a pastor’s calling, they should begin to see that it is too big for one man, and I believe this is by design. It seems the reason God gives pastors a job that is too big for one man is that he never intended for one man to do it alone! Though we want to avoid coming across as complaining about our job, particularly given that many members also have difficult jobs, we can be honest with them about the strain of pastoring alone. I told the congregation I often had to look at two pastoral responsibilities and choose which one to neglect. There were days when I didn’t have tim
articles.content_zh: 摘要:扎克·基尔帕特里克(Zach Kilpatrick)鼓励牧师们帮助他们的会众认识到需要多种长者,首先从"圣经"中,然后从它能够祝福教会及其牧师的各种方式中. 许多基督徒并不知道《圣经》关于长老的教义, 在三篇文章的第二篇论述教会从一个单一的牧人模式向多位长者过渡,基尔帕特里克通过教育他们的人民了解这一重要变化,帮助牧师思考. 我从不理解代数 直到我接受了物理。 代数只是抽象的数字,直到物理学使这些数字发挥作用。 例如,四极方程有助于确定足球在空中能停留多久,以及一个以一定速度运行的接球员能否赶上. 现在我感兴趣了。 这是大多数人想要的, 不只是抽象理论, 当带领教会经历重大改变时,你应该同时提供两种条件. 这篇文章是三部曲系列中的第二篇,内容是带领教会从一派政体到一派多翼模式. 与上篇文章一样,我用 " pastor " 和 " elder " 两词互换。 在第一篇文章中,我们看到了评估你教会历史的重要性,以帮助预测你可能遇到的危险。 在本篇文章中,我们将看到教育在过渡进程中的重要性。 帮助他们从圣经中看到需要 在五旬节日,彼得告诉聚集的人群“忏悔并接受洗礼......”(法案2:38)。 然而,在他下达这一命令之前,他鼓吹布道,布道中充满了他们应该急切这样做的理由. 在解释为何需要改变政体之前, 帮助你的教会看到 多元的长者如何更好地适应 我们发现的教学和例子 在新约。 一旦他们掌握了《圣经》的模式, 我确信许多基督徒会惊讶地得知《圣经》对政体的实际说法。 更何况, 因此,我们需要帮助我们的成员在他们的圣经中找到古典处方。 以保罗在20:17-35号法案中的榜样和指示为例:长者应该公开和私下教书;教导信徒并传福音给不信者;宣布“真主完全的教诲”;了解和关心所有羊群成员;保护教会免遭错误的教诲。 根据以弗所书4:11-12, 长者是基督献给教会的“为圣人提供大臣工作设备”的人。 当保罗告诉蒂莫西作为长者的资格时,他说长者应该"管理好自己的家庭","照顾上帝的教会",并被"超越责难"(1 Tim. 3: 1-7). 鉴于这些牧业责任的广度,《新约》一再强调每个地方教会都有多名长老(第14:23;Titus 1:5;Jas. 5:14)。 即使在实际层面,多位长者似乎是牧业部更可持续的模式。 许多人永远不会看到。 帮助他们感受需要, 一旦成员了解牧师的召唤的范围和难度, 他们应该开始看到,这对一个人来说太大了, 我认为这是设计。 看来上帝给牧师一份对一个人来说太大的工作 是因为他从来没有打算让一个人单独干! 尽管我们想避免抱怨我们的工作,特别是鉴于许多成员也有困难的工作,但我们可以对他们诚实地说,独自做点事的压力很大。 我告诉众会,我经常不得不看两个牧区的责任,选择哪个要忽略. 有几天我没有Tim

articles.content: 1. “ ‘I Shall Be Very Surprised If There Isn’t A Next Chapter’ ” is the title of the remarkable interview with English theologian Sarah Coakley that appeared on the New York Times website this past week, courtesy of Peter Wehner. We’ve been at this Another Week Ends game for a couple decades now, and I’m not sure I’ve ever seen so much theological substance published in America’s once-and-future(?) paper of record. I’ve been aware of Coakley’s work and reputation for some time but never taken the plunge, which, after reading their conversation, feels like a bit of a shame-on-me situation. One of my favorite bits comes at the very beginning, when Coakley talks about her teenage years. Apparently the confirmation classes at her little Church of England parish lacked the rigor she was hoping for. Thus, she did what all kids that age do these days: My eldest brother and I organized our own theological discussion group in that same parish. We brought a lot of our atheistical and skeptical school friends into it. And this very holy rector was very clever at this point, because he just sat watching the arguments go backward and forward, rather like the umpire at Wimbledon. He never intervened, never put us right, never told us what the right answer was. When my brother and I recently thought about who had attended those discussions, the vast majority of our friends who attended at that age, 14 to 16, subsequently became Christians. So that tells you something about opening the Pandora’s box theologically and how important it is for the clergy not to stifle that. A lovely little testament to the power of grace in practice, I’d say, and one which jibes with my own decades working with young people. Allow students to ask their questions, raise their objections and air their doubts without threat of defensiveness — let that stuff hang in the air — and the craziest things can happen, especially over the long haul. Squash their arguments with doctrine, even right doctrine, and you risk alienating them forever. Such is the emotional wallop of correction, however well intentioned. Coakley goes on to provide some rather damning commentary on the gap in theology between the academy and the pew, the professor and the layperson. One of the core hopes of her own work, she claims, is the closing of that gap chasm, to which I can only add a hearty amen. I’ve tried to do something similar in my own books, albeit on a much smaller scale. (Whether utilizing a French phrase for that project — théologie totale — screams accessibility is a separate question.) In Coakley’s view, uncoupling the study of theology from the practice of prayer is dangerous. This leads her into one of the most beautiful articulations of prayer I’ve read anywhere, let alone the New York Times : How do I pray? Well, you hand yourself over to the source of your being, and then you ask some things. But the handing over is primary, and learning how to do that. It changes your perspective on God — because when you practice this, even for a very short time each day, simple opening up space in which God is God. You don’t control it. That’s what’s so frightening. This is not a new skill, like learning how to make a very good omelet or to ride a bicycle. This is a nonskill. It’s an unskilling, an unmastery. It completely changes your view of God, because up to that point you’ve probably subliminally been thinking about God as a very large entity, the largest and the best in a universe of entities whom somehow you’ve got to get on your side or cajole or get to answer your request. I know that’s a very naïve sounding description, but as a priest I can tell you that’s the God I hear about all the time. All the great theologians of the tradition have slain that God, and they’ve had to slay that God — think of Luther — with great terror. It’s really just opening up to the possibility of grace. Contemplation isn’t special. It’s just very difficult for people who are relatively educated and pri
articles.content_zh: 1. " `I Shall Be very Surprise If There Isout A Next Chapter ' ”是英国神学家Sarah Coakley在上周在纽约时报网站上发表的令人瞩目的访谈的标题,由Peter Wehner主持。 我不确定我是否曾见过如此多的神学物质, 我了解Coakley的作品与名声已有一段时间, 我最喜欢的一点 是在一开始, 当Coakley谈论她的青少年时代。 显然,她的英格兰小教堂的确认课 缺乏她希望的严格度。 因此,她做了所有的孩子 这些天做: 我的长兄和我在同一堂区组织了我们自己的神学讨论小组。 我们把许多无神论和怀疑论的学校朋友都带进了其中. 而这位非常神圣的校长 此时非常聪明, 因为他只是坐着看着这些争论往后走, 就像温布尔登的裁判。 他从来没有干预,从来没有让我们正确,从来没有告诉我们什么是正确的答案。 当我和我兄弟最近想到谁参加了这些讨论时,14至16岁的我们绝大多数朋友后来成为基督徒。 因此,这可以说明在神学上打开潘多拉的盒子,以及神职人员不要扼杀它的重要性。 一个可爱的小证明, 在实践中, 允许学生提问,提出反对意见并表达他们的疑虑,而不会受到防卫威胁——让这些东西被挂在空中——最疯狂的事情可能会发生,特别是在漫长的时间内. 用学说,甚至正确的学说来压制他们的论点,你冒着永远疏远他们的危险. 这是一种精神上的纠错,无论用意如何。 Coakley继续就学院与皮尤,教授和外行人之间的神学差距提供一些相当可憎的评论. 她声称,她自己工作的一个核心希望是,缩小了这一差距,我只能为这一差距增添一个心地阿门。 尽管规模要小得多, (该项目是否使用法语短语-总词-尖叫无障碍是一个单独的问题。 ) 科克利认为,将神学研究与祈祷实践脱钩是危险的. 更别说纽约时报:我该如何祈祷? 你把自己交给你生命的来源 然后问些问题 但交接是初级的, 并学习如何做到这一点。 它改变了你对上帝的看法——因为当你练习这个时,即使每天非常短的时间,简单的打开了上帝是上帝的空间. 你无法控制它。 这才是最可怕的。 这不是一种新的技能,比如学习如何做一个非常好的煎蛋卷或者骑自行车。 这是非技能。 是个没有技能, 这完全改变了你对上帝的看法,因为直到那个时候,你可能一直在深思上帝是一个非常大的实体,是一个最大和最好的实体,你不得不站在你一边,或者说去回答你的要求。 我知道这听起来很天真, 但作为一个牧师,我可以告诉你,这就是我一直听到的上帝。 传统中所有伟大的神学家都杀死了上帝, 他们不得不用巨大的恐怖来杀死上帝—— 想到路德。 这其实只是打开了宽宏大量的可能性。 考虑并不特殊。 这对受过相对教育的人来说非常困难。

articles.title_zh: 一位珍惜自己遗产的作家
articles.content: Welcome back, fiends! Blaine Grimes, Blake Collier, Caleb Stallings, and I are back with the Spooky Season film roundtable, and this week we are watching John Carpenter’s In the Mouth of Madness , the third of his “Apocalypse” films. So file in to Row D, your seat’s a few down from ours and right next to Sam Neill, who’s gulping down popcorn and drawing more crosses on his face. Let’s go a little crazy! Ian : Caleb, what led you to pick In the Mouth of Madness ? Caleb : I actually watched it earlier this year on my quest to see every John Carpenter film. This was the final movie of his I hadn’t seen. And it was the perfect one to end on. An autumnal, meta movie about authorship and terror. Just right up my alley. And what better way to go insane than in an impossibly dark cathedral in an autumnal New England town? Who wouldn’t want to watch a movie about that? And who wouldn’t want it to happen to them too? Ian : Well, when you put it that way … Blake : I was really struck this time by Trent and Cane’s dialogue when Cane states, “I am God now …” and Trent responds something to the effect of “I didn’t know God was a hack horror writer.” It’s a great comeback but also chilling in that humans, no matter their brilliance and no matter how well-adjusted they present as being, are hacks when it comes to authoring their own stories, let alone the stories of others. Only God can weave the narrative in such a way that the goodness, justice, and mercy of the ending is earned. Caleb : And that sanity is maintained! Blake : Exactly! Caleb : If fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, then trying to usurp him is entering the Mouth of Madness. Ian : It is, but it’s a sanity that might look insane to the surrounding world. And that’s the question with Trent, isn’t it? He sounds insane, but he sees through the bogus story Cane is weaving. Blake : In this way, I think the film makes for a thrilling blueprint of the failures of humans trying to weave together the grand narrative of existence, and how fiction can portray our own failures to usurp God’s position and role. Caleb : This reminded me of Tim Keller recounting how Dorothy Sayers wrote herself into her own detective novels to be a help and savior of a sort to her own protagonist, Peter Wimsey. In the Mouth of Madness tells the opposite story: Sutter Cane writes himself into his stories to destroy his characters. Blake : So in this way, Cane is a type of Satan … which means Dante’s footprint is all over this film as well. Blaine : *In Gordon Ramsey voice* Bloody hell. Here we go again … Ian : You know, I’m something of a Dante adaptation myself! We are all creatures spoken into existence, in a story in which, like Sayers, the Teller, the Creator, becomes a character. And there are so many stories vying for authoritative interpretation of the world and of what we are. Caleb : There’s something interesting too in how many times it’s mentioned that the film rights to Cane’s book have been optioned. I think Carpenter was playing with how many people are only familiar with these stories via the film medium, which I imagine is even more true now, 30 years later. And the movie ends, not with Trent rereading Cane’s book to find out how it all ends but rather alone in a theater, eating popcorn and laughing hysterically (almost weeping) as he watches his own life play out, rather absurdly, on the silver screen. Blake : In some ways it is the mixed moral affection of giving oneself over to something that isn’t a wholly moral good. I think again of the ending of THE VVITCH where our protagonist is levitating in the air, and her face is both ecstatic and terrified with tears rolling down. Ian : It seems like the insane ecstasy of embracing oblivion. Here it’s the film adaptation, but this could just as easily be a Reel or a TikTok: all of which are in the mouth of madness. And all feature subjects playing at being the main character of a story they’re manufacturing, one that reduces and demeans a
articles.content_zh: 欢迎回来,恶魔们! Blaine Grames, Blake Collier, Caleb Stallings, 我又回到了Spooky Season电影圆桌会议上, 本周我们正观看约翰·卡彭特的"疯狂之口", 这是他第三部"启示录"电影。 因此,请向D行报告,你的座位从我们的座位倒下,紧挨着Sam Neill。 Sam Neil正在倒下爆米花并画出更多的十字架。 让我们有点疯狂吧! Caleb,是什么让你选的? 在疯狂之口? 凯勒布(Caleb):我今年早些时候在看约翰·卡彭特的电影时看过。 这是我从未看过的最后一部电影。 它是一个完美的结束。 一部秋天的,关于作者和恐怖的电影. 就在我的小巷边 比起在秋天的新英格兰小镇 一个不可想象的黑暗大教堂里 还有什么更好的办法去疯狂? 谁不想看电影? 谁不希望他们也遭遇这样的事? Ian:当你这么说的时候... 布莱克(Blake):这次我被特伦特和肯恩的对话深深地打击了,当时肯恩说,“我现在是上帝了......”而特伦特却回应了“我不知道上帝是黑客恐怖作家”这样的大意。 写自己的故事, 更不要说别人的故事了。 只有上帝才能编织叙事,使结局的善良,正义和慈悲得到伸张. 凯勒布: 保持这种理智! 布莱克:没错! 迦勒:如果对耶和华的恐惧是智慧的开始,那么试图篡夺他就是进入了疯狂之口. 伊恩(Ian):的确如此,但对于周围的世界来说,这是一种可能显得疯狂的理智。 这就是特伦特的问题,不是吗? 他听起来很疯狂 但他从假故事中看出 坎恩在编织 布莱克: 我认为这部电影为人类试图编织出关于存在的宏伟故事的失败,以及虚构如何描绘我们自己篡夺上帝的地位和角色的失败,提供了令人惊叹的蓝图。 凯勒布: 这让我想起了蒂姆·凯勒(Tim Keller)讲述了多萝西·赛耶斯(Dorothy Sayers)如何把自己写入她自己的侦探小说中,成为她自己的主角彼得·温西(Peter Wimsey)的某种帮助和救世主. 在"疯狂之口"(The Mouth of Madness)中讲述了相反的故事:萨特·克恩将自己写入他的故事来毁灭他的角色. 布莱克: 因此,通过这种方式,甘恩是撒旦的一种类型... 这意味着但丁的足迹也遍布本片. 布莱恩:*在戈登·拉姆齐的声音*血腥地狱. 伊恩:你知道,我自己也是但丁的适应者。 我们都是生命中的生物, 在一个故事里,像塞耶斯,特勒尔,造物主,成为一个人物。 有许多故事要求权威地解释世界和我们是什么。 Caleb : 多少次提到对Cane书的电影权被选择, 我认为卡彭特在和多少人通过电影媒介 对这些故事很熟悉, 我想现在,30年后,这更真实了。 电影的结局不是在特伦特重读了肯恩的书之后,他才知道这一切的结局,而是在剧院里独自一人,一边吃爆米花一边歇斯底里地取笑(几乎哭泣),一边在银幕上看自己的生活。 布莱克: 在某些方面,将自己交给并非完全出于道德利益的东西是一种混合的道德情感。 我又想起了VVITCH的结局 主角在空中飘来飘去 她的脸既兴奋又被泪水所吓倒 伊恩: 这似乎像疯狂的迷幻 拥抱遗忘。 这是电影的改编, 但这是Reel或TikTok, 所有玩耍的题材都是他们制作的故事的主角 一个减少和贬低

articles.title_zh: IMB的Barger因任务创新而获得2026 Excelerate奖
articles.content: Don Barger, left, IMB director of innovation and artificial intelligence, receives the Excelerate Award at the Missio Nexus Mission Leaders Conference in Orlando, Florida. The award recognizes individuals who demonstrate exceptional leadership and creativity in advancing missions through innovation. Photo provided Don Barger, director of innovation and artificial intelligence for the International Mission Board, received the 2026 Excelerate Award from Missio Nexus during the Mission Leaders Conference, Sept. 24 in Orlando, Florida. According to Missio Nexus, a network of mission-focused organizations and churches, the Excelerate Award recognizes individuals who demonstrate exceptional leadership and creativity in advancing missions through innovation. Barger has earned a reputation for identifying emerging technologies and applying them to ministry challenges, helping pioneer the use of artificial intelligence in global missions while promoting a biblically grounded approach to innovation. Barger said receiving the award was both surprising and encouraging. “I realized it was an affirmation not only of my work, but of the work our entire team has been doing,” he said. “It’s encouraging to see the IMB recognized as an organization willing to invest in innovation, think creatively and explore new ways to reach the nations.” Barger has served with the IMB for 29 years in a variety of roles. He was involved in church planting and led indigenous work in Mexico and Central America. Most of his work as a missionary focused on oral learners and Bible storying. Long before artificial intelligence became mainstream, Barger and his team began examining its potential for missions. IMB team members developed a framework to guide appropriate and inappropriate uses of AI in ministry settings. One principle that continues to shape that framework is Barger’s conviction that “souls should care for souls.” “We do not use AI for counseling or to replace human spiritual care,” Barger said. “Instead, we use AI to handle tasks that free people to spend more time ministering directly to people.” While much of his work centers on technology, Barger emphasizes that innovation extends far beyond technical advances. He defines innovation as a willingness to ask new questions and explore new approaches while remaining faithful to biblical truth. “Too often the response is, ‘That’s not how we’ve always done it,'” Barger said. “Innovation that advances the Great Commission begins by asking new questions and exploring new possibilities.” Barger noted that Christians have a long history of embracing new tools to support gospel ministry, from the printing press to broadcasting and healthcare advances. As artificial intelligence continues to generate discussion among ministry leaders, Barger encourages both optimism and discernment. He points to AI’s potential to improve communication, accelerate training and remove barriers that can hinder ministry efforts. At the same time, he cautions leaders to recognize the limitations of AI and ensure people remain responsible for ministry decisions and engagement. “Every tool throughout history has been capable of both good and evil,” Barger said. “The opportunity is to use AI for redemptive purposes.” Barger’s work includes developing faithbot.tools , a collection of AI tools designed for evangelical Christians. Throughout his career, he has advocated using technology not as an end in itself, but as a means of strengthening ministry and supporting relationships. Looking ahead, Barger hopes his greatest contribution will be encouraging future mission leaders to think creatively while remaining committed to God’s mission. “I hope mission leaders develop a mindset of curiosity,” he said. “Instead of simply accepting, ‘This is how we’ve always done it,’ I want them to ask, ‘How might we do this better?'” For Barger, innovation is ultimately about stewarding available tools in ways that help advance the Great Commission. articles.title_zh: 新教改革的原因是什么？
articles.content: What was the matter with the Protestant Reformation? It might seem like a strange question. Some might say that there was nothing the matter with the Reformation, that it was the acme of spiritual recovery of biblical Christianity in church history and therefore was a sort of golden age of biblical faith. Others might say that the matter with the Reformation was that there was one at all, since it produced the largest schism in church history. That’s not what I mean, however, when I ask about what was the matter with the Protestant Reformation. I’m not using the word matter in the normal way, which typically indicates that something is wrong. When we ask, “What’s the matter with you?” we are assuming that something is wrong or that we’re looking for fault. What I mean, by contrast, is this: What was the essence, the substance, or what is called in philosophy the material cause of the Protestant Reformation? Another way to ask it would be this: What was the chief issue that provoked such massive consequences as this split that occurred in the sixteenth century? When historians consider the causes of the Protestant Reformation, they often use distinctions originally set forth by the philosopher Aristotle, and they distinguish between the formal cause and the material cause . The formal cause, the intellectual background to the issue, was a dispute over the seat of final authority that binds the Christian conscience. We’ll look at that under the heading of sola Scriptura . The material cause , however, the substantive issue that was the core point of dispute, was the doctrine of justification. The Protestant view of this matter is expressed in the shorthand of the Latin phrase sola fide . This is the first of the Latin slogans of the Reformation known as the five solas . They are sola fide , justification is by faith alone; sola gratia , salvation is by grace alone; solus Christus , salvation is through Christ alone; sola Scriptura , the sole authority that binds the conscience of the Christian is the Bible alone; and then, finally, soli Deo gloria , to God alone belongs the glory. Sola fide is shorthand for the central issue of the Reformation, the material cause, which was the question of justification. The Protestant Reformers set forth a doctrine that our justification is by faith and by faith alone without any mixture of good works or merit on our part. To understand sola fide in its historical context, we have to understand something about the theological dispute based on the Roman Catholic understanding of justification. At the heart of this dispute was not a tangential debate over how many angels can dance on the head of a pin or a needless controversy over pedantic points of theology that only academics care about. Rather, this issue touched the very heart of the Christian faith because the question of justification is designed to answer this deeper question: How can an unjust person possibly survive the judgment of a just and holy God? In our day, the doctrine of justification has been degraded in terms of its perceived importance. Historically, the differences among churches over how we obtain a right standing before God were considered significant; those differences have now been minimized as having no great weight. We’re living in a time of relativism, which says that there is no objective truth, and pluralism, which declares that there are many different approaches to truth and views of truth. Therefore, people assert, doctrinal issues should never divide us because what really counts are personal relationships, not doctrine. That notion is propounded even though the New Testament is replete with Apostolic concern about correct doctrine. Sadly, that’s not where the church is in this day and age, and sometimes we have to ask, Why? Some people are in church Sunday after Sunday, are continually exposed to the preaching of the gospel, and are members of the church but have never really committed their lives to Christ. S
articles.content_zh: 新教改革有什么问题? 这似乎是一个奇怪的问题。 有人可能会说"改革"没有问题,它是圣经基督教在教会历史上的精神恢复的一环,因此是某种圣经信仰的黄金时代. 其他人可能会说,改革派的问题是,它完全是一个问题,因为它产生了教会历史上最大的分裂。 我问新教改革有什么问题, 我并不以正常方式使用这个词, 当我们问:“你怎么了? ”我们假设有些事情是错的,或者我们在找错。 我的意思是,反之,这是: 什么是实质,实质,或者哲学中所谓的"新教改革的物质事业"? 另一种方式是问: 十六世纪这种分裂造成如此巨大后果的主要问题是什么? 当历史学家考虑新教改革的原因时,他们经常使用哲学家亚里士多德最初提出的区别,并且区分了形式原因和物质原因. 正式的原因,即问题的知识背景,是对约束基督教良知的最终权威所在地的争议. 我们将在索拉·斯克里普图拉(Sola Scriptura)的标题下审视这一点。 然而,实质原因,即作为争议核心问题的实质性问题,是理由理论。 新教徒对此事的看法用拉丁语中的"sola refine"的简写来表达. 这是改革派的拉丁口号中的第一个, 他们都是虔诚的,只有信仰才是正当的;索拉恩典,只有恩典才有救赎;索卢斯·克赖斯,只有基督才有救赎;索拉·斯克利普图拉,将基督教良知捆绑的唯一权威就是《圣经》;最后,索利·德奥·克罗里亚,光靠上帝才是荣耀。 Sola true是改革这一中心问题的简称,即物质原因,即理由问题。 新教改革者提出了一种理论,即我们的理由仅靠信仰和信仰,而没有任何好的工作和功绩。 为了在历史背景中理解 sola true,我们必须根据罗马天主教对理由的理解来理解神学争议. 这场争论的核心不是一场关于有多少天使可以在一针头上跳舞的微小争论,也不是一场关于只有学者关心的神学的教条点的不必要的争论. 相反,这个问题触动了基督教信仰的核心,因为辩解问题旨在回答这个更深层的问题: 一个不公正的人怎么能活过一个公正和神圣的上帝的判断呢? 在我们这个时代,正当理论在被认为的重要性方面已经退化。 历史上,各教会在如何在上帝面前获得权利问题上的分歧被认为是重大的;这些分歧现在已最小化,因为没有很大的分量。 我们生活在相对主义的时代, 说没有客观的真理, 因此,人们断言,理论问题绝不应该分裂我们,因为真正重要的是个人关系,而不是理论。 尽管《新约》充满了使徒对正确学说的关切,但这一概念还是被提出来。 可悲的是, 教堂现在不是这个时代, 有时我们不得不问, 为什么? 有些人周日后在教堂礼拜,不断被传出福音的传道,并且是教堂的成员,但从未真正为基督献出生命. 页:1

articles.title: 你的忧伤，如何融入福音的故事？
articles.summary: 父亲离世后，迈克尔·凯勒在悲伤中重新认识了基督的爱。福音没有抹去失落，却使他在眼泪中找到安慰，也找到再相见的盼望。
articles.content: 每个人都有自己的故事，而你所处的文化，也在塑造你的故事。在我生活的城市，人们深信一套关于成功的说法：你的价值，取决于上一次的成就，或最近的一次升职。我们也相信另一套说法：只要不断优化自己，找到合适的营养补充剂、多肽制剂、饮食方案，就终于能安心了。一套不言而喻的生活剧本驱使着我们，令人疲惫不堪：我们必须在工作和社交生活中不断积累亮眼的成绩，才能证明自己值得在这个世界占有一席之地。 这些故事不只是一些观念。我们切身感受着它们，也照着它们生活。它们占据我们的想象，支配我们的情绪。可是，当这套剧本不灵了，会怎样？当你守了所有规矩，达成了所有目标，生活却依然轰然坍塌，又该怎么办？ 不久前，我和孩子们一起看了《公主新娘》（ The Princess Bride ）。电影快结束时，剑客伊尼戈·蒙托亚（Inigo Montoya）终于找到了杀父仇人——六指人。眼看就要击败这个追寻多年的仇敌，蒙托亚说：“拿钱来求我饶你。”“好！”那人回答。蒙托亚接着说：“答应给我想要的一切。”“你要什么都行！”那人苦苦哀求。蒙托亚回答：“我要我父亲回来。” 我哭了。这部电影我看过十来遍。几十年来，每次看到这一幕， 我都不曾落泪。但如今不同了。我也想要父亲回来。他几年前去世了，那份悲伤却始终没有离开。它不会离开，因为再多的金钱、权势和成就，都换不回你失去的人。六指人死了，蒙托亚的父亲却依然回不来。 除了基督教所讲述的故事，其他故事都在这里无能为力。身份、权力、自由、道德、真理、幸福、进步，没有一样能给我一个答案，支撑我走过父亲离世后的日子。《公主新娘》前面有一句台词：“死亡无法阻止真爱，最多只能让它迟来一会儿。”对一个在死亡之外毫无盼望的人来说，这句话不过是谎言和幻想。 如果有一个更大的故事，既能指出这些文化故事的不足，又能成全其中那些美好的渴望呢？无论你是委身跟随基督的人，还是心存疑虑、尚未确信的人，都值得探究：是否有一个更美的故事，足以回应我们内心最深的需要与渴望？基督教所讲述的故事，不只是批判我们的故事，更使它们得以圆满。这是怎么做到的？ 福音如何回应我的悲伤 基督教的故事能使我们人生中的许多故事得以圆满，但在悲伤中，我最需要的是它对爱的认识。圣经宣告，神就是爱（约壹 4:8）；我们也承认，这个世界是为爱而造的。真正的爱，是甘愿付出代价、忠诚相守，寻求对方的福祉，单单因为对方值得这样去爱。 这样的爱从何而来？宇宙的中心并不是某个模糊不清的神明，而是三一神——圣父、圣子、圣灵。三个位格彼此相爱，正如约拿单·爱德华兹（Jonathan Edwards） 所说 ，“圣父、圣子、圣灵彼此相爱，这爱无限深厚，超乎我们的理解。”三个位格以我们无法想象的喜乐与能力，将无限的爱倾注于彼此。这“爱的泉源”，“涌流出爱与喜乐的溪流江河，足够所有人饮用、畅游，甚至仿佛以爱的洪流淹没整个世界”。这就是一切存在的核心。爱不只是神所做的事；神就是爱。 可是，如果宇宙的中心是一眼不断涌流的爱泉，为什么我们的世界如此悲伤？为什么有这么多伤害与孤独？ 基督教的故事告诉我们，这是因为人类离开了那爱的泉源。从伊甸园里的亚当和夏娃开始，直到今天的我们，人总以为，没有神也能找到生命。于是，我们在事业、银行存款和爱情里，为自己凿出蓄水池，指望它们满足内心最深的需要。但池里的水不够，无法解我们的渴。这些水源给不了我们终极的意义，因为它们原本就不是为此而设的。圣经的故事告诉我们：我们虽然离开了神，他却没有离开我们。他亲自进入了我们干旱的生命。 在各各他的十字架上，我们最清楚地看见了这一点。神没有要我们先为他付出，自己却先为我们的益处舍己。他亲自为我们受死，显明了那舍己、甘愿付上代价的爱。因此，人要活得丰盛，关键就在于去爱，也寻求从他人领受爱。 当我们信靠这故事所宣告的真理，圣父、圣子、圣灵之间永恒流淌的爱，就将我们也拥入其中。爱德华兹曾试着描绘这一切：蒙救赎的人要将“爱倾注回那爱的泉源；他们从这泉源得到供应，满有爱与荣耀……就这样，他们要活着作王，直到永永远远”。 爱德华兹的意思是，我们在人间经历过最美的爱——真正被了解、被爱，在亲密关系中满心喜悦的时刻——并不是虚幻的，而是让我们预尝一个更伟大的真实。这也是耶稣宣告“我就是道路、真理、生命；若不藉着我，没有人能到父那里去”的意思（约 14:6）。他是在说：“人心对意义、真理与生命最深的渴望，最终都要在认识我、与我同在中得到满足。” 我以为失去的，在耶稣里找到了 如果一切存在的中心是一位有位格的主，那么人生最深的悲剧，就是失去我们所爱的人。神学就在这里与我们的亲身经历相遇。对我来说，那是在一个主日早晨，恰好是父亲去世一周年。几个月前就定好的讲道主题，是如何赞美神。可我自己在悲伤中，连赞美他都如此艰难，又怎能站上讲台，教人赞美神呢？ 预备讲章时，我重读了爱德华兹 1741 年在叔父葬礼上所讲的一篇道，题为《将丧亲之痛陈明在耶稣面前》（ The Sorrows of the Bereaved Spread Before Jesus ）。临近结束时，爱德华兹转向婶母和她那些正在哭泣的孩子，说了一番话，直入人心： 孩子们……如今，你们为亲爱的父亲离世而哀哭，不知该往哪里去，也不知该怎么办。你们再也得不到父亲智慧的引导，不能再让他温柔的爱安慰你们、使你们欢喜，也不能再靠他慈爱的照料得到保护与帮助……但在蒙福的耶稣里，在你们父亲的主与救赎主里面，你们所能得着的，比这一切还要多。你们父亲身上的美德，使他成为你们莫大的祝福；而这些美德，不过是基督美德的映照。 作者这样概括爱德华兹对孩子们的劝勉，大意是：“你们的父亲固然可敬可爱，但使他成为这样一位父亲的一切——他给你们的爱、他拥有的智慧——全都来自耶稣。所以，当你们来到耶稣面前，就会发现，父亲虽然离世了，但他给你们的爱与智慧，都来自耶稣。来到耶稣面前，你们仍能从那爱的源头得着供应。” 那一刻，我独自坐在书房里，身边放着父亲的笔记，泪水涌上眼眶，但那不是绝望的泪。我的故事融入了耶稣正在这个世界展开的救赎故事。这意味着，父亲并没有就此消失，他身上一切美好的、我所深爱的，都来自耶稣。 无论你失去的是父亲、母亲，还是朋友，他们身上那些美好、可敬的品格，你随时都能在耶稣里寻见。你渴望那份安慰吗？耶稣就在这里。你怀念那份恩慈吗？耶稣就在这里。你需要那样的智慧吗？耶稣拥有它。你想念那份耐心吗？这一切都在耶稣里面。 我们该如何面对忧伤与悲痛？不要忽视它们，不要压下自己的感受，也不要一味用属灵的话把它们掩盖过去。要将这一切带进神的爱里，在他的性情中找到安慰。无论你失去了家人、朋友、名声还是财富，都将这份失落浸入神的爱中——这爱已经在耶稣成就的救赎中显明。你会发现，赞美与喜乐开始一点点流出，最终奔涌而出。在耶稣里，爱确实得胜了。死亡真的只让相聚迟来一会儿。我终将再见到父亲。 让你的故事融入他的故事 让基督的故事使你的故事得以圆满，意思就是如此。每个人生故事中那些美好的渴望，以及对真理虽不完全却真实的认识，都在他里面得到成全。当我们忧伤低落时，需要一次次记起：耶稣已经真正胜过死亡。知道我们所能遭遇的最坏之事已经被击败，会改变一切。你愿意让这真理改变你吗？ 父亲离世已经有一段时间了。我原以为，再也得不到他的智慧、关爱、恩慈和鼓励。但当我在耶稣的故事中扎下根，开始发现，一个人的离去，竟能让我更清楚地看见主的同在。父亲走后，我才意识到，以前有多少次，我去找爸爸，却没有在祷告中来到天父面前。自从父亲去世，我更多地呼求耶稣，也更深地需要他。其实，他一直都在，只是从前我没有这样迫切地寻求他。 神竟能把我们的苦难与悲伤，编织进一个更宏大的盼望与救赎的故事，岂不奇妙吗？他使用那些最令我们伤痛的事，不是要宣告人生就此结束，而是要向我们显明，他为我们预备了何等丰富的恩典。你正在寻求什么，以致不再寻求他？你紧抓着哪一种文化所讲述的故事、哪一种虚假的盼望、哪一套不足以支撑人生的说法？那些你以为不可或缺的东西，如今不在了，会不会恰好为耶稣进入你的生命打开了一扇门？ 也许，在最深的失落中，你会开始更清楚地看见耶稣的同在。也许，你以为人生脱离剧本的那一刻，恰恰是你的故事融入神救赎与更新的大故事之时。这个故事邀请我们，把最深的忧伤带到救主面前。他在悲痛中与我们相遇，更在十字架上亲自承担、回应了我们的痛苦。 看见耶稣，会改变我们的故事。如果你让他成为生命的中心，他的同在不会让你不再感到失落。但你会发现，那些曾经带给你喜乐的、你所怀念的，甚至可能永远失去的美好，最终都能在他里面寻见。你愿意把自己的悲伤、忧愁和失望，都浸入他的爱中吗？ 以下三个操练，可以帮助你这样做。 第一，在读经和祷告中，定睛仰望耶稣。 读经不要只为获取知识，要继续默想，直到所读的真理对你变得真切。我们知道怎样仔细阅读文献、分析内容，也应当以同样认真的态度读圣经。 同时，你不只是研读圣经，也要让圣经光照、鉴察你的内心。定睛默想圣经，就是在经文前停留，直到你真切地认识神的性情。问问自己：如果今天我比昨天更深地相信这段经文，我的生活会有什么不同？ 当圣经的真理充满你的思想，你就能让头脑所知道的，逐渐进入心里。祷告时，不要只是提出请求，也要安静在他面前。仅在理智上认识耶稣，与亲身经历他的爱和恩典，是不同的。你不只是知道许多关于神的事，更要真实地经历他的爱。 第二，走进群体，寻找爱人和服侍人的机会。 基督教的故事从来都关乎群体。我们不只是各自寻找人生意义的个人，而是同一个身体上的肢体，是神家里的人。孤身一人时，文化中的各种故事对我们的影响最强。在真正的群体生活中——不只是偶尔出席聚会，也不只是经营人脉——即使你忘记了真理，也会有人向你说出真

articles.title: 不问对错，先贴标签：路易斯揭露现代思想的常见谬误
articles.summary: “你这么说，还不是因为你是……”这句话看似揭穿了对方，却可能绕开了真正的问题：他说的究竟对不对？路易斯用一个虚构人物的故事，揭露了这种以揣测动机代替认真论证的常见谬误。
articles.content: 布拉德·利特尔约翰（Brad Littlejohn）在 一篇文章 中写道： 怀特海（Whitehead）和佩里（Perry）所做的这类分析，说到底，不过是把“布佛式论证”变成了一套系统化的做法。他们不去说明一个人的观点究竟错在哪里，而是把那些他们不认同的观点归因于某种身份，再以此为由，将这些观点一并否定。这在逻辑上根本站不住脚。 “布佛式论证”（Bulverism）是C. S. 路易斯发明的一个词，指的是一种随处可见的逻辑谬误：“你这么说，无非因为你是个____（男人／女人／民主党人／共和党人／基督徒／无神论者，等等）。” 其中最恶劣的做法，是借助人为建构的标签或身份，例如“基督教国族主义”，来否定别人的观点。 他们先观察到某些观点之间存在关联：相信X的人，也更可能相信Y。接着，他们造出一个标签，来概括这种关联。 然后，他们反过来说，正是这个标签所代表的身份，导致人们持有这些观点。这样一来，他们既把相关性混同于因果关系，又陷入了循环论证。 由于他们早已认定，这一整套观念中的某个部分令人反感，这种所谓的因果联系便成了他们否定整套观念的理由。 路易斯在 1941 年的文章《布佛式论证》（Bulverism）中，解释了自己为什么创造这个词： 你必须先证明一个人确实错了，才能解释他为什么会持有这种错误观点。 现代人的做法却是，不加讨论就认定对方错了，然后忙着解释他怎么会变得如此愚蠢，借此转移他的注意力，让他不再追问自己究竟有没有错——而这才是唯一真正需要讨论的问题。 过去十五年间，我发现这种毛病实在太普遍，只好给它起个名字。我称之为“布佛式论证”。将来有一天，我要为它那位虚构的发明者——以西结·布佛（Ezekiel Bulver）——写一部传记。他五岁时，命运就已注定。那天，他听见父亲坚持说，三角形任意两边之和大于第三边，母亲却对父亲说：“哼，你这么说，还不是因为你是个男人。”布佛向我们保证：“就在那一刻，我幼小的心灵忽然领悟了一条伟大的真理：跟人争论，原来根本不必反驳他的论点。只要认定对手错了，再解释他为什么会错，整个世界就会拜倒在你脚下。可你若试图证明他错了，或是更糟，想弄清他究竟是对是错，你就会被这个时代的强大潮流挤到一边。” 布佛就这样成了塑造二十世纪的人物之一。 假设我算完账，认为自己在银行里还有一大笔存款。你想知道，这是不是我的“一厢情愿”。单凭分析我的心理状态，你永远得不出答案。要弄清楚，唯一的办法就是坐下来，亲自把账算一遍。只有核对了那些数字，你才知道我到底有没有这笔钱。如果我的账算得没错，那么，无论你怎样对我的心理状态高谈阔论，都只是在浪费时间。如果我的账算错了，从心理层面解释我为什么会算得这么差，或许才有意义；所谓“隐藏的愿望”也才可能与此有关。但前提是，你已经亲自算过，并且单凭算术就确认我错了。一切思考和思想体系都是如此。如果你想靠揣测一个人内心的愿望，来判断他的思想是否有问题，那只会让自己出洋相。你必须先从逻辑上检验，哪些论证确实站不住脚。之后，你若愿意，再去探究这些错误背后的心理原因。 一旦看清“布佛式论证”的谬误，你就会发现它无处不在，尤其是在讨论当代福音派的书籍和各种热点评论中。 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： C. S. Lewis on the Ubiquitous Fallacy that Lies at the Foundation of Modern Thought .

articles.summary: Several features indicate that the eyewitness accounts of Simon stand behind Mark’s Gospel.
articles.summary_zh: 有几个特征表明，西门的目击者叙述支持马可福音。
articles.title_zh: 西蒙说：马可福音中不明显的目击者证据
articles.content: When I watch Jesus films, whether the current series The Chosen , The Passion of the Christ in the early 2000s , or even Godspell from the 1970s, I can’t help but ask, Where did they get those stories? Sometimes I can piece together bits from Matthew, Mark, Luke, or John. Occasionally I detect legendary material from church history or the apocryphal gospels. But at other times, my best guess is “They made it up,” and I ascribe the scene to creative liberty. When we turn to the Gospel of Mark, which most scholars see as the first extant telling of the story of Jesus, we might also wonder, Where did Mark get these stories? Around the 1920s to ’50s, the fashionable scholarly answer was found in a field of study known as form criticism . This enterprise tried to tie different sayings and stories of Jesus back to an occasion within the early church that would have prompted their creation. Though the heyday of form criticism has passed, the legacy of seeing the Gospels as a “mixtape” of various ad hoc literary traditions can still be seen today. In contrast to form criticism and the Jesus-film industry, the canonical Gospels are sourced in eye-witness testimony and were written within living memory of the events they describe. Perhaps no other scholar has written so persuasively on this subject as Richard Bauckham in his magisterial Jesus and the Eyewitnesses . Indications of eye-witness testimony are peppered throughout Mark’s gospel. Here we will consider just a few, each revolving around the name “Simon.” These are more obscure than what normally make their way into works on apologetics, but their subtlety is a strength since they are not the kind of details one fabricates. We will discover that inconspicuous indicators of eyewitnesses reveal what is happening behind the scenes more than front-and-center observations. Evidence of Simon Peter There are signs that Simon Peter has been a significant source for Mark’s Gospel, despite Mark not making a show of it. The church father Papias famously stated that Mark was Peter’s interpreter, who wrote down what he remembered from his preaching. Though many scholars doubt Papias here, Mark goes out of his way to emphasize Simon Peter. Several features indicate that Mark is particularly told from a Petrine perspective. For example, his prominence verges on redundancy when he is introduced in 1:16: “Passing alongside the Sea of Galilee, [Jesus] saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.” This is part of what Bauckham calls a Peter inclusio, so that his testimony brackets the Gospel of Mark (see 16:7). Later in the narrative, those “sick or oppressed by demons” are brought to Jesus in Capernaum (1:32), the summary after the climactic exorcism at the synagogue (vv. 21–28). But sandwiched in the middle is the healing of Simon’s mother-in-law (vv. 29–31). Similarly, Mark writes of when the disciples look for Jesus, “Simon and those who were with him searched for him” (v. 36). Details like these betray a “Simon-centric” source. Bauckham argues that, with few exceptions, “Peter is actually present through a large proportion of the narrative from 1:16 to 14:72.” Several features indicate that Mark is particularly told from a Petrine perspective. An oddity in Mark’s grammatical style reinforces not just Simon Peter’s perspective but that of all the disciples: Mark uniquely favors using plural verbs to introduce singular ones. For example, Mark 11:12 reads, “On the following day, when they came from Bethany, he [Jesus] was hungry” (emphasis added). This provides the perspective of the group, as opposed to Matthew’s retelling: “In the morning, as he was returning to the city, he became hungry” (21:18). This literary device occurs 21 times in Mark’s narrative. Evidence of Many Simons The name “Simon” occurs 11 times in Mark. It most famously refers to Peter (1:16 [twice], 29, 30, 36; 3:16; 14:37), but it also refers to the other apostle, “Simon the Z
articles.content_zh: 当我看耶稣的电影时,无论是现在的系列"选择"(The Chosen, The Passion of the Christ in 20世纪20年代早期),还是甚至从20世纪70年代起的"神话"(Godspell),我都不得不问,他们从哪里得到这些故事的? 有时我可以拼凑出马修,马克,卢克或约翰的位子. 偶尔我也会从教堂历史或启示录中 发现传奇材料 但在其他时候,我的最佳猜测是“他们编造的”,我把场景描述为创造性的自由。 当我们转向"马克福音"时,大多数学者认为它是第一个讲述耶稣故事的现存者,我们也可能会想,"马克从哪里得到这些故事的? 20世纪20至50年代, 时髦的学术答案出现在一个研究领域, 这个事业试图把耶稣的不同说法和故事与早期教会内部本来会促使他们创造的机会联系起来. 尽管形式批评的热潮已经过去,但今天仍然可以看到将福音书视为各种临时文学传统“混合”的遗产。 与形而上学的批评和耶稣-电影行业形成对比的是,"神舟福音"来源于目击证人的证词并被写在了他们描述的事件活生生的记忆中. 可能没有其他学者如此有说服力地写了 理查德·鲍克汉姆 在他的大法官耶稣和目击证人。 在马克的福音中, 在这里,我们将只考虑几个,每个环绕“西蒙”的名称。 这些比平时在古琴系上的工作更为模糊,但是其微妙性是一种力量,因为它们不是一种编织出来的细节。 我们将发现,目击证人的不显眼指标显示在幕后发生的情况比前中观察更明显。 西蒙·彼得的证据 有迹象表明西蒙·彼得一直是"马克福音"的重要出处,尽管马克没有对此表态. 教父帕皮亚斯出名地说,马克是彼得的翻译,他记下了他在布道时所记得的. 虽然许多学者怀疑这里有帕皮阿斯,但马克却不择手段地强调西蒙·彼得. 一些特征表明,马克尤其被从Petrine的角度讲述. 例如,在1:16介绍他时,他的突出之处是冗余:“[耶稣]在加利利海一并看到西蒙的兄弟西蒙和安德鲁将网投入大海,因为他们是渔民。” 这是Bauckham称之为"彼得·因克利奥"的一部分,因此他的证词将马克福音(见16:7)置于其中. 后来在叙事中,那些"被恶魔所生病或被压迫"的人被带到了卡佩尔瑙姆的耶稣面前(1:32),即犹太会堂的高潮驱魔后的摘要(v. 21–28). 但中间的三明治是西蒙婆婆(vv. 29–31)的治愈. 同样地,马克写道,当门徒们寻找耶稣时,“西蒙和与他在一起的人寻找他”(v.36)。 这些细节背叛了“以西蒙为中心”的来源。 Bauckham认为,除了少数例外,“彼得实际上通过1:16至14:72的很大一部分叙述存在。” 一些特征表明,马克尤其被从Petrine的角度讲述. 马克语法风格的奇特之处不仅强化了西蒙·彼得的观点,而且强化了所有门徒的观点: 使用复数动词标记独有的偏好来引入单数。 例如,Mark 11:12写道:“第二天,当他们从Bethany来时,他[耶稣]饿了”(着重号由作者标明)。 这提供了这个团体的视角,而不是马修的重述:"早上,当他回到城市时,他变得饥饿"(21:18). 这个文学装置在马克的叙述中发生21次. 许多西蒙的证据 “西蒙”这个名字在马克有11次出现。 最出名的是彼得(1:16 [两次],29,30,36;3:16;14:37),但也指另一位使徒"Simon the Z".
articles.author: Bruce Henning

articles.summary: The world watched the news in horror as the sightseeing helicopter flying over the river tore into pieces. As the main rotor and tail broke off, the cabin plunged into the waters below, with the pilot and a family of five trapped inside. Just days after the tragedy that had taken the lives of his sister, brother-in-law, niece, and two nephews, the brother was at the site honoring his loved ones.

articles.title: Works & Wonders: October 25
articles.summary: This week’s Works & Wonders: God’s wisdom and power aimed at our good, a 7.5-hour trip around the earth, top wildlife photos, bird radio, and new songs. See Also Works & Wonders (Oct 11) Works & Wonders (September 27) Works & Wonders (August 30)
articles.summary_zh: 本周的工作与奇迹：上帝的智慧和力量瞄准了我们的好处，环游地球7.5小时的旅程，顶级野生动物照片，鸟类广播和新歌。另请参阅作品与奇观（ 10月11日）作品与奇观（ 9月27日）作品与奇观（ 8月30日）

articles.content: In my weekly Works & Wonders column, I combine a brief devotional with other interesting and uplifting bits and pieces I gleaned throughout the week. I hope you enjoy this week’s collection! It includes: What a God We Serve! (A Devotional) Ambient Earth Wildlife Photographer of the Year What Animals Can You Outrun? Who Would Have Dreamed 🎵 Bird Radio Who Is Like the Lord? 🎵 1. What a God We Serve! God has wisdom to know what is best and wisdom to know how to accomplish it by the best possible means. He also has power to execute it all. But we may wonder, as it pertains to us, what is his will? What does his wisdom determine is best? What is he accomplishing through the execution of his power? The book of Romans contains words of tremendous comfort: “And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose” (Romans 8:28). God’s will is our good, which means that God’s wisdom and power are directed at accomplishing what is ultimately for our good, and accomplishing it all in the best ways. All the things we experience, all the things we undergo, all the things we endure, all the things we celebrate and lament, the things that make us laugh and cry—all of them are born of God’s love, directed at our good, and executed in a way that is nothing short of perfect. What a God we serve! And what a God we worship today. 2. Ambient Earth Ambient Earth is a great project! A guy named Seán Doran took 49,000 of Butch Wilmore’s photos taken aboard the International Space Station, then repaired, remastered, and retimed them to create an incredible 7.5-hour, 4K journey around the earth. He also added Chris Hadfield’s recording of the sounds of the ISS, which honestly gets a bit annoying, so you may want to mute it and then put on some nice instrumental music in its place. This is a great video to just leave playing on a TV in a public place. (While we’re on the subject of Butch Wilmore, he’s a believer and recently wrote Stuck in Space , which you may enjoy.) 3. Wildlife Photographer of the Year I always enjoy a good photography contest and, for whatever reason, this is the time of the year when many of them announce their winners. That’s the case with the Wildlife Photographer of the Year contest, which had 65,000 entries from 121 countries and territories. That link leads to The Atlantic ‘s gallery of highlights, though if you prefer to see the official site, you can find it here . As you’d expect, many of the photos are nothing short of stunning. 4. What Animals Can You Outrun? I suppose we all wonder at one time or another whether we would be able to outrun certain animals. The BBC did some research to find out which animals we’d possibly be able to outrun and the ones we definitely wouldn’t. Overall, the news isn’t particularly good. It’s a good thing God made us smart, since he didn’t make us particularly fast. See: The animals you can’t outrun – and the ones you can . 5. Who Would Have Dreamed Over a decade ago, Sovereign Grace Music released a Christmas album titled Prepare Him Room . I guess they have dusted off that album and decided to give it new life by recording a live version of it. I’m glad they’ve done so, because it has some really good songs on it. My favorite, and one we sing seasonally at Grace Fellowship Church, is also the first track they’ve re-released: “ Who Would Have Dreamed .” 6. Bird Radio Bird Radio is a neat concept—you simply tune in to hear the calls of different birds from all around the world. God displays his creativity in many different ways and the sheer variety of bird calls is a pretty impressive one. (Also on the subject of birds, did you know the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service maintains a feather atlas so you can learn about the ones you happen to find?) 7. Bonus: Who Is Like the Lord? That well-known and much-loved songwriting combination of Matt/Matt/Keith/Kristyn released a new song this week: “ Who Is Like the Lord? “ Whose wisdom s
articles.content_zh: 在每周的Works & Wonders专栏中,我把简短的奉献与我整个星期所收集的其他有趣而令人振奋的作品结合起来。 希望你们能欣赏这周的作品! 它包括:我们所崇拜的神! 地球野生生物年度摄影师, 谁会梦见"鸟之电台" "谁像上帝"? 上帝有智慧,知道什么是最佳的,有智慧,知道如何用尽可能好的手段完成它. 他也有权力执行这一切。 但是,我们可能会怀疑,它与我们有关,他的意志是什么? 他的智慧决定什么是最好的? 他通过行使权力取得了什么成就? 罗马人书中载有令人极为慰藉的话:“我们知道,对于热爱上帝的人来说,一切事情都为善而工作,对于按照他的目的被召唤的人来说”(罗马人8:28)。 上帝的旨意是我们的好意,这意味着上帝的智慧和力量旨在完成最终为我们造福的事业,并以最好的方式完成这一切. 我们所经历的一切,我们所经历的一切,我们所忍受的一切,我们所庆贺和哀叹的一切,我们所欢笑和哭泣的一切——所有这一切都是由上帝的爱所生出,以我们的利益为目标,并以完全完美的方式被处决. 我们所崇拜的神啊! 今天我们崇拜的神是什么? 2. 地球环境是一个伟大的项目! 一位名叫Seán Doran的人在国际空间站上拍摄了49,000张布奇·威尔莫尔的照片,随后修复,重新制作,并重新定时,创造了令人难以置信的7.5小时4K环绕地球的旅程. 他还加入了克里斯·哈德菲尔德(Chris Hadfield)对国际空间站声音的录制, 老实说,这有点烦人,所以你可能想关掉它,然后用一些很好的器乐代替它。 这是一个伟大的视频 只是离开 在电视播放 在公共场所。 (虽然我们讨论的是Butch Wilmore, 他是一个信徒, 3. " 我年度野生生物摄影师 " 一向享受良好的摄影比赛,无论出于何种原因,今年是许多人宣布获奖者的时刻。 今年野生生物摄影师的比赛就是这样, 但若你想看到官方网站, 照片中有许多是惊人的。 4. 什么动物能跑出? 我想我们都会在某个时候怀疑 我们是否能够跑出某些动物 BBC做了一些研究, 找出哪些动物能跑得远, 总体来说, 幸好上帝让我们聪明, 见:你跑不掉的动物,以及你能跑的动物。 5. 10多年前,Who would have Dreamed over a 10 years ago, West Grace Music发行了一张圣诞节专辑"准备他的房间". 我猜他们把这张专辑弄得一团糟 决定通过录制一个现场版本来给它新的生活 我很高兴他们这样做了, 因为上面有很棒的歌曲。 我最喜欢的,还有我们在格蕾丝联谊会(Grace Fellowship Church)上季节性地唱的一首曲子,也是他们重新发行的第一首曲子: “谁会做梦 ” 。 Bird Radio Bird Radio是一个很好的概念, 神以多种不同的方式展现出他的创造力,鸟叫的种类繁多,令人印象深刻. (关于鸟类,你是否知道美国鱼类和野生动物服务局维持了羽毛图集,以便你了解你偶然找到的?) 7. 奖金:谁像主? 马特/马特/凯斯/克里斯廷的这首著名和受人喜爱的歌曲的组合本周发行了一首新歌:“谁像主?”

articles.title: 成年子女为何会与父母断绝往来？
articles.summary: 意见不同，为何竟成了与父母断绝往来的理由？《断联》追问这股风潮背后的文化根源，也探讨我们如何在分歧中守护亲情，以谦卑和恩典寻求和好。
articles.content: 在美国，成年子女与父母断绝往来的现象，正引起越来越多的关注。对长期遭受虐待和忽视的人来说，断联可能是走投无路时的最后选择。但如今，也有越来越多的人仅仅因为政治观点不同，就与父母切断一切联系，拒绝任何和好的尝试。 伦理与公共政策中心（Ethics and Public Policy Center）研究员诺埃尔·梅林（Noelle Mering）在《断联：一种蛊惑人心的意识形态如何撕裂亲友关系，以及我们如何修复》（ No Contact: How a Seductive Ideology Broke Families and Friendships and How We Can Repair Them ）一书中，分析了主动与家人断绝关系的趋势，以及这种分离带来的后果。她写道：“那种痛苦令人难以承受，而且始终无法释怀。人去世了……事情就有了终点，你会经历哀伤，但最终慢慢往前走。然而，断联却不一样。”（214 页）这是一道始终难以愈合的伤口。 书中一些年轻人，仅仅因为家人看似微小的过失，就与他们断绝往来，给家人留下沉重的伤痛。一名男子怀疑母亲把票投给了他不支持的候选人，便与她断绝关系。另一名女子则因为父亲对她姊妹的性别转换不够热情，停止了与父亲的一切沟通。这些亲身讲述，既是本书最有力量、也最令人难以卒读的部分：它们让人看清现实，也令人心碎、震惊。 基督徒需要认识“断联”运动是什么、从何而来，以及我们可以如 何抵挡它。 《断联：一种蛊惑人心的意识形态如何撕裂亲友关系，以及我们如何修复》 （No Contact: How a Seductive Ideology Broke Families and Friendships and How We Can Repair Them） 诺埃尔·梅林 在《断联》一书中，梅林结合访谈与历史研究，指出推动“断联”运动兴起的五个主要因素：身份政治、消解家庭的神圣意义、心理治疗文化、将受害者视为绝不会错的一方，以及伴随属灵衰退而来的自恋文化。她揭示了这场破坏关系的运动背后的力量，以及它们如何影响个人、家庭和社会，帮助读者看清正在发生的事，勇于面对，并与家人一同医治伤痛、修复和巩固关系。 论坛出版社（Forum），288 页。 像野火一样蔓延的“断联” 梅林指出，“断联”运动正在 年轻成年人 中像野火一样蔓延。这是多种因素共同作用的结果，包括 心理治疗文化 的兴起、强调忠于内心感受和表达自我的表现型个人主义的盛行，以及对家庭的刻意解构。 过去，“创伤”指的是“参战或在火车事故中幸存这类异常、灾难性事件”造成的严重心理伤害。如今，人们却用这个词描述“政治分歧或情感需求未被满足”所带来的不适（18–19 页）。童年中那些令人不快、却属正常范围的经历，如今也被贴上“创伤”的标签，成为与父母断绝关系的理由。 有些所谓的创伤听起来或许言过其实，却因为属于个人的“亲身经历”，便被视为不容质疑。帕特里克·蒂汉（Patrick Teahan）这类“断联”导师向子女保证，他们的直觉和感受是正确的，任何人都无权质疑。若父母认为，成年子女“受到了心理治疗师或TikTok的不当影响”，那只不过进一步证明了父母自身“有毒”。蒂汉甚至提出，如果兄弟姊妹不“全力支持”你的“断联”决定，你可能也需要与他们断绝往来（22 页）。这简直是将 表现型个人主义 推向了极端。 文化对家庭的解构，也使人更愿意斩断亲情。家庭不再被视为归属、成长和安定的来源，反而成了限制个性、强求一致、施加压迫的场所。在一个追求不受约束的自主权和个人自我表达的文化中，就连家庭所要求的责任与牵挂，也成了个人自主权不可容忍的束缚。 放在更大的背景下看 梅林书中记述的案例，大多是政治立场偏左的子女，与立场偏右、信仰宗教的父母之间的冲突。她承认，这种倾向可能来自样本选择上的偏差，也一再提醒，保守派同样可能陷入其中某些不健康的思维和行为模式。 不过，卡托研究所（Cato Institute）2021 年的一项 调查 发现，与立场坚定的保守派相比，立场坚定的自由派因社交媒体帖文而拉黑或删除好友的可能性接近两倍，举报他人的可能性则超过两倍。同样，公共宗教研究所（PRRI）2024 年的一项 调查 发现，23%的民主党人表示，他们会因为某些家人的政治观点而减少与其相处的时间；共和党人的这一比例则是 5%。因意见不同而疏远家人的，往往是政治进步派。 考虑到“断联”运动背后的观念源自卡尔·马克思（Karl Marx）、赫伯特·马尔库塞（Herbert Marcuse）、西奥多·阿多诺（Theodor Adorno）和威廉·赖希（Wilhelm Reich）所代表的左翼批判传统，这种差异也就不难理解。在这种思想看来，家庭是“资本主义、父权制和殖民体系的产物，强化了不平等与压迫”（82 页）。父母则是一个压迫者阶层，将自己的价值观和规范强加给子女。 梅林看到了一个关键问题：今天，许多政治分歧源于世界观的分歧。她写道：“过去，政治争论通常是在讨论，怎样才能最好地实现一个共同目标……今天，争论不只是关乎手段，更关乎目的，所涉及的问题直指人的本质。”（14 页）因此，预防尤为重要。基督徒父母必须教导孩子，辨认并拒绝那些与圣经关于人的身份、公义和罪的教导 根本不相容 的意识形态。 扑灭这场火 除了世界观方面的教导，父母还可以从其他方面巩固与子女的关系。梅林劝勉家庭“积攒丰富的美好回忆”，提醒父母“按照孩子所处的世界来养育他们，而不是照着自己长大的那个世界”，也要警惕社交媒体，倾听时以理解为目的，而不是急于批评（229 页）。 这些建议很有智慧，却也带出一个重要问题：如果某些政治立场确实反映了一个人的品格呢？在一些明显的例子中，我们已经承认这一点。假如邻居真心支持纳粹主义，认为它是好的，这就显明了他品格中某些不可忽视的问题。当政治涉及奴隶制、堕胎或生殖器残割等不义行为时，我们就无法把政治与道德截然分开。 与其天真地坚持政治观点与品格无关，圣经为我们指出了另一条路。梅林转述亚历山大·索尔仁尼琴（Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn）的名言，恰好体现了这一点：“善恶的分界线，不是在不同群体或政治阵营之间，而是在每个人的内心。”（234 页）作为基督徒，我们的政治立场理当以道德律为根基；但也正是这道德律，宣告我们都是违背律法的人。政治判断正确的人和政治判断错误的人，都是需要福音的罪人。 认识到这一点，无论在私人关系中，还是在公共生活中，我们都应当更加温柔、谦卑。正因为我们同样需要神的恩典，我们才能爱那些在重大问题上与自己意见不同的人。梅林在《断联》中提醒我们：我们的盼望，不在于自己能把孩子教养得尽善尽美，而在于神借着基督的十字架与复活更新万有。 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： Why Adult Children Are Cutting Off Their Parents 。

articles.title: What My Grandparents Taught Me About Pastoral Ministry
articles.summary: You’re being prepared for the work the Lord has for you in ways you may not understand until you’re standing in a hospice living room.

articles.title_zh: 关于牧灵事工，我的祖父母教会了我什么
articles.content: When I was in high school, and early on during the summers in college, I spent my days working at a local pharmacy. I got a one-hour lunch break, and I ended up going almost every day to lunch at my favorite place: Granny and PawPaw’s house. I don’t remember how it started. One day, I drove over on my lunch break, and after that, it became my routine. They wanted to see me, and I wanted to see them. Sitting at their table instead of alone at a restaurant was comfortable and unhurried. At the time, I didn’t think much about it. I was just eating lunch with my grandparents. But looking back, I realize the Lord was doing more than I understood. Having now sat beside countless hospital beds and in living rooms with families walking through suffering, I can see how those lunches prepared me for ministry in ways I didn’t yet understand. My grandparents taught me how to slow down, listen, and simply be present with people. PawPaw When we ate, my grandfather talked mostly about his time serving in the Korean War, his years as an insurance agent for Liberty National, or fishing, which he loved almost as much as anything in the world. Courtesy Jared Cornutt Of the three topics, he talked about Korea the most. The war had ended decades earlier, but it hadn’t really ended for him. It shaped the rest of his life. PawPaw survived the war; he never escaped it. He talked around it in the way men of his generation often did when they carried wounds no one had given them language for. They wanted to see me, and I wanted to see them. At the time, I didn’t think much about it. I was just eating lunch with my grandparents. When I sat across from him at that table, I didn’t know what PTSD was. I just knew Korea was never far from his mind. Now I realize why. My PawPaw came home from the war during an era when PTSD wasn’t understood. Men like him were told to put the war behind them. They were expected to come home, go to work, raise a family, and move on. Many did. But many, like my grandfather, carried the war with them for the rest of their lives. As a boy, I didn’t understand that. I just knew him first as my grandfather, and I knew he loved me. I’m thankful that’s how I got to know him. Granny My grandmother had an tenth-grade education. She grew up on a farm in a poverty she also never fully escaped. She never had much of a formal education, but I can tell you this: She knew the Lord, and the Lord knew her. If you heard her whole story, you might call her life a tragedy. But due to her remarkable faith, she wouldn’t describe it that way. Courtesy Jared Cornutt I can still see her sitting in that rocking chair when I’d come over, reading glasses on and her Bible open in her lap. She was eager to tell me what she’d read that morning. She loved God’s Word because she needed it and depended on it. Every time I left her house, she’d tell me the same thing: “I’m praying for you.” That meant more to me than any gift she could’ve ever given, because I knew she wasn’t just saying it. She really was praying for me . I now know there was much about her life I didn’t understand. But what stayed with me was that my grandmother loved Jesus, loved his Word, and faithfully prayed for her grandson. The Lord didn’t answer every prayer she prayed the way she hoped. But I’ve often wondered how many of God’s kindnesses in my life came through Granny’s faithful prayers. Ministry Now I share all this because I recently sat in another living room. It was different, but it felt oddly familiar. As I left that room, it dawned on me almost immediately that I was equipped to minister there only because of those lunches years before. Every time I left her house, she’d tell me the same thing: ‘I’m praying for you.’ That meant more to me than any gift she could’ve ever given. articles.title_zh: 周末点菜（ 10月24日）
articles.content: Good morning. This Weekend edition of A La Carte has some long-form content, some think pieces, some lists of the most popular articles from the week gone by, and a whole collection of recommendations from readers like you. Enjoy! Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include books on sexuality, forgiveness, Habakkuk, Revelation, and more. Recommended Reading Not everyone is familiar with the term concupiscence , but most of us are familiar with some of the debates surrounding it. For example, are our unholy desires sinful, or is it only sinful to act out on those desires? This question often arises when we discuss same-sex attraction. Writing for Logos, Mark Jones explores the concept of concupiscence from a Reformed perspective. In brief, concupiscence (concupiscentia) originates from the Latin verb concupisco, which means ‘to ardently desire.’ There are proper, non-sinful forms of desire, which we would call ‘non-sinful concupiscence.’ For example, Jesus said to his disciples, ‘I have earnestly desired [ἐπεθύμησα] to eat this Passover with you before I suffer’ (Luke 22:15). But because we live in a fallen world, concupiscence typically has in view sinful desire, and usually in reference to sinful sexual desires. Because sin is the privation (lack) of righteousness and proneness to evil, concupiscence involves not just the acts but the desire of the person. Sinful concupiscence can be understood from God’s moral law: ‘You shall not covet’ (Exod 20:17). Concupiscence: Are Our Unholy Desires Sinful? The Guardian tells a strange and twisting tale of a death, a scandal, and a desire for revenge, which it summarizes like this: “After his mother died, Otto became convinced he’d been wronged by the forensic investigators – and that one of them was a fraud. The truth was even stranger.” Here’s how the article begins: On a balmy, quiet evening in June 2020, Otto’s elderly mother, Doria, was fading in her Munich apartment. As she lay with her eyes closed, her pale face, framed by her white hair, was calm. Otto, masked, gloved and draped in a sterile apron, dozed in a chair beside her. Otto, who sometimes goes by the name Rainer, and whose last name is only known as “Z” because of Germany’s strict privacy laws, was a doctor who had cared for his mother for years, ever since she had suffered a stroke and moved in with him. He described the course of that night to me. He woke to the sound of her short breath and tried to sit her upright. Her eyes were shut, and her lips pursed. She stopped breathing. Otto reached for his phone to call for help, but then Doria opened her eyes and stared into his. She smiled, drew one last deep breath, shut her eyes again, and lay still. A Death, a Plagiarism Scandal and a Quest for Revenge: The Bizarre Tale of Otto Z. Jonathon Van Maren sees Beatrix Potter as an example of true conservatism, and explains why that’s the case in a really interesting article about the life of someone whose work we are probably all familiar with. There is a type of academic who can only get noticed by attacking the legacies of greater men and women, and a prime example was cited by Matthew Dennison in The Spectator in his essay “Don’t Cancel Beatrix Potter.” The beloved children’s author has become the target of “specialist in postcolonial literature” Dr. Emily Zobel Marshall, who hilariously claims that Potter failed “to acknowledge her indebtedness to an oral storytelling tradition of enslaved Africans working on American plantations” and that this contributes to “a damaging and recurring appropriation of Black cultural forms that continues today.” This is frivolous stuff, and Marshall’s claims are a parasitic attempt to gain fifteen minutes of fame by slandering a woman who cannot defend herself. Dennison handily rebuts Marshall, and I’m glad he did—but I can’t help but think that fortunately, some writers are uncancellable. Potter’s books have sold 250 million copies. articles.content_zh: 早上好,你好吗? 这本周末版的A La Carte 有一些长式内容,一些思想作品,一些周来最受欢迎的文章列表,还有你这样的读者提出的一整套建议. 慢慢来! 今天的销售和交易包括性、宽恕、哈巴克克、启示录等书籍。 建议阅读 并非每个人都熟悉“巧妙”一词, 例如,我们的恶性欲望是有罪的,还是只对这些欲望采取行动是有罪的? 这个问题经常在我们讨论同性吸引力时出现. 为Logos写作,马克·琼斯从改革的视角探索了巧妙的概念. 简而言之,康克塞克语(concupiscentia)起源于拉丁语动词concupisco,意为"强烈的欲望". 我们称之为“无耻的谦虚”。 例如,耶稣对他的门徒说:我的确希望在我受苦之前与你们一起吃这个逾越节。 但是,因为我们生活在一个堕落的世界中,巧妙通常会考虑到罪恶的欲望,通常会提到罪恶的性欲望。 因为罪恶是正义被剥夺(黑暗),容易被邪恶所侵扰,所以巧妙的行为不仅涉及行为,而且涉及人的欲望. 从上帝的道德法则可以理解罪恶的欺骗: " 你不应该贪婪 " (20:17). 混淆:我们的不祥愿望是否有罪? 《卫报》讲述了一个奇怪而曲折的死亡、丑闻和复仇欲望的故事,它这样总结道 : “ 在他母亲死后,奥托开始相信自己被法医调查人员冤枉了 — — 其中一人是骗子。 真相甚至是陌生的。” 以下是文章的开头: 2020年6月,奥托的年长母亲多莉亚正在慕尼黑的公寓中消亡。 当她闭上眼睛躺下时,被她白发所陷的她苍白的脸色是平静的. Otto被蒙上面具 被手套并被涂上不育的围裙 睡在她旁边的椅子上 奥托有时取名"雷纳"(Rainer),由于德国严格的隐私法,他的姓只被称作"Z",自她中风后一直和他一起住入,他是一个照顾他母亲多年的医生. 他向我描述了那晚的经过。 他醒来时听到她短促的呼吸声,想让她坐直. 她的眼睛被闭上了 嘴唇被包住了 她停止了呼吸。 奥托打电话求救,但后来多莉娅睁开眼睛并盯着他. 她微笑了,画了最后一口深呼吸,又闭上了眼睛,躺了下来。 A Death, a Plagiarism Sandal and a Quest for Evention: The Bizarre Tale of Otto Z. Jonathon Van Maren将Beatrix Potter视为真正保守主义的典范, 并解释为什么在一篇非常有趣的文章中会出现这种情况, 有一类学者只能通过攻击大男人和大女人的后遗症来引起人们的注意,马修·丹尼斯森在"观察者"一文中引用了"别取消碧翠克丝·波特"中的主要例子. " 后殖民时期文学专家 " 已成为受爱戴的儿童作家的目标。 Emily Zobel Marshall博士幽默地声称波特没有“承认她欠一个口头讲故事的传统,即在美国种植园工作的被奴役的非洲人的债”,这助长了“对黑人文化形式的破坏和反复侵吞,这种掠夺今天仍在继续 ” 。 Marshall的主张是企图通过诽谤一个不能自卫的妇女来赢得十五分钟的名声。 我很高兴他这样做了, 但我不禁觉得幸运的是, 一些作家是无法取消的。 波特的书已经售出2.5亿册. 她的遗产很好 她的角色会继续

articles.title: 预测市场：换汤不换药的赌博
articles.summary: 从体育赛事到战争灾难，预测市场几乎让一切都成了下注的对象。看似只是猜一猜未来，背后却牵动着贪欲、金钱与人的苦难。面对赚快钱的诱惑，基督徒该如何选择？
articles.content: 我从小就常听人说：“不是所有的钱都该赚。”这句朴素的话提醒我们，不该为了改善经济状况而牺牲做人的原则。如今，社交媒体上充斥着各种应用程序的广告，声称只要猜中未来会发生什么，就能迅速致富。说实话，这个时代很需要听听这句提醒。 预测市场已从一个鲜有人关注的现象，变成了一个 严重问题 。一名白宫提词器操作员因押注特朗普总统会在演说中说什么，获利超过 10 万美元，于 7 月 被停职，并接受调查。 4 月 ，一名美国特种作战军人遭到逮捕和起诉。他参与了抓捕委内瑞拉总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗（Nicolás Maduro）的行动，却涉嫌利用掌握的机密信息，对行动相关事件下注，获利超过 40 万美元。 这些事件不只是滥用内幕消息的问题，更显出一种令人深感不安的文化倾向：每一条信息都有了价码，人们正想方设法将其变现。 更糟的是，Kalshi和Polymarket等应用程序，把赌场里那种令人兴奋、欲罢不能的刺激，送进了我们的口袋。它们用“预测市场”的说法推销产品，但实际提供的服务，与DraftKings或FanDuel等博彩平台并没有多大区别。真正不同的，只是下注的对象。这些预测市场应用，说到底就是换汤不换药的赌博。 何为预测市场？ 预测市场是一种交易平台，人们买卖与未来事件结果挂钩的合约。合约价格反映市场对事件发生概率的判断。交易双方分别押注某件事会发生或不会发生。这本质上是参与者之间的对赌，双方就某件事签订结果为“是”或“否”的合约。 例如，克里斯托弗·诺兰（Christopher Nolan）会不会凭借《奥德赛》（ The Odyssey ）赢得奥斯卡奖？如果你买入的是“是”合约，预测成真时，每份合约结算支付 1 美元；预测落空，则归零。若这份合约当前以 0.75 美元成交，通常可以理解为，市场价格隐含的发生概率约为 75%。任何可能影响结果的新信息，都可能改变合约价格。通过这款应用，人们就能对政治、 体育 乃至文化活动等各类事件下注。 赌博与预测市场的相似之处，多于不同之处。两者都让人对不确定的结果下注，参与者也都根据最终结果赢钱或输钱。 主要区别在于下注的机制，以及由谁决定概率和赔率。在体育博彩中，庄家设定赔率，以降低自己的风险，提高 获利的可能性 。庄家的目标是赚钱，因此，本质上它就是赌客的对手。赌客的目标则是赢过庄家。 预测市场采用汇集众人判断的预测模式，价格反映参与者对概率的估计。人们根据自己对结果的判断进行交易，因此，对手是其他交易者。 另一个主要区别是监管机构。在美国，体育博彩及更广泛的博彩业，由各州的博彩委员会等机构分别监管。预测市场目前则由联邦层面的商品期货交易委员会（Commodity Futures Trading Commission）监管，不过， 新泽西州 正在争取这项监管权。 预测市场有什么问题？ 预测市场尤其令人担忧的一点，是它们绕过了体育博彩法规。美国最高法院推翻职业与业余体育保护法（Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act，简称PASPA）后，体育博彩的监管权交由各州行使。在禁止体育博彩的州，预测市场便成了规避州法的途径。 人们可以就运动员的具体表现进行所谓的“交易”——这实际上属于“ 特殊项目投注 ”；也可以押注超级碗、美国大学体育协会（NCAA）篮球锦标赛或其他体育赛事的结果。预测市场由此为体育博彩提供了绕过限制的途径，实际运作起来，不过是又一个赌博平台。 预测市场也为内幕交易提供了机会，使人能够利用未公开的信息操纵市场、谋取利益。在前面提到的提词器操作员和特种作战军人的案例中，内幕消息极大地影响了他们的交易和下注，让他们获得巨额利润。能够掌握内幕消息，或直接左右事件结果的交易者，实际上成了庄家，把赌局变成了对自己有利的游戏。 但最令人担忧的问题，是人的生命与苦难也可能成为下注牟利的对象。人的生命与苦难，也可能成为下注牟利的对象预测市场涵盖的事件极其广泛，人们可以对军事行动、伤亡人数、自然灾害、疫情，甚至公众人物的死亡下注。这令人不安，因为它把人的生命和苦难变成了投机牟利的对象。 例如 ，2025 年，有人买卖合约，押注洛杉矶山火会以多快的速度蔓延、造成多大的损失。公共灾难就这样成了赚快钱的机会。这类交易还会产生扭曲的动机：为了让押注的结果成真，有人可能会设法让灾难变得更加严重。 基督徒应当参与预测市场吗？ 大量报道和研究 已经揭示了赌博的危害，这也是许多基督徒反对 体育博彩 的原因。同样的理由，也适用于 预测市场 。 考虑到赌博对社会造成的伤害，以及 预测市场 依靠人的贪欲运转的商业模式，我们很难认为，参与其中有助于结出圣灵的果子。 基督教传统 对赌博虽有不同看法，我们仍应当问：这些活动能否结出“仁爱、喜乐、和平、忍耐、恩慈、良善、信实、温柔、节制”？（加 5:22–23） 基督徒蒙召，要倚靠神的供应，以智慧和知足的心管理祂所赐的资源。预测市场却诱惑我们，把神赐的资源押在对未来的猜测上，追逐快钱，而非作智慧的投资。正如雅各提醒我们的：“其实明天如何，你们还不知道。”（雅 4:14）与其拿钱押注自己的预测，我们更应当努力培养美好的品格。 各种形式的赌博，常常以无伤大雅的娱乐为卖点。我们应当警惕，这些活动会如何助长我们的贪欲，而贪财正是万恶之根（提前 6:10）。我们或许很想把预测市场当作一种无害的消遣，但最好记住：“不是所有的钱都该赚。” 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： Prediction Markets: Gambling by Another Name .
articles.author: RaShan Frost

articles.title: 编辑荐书：七本滋养灵命的神学好书
articles.summary: 研读神学，也能使人心生敬拜。从通俗入门到经典巨著，这七本书帮助我们更深认识神，让教义滋养灵命，也装备我们服侍教会。
articles.content: 基督徒在今生追求圣洁，也应当渴望更深地认识神。各样新书不断出版，承诺帮助读者深化灵修生活，其中不少确实很好，也很有帮助。 不过，我更认同C. S. 路易斯在 论阅读古书（ On the Reading of Old Books ） 一文中的话： 就我个人而言，教义书籍往往比灵修书籍更能帮助我亲近神。我想，许多人也可能有同样的体验。有些人坐下来，或跪下来读灵修书，却觉得“什么也没发生”。我相信，如果他们嘴里叼着烟斗，手里拿着铅笔，努力读懂一段艰深的神学论述，反倒会发现，自己的心不由自主地歌唱起来。 烟斗就免了，但他描述的情景，我很熟悉。许多灵修著作固然有益，我灵命中的一些高峰，却是在埋头研读厚重的系统神学著作时经历的。这或许与我的性格有 关，但我相信，有这种体验的不只我一个。 下面这份书单收录了近期出版或再版的神学著作。无论你目前的属灵生命处于哪个阶段，都能从中得到鼓励，也能更好地装备自己，服侍教会。 《滋养生命的神学：在喜乐中认识基督教教义》（ Theology for Life: A Joy-Filled Introduction to Christian Doctrine ） 罗尼·库尔茨（Ronni Kurtz）著 我们受造，是为要认识神，永远以祂为乐。但在这个待办事项排得满满、凡事讲求实用的世界里，花时间默想神的荣美与荣耀，似乎是一件奢侈的事，甚至有些放纵自己。 《 滋养生命的神学》 却要说，并非如此。思考神的荣美与荣耀，是其他一切的根基。 贝克出版社（Baker Books），256 页。 1.罗尼·库尔茨著，《滋养生命的神学：在喜乐中认识基督教教义》 （贝克出版社，2026） 学习基督教教义，入门并不容易，尤其是在神学院之外。神学有一套专门词汇，可能要花上几年才能熟练掌握。有时，一章罪论就长达 70 页。我们努力弄懂各种比喻，理解人如何偏离神圣洁的要求，读着读着却不免两眼发直。 《 滋养生命的神学 》是一本面向普通会众的基督教神学入门书。更重要的是，正如副标题所说，库尔茨希望帮助读者在学习重要的基督教真理时，尝到其中的喜乐。教会若想带领全体会众认识系统神学，这会是一本很好的教材。牧者如果在繁重的事奉中疲惫不堪，这本书也能帮助他们重新燃起对神的爱。 2.丹尼尔·阿金（Daniel Akin）、肯尼斯·基思利（Kenneth Keathley）、基思·惠特菲尔德（Keith Whitfield）编，《为教会而写的神学》（ A Theology for the Church ）第二版， （B&H 学术出版社，2026） 《 为教会而写的神学 》初版问世时，我刚开始读神学院。这本书于 2014 年修订，如今又在 2026 年作了更全面的更新。每一版都增添或修订了一些章节，也比上一版更好。 我最欣赏这本书的一点是它始终以服侍教会为目标。书中内容无疑具有学术深度，普通会众读起来可能颇为吃力，但对牧者和教会领袖尤其有帮助，因为它的论述总是从圣经怎么说开始。每一章也探讨教会历来相信什么，以及各项教义如何影响今天的教会生活。虽然本书从浸信会的立场出发，其他传统的读者也能从中获益。 3.周毕克（Joel Beeke）、保罗·斯马利（Paul Smalley），《改革宗系统神学精要》（ Essentials of Reformed Systematic Theology ） （十架路出版社〔Crossway〕，2025） 这部 单卷本 很好地浓缩了原先 四卷本 的内容。希望更深入认识当代改革宗神学的基督徒，会从中受益。全书删编得流畅自然，读者不会总觉得自己是不是错过了完整版中的什么重要内容。周毕克和斯马利用简洁而优美的篇章，呈现核心教义。这是一本适合每个基督徒家庭收藏的好书。 4.弗朗西斯·图伦丁（Francis Turretin）著，《辩证神学要义》（ Institutes of Elenctic Theology ），全三卷（P&R，2025） 许多最好的神学著作都是数十年课堂教学的结晶。17 世纪，图伦丁在日内瓦教授神学约 30 年。阅读 图伦丁 ，就是向一位经过多年教学与思考、神学见解成熟的老师学习。这套神学直接或间接地塑造了一代又一代长老会及改革宗神学家。 有时，我们把古老的神学著作当作历史文献来读，也会觉得饶有趣味。但图伦丁采用的“辩证”方法，与一般系统神学的写法不同，令人耳目一新。他将非信徒及其他信仰传统对改革宗神学的异议，整理成问题，逐一作答。这种写法常常让神学的护教作用显得格外清楚。令人惊讶的是，其中许多回答，至今仍能帮助我们看清 21 世纪的神学争议。 5.霍志恒（Geerhardus Vos）著，《改革宗教义学：基督教神学体系》（ Reformed Dogmatics: A System of Christian Theology ） （贝克学术出版社〔Baker Academic〕，2026） 直到最近我才知道，霍志恒这位圣经神学的重要奠基者，也写过系统神学。其实，这并没有乍听之下那么令人意外。因为他在 19 世纪末出版这部五卷本著作时，圣经研究与神学等学科之间的界限，远没有今天这么分明。 霍志恒的《改革宗教义学》直到 2014 至 2016 年，才由莱克瑟姆出版社（Lexham Press）陆续推出 五卷英文译本 ，并于 2020 年合并为单卷本出版。此次 新版 则改由贝克学术出版社重新发行。尽管如此，初学神学、又对改革宗传统感兴趣的读者，仍能从霍志恒这部文笔优美、论证严谨的著作中大有收获。 6.斯科特·克拉克（R. Scott Clark），《海德堡要理问答：历史、神学与牧养注释》（ The Heidelberg Catechism: A Historical, Theological, and Pastoral Commentary ） （Lexham Press，2025） 随着要理问答在福音派中越来越受重视，读者很可能会提出一些问题：为什么选这些主题？为什么答案要这样措辞？ 这部注释 着重说明海德堡要理问答各项问答的圣经依据，也从历史和神学的角度，解释这部经典门训教材为何采用这些表述。 无论我们是在追问，生与死中唯一的安慰是什么（第 1 问），还是想弄清善行的本质（第 91 问），这本书都能为牧者、父母和神学初学者提供丰富的帮助。 7.费斯科（J. V. Fesko）、约翰·缪瑟（John Muether）、布莱尔·史密斯（D. Blair Smith）编，《威斯敏斯特信仰告白：历史、神学与应用综合注释》（ The Westminster Confession of Faith: A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application ） （十架路出版社，2026） 《威斯敏斯特信仰告白》 或许是新教神学最重要的信仰表述。它写于宗教改革开始约一个世纪之后，当时，许多关键教义问题已历经反复讨论，形成了较为明确的答案。这份信条也因此成为不同新教传统的重要参照。 这部 注释 由改革宗神学院的教师共同撰写，能帮助长老会、浸信会及其他新教传统的神学工作者。对牧者和神学生而言，它也是一本实用的参考书。 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： Editor’s Pick: 7 Theology Books That Encourage Devotion .

articles.title: What You Should Know About the Hebrew Roots Movement
articles.summary: The Hebrew Roots Movement is a modern version of the New Testament Judaizers who were rebuked by Paul.
articles.summary_zh: 希伯来根源运动是新约犹太人被保罗斥责的现代版本。
articles.title_zh: 关于希伯来根源运动，你应该知道什么
articles.content: The hiss of the cappuccino machine filled the coffee shop, forcing him to lean in and raise his voice. “Show me,” he said, “where Jesus or the apostles ever told Christians they no longer had to keep the law of Moses.” I remember realizing that, if I were honest, I wasn’t entirely sure how to answer that challenge. I knew Christians weren’t under that law, but where in the Bible would I go to explain why? In the years since that initial encounter, I’ve had countless such conversations with Christians who have become involved in the growing restorationist movement most often known as Hebrew Roots. This movement teaches that Christians are obligated to keep the ceremonial law—especially the feast days, the dietary laws, and the seventh-day Sabbath. For most Christians, it appears out of nowhere. A church member begins lobbying for the Old Testament dietary laws. A spouse begins denouncing Easter, believing Christians are required to keep Passover instead. A small-group leader starts recommending YouTube channels that teach Christians are sinning if they don’t observe Shabbat . Before you know it, long-held historical Christian beliefs about the gospel, the church, and the new covenant are being openly challenged. These aren’t isolated stories. I regularly hear from pastors, leaders, and believers seeing Hebrew Roots theology sow confusion, strain relationships, and, in some cases, draw believers away from Christ’s sufficiency. They want to know what it actually teaches and why so many Christians are being drawn into it. And perhaps most importantly, how should pastors and church leaders respond? Hebrew Roots Defined To answer those questions, we must first understand what the Hebrew Roots Movement is—and what it isn’t. Over the past few decades, many Christians have grown disillusioned with shallow expressions of Christianity and begun looking for something deeper and more ancient. That desire has led some to seek out more liturgical and traditional Christian denominations. Others, however, are drawn to Torah-keeping communities, believing these groups more closely align with the beliefs and practices of the earliest Christians. But careful study of history shows that isn’t the case. Rather than uniting believers to ancient Christian practices, Hebrew Roots provides a highly diverse movement that emphasizes ongoing obedience to portions of the Old Testament . Before you know it, long-held historical Christian beliefs about the gospel, the church, and the new covenant are being openly challenged. The Hebrew Roots movement isn’t a monolithic organization. Most groups don’t even call themselves “Hebrew Roots,” preferring terms such as “Torah-observant,” “Torah-keepers,” or “Pronomian.” It’s a loose collection of teachers, ministries, and online communities that have emerged from mainstream Christianity and believe they’re recovering the “true faith” taught by Jesus and the apostles. The emphasis on recovering long-lost and hidden truths sometimes leads to highly individualistic interpretations among Hebrew Roots adherents. Despite their diversity, these groups share one central theological conviction: New-covenant Christians are required to keep the old-covenant law, and not doing so is sinful. This errant theology is commonly known as Torahism. Whereas the Torah (the first five books of the Old Testament) is a beautiful and fundamental part of the Christian faith, Torah ism is a dangerous misapplication of the old-covenant commands God gave to Israel. And if the theology sounds a little familiar, yes, this is a modern version of the beliefs taught by the New Testament Judaizers and rebuked by Paul in Galatians. It’s important to distinguish between Hebrew Roots and Messianic Judaism. The two movements are sometimes conflated because they look similar on the surface, but there’s an important difference: Hebrew Roots teaches Torahism ; Messianic Judaism doesn’t. articles.title_zh: 在终身事工中茁壮成长的7个关键
articles.content: At the starting line of an Olympic race, nothing looks particularly dramatic. The athletes stand still. The crowd waits. The runners’ muscles are motionless. The track lies open. Then the signal sounds, and in a matter of seconds the race is over. To the spectator, it may seem almost natural: a brief flash of speed followed by applause. But those few seconds are never merely a few seconds. They’re the visible tip of years hidden from public view. Behind that moment lie thousands of hours of training. Victory isn’t won merely by speed on race day; it’s won through long obedience before the race ever begins. If you’re a believer, you’re in a daunting spiritual race with eternal consequences. How much truer is this of the pastor, who also has the weighty task of shepherding other believers? If we want to avoid the all-too-common pitfalls of burnout, scandal, and disillusionment, we must follow seven keys to pastoral perseverance rooted in Scripture and biblical wisdom. Key #1: Radically Trust the Holy Spirit If we’re prone to neglect one person of the Trinity, it’s probably the Holy Spirit. This is a tragedy. If we can’t draw one breath of oxygen into our lungs without his aid (Ps. 104:29–30), how much less can we persevere in the ministry without his constant breathing of empowerment (John 20:22)? I wonder if one of the reasons for a high dropout rate among pastors is that we often try to do the Lord’s work without seeking his rejuvenating power. This divine power comes only through ardent faith and prayer. Oh, how we need conscious, wholehearted dependence on the Spirit! Those who sit under our ministry and preaching will be as dead as dry bones unless the sovereign Spirit breathes on them and transforms them into a mighty spiritual army (Ezek. 37:1–14; Eph. 2:1). Key #2: Pray Like Your Life Depends on It Prayer is the breath of the Christian and the heartbeat of persevering ministry. If you want to persevere, dear pastor, take every aspect of your ministry to the Lord in prayer—every sermon you preach, every class you teach, and every visit you make. Pray, pray, pray your way through the ministry! Oh, what sweetness you’ll find in sacred, childlike dependence on your heavenly Father. As John Calvin puts it , in prayer we climb into the lap of our heavenly Father and whisper our needs in his ear. Prayer is the breath of the Christian and the heartbeat of persevering ministry. As ministers, we must be much on our knees in prayer. Our method of study should be on our knees, then back to our books, then back to our knees again. We never do our theology alone; we do so in the presence of the triune God. Perhaps we don’t cry out to God more in secret—begging for his help in holy desperation and importunity—because we often don’t recognize how weak and needy we truly are. Key #3: Soak Up the Bible as Your Highest Calling As pastors, our power in public depends in large part on the quality and quantity of time we spend with God in secret (Matt. 6:6). We abide in Christ in proportion to the degree that his Word abides in us, and the Word abides in us in proportion to how much quality time we spend absorbing it—reading it, meditating on it, praying over it, memorizing it, internalizing it, preaching and teaching it, speaking it, trusting it, applying it, and fleshing it out through practical obedience. With the Spirit’s help, digest God’s Word with consistency, read it systematically, and absorb it experientially. Linger over every divine word. Bask every day in God’s presence. Cultivate holy familiarity with him. As you do so, your soul will be invigorated with life, strength, and vitality. By marinating in Scripture as pastors, we can walk with God like Enoch (Gen. 5:24), cultivate friendship with him like Abraham (James 2:23), know him face-to-face like Moses (Ex. 33:11), and enjoy sweet intimacy with him like the psalmist (Ps. 25:14). Through the Word, we can savor God’s presence and gaze on his beauty (27:4). As you soak in the Wor

articles.title_zh: 卡尔和劳拉·伦茨谈论五年的公开判断： “你不能从我们的故事中看不到上帝”
articles.content: Five years ago, Laura Lentz had more advice than she wanted. People who had never met her were telling her what to do about her husband, her marriage and her future. “Getting all these opinions and judgments from the outside when no one really knows what’s going on,” she says. “Only the people that are in this know what it takes.” In November 2020, Hillsong founder Brian Houston told staff that Carl Lentz was out at the church’s Manhattan campus, citing breaches of trust. An extramarital affair had come to light. Laura, who had done nothing to land in that spotlight, found herself in it anyway. This month the two of them released a book, Overcoming Infidelity: 10 Conversations To Help Heal the Hurt , and the couple sat down with us to talk about how they got from there to here. “I struggled with a lot of anxiety and just struggling with the opinions of others,” Laura says. “I had to really make sure that didn’t get in here and just remind myself that this is what matters and only we know what’s going on. Lots of therapy has been great. And Jesus, of course, helping through this.” The criticism hasn’t ended, but she says it has changed. “Now I find that’s really gotten quite silent. I think the fruit of our relationship and the fruit of our kids’ lives and where we are now and even writing the book, like you can’t not see God through our story. You can’t not see the miracle through our story.” She is clear about what the book is not. “We’re not out here promoting the book like we’re out to save marriages,” she says. “It’s about me healing, him healing and seeing where that takes us.” The Secrets That Started Small Asked what signs a young married couple should watch for, both of them go to the same place: secrets. “It’s not just big secrets, it’s like the little things,” Laura says. “If you can’t be honest or you’re hiding things from your spouse, those are dangerous and they just compound.” She remembers praying in the weeks before everything surfaced. “I don’t know what it is, but God, you’ve got to get this, just get it out.” Carl says the distance did not begin with the affair. “You don’t start keeping secrets about cheating. You start keeping secrets about fear.” He describes deciding what his wife could handle and keeping the pressure to himself. “It’s when I made the decisions for her on what she was capable of holding,” he says. “Then you stack them and you stack them. By the time you get to the horrific stuff, you’ve already got a pattern of hiding stuff.” What he tells young men now is blunt: get used to being vulnerable with your wife. “It turns out it’s very attractive.” He also rejects the idea that pastors have nobody to tell. “If anybody ever says ‘I didn’t have anybody to be open with,’ I lovingly say I don’t believe you. You chose to not tell anybody.” He says that if he had called Houston on a bad day, he would have been flown out to help. “I did not call. I was not honest. That’s on me.” What Staying Actually Looked Like People tell the spouse who stays that she is brave. Laura is not sure that’s the right word. “It’s so hard to stay, it’s so hard to go,” she says. “Yes, I was brave, I guess, but I was also taking a risk.” She says she would never tell someone to stay in an adulterous relationship, and that she herself saw evidence of change before she did. “There’s gotta be evidence of things that are changing for you to stay and he’s gotta be doing his work.” She describes the early days in small units of time. “We literally went one day at a time. I would wake up and go, okay, I can do today. And that was it.” Carl, a basketball fan, says she has learned the language for it. “Every day, I’m on a one-day contract. That’s an upgrade from a two-hour contract that I was on for quite a long time.” The marriage that came out of that, Laura says, is not the one they had before. “Marriage 2.0 is like so much deeper. articles.title: Meet Elle Limebear, the British Artist Who Turned a School-Assembly Hymn Into a UK No. 1
articles.summary: The daughter of Delirious? frontman Martin Smith rebuilt “Oil in My Lamp” for a new generation, and “Give Me Joy” has spent nine weeks atop the UK Christian chart.
articles.summary_zh: Delirious主唱马丁·史密斯（ Martin Smith ）的女儿为新一代重建了“Oil in My Lamp” ， “Give Me Joy”在英国基督教排行榜上排名第九。
articles.title_zh: 认识英国艺术家Elle Limebear ，他将学校集会赞美诗变成了英国第一
articles.content: Elle Limebear used to have a hard time describing her dad’s job. When classmates asked what he did, she’d say he was in a band, then that it was Christian music, then that it was sort of rocky, and then she’d watch the conversation go nowhere. Some days she wished he were “just a plumber dad.” Her father is Martin Smith, the frontman of Delirious?, the British band behind “History Maker” and “Did You Feel the Mountains Tremble?” and one of the defining worship bands of the late ‘90s and 2000s. She remembers touring the US as a kid, on big tour buses, with people lining up for photos with him. Back home in their English village, “no one really cared.” Limebear now lives in Brighton with her husband, Tom, and their three young children, and the song she’s best known for is one almost every British adult has sung. “Give Me Joy,” released in July, reworks the hymn “Oil in My Lamp.” It debuted at No. 1 on the Official UK Christian & Gospel Singles Chart and has held the top spot for nine weeks since. Decca Records, which announced her signing the same month, calls her its first contemporary Christian artist. The hymn was a fixture of British school assemblies, whether or not the school was religious. “If you sing ‘Oil in My Lamp,’ probably everyone will know it,” Limebear told RELEVANT. “It’s in our childhood. It’s in our bones almost.” She started slipping it into her live sets a few years ago. The reaction surprised her. “There was this eruption of, I know this. I remember being a kid singing this,” she said. “People just belted it, absolutely belted it.” Her husband suggested she rewrite it for people who never grew up singing it. Her first reaction was that the song was already a banner. “What a challenge.” She wrote new verses and melodies and kept the heart of it. When her new label asked whether she had anything to lead with, she figured the answer was no. “It’s a British kind of hymn-like thing,” she said. “Not super cool.” Then she played it for the team, a room of people who, in her words, don’t know Jesus. “They absolutely loved it and it brought them alive. They’re like, I remember singing this song.” The song was only a chorus and a verse at that point, and the response is what pushed her to finish it. Limebear never planned to be a songwriter. At 20 she was set on photography, which felt safe. “I could contain it, control it,” she said. Then she felt God tell her, clearly, to do music. “It didn’t feel like my thought.” She says fear kept her from believing she had anything to bring, and she didn’t know how to write songs. “Back then I was definitely hesitantly walking through these doors full of fear. Now I feel like I’m skipping through them.” The version of England she’s skipping through is a different one from the England she grew up in. She was the only Christian in her whole school, she said, and her youth group “saved my life.” Lately she hears from friends and church leaders across the country about people walking into church out of plain curiosity about Jesus. “There’s this thing called the quiet revival that they say is going on,” she said, “where people are just finding him in all sorts of places.” She remembers being the weirdest person in the room for it. Now, she says, people are discovering that “actually, being a Christian isn’t that weird.” Her takeaway for believers is the same one. “I think we should all be more curious, even as Christians,” she said. “Get more curious. Ask more questions.” Asked what’s behind it, she didn’t pretend to know. “I don’t know is the answer.” She pointed to decades of quiet prayer, from older women in church prayer meetings to families praying at home for relatives to come to faith, and added: “God hears every prayer, doesn’t he?” and “nothing’s wasted.” She also described the last few years in the Church as “good, sad, confusing,” with “lots of walls” coming down, and says she senses something being built back up that looks different from before. She says the change show
articles.content_zh: Elle Limebear曾经很难描述她父亲的工作。 当同学们问他做了什么时, 她会说他在一个乐队里, 然后说这是基督教音乐, 然后是有点摇滚, 然后她会看着谈话无所作为。 她希望他“只是一个水管工爸爸”。 她的父亲是马丁·史密斯(Martin Smith),他是Delirious的前锋?),是“历史制造者”和“你感受了山地的风暴吗?” 背后的英国乐队,也是90年代后期和2000年代的决定性的崇拜乐队之一。 她记得小时候在美国巡演, 在大型旅游巴士上, 人们排队与他合影。 回到家乡的英国村落, Limebear现在与她的丈夫汤姆和他们三个年幼的孩子住在布莱顿,她最著名的一首歌是几乎每个英国成年人都有一首歌. “给我欢乐”,7月发行, 它在英国官方"基督教与福音单行道图"第1期首发并连续9周保持了顶尖位置. Decca唱片公司宣布同月签约,称她为"第一位当代基督教艺术家". 赞美诗是英国学校集会的定律,无论学校是否是宗教. “如果你唱出‘Oil in My Lamp', “这是在我们童年时期。 这几乎是在我们的骨头里。 她几年前开始把它滑入她的现场 反应让她吃惊了. “有一次爆发,我知道这一点。 我还记得小时候唱这个, “人们只是把它系上,绝对把它系上。” 她丈夫建议她为从未长大的歌唱者改写. 她的第一个反应是这首歌已经是一面旗帜. “真是挑战。” 她写了新的诗和旋律,并保持了它的心脏. 当她的新标签问她是否有 任何领导,她认为答案是否定的。 “这是英国的一种赞美诗。 “不是超级酷。” 她为球队演奏, “他们绝对喜欢它,它使他们生还。 他们喜欢, 我记得唱这首歌。 这首歌当时只是一首合唱和一首诗作曲,回应是促使她完成的. Limebear从未计划做作曲家. 20岁时她被设定在摄影上 这感觉很安全 她说,“我可以控制它,控制它。” 然后她觉得上帝告诉她,很明显, 做音乐。 “这不像我的想法。” 她表示害怕让她无法相信她有什么要带的东西, “那时我确实犹豫地走进这些充满恐惧的门去。 现在我觉得自己正在跳过它们。 她跳过英国的版本与她成长的英国不同. 她说她是全校唯一的基督徒, 最近她从全国各地的朋友和教会领袖那里听到人们出于对耶稣的纯粹好奇而走入教堂. 她说 , “ 有一种叫静静的复兴的东西, 他们说,“人们正在各种地方找到他。 ” 她记得是房间里最怪的人 现在,她说,人们正在发现,“事实上,作为一个基督徒并不奇怪。 她的信徒们的外出也是一样 她说,“我认为我们都应该更加好奇,即使是基督徒。” “更加好奇。 问出更多问题。” 她并没有假装知道。 “我不知道答案是什么。 她提到了数十年的静静祈祷,从在教堂祈祷会的年长妇女到在家里为亲戚们祈祷的家庭,并补充说:“上帝听到每一个祈祷,不是吗?”和“没有浪费的东西。 ” 她还将教会的过去几年描述为"美好,悲伤,困惑","许多墙壁"倒下,并说她感觉到一些正在被重建起来的东西看起来与以前不同. 她说是换衣服
