featured.content: 1. “ ‘I Shall Be Very Surprised If There Isn’t A Next Chapter’ ” is the title of the remarkable interview with English theologian Sarah Coakley that appeared on the New York Times website this past week, courtesy of Peter Wehner. We’ve been at this Another Week Ends game for a couple decades now, and I’m not sure I’ve ever seen so much theological substance published in America’s once-and-future(?) paper of record. I’ve been aware of Coakley’s work and reputation for some time but never taken the plunge, which, after reading their conversation, feels like a bit of a shame-on-me situation. One of my favorite bits comes at the very beginning, when Coakley talks about her teenage years. Apparently the confirmation classes at her little Church of England parish lacked the rigor she was hoping for. Thus, she did what all kids that age do these days: My eldest brother and I organized our own theological discussion group in that same parish. We brought a lot of our atheistical and skeptical school friends into it. And this very holy rector was very clever at this point, because he just sat watching the arguments go backward and forward, rather like the umpire at Wimbledon. He never intervened, never put us right, never told us what the right answer was. When my brother and I recently thought about who had attended those discussions, the vast majority of our friends who attended at that age, 14 to 16, subsequently became Christians. So that tells you something about opening the Pandora’s box theologically and how important it is for the clergy not to stifle that. A lovely little testament to the power of grace in practice, I’d say, and one which jibes with my own decades working with young people. Allow students to ask their questions, raise their objections and air their doubts without threat of defensiveness — let that stuff hang in the air — and the craziest things can happen, especially over the long haul. Squash their arguments with doctrine, even right doctrine, and you risk alienating them forever. Such is the emotional wallop of correction, however well intentioned. Coakley goes on to provide some rather damning commentary on the gap in theology between the academy and the pew, the professor and the layperson. One of the core hopes of her own work, she claims, is the closing of that gap chasm, to which I can only add a hearty amen. I’ve tried to do something similar in my own books, albeit on a much smaller scale. (Whether utilizing a French phrase for that project — théologie totale — screams accessibility is a separate question.) In Coakley’s view, uncoupling the study of theology from the practice of prayer is dangerous. This leads her into one of the most beautiful articulations of prayer I’ve read anywhere, let alone the New York Times : How do I pray? Well, you hand yourself over to the source of your being, and then you ask some things. But the handing over is primary, and learning how to do that. It changes your perspective on God — because when you practice this, even for a very short time each day, simple opening up space in which God is God. You don’t control it. That’s what’s so frightening. This is not a new skill, like learning how to make a very good omelet or to ride a bicycle. This is a nonskill. It’s an unskilling, an unmastery. It completely changes your view of God, because up to that point you’ve probably subliminally been thinking about God as a very large entity, the largest and the best in a universe of entities whom somehow you’ve got to get on your side or cajole or get to answer your request. I know that’s a very naïve sounding description, but as a priest I can tell you that’s the God I hear about all the time. All the great theologians of the tradition have slain that God, and they’ve had to slay that God — think of Luther — with great terror. It’s really just opening up to the possibility of grace. Contemplation isn’t special. It’s just very difficult for people who are relatively educated and pri
featured.content_zh: 1. " `I Shall Be very Surprise If There Isout A Next Chapter ' ”是英国神学家Sarah Coakley在上周在纽约时报网站上发表的令人瞩目的访谈的标题,由Peter Wehner主持。 我不确定我是否曾见过如此多的神学物质, 我了解Coakley的作品与名声已有一段时间, 我最喜欢的一点 是在一开始, 当Coakley谈论她的青少年时代。 显然,她的英格兰小教堂的确认课 缺乏她希望的严格度。 因此,她做了所有的孩子 这些天做: 我的长兄和我在同一堂区组织了我们自己的神学讨论小组。 我们把许多无神论和怀疑论的学校朋友都带进了其中. 而这位非常神圣的校长 此时非常聪明, 因为他只是坐着看着这些争论往后走, 就像温布尔登的裁判。 他从来没有干预,从来没有让我们正确,从来没有告诉我们什么是正确的答案。 当我和我兄弟最近想到谁参加了这些讨论时,14至16岁的我们绝大多数朋友后来成为基督徒。 因此,这可以说明在神学上打开潘多拉的盒子,以及神职人员不要扼杀它的重要性。 一个可爱的小证明, 在实践中, 允许学生提问,提出反对意见并表达他们的疑虑,而不会受到防卫威胁——让这些东西被挂在空中——最疯狂的事情可能会发生,特别是在漫长的时间内. 用学说,甚至正确的学说来压制他们的论点,你冒着永远疏远他们的危险. 这是一种精神上的纠错,无论用意如何。 Coakley继续就学院与皮尤,教授和外行人之间的神学差距提供一些相当可憎的评论. 她声称,她自己工作的一个核心希望是,缩小了这一差距,我只能为这一差距增添一个心地阿门。 尽管规模要小得多, (该项目是否使用法语短语-总词-尖叫无障碍是一个单独的问题。 ) 科克利认为,将神学研究与祈祷实践脱钩是危险的. 更别说纽约时报:我该如何祈祷? 你把自己交给你生命的来源 然后问些问题 但交接是初级的, 并学习如何做到这一点。 它改变了你对上帝的看法——因为当你练习这个时,即使每天非常短的时间,简单的打开了上帝是上帝的空间. 你无法控制它。 这才是最可怕的。 这不是一种新的技能,比如学习如何做一个非常好的煎蛋卷或者骑自行车。 这是非技能。 是个没有技能, 这完全改变了你对上帝的看法,因为直到那个时候,你可能一直在深思上帝是一个非常大的实体,是一个最大和最好的实体,你不得不站在你一边,或者说去回答你的要求。 我知道这听起来很天真, 但作为一个牧师,我可以告诉你,这就是我一直听到的上帝。 传统中所有伟大的神学家都杀死了上帝, 他们不得不用巨大的恐怖来杀死上帝—— 想到路德。 这其实只是打开了宽宏大量的可能性。 考虑并不特殊。 这对受过相对教育的人来说非常困难。

featured.content: Welcome back, fiends! Blaine Grimes, Blake Collier, Caleb Stallings, and I are back with the Spooky Season film roundtable, and this week we are watching John Carpenter’s In the Mouth of Madness , the third of his “Apocalypse” films. So file in to Row D, your seat’s a few down from ours and right next to Sam Neill, who’s gulping down popcorn and drawing more crosses on his face. Let’s go a little crazy! Ian : Caleb, what led you to pick In the Mouth of Madness ? Caleb : I actually watched it earlier this year on my quest to see every John Carpenter film. This was the final movie of his I hadn’t seen. And it was the perfect one to end on. An autumnal, meta movie about authorship and terror. Just right up my alley. And what better way to go insane than in an impossibly dark cathedral in an autumnal New England town? Who wouldn’t want to watch a movie about that? And who wouldn’t want it to happen to them too? Ian : Well, when you put it that way … Blake : I was really struck this time by Trent and Cane’s dialogue when Cane states, “I am God now …” and Trent responds something to the effect of “I didn’t know God was a hack horror writer.” It’s a great comeback but also chilling in that humans, no matter their brilliance and no matter how well-adjusted they present as being, are hacks when it comes to authoring their own stories, let alone the stories of others. Only God can weave the narrative in such a way that the goodness, justice, and mercy of the ending is earned. Caleb : And that sanity is maintained! Blake : Exactly! Caleb : If fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, then trying to usurp him is entering the Mouth of Madness. Ian : It is, but it’s a sanity that might look insane to the surrounding world. And that’s the question with Trent, isn’t it? He sounds insane, but he sees through the bogus story Cane is weaving. Blake : In this way, I think the film makes for a thrilling blueprint of the failures of humans trying to weave together the grand narrative of existence, and how fiction can portray our own failures to usurp God’s position and role. Caleb : This reminded me of Tim Keller recounting how Dorothy Sayers wrote herself into her own detective novels to be a help and savior of a sort to her own protagonist, Peter Wimsey. In the Mouth of Madness tells the opposite story: Sutter Cane writes himself into his stories to destroy his characters. Blake : So in this way, Cane is a type of Satan … which means Dante’s footprint is all over this film as well. Blaine : *In Gordon Ramsey voice* Bloody hell. Here we go again … Ian : You know, I’m something of a Dante adaptation myself! We are all creatures spoken into existence, in a story in which, like Sayers, the Teller, the Creator, becomes a character. And there are so many stories vying for authoritative interpretation of the world and of what we are. Caleb : There’s something interesting too in how many times it’s mentioned that the film rights to Cane’s book have been optioned. I think Carpenter was playing with how many people are only familiar with these stories via the film medium, which I imagine is even more true now, 30 years later. And the movie ends, not with Trent rereading Cane’s book to find out how it all ends but rather alone in a theater, eating popcorn and laughing hysterically (almost weeping) as he watches his own life play out, rather absurdly, on the silver screen. Blake : In some ways it is the mixed moral affection of giving oneself over to something that isn’t a wholly moral good. I think again of the ending of THE VVITCH where our protagonist is levitating in the air, and her face is both ecstatic and terrified with tears rolling down. Ian : It seems like the insane ecstasy of embracing oblivion. Here it’s the film adaptation, but this could just as easily be a Reel or a TikTok: all of which are in the mouth of madness. And all feature subjects playing at being the main character of a story they’re manufacturing, one that reduces and demeans a
featured.content_zh: 欢迎回来,恶魔们! Blaine Grames, Blake Collier, Caleb Stallings, 我又回到了Spooky Season电影圆桌会议上, 本周我们正观看约翰·卡彭特的"疯狂之口", 这是他第三部"启示录"电影。 因此,请向D行报告,你的座位从我们的座位倒下,紧挨着Sam Neill。 Sam Neil正在倒下爆米花并画出更多的十字架。 让我们有点疯狂吧! Caleb,是什么让你选的? 在疯狂之口? 凯勒布(Caleb):我今年早些时候在看约翰·卡彭特的电影时看过。 这是我从未看过的最后一部电影。 它是一个完美的结束。 一部秋天的,关于作者和恐怖的电影. 就在我的小巷边 比起在秋天的新英格兰小镇 一个不可想象的黑暗大教堂里 还有什么更好的办法去疯狂? 谁不想看电影? 谁不希望他们也遭遇这样的事? Ian:当你这么说的时候... 布莱克(Blake):这次我被特伦特和肯恩的对话深深地打击了,当时肯恩说,“我现在是上帝了......”而特伦特却回应了“我不知道上帝是黑客恐怖作家”这样的大意。 写自己的故事, 更不要说别人的故事了。 只有上帝才能编织叙事,使结局的善良,正义和慈悲得到伸张. 凯勒布: 保持这种理智! 布莱克:没错! 迦勒:如果对耶和华的恐惧是智慧的开始,那么试图篡夺他就是进入了疯狂之口. 伊恩(Ian):的确如此,但对于周围的世界来说,这是一种可能显得疯狂的理智。 这就是特伦特的问题,不是吗? 他听起来很疯狂 但他从假故事中看出 坎恩在编织 布莱克: 我认为这部电影为人类试图编织出关于存在的宏伟故事的失败,以及虚构如何描绘我们自己篡夺上帝的地位和角色的失败,提供了令人惊叹的蓝图。 凯勒布: 这让我想起了蒂姆·凯勒(Tim Keller)讲述了多萝西·赛耶斯(Dorothy Sayers)如何把自己写入她自己的侦探小说中,成为她自己的主角彼得·温西(Peter Wimsey)的某种帮助和救世主. 在"疯狂之口"(The Mouth of Madness)中讲述了相反的故事:萨特·克恩将自己写入他的故事来毁灭他的角色. 布莱克: 因此,通过这种方式,甘恩是撒旦的一种类型... 这意味着但丁的足迹也遍布本片. 布莱恩:*在戈登·拉姆齐的声音*血腥地狱. 伊恩:你知道,我自己也是但丁的适应者。 我们都是生命中的生物, 在一个故事里,像塞耶斯,特勒尔,造物主,成为一个人物。 有许多故事要求权威地解释世界和我们是什么。 Caleb : 多少次提到对Cane书的电影权被选择, 我认为卡彭特在和多少人通过电影媒介 对这些故事很熟悉, 我想现在,30年后,这更真实了。 电影的结局不是在特伦特重读了肯恩的书之后,他才知道这一切的结局,而是在剧院里独自一人,一边吃爆米花一边歇斯底里地取笑(几乎哭泣),一边在银幕上看自己的生活。 布莱克: 在某些方面,将自己交给并非完全出于道德利益的东西是一种混合的道德情感。 我又想起了VVITCH的结局 主角在空中飘来飘去 她的脸既兴奋又被泪水所吓倒 伊恩: 这似乎像疯狂的迷幻 拥抱遗忘。 这是电影的改编, 但这是Reel或TikTok, 所有玩耍的题材都是他们制作的故事的主角 一个减少和贬低

featured.title_zh: 卡尔和劳拉·伦茨谈论五年的公开判断： “你不能从我们的故事中看不到上帝”
featured.content: Five years ago, Laura Lentz had more advice than she wanted. People who had never met her were telling her what to do about her husband, her marriage and her future. “Getting all these opinions and judgments from the outside when no one really knows what’s going on,” she says. “Only the people that are in this know what it takes.” In November 2020, Hillsong founder Brian Houston told staff that Carl Lentz was out at the church’s Manhattan campus, citing breaches of trust. An extramarital affair had come to light. Laura, who had done nothing to land in that spotlight, found herself in it anyway. This month the two of them released a book, Overcoming Infidelity: 10 Conversations To Help Heal the Hurt , and the couple sat down with us to talk about how they got from there to here. “I struggled with a lot of anxiety and just struggling with the opinions of others,” Laura says. “I had to really make sure that didn’t get in here and just remind myself that this is what matters and only we know what’s going on. Lots of therapy has been great. And Jesus, of course, helping through this.” The criticism hasn’t ended, but she says it has changed. “Now I find that’s really gotten quite silent. I think the fruit of our relationship and the fruit of our kids’ lives and where we are now and even writing the book, like you can’t not see God through our story. You can’t not see the miracle through our story.” She is clear about what the book is not. “We’re not out here promoting the book like we’re out to save marriages,” she says. “It’s about me healing, him healing and seeing where that takes us.” The Secrets That Started Small Asked what signs a young married couple should watch for, both of them go to the same place: secrets. “It’s not just big secrets, it’s like the little things,” Laura says. “If you can’t be honest or you’re hiding things from your spouse, those are dangerous and they just compound.” She remembers praying in the weeks before everything surfaced. “I don’t know what it is, but God, you’ve got to get this, just get it out.” Carl says the distance did not begin with the affair. “You don’t start keeping secrets about cheating. You start keeping secrets about fear.” He describes deciding what his wife could handle and keeping the pressure to himself. “It’s when I made the decisions for her on what she was capable of holding,” he says. “Then you stack them and you stack them. By the time you get to the horrific stuff, you’ve already got a pattern of hiding stuff.” What he tells young men now is blunt: get used to being vulnerable with your wife. “It turns out it’s very attractive.” He also rejects the idea that pastors have nobody to tell. “If anybody ever says ‘I didn’t have anybody to be open with,’ I lovingly say I don’t believe you. You chose to not tell anybody.” He says that if he had called Houston on a bad day, he would have been flown out to help. “I did not call. I was not honest. That’s on me.” What Staying Actually Looked Like People tell the spouse who stays that she is brave. Laura is not sure that’s the right word. “It’s so hard to stay, it’s so hard to go,” she says. “Yes, I was brave, I guess, but I was also taking a risk.” She says she would never tell someone to stay in an adulterous relationship, and that she herself saw evidence of change before she did. “There’s gotta be evidence of things that are changing for you to stay and he’s gotta be doing his work.” She describes the early days in small units of time. “We literally went one day at a time. I would wake up and go, okay, I can do today. And that was it.” Carl, a basketball fan, says she has learned the language for it. “Every day, I’m on a one-day contract. That’s an upgrade from a two-hour contract that I was on for quite a long time.” The marriage that came out of that, Laura says, is not the one they had before. “Marriage 2.0 is like so much deeper. Our marriage was fine, but it wasn’t like it is now.” Carl is careful to say it isn’t easy. Some da

featured.title: Meet Elle Limebear, the British Artist Who Turned a School-Assembly Hymn Into a UK No. 1
featured.summary: The daughter of Delirious? frontman Martin Smith rebuilt “Oil in My Lamp” for a new generation, and “Give Me Joy” has spent nine weeks atop the UK Christian chart.
featured.summary_zh: Delirious主唱马丁·史密斯（ Martin Smith ）的女儿为新一代重建了“Oil in My Lamp” ， “Give Me Joy”在英国基督教排行榜上排名第九。
featured.title_zh: 认识英国艺术家Elle Limebear ，他将学校集会赞美诗变成了英国第一
featured.content: Elle Limebear used to have a hard time describing her dad’s job. When classmates asked what he did, she’d say he was in a band, then that it was Christian music, then that it was sort of rocky, and then she’d watch the conversation go nowhere. Some days she wished he were “just a plumber dad.” Her father is Martin Smith, the frontman of Delirious?, the British band behind “History Maker” and “Did You Feel the Mountains Tremble?” and one of the defining worship bands of the late ‘90s and 2000s. She remembers touring the US as a kid, on big tour buses, with people lining up for photos with him. Back home in their English village, “no one really cared.” Limebear now lives in Brighton with her husband, Tom, and their three young children, and the song she’s best known for is one almost every British adult has sung. “Give Me Joy,” released in July, reworks the hymn “Oil in My Lamp.” It debuted at No. 1 on the Official UK Christian & Gospel Singles Chart and has held the top spot for nine weeks since. Decca Records, which announced her signing the same month, calls her its first contemporary Christian artist. The hymn was a fixture of British school assemblies, whether or not the school was religious. “If you sing ‘Oil in My Lamp,’ probably everyone will know it,” Limebear told RELEVANT. “It’s in our childhood. It’s in our bones almost.” She started slipping it into her live sets a few years ago. The reaction surprised her. “There was this eruption of, I know this. I remember being a kid singing this,” she said. “People just belted it, absolutely belted it.” Her husband suggested she rewrite it for people who never grew up singing it. Her first reaction was that the song was already a banner. “What a challenge.” She wrote new verses and melodies and kept the heart of it. When her new label asked whether she had anything to lead with, she figured the answer was no. “It’s a British kind of hymn-like thing,” she said. “Not super cool.” Then she played it for the team, a room of people who, in her words, don’t know Jesus. “They absolutely loved it and it brought them alive. They’re like, I remember singing this song.” The song was only a chorus and a verse at that point, and the response is what pushed her to finish it. Limebear never planned to be a songwriter. At 20 she was set on photography, which felt safe. “I could contain it, control it,” she said. Then she felt God tell her, clearly, to do music. “It didn’t feel like my thought.” She says fear kept her from believing she had anything to bring, and she didn’t know how to write songs. “Back then I was definitely hesitantly walking through these doors full of fear. Now I feel like I’m skipping through them.” The version of England she’s skipping through is a different one from the England she grew up in. She was the only Christian in her whole school, she said, and her youth group “saved my life.” Lately she hears from friends and church leaders across the country about people walking into church out of plain curiosity about Jesus. “There’s this thing called the quiet revival that they say is going on,” she said, “where people are just finding him in all sorts of places.” She remembers being the weirdest person in the room for it. Now, she says, people are discovering that “actually, being a Christian isn’t that weird.” Her takeaway for believers is the same one. “I think we should all be more curious, even as Christians,” she said. “Get more curious. Ask more questions.” Asked what’s behind it, she didn’t pretend to know. “I don’t know is the answer.” She pointed to decades of quiet prayer, from older women in church prayer meetings to families praying at home for relatives to come to faith, and added: “God hears every prayer, doesn’t he?” and “nothing’s wasted.” She also described the last few years in the Church as “good, sad, confusing,” with “lots of walls” coming down, and says she senses something being built back up that looks different from before. featured.content_zh: Elle Limebear曾经很难描述她父亲的工作。 当同学们问他做了什么时, 她会说他在一个乐队里, 然后说这是基督教音乐, 然后是有点摇滚, 然后她会看着谈话无所作为。 她希望他“只是一个水管工爸爸”。 她的父亲是马丁·史密斯(Martin Smith),他是Delirious的前锋?),是“历史制造者”和“你感受了山地的风暴吗?” 背后的英国乐队,也是90年代后期和2000年代的决定性的崇拜乐队之一。 她记得小时候在美国巡演, 在大型旅游巴士上, 人们排队与他合影。 回到家乡的英国村落, Limebear现在与她的丈夫汤姆和他们三个年幼的孩子住在布莱顿,她最著名的一首歌是几乎每个英国成年人都有一首歌. “给我欢乐”,7月发行, 它在英国官方"基督教与福音单行道图"第1期首发并连续9周保持了顶尖位置. Decca唱片公司宣布同月签约,称她为"第一位当代基督教艺术家". 赞美诗是英国学校集会的定律,无论学校是否是宗教. “如果你唱出‘Oil in My Lamp', “这是在我们童年时期。 这几乎是在我们的骨头里。 她几年前开始把它滑入她的现场 反应让她吃惊了. “有一次爆发,我知道这一点。 我还记得小时候唱这个, “人们只是把它系上,绝对把它系上。” 她丈夫建议她为从未长大的歌唱者改写. 她的第一个反应是这首歌已经是一面旗帜. “真是挑战。” 她写了新的诗和旋律,并保持了它的心脏. 当她的新标签问她是否有 任何领导,她认为答案是否定的。 “这是英国的一种赞美诗。 “不是超级酷。” 她为球队演奏, “他们绝对喜欢它,它使他们生还。 他们喜欢, 我记得唱这首歌。 这首歌当时只是一首合唱和一首诗作曲,回应是促使她完成的. Limebear从未计划做作曲家. 20岁时她被设定在摄影上 这感觉很安全 她说,“我可以控制它,控制它。” 然后她觉得上帝告诉她,很明显, 做音乐。 “这不像我的想法。” 她表示害怕让她无法相信她有什么要带的东西, “那时我确实犹豫地走进这些充满恐惧的门去。 现在我觉得自己正在跳过它们。 她跳过英国的版本与她成长的英国不同. 她说她是全校唯一的基督徒, 最近她从全国各地的朋友和教会领袖那里听到人们出于对耶稣的纯粹好奇而走入教堂. 她说 , “ 有一种叫静静的复兴的东西, 他们说,“人们正在各种地方找到他。 ” 她记得是房间里最怪的人 现在,她说,人们正在发现,“事实上,作为一个基督徒并不奇怪。 她的信徒们的外出也是一样 她说,“我认为我们都应该更加好奇,即使是基督徒。” “更加好奇。 问出更多问题。” 她并没有假装知道。 “我不知道答案是什么。 她提到了数十年的静静祈祷,从在教堂祈祷会的年长妇女到在家里为亲戚们祈祷的家庭,并补充说:“上帝听到每一个祈祷,不是吗?”和“没有浪费的东西。 ” 她还将教会的过去几年描述为"美好,悲伤,困惑","许多墙壁"倒下,并说她感觉到一些正在被重建起来的东西看起来与以前不同. 她说是换衣服

featured.title_zh: 你能在积累财富的同时仍然跟随耶稣吗？是的，但首先定义“足够”。
featured.content: The first decent paycheck can come with an unexpected side of guilt. Maybe your salary no longer starts with a 4, or your savings finally hit a number that once sounded rich. The relief is real. So is the question: Am I allowed to want more? For Christians raised to view wealth with suspicion, professional success can feel surprisingly complicated. The paychecks get bigger, but the question of what faithful ambition looks like often goes unanswered. Paige Whitaker thinks the question is worth asking, and that the guilt is pointed at the wrong thing. “I don’t believe wealth and purpose are competing pursuits,” says Whitaker, brand growth and partnerships manager at 316 Financial, a faith-forward bank. “Throughout Scripture, we see faithful people who were blessed with significant resources. The real question is whether we own our money or our money owns us.” Abraham was rich. So were Job, Lydia and Joseph of Arimathea. Scripture doesn’t treat having money and worshiping it as the same thing. Jesus put it plainly: you just can’t serve two. “Wealth becomes dangerous when it becomes our identity, our measure of success, or the thing we rely on most,” Whitaker says. Define “enough” before you get there One practical move: Define enough before your income makes it easy to keep moving the goalposts. “Purpose acts as a guardrail,” Whitaker says. “It helps us define ‘enough’ and reminds us why we’re pursuing financial success in the first place. Without purpose, it’s easy to spend a lifetime chasing bigger numbers while missing what truly matters.” Write it down. A number for the emergency fund. A lifestyle line you won’t cross even when you could. A giving percentage that goes up with your income instead of down. The point is to make the decision once, on purpose, so you’re not renegotiating it with yourself every time a bonus hits. Ask a different set of questions Building wealth with purpose, Whitaker says, starts by changing the questions. Instead of “how do I get more,” ask what the money is for. She points to serving others, providing for family, supporting churches and investing in communities and causes that matter. Run your own money through it. What does your current budget say you care about? If the honest answer is DoorDash and a car payment, that’s data, and now you know what to change. When the increase comes Markeia Johnson leads the Financial Stewardship Committee at 316 Financial, and she gets specific about what to do when the raise actually lands. “When financial increase comes, our response should be guided by prayer and purpose rather than increased spending,” she says. “Additional resources can be used to reduce debt, build savings, invest for the future, support ministry and help those in need.” Notice what’s missing: “upgrade everything.” Lifestyle creep is the quiet way money takes over. Every raise gets absorbed, enough keeps moving, and ten years in you make three times what you did and feel exactly as stretched. “Having the means to make a purchase does not always make it the right decision,” Johnson says. Money as a tool Both return to Matthew 6:33, where Jesus tells His followers to seek God’s kingdom first. “When we seek God’s Kingdom first, money becomes a tool for stewardship rather than a source of security or identity,” Johnson says. “True prosperity is measured not by how much we possess, but by how faithfully we use what God has entrusted to us.” “Money is a tool, not a destination,” Whitaker says. “Wealth is valuable because of what it enables us to do, not because of what it says about us.” Build wealth. Negotiate the raise. Learn how a Roth IRA works. But decide what the money is for before it starts making those decisions for you. “Wealth is a wonderful servant but a terrible master,” Whitaker says. “The goal isn’t simply to build more wealth. The goal is to use what God has entrusted to us to make a meaningful impact.” This article is presented in partnership with 316 Financial, a faith-forward
featured.content_zh: 首个体面的薪水 会有出乎意料的负罪感 也许你的薪水不再从4分开始 或者你的积蓄终于打入了一度听起来很有钱的数字 解脱是实相. 问题是:我是否可以要求更多? 对于被培养成以怀疑来看待财富的基督徒来说,职业上的成功会感到令人惊讶地复杂. 薪水越来越高,但关于什么是忠诚的野心的问题往往得不到答复。 佩奇·惠特克(Paige Whitaker)认为这个问题值得问起,而内疚被指向了错误的东西. “我不相信财富和目的是相互竞争的追求, ”惠特克说, “我们通过《圣经》看到那些获得大量资源的忠实的人们。 真正的问题是,我们是拥有我们的钱还是拥有我们的钱。” 亚伯拉罕很有钱. 约伯,莉迪亚和阿里玛西亚的约瑟夫也是 圣经不把有钱当做同一件事。 耶稣直言不讳地说, Whitaker说,“当Wealth成为我们的身份、衡量成功或我们最依赖的东西时,Wealth变得危险。” 在你到达之前定义“足够” 。 一个实际动作:在收入允许继续移动门柱之前定义足够。 Whitaker说,“目的充当护卫。 “这帮助我们定义`足够', 却忽略了真正重要的东西。 写下来 紧急基金号码 即使可以, 你也不会跨越生活方式界线。 给定的百分率随着收入的上升而不是下降。 关键是要有目的地做一次决定, Whitaker说,从改变问题开始, 而不是“我怎样得到更多”, 她提到为他人服务,提供家庭,支持教会,投资于社区,并造成这一问题。 自己用自己的钱 你的当前预算是怎么说的? 如果诚实的答案是DoorDash和汽车付款,那就是数据,现在你知道该改变什么。 当增加额出现时,Markeia Johnson 领导金融管理委员会 316 Financial, 她得到了具体如何做 当提高额实际落地。 她说,“当资金增加时,我们的反应应以祈祷和目的为指导,而不是增加开支。” “额外资源可用于减少债务、建立储蓄、对未来进行投资、支持部委和帮助需要帮助的人。” 注意所缺少的:“提升一切。” 生活方式的变态是金钱占据的安静方式. 每次加薪都会被吸收, 足够继续移动, 十年里你做出三倍的功劳, 感觉完全一样拉长。 Johnson说,“拥有购买手段并不总是做出正确的决定。” 钱作为工具 两人回到马太福音6: 33 他的追随者首先寻求上帝的王国. “当我们首先寻求上帝的王国时,金钱成为管理的工具,而不是安全或身份的来源。” “真正的繁荣不是以我们拥有多少来衡量的,而是以我们如何忠实地使用真主所委托我们的东西来衡量的。” Whitaker说:“金钱是一种工具,而不是目的地。” “韦尔斯之所以有价值,是因为韦尔斯使我们能够这样做,而不是因为它对我们所说的话。” 建设财富. 谈判加薪。 学着罗斯爱尔兰共和军的工作原理 但是在它开始为你做那些决定之前 先决定这笔钱是用来做什么的 Whitaker说:“韦尔是一个出色的仆人, “目标不仅仅是创造更多的财富。 目的是利用上帝赋予我们的东西来产生有意义的影响。” 本条是与316 Financial合作提出的,后者是信仰前卫。

featured.title_zh: 在华盛顿巫师队输给猛龙队之后，他们邀请了斯科蒂·巴恩斯加入他们的祈祷圈
featured.content: In the NBA, the postgame TV interview moves fast. The horn sounds, the star of the night gets steered toward the sideline and a reporter is waiting with a microphone before he’s caught his breath. After the Toronto Raptors beat the Washington Wizards 112-102 on Friday, Oct. 23, the microphone was ready. But Scottie Barnes was walking across midcourt with a Gatorade towel over his head, headed for the Wizards’ postgame prayer circle. A player in the Washington group waved him over. Barnes stepped in among forward Anthony Gill and a handful of Wizards players, and the circle closed around him. Barnes, Toronto’s 25-year-old forward and a former NBA Rookie of the Year, had just finished with 28 points, 14 rebounds and five assists. Toronto’s TV broadcast, meanwhile, was holding for him. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bleacher Report (@bleacherreport) “He just took off,” one of the Raptors’ broadcasters said as Barnes joined the huddle. “So we’ll wait a minute for him to return.” A few seconds later, the call caught up to the picture: Barnes was “in the huddle there with the Wizards players, sharing a prayer as the Toronto Raptors come away with this victory.” When the circle broke, there were hugs all around, and Barnes started back across the floor with the towel around his neck. “Here comes Scottie,” the broadcast said, sending it down to the sideline. The microphone was still waiting. Gill, in his seventh season with Washington, was one of five finalists for the J. Walter Kennedy Citizenship Award in 2024, which NBA writers give for community service. He has talked publicly about his faith, too. Sharing the stage with Orlando Magic forward Jonathan Isaac at Liberty University’s convocation in 2024 , he told students that people assume an NBA player has “it all figured out.” “They assume that just because you’ve been blessed with a lot of money, life should be easy,” he said. He also said, “I tell myself I need to be more like Jesus. And what was Jesus? The ultimate servant. So, I serve the people around me.”
featured.content_zh: 在NBA,游戏后电视采访动作快. 一名记者拿着麦克风在等待, 在多伦多猛禽于10月23日(星期五)击败华盛顿巫师112-102后,麦克风已经准备好了. 但史考特·巴恩斯正带着加多拉德的毛巾走过中庭, 华盛顿集团的一位球员向他挥手. 巴恩斯在前锋安东尼·吉尔和少数"巫师"球员中出场,圆圈就围住他. 巴恩斯,多伦多25岁的前锋和前NBA年度Rookie,刚刚完成了28分,14回升和5次助攻. 多伦多的电视广播也支持他。 在Bleacher Report(@bleacherreport)分享的Instagram A文章上, 我们等一等他回来。 数秒钟后,这个电话紧紧抓住了画面:巴恩斯“与巫师队的球员们站在那里,在多伦多猛禽队获得这场胜利时分享祷告。” 圆相破裂后,周围都抱了起来,巴恩斯从对面的地上起,脖子被毛巾缠住. Scottie说, 麦克风还在等呢 吉尔在与华盛顿的第七季中,是2024年J. Walter Kennedy Citizenry奖的5名决赛选手之一,NBA作家们为社区服务献出. 他也公开谈论他的信仰。 他在2024年自由大学的集会上与奥兰多魔术前锋乔纳森·艾萨克分享舞台, 生活应该很轻松。 他还说:"我对自己说,我需要更像耶稣. 耶稣是什么? 终相侍从. 因此,我为身边的人服务。”

featured.content: Forrest Frank has released the first trailer for The Jesus Generation , a documentary about his record-setting Jesus Generation Tour. Lionsgate will distribute the film, which includes appearances by Rick Rubin, Philip Anthony Mitchell and Sadie Robertson, among others. Forrest posted the teaser to YouTube and Instagram, with a sign-up page for updates at forrestfrank.com . A director and release date haven’t been announced yet. The Jesus Generation Tour ran 29 cities from June 1 at the BOK Center in Tulsa, Oklahoma, to a sold-out finale at Globe Life Field in Arlington, Texas, where more than 35,000 people came. More than 519,000 people attended in two months, which makes it the biggest Christian music tour in history. It also registered outside Christian music. One count named it the biggest arena tour overall. Pollstar ranked the tour No. 5 on its LIVE75 chart in late June, behind Bad Bunny, BTS, Luke Combs and Iron Maiden, who were all playing stadiums. Pollstar said it was the highest chart position of any artist booked primarily in arenas. Early reported shows averaged about 18,000 tickets a night. Hersheypark Stadium in Pennsylvania drew 27,365 people on June 15, and GEODIS Park in Nashville drew 23,667 four days later. Tori Kelly, Cory Asbury and The Figs supported the tour. Demand was there before the first show. Pollstar reported in December that the tour had already passed 470,000 tickets sold. The growth is steep. His first headline run, the 2024 Child of God Tour, drew 48,246 people over 17 shows. The following year, the Child of God Tour Part 2 drew 214,626 fans to 26 shows. This year’s tour more than doubled that attendance. The music behind it has been on a similar run. Child of God II debuted at No. 12 on the Billboard 200 and logged the most weeks at No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Christian Albums chart. “Your Way’s Better” was the No. 1 Hot Christian Song of 2025 and broke into the Hot 100. Forrest has also placed 70 songs on the Hot Christian Songs chart, the most of any artist. Here is the teaser:

featured.title_zh: 购买10种主食需要美国人平均花费一小时的工作时间。在某些国家/地区，这需要超过19天
featured.content:
Ten basic foods now cost more than a week of work in 11 of the 56 countries surveyed in a new
Price Shocks report
from World Vision, and nine of those 11 are in Sub-Saharan Africa. In Sudan, buying them takes 19.3 eight-hour workdays. In Myanmar, 10.1, and in Haiti, 9.5. In the Central African Republic, buying them takes 30.1 days. In the U.S., it takes an hour.
Between November 2025 and May 2026, researchers priced the same ten foods at local markets, shops and supermarkets: a kilogram each of bananas, rice, wheat flour, sugar, maize and tomatoes, a dozen eggs, a liter of cooking oil, a liter of milk and one raw chicken. They then compared the cost of those ten foods with each country’s average income per person, adjusted for purchasing power, to work out how many hours of work it takes to afford them. That is a national average, not a minimum wage, so a lower-paid worker would need even longer.
Average income can hide inequality and may overstate what the poorest families can buy. Four countries with active conflict or collapsed institutions, South Sudan, Afghanistan, Syria and Venezuela, were left out of the hours analysis because there was no income data to compare, so the survey found bad situations but misses the worst ones.
Sudan shows how hard a conflict zone is to measure. The survey recorded the Sudanese price of the ten foods getting 36 percent cheaper than in 2024, yet the report says famine was present in parts of the country in 2025 and 2026, and Sudan is still one of the least affordable places in the study.
The report also profiles families living with the numbers.
Khin, 45, earns money ironing and washing clothes in Myanmar’s Yangon Region. Her husband can’t work because of poor health, and they have eight children. “There are days when my children eat rice with only oil and salt,” she is quoted as saying. “This is no longer occasional; it has become a daily reality.”
She says her twins are becoming malnourished and having digestive issues. Her 12-year-old daughter, Chit, told the report’s authors that fish and chicken have given way to spinach, tea leaf salad and fermented fish sauce.
In Hinche, Haiti, Cherlande runs a market stall that pays for her children’s school, their clothes and the family’s food, and she says she has no other income. A cup of rice that cost 20 or 25 gourdes now costs 50, she says, and a small packet of spaghetti has gone from 50 gourdes to 100. “You can’t afford to eat meat every day,” she said.
In 2025, an estimated 35.5 million children were acutely malnourished worldwide, nearly 10 million of them severely, according to the Global Report on Food Crises figures the report cites. Malnutrition can damage a child’s physical and cognitive development and weaken immunity, and the effects can last into adulthood.
The report asks governments, donors and businesses to protect children’s access to food during crises, expand school meals and social protection, and invest in local food systems.
Compassion International
works on the same problem from another angle, and says it provides children living in poverty with care that includes meals, tutoring and medical care.
TAKE ACTION
Read the
full report
, pass it to someone who has never thought about groceries in terms of days of work, and pray for the families behind the numbers.
featured.content_zh:
在新调查的56个国家中,有11个国家现在有10个基本食品需要一周以上的工作。
价格冲击报告
这11个国家中有9个位于撒哈拉以南非洲。 在苏丹,购买它们需要19.3个8小时的工作日。 分布于缅甸,10.1,以及海地等地. 9.5. 在中非共和国,购买它们需要30.1天。 在美国,需要一个小时.
2025年11月至2026年5月,研究人员在当地市场,商店和超市对同10种食品进行了定价:香蕉,大米,小麦面粉,糖,玉米和番茄各一公斤,鸡蛋一打,食用油一升,牛奶一升和生鸡一分. 然后,他们将这十种食品的成本与每个国家的人均收入进行比较,根据购买力进行调整,以确定支付这些食品需要多少工时。 这是全国平均工资,而不是最低工资,因此工资较低的工人需要更长的时间。
平均收入可以掩盖不平等,可能过分夸大最贫穷家庭可以购买的东西。 南苏丹、阿富汗、叙利亚和委内瑞拉四个冲突频繁或机构崩溃的国家没有时间分析,因为没有收入数据可供比较,因此调查发现情况不佳,但错过了最糟糕的情况。
苏丹表明,冲突地区的衡量有多难。 调查记录了这十种食品的苏丹价格比2024年便宜36%,然而报告却说该国部分地区在2025年和2026年发生了饥荒,而苏丹仍然是研究中最负担得起的地方之一.
报告还描述了与人数有关的家庭。
在缅甸仰光地区, 她丈夫因健康不佳无法工作, “有些时候,我的孩子只用油和盐来吃米饭。” “这不再是偶然的;它已成为日常的现实。”

featured.title: What Is Rest For?
featured.summary: Reflections on a Sabbatical   The post  What Is Rest For?  appeared first on  Mockingbird .
featured.summary_zh: 关于学术休假的思考文章《休息是为了什么？》首先出现在《知更鸟》上。
featured.title_zh: 休息的目的是什么？
featured.content: This past summer marked my eighteenth year in full-time pastoral ministry work. I have served churches in Sacramento, Hawaii, and now Minnesota (makes perfect sense). My congregation here in Bloomington (we just hosted the fall Mbird conference!) decided several years ago to establish a sabbatical policy for our pastors. A sabbatical is extended paid time off, anywhere from a month to a year, for the individual to rest and/or research. The modern versions of this started at Harvard in the late 1800s as a way for professors to have a break from the grind of classrooms to dive deeper into some form of research. In recent years, this concept has expanded to many professions, and particularly into ministry. The sabbatical I received this past summer was three months and carried no requirement for continuing ed or book writing. The goals were to unplug, rest, and spend time with family. They also wanted me to provide some reflections on the experience. Not wanting this to be a summer vacation report on steroids, I thought I would provide a general view to the experience, with some deeper reflection on the nature and purpose of rest. My hope is that you will be able to recognize God’s gifts of rest in your own life. Though I gave you the quick definition of a sabbatical, the concept is rooted in God’s Word, so I turned there first to try and make sense of the strangeness I just experienced. Leviticus isn’t the first place I think of in terms of grace and rest, and yet in chapter 25 the Lord instructs the following: “For six years sow your fields, and for six years prune your vineyards and gather their crops. But in the seventh year the land is to have a year of sabbath rest” (Lev 25:3–4). He goes on to describe how the land going a bit wild will still provide food to eat but shouldn’t be in any sense “worked on.” It sounds strange to my ears to hear that the land itself needs a break. Does it manage a life/work balance? Is there a time when it stops doing what it’s doing? Jesus doesn’t add much clarity for me on this. In one instance he tells us that the flowers don’t “labor or spin” (Matt 6). In another the plants are described as growing unceasingly: “Night and day, whether he sleeps or gets up, the seed sprouts and grows, though he does not know how” (Mk 4). It’s helpful to not have clear pragmatism about the command to give land rest. We can, of course, point to studies about fallow fields. We can see that the lack of harvesting is about rest for the people. But the truth remains that God commands rest and doesn’t give us all the reasons why. The idea of sabbath is built into God’s created order. In other words, our discomfort with rest is strange, not the rest itself. Beyond Deserving But did I deserve a sabbatical? The very first Mockingbird conference I attended was in 2019 and titled: “Beyond Deserving: Hope in a World of Performance.” To say that I was at a point of burnout would be an understatement, and that conference and phrase are forever embedded in my heart. Grace is all about being beyond the question of what is deserved, and a true sabbatical is rooted in this. In the lead-up to my planned break, I tended to receive two kinds of responses from people concerning the idea. The first kind was more common and positive. Many people told me I deserved it and that pastors work hard and that I’ve earned it. These are kind words from kind people and rooted in love, and I accept them as such. But as I think about my life, I can’t say that I deserve three months of paid vacation to do what I want. Every time someone has asked about this, I feel a little uneasy and am certain there are way more deserving people who aren’t receiving such a gift. And some people told me as much! The second kind of response I received was along the lines of “Well, I pastored for 40 years and never had a break.” In other words, you young’uns are soft and you don’t deserve this sabbatical, so you shouldn’t have gotten one. featured.content: The Battle of Kadesh in the thirteenth century BC, between Egypt and the Hittite Empire, was one of the great battles of the ancient world, notable for both sides making heavy use of chariots. Archaeological and textual sources indicate that Kadesh was a bloody, chaotic stalemate that nearly ended in disaster for Pharoah Ramesses II and the Egyptian army. But Ramesses knew as well as any contemporary influencer that, sometimes, you have to dress things up a bit for your followers. Accordingly, he commissioned a set of temple reliefs at various sites in Egypt and Nubia depicting himself as a gargantuan, godlike being smiting the helpless Hittite warriors in a glorious victory for Egypt. The phenomenon of false or misleading images, it turns out, long predates large language models, Photoshop, or even the camera. On the other hand, the growing ubiquity of AI-produced content has certainly exacerbated the problem. In a recent article , Tyler Austin Harper — staff writer for the Atlantic and probably my favorite lefty writer — describes his love of “wetsuiting,” that is, wading out at night to remote sandbars or rocks to fish for striped bass. Some in this niche community post pictures of their catches on Instagram. “People who fish are habitual liars,” as Harper notes, fondly, but the increasing prevalence and sophistication of AI platforms now leaves Harper and his friends questioning not only the purported size of the pictured bass but whether it even exists at all. While photoshopping otherwise genuine images has long been an issue in the angling world, Harper complains that AI’s capability to create images from scratch “automates away the need not only to photograph a fish, but to even catch one in the first place.” Combined with the “documentary impulse” to gain notoriety online for one’s (ostensible) skills, AI tools provide an avenue to impressing others without the hassle of building those skills in the first place. For Harper, the worst part of it is the reflexive skepticism engendered by the pervasiveness of AI-produced slop. It’s a very human thing to be amazed by displays of skill — but now, if “AI makes it impossible to trust what we see … [then we] have lost the ability to believe in the accomplishments of others.” To be fair, there is such a thing as “healthy” skepticism. Even without AI, there’s no end to noise, rumor, speculation passed off as fact, and half-truths percolating about the internet and airwaves. Sometimes the effects are harmless enough. During Russia’s first invasion of Ukraine (c. 2014), I came across an article that Netflix had responded by suspending Vladimir Putin’s personal account. I shared the article completely in earnest, partly because I thought it was funny, partly as an indictment of the West’s weak response to Russian aggression. I had, in fact, fallen victim to “satire,” which was embarrassing enough, but hardly damaging to myself or anyone else. Other examples are less benign, like my online ranting against Elon Musk’s perceived Nazi salute — when, as it happened, even the ADL was urging the public to give Musk the benefit of the doubt. It’s probably unlikely, but certainly not impossible, that I tipped somebody somewhere a bit more in the direction of fear and resentment, in service of venting my feelings about my own hasty interpretation of a picture. *** Again, none of this is new. The world has always contained its share of charlatans, fraudsters, and demagogues making use of fact-free propaganda. Jesus himself encourages suspicion in some situations: Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look! Here is the Messiah!’ or ‘There he is!’ — do not believe it. For false messiahs and false prophets will appear and produce great signs and wonders, to lead astray, if possible, even the elect. (Mt 24:23–24) The problem is when skepticism becomes a baseline disposition or attitude. As Harper implies, it’s spiritually toxic to assume that one is being fed lies, that every claim or report (or image) i

featured.content: Welcome to the tenth edition of Mockingbird’s preacher interview series ! Over the past year, we’ve been interviewing some of our favorite ministers from diverse church contexts around the country to find out more about what is really working in American Christianity today and how to do church well. Our tenth interview is with one of Mockingbird’s OG contributors (active since 2007!), beloved co-host of The Mockingcast , and the current rector of Holy Trinity Episcopal Church in West Palm Beach, Florida, R-J Heijmen. [Note: If you want to hear more, make sure to check out R-J and Aaron Zimmerman’s conversation on “Renewing Your Local Congregation” from the spring 2026 Mockingbird Conference.] M: R-J Heijmen! Thank you so much for doing this. I’m a big fan. Why don’t you start by describing your current congregation for us? RH: Well, I’m at Holy Trinity, which is right downtown West Palm Beach. I’m sitting here in my office looking out at the Intracoastal Waterway in front of me, and then on the other side of me is Palm Beach, like the Palm Beach. I’ve been here for six-and-a-half years — I started in 2020. It’s a beautiful and historic church. It’s had its ups and downs, but at least since I’ve been here, and for a good long while before me, it’s been a warm, welcoming, easygoing, generous, serving, and reasonably diverse — for an Episcopal church — kind of place. Of course, when I got here in January 2020, the pandemic happened two months later. M: I was going to ask about that. RH: It was great timing … haha. When I started, my family was still back in Texas because our oldest son was a senior in high school. So I started in January and I said, “Hey, why don’t you guys just stay until school is out, and then we’ll move here together.” But I went home to Texas for spring break in March, and that’s when everything shut down. And the church was like, “Well, just stay in Texas, and come back when things open up.” So I started doing video worship in my backyard and posting it to YouTube, and then we started doing Zoom coffee hour and Zoom records forum and Zoom youth group and all that sort of stuff. We did finally move to Florida in June, but things were still shut down, obviously. So we installed a camera system in the church and started livestreaming. Then in September, we started doing drive-in worship — we bought an AM radio transmitter and people pulled into our parking lot, and we told them what frequency to tune to on the dial, and I was outside preaching and doing communion and whatever else. M: That’s so funny. RH: It was really funny. When it came time for communion, people would roll down their windows a little bit and I’d, like, slip the wafer in through the window. Anyway, our diocese was pretty flexible, so we were back in the church by October, I think, but with social distancing and masking. But within a few months, we were too many people for our space. Our church could normally fit 300, 350, but with social distancing it was like 100, depending on how many family groups there were. So then in January 2021, we started talking about, like, what do we do? Do we add another service? And then we decided to actually start worshiping outside — under a tent on our front lawn. It was Lent, so we called it “Lent in the Tent” to begin with. But it extended through June, and it was a really amazing time because a lot of other churches were closed, and people had nothing to do. So a lot of new people started coming, they brought their own chairs, they brought their coffee, they brought their dogs, their kids were running around, whatever. And because we’re downtown, people would be out, like, walking their dogs down our sidewalk, and they’d be looking over, like what is going on over there? So the pandemic ended up becoming a really good time for us. We were already a congregation willing to try things and take risks, which I liked. You know, we’re true to our Episcopal identity — we love that, but we were willing to try th
featured.content_zh: 欢迎来到Mockingbird的传教士访谈系列的第十版! 在过去一年里, 我们一直在采访一些我们最喜欢的部长, 他们来自全国各地不同的教会背景, 我们的第十次采访是Mockingbird的OG撰稿人之一(自2007年起活跃!),是TheMockingcast的受人喜爱的同台主播,也是佛罗里达州西棕榈滩圣三一主教座堂的现任校长R-J·海杰门. [注:如果你想听更多的话,请务必检查一下R-J和Aaron Zimmerman在2026年春季"Mockingbird Conference"上的谈话. ] M:R-J海门! 非常感谢你这样做。 我是一个伟大的粉丝。 为何不首先为我们描述你们目前的集会? (掌声) RH:嗯,我在圣三一, 位于西棕榈滩市中心。 我坐在我的办公室, 看着位于我面前的内海岸水道, 我在这里已经六年半了, 这是一个美丽而历史性的教堂。 但至少自从我来到这里, 在我之前的很长一段时间里, 这是一个温暖、欢迎、轻松、慷慨、服务、合理多样的地方, 当然,当我在2020年1月来到这里时,这种流行病发生在两个月后。 M:我本来要问的。 RH:这是很好的时机... 哈哈。 当我开始的时候,我的家人仍然在德克萨斯州,因为我们的长子是高中的高年级生. 我从一月份开始,我说:“嘿,你们为什么不呆到学校毕业,然后我们一起搬到这里去呢?” 我回到德克萨斯州, 在3月春假, 教会说,“好吧,留在德克萨斯,当事情开放时再来吧。” 于是我开始在我的后院进行视频崇拜, 并把它张贴到YouTube上, 然后我们开始做Zoom Coffee Hour和Zoom唱片论坛,Zoom青年团体等等。 我们终于在6月搬到了佛罗里达州 但显然事情还是被关闭了 于是我们在教堂安装了相机系统,并开始了活流. 然后在9月份,我们开始做驱入式礼拜——我们买了一台AM收音机,人们拉入了我们的停车场,我们告诉他们在拨号上要调频,我在外面传道,做圣餐等等。 M:这很有趣。 (笑声) (掌声) 这真的很有趣。 当圣餐到来的时候,人们会把窗户翻下一点,然后我从窗户里滑出蜡烛。 总之,我们的主教座堂是相当灵活的, 所以,我们回到了教堂 在10月,我想,但与 社会距离和面具。 但是在几个月内,我们的人太多了 我们的教堂通常可以容纳300到350人,但是随着社会距离的扩大,它就像100人,这取决于有多少家庭群体。 所以2021年1月,我们开始谈论,比如,我们该怎么办? 还要再加服务吗? 然后我们决定开始到外面去崇拜——在我们前草坪的帐篷下. 这是伦特,所以我们称它为“帐篷中的伦特”。 但是,它一直延续到6月,由于许多其他教堂关闭,人们无所事事,这真是令人惊叹的时刻. 所以很多新人开始来, 他们带来了自己的椅子, 他们带来了咖啡, 他们带来了他们的狗, 他们的孩子在跑来跑去,什么的。 因为我们是在市中心, 人们会出去, 像,走他们的狗走我们的人行道, 他们会看着, 像那里发生了什么? 因此,这种流行病最终成为了我们真正的好时机。 我们已经是一个会众 愿意尝试 和冒险,我喜欢。 你知道,我们忠于我们的主教身份——我们很喜欢,但我们愿意尝试

featured.content:
Six months ago, Togi said he spent $300,000 on a bender with his friends and that none of it came close to what his relationship with God gave him. Now he says his faith is lukewarm.
The Kick streamer, who has 1.9 million followers on Instagram, reposted the clip in his newest post with a caption that reads: “This is from about 6 months ago. A nice watch because right now at this moment in time my faith is lukewarm warm and idk why.” The post has more than 52,000 likes and 745 comments.
In the video, filmed in a car, he asks how many more women, drugs and yachts it would take to be happy. He says a lot of people don’t like it when he talks about God, and that no matter how many friends and boats you have, it means nothing without God. “If I have nothing but I have God,” he says, “I have everything that I would ever need.”
Togi’s baptism spread online in late January when he shared images of it after Christian influencer Bryce Crawford baptized him.

featured.title_zh: 乔纳森·艾萨克是NBA最直言不讳的基督徒之一。他最近更安静了，这是有目的的。
featured.content:
Near the end of his interview on the new RELEVANT Podcast,
Jonathan Isaac
was asked for the sound bite: one way the Lord’s been encouraging him lately, the kind of clip that does numbers on Instagram, a professional athlete saying something encouraging about faith.
Isaac laughed. “I wish it was that simple, right?”
A few years ago it might have been. Isaac, who’s starting his 10th season with the Orlando Magic, spent a stretch of his career as one of the league’s most visibly Christian players, with invitations to talk about faith on stages and broadcasts. Lately, he’s been quieter. He says that’s on purpose.
“I definitely felt the pressure of feeling like I had to speak out or say something, or kind of just wear my Christianity on my sleeve in a way that was going to make everybody else feel good,” he told RELEVANT. “And that really is tough. It’s a tough thing to deal with, even when you’re struggling in the background with faith or with your own struggles, while still having to present a certain way to other people.”
Eventually, Isaac decided to pull back.
“I’ve definitely taken a step back from being as vocal,” he said. “I don’t speak as much. I don’t do as much as I’ve done in the past, just from a standpoint of wanting to focus on myself and my relationship with Christ and growing in that way, rather than being what everybody else needs you to be.”
The pedestal problem
Isaac came to faith the way a lot of people do — church as a kid, songs and youth group and none of it his own — and then lost it to basketball, which he called “my god” from middle school through the draft. What changed him was getting everything the NBA had to offer and finding he “still felt as unfulfilled as I felt chasing the thing.” Faith became the identity that wasn’t a stat line.
As Isaac’s faith became more public, the invitations followed.
“We see somebody that agrees with us on something and they’re in some type of status,” he said, “and we want to have them out to all the speaking engagements and get them on all the podcasts and everything.”
Isaac doesn’t frame that attention as malicious. “It’s just a nature of the beast kind of thing,” he said. But it put public expectations around a faith he was still working out while, in his words, “fighting for faith, staying faithful, losing faith, all those different things.”
The way he puts it now is that following Jesus is hard enough without an audience.
“Just Christianity as a whole — it’s hard enough in today’s age to be faithful, to seek and search after God and to cultivate that relationship. It’s hard enough to do that, period,” he said. “Then to do it with eyes on you, and pressure, and people coming around for the wrong reasons, and having difficulty trusting it. It’s a lot.”
What he’d tell the next guy
The last few seasons have produced a steady stream of athletes going more public with their faith — public baptisms, online Bible studies, postgame interviews that open with Jesus. Asked whether Christian athletes talk to each other about the pressure that comes next, Isaac didn’t pretend they do.
“Man, I wish we did more than what it is,” Isaac said.
For Isaac, the important question is who is close enough to tell the truth when the platform gets bigger.
“It really is about the people that are around you, and having people that you really, really trust — especially when it comes to your leaders in a church setting,” he said. “Just having somebody where it’s not just you having this platform and navigating it by yourself. Because then, in my opinion, it’s easier to fall for that pressure of feeling like you need to present a certain way.”
When Isaac tore his ACL in 2020 and his Nike shoe deal ran out, his pastor at the time told him he should make his own shoe. So he surrounded himself with people he trusted in the industry and launched
UNITUS.

featured.title_zh: ChatGPT每周收到超过7000万个宗教问题
featured.content:
Turns out plenty of people are asking ChatGPT to explain the hard parts of the Bible. OpenAI says it gets more than 70 million religion-related requests every week, according to
an analysis it published
Oct. 8.
About 22 million of them are about studying religious texts. Another 16 million are about practices, holidays and observance, and 16 million more are about beliefs, meaning and spiritual guidance. The analysis covers September 2025 through September 2026.
Islam accounted for roughly 45% of the requests and Christianity for 34%, with Hinduism at 4%, Judaism at 2% and Buddhism at 1%. Christianity questions spike around Easter. Islam questions spike around Ramadan and Eid al-Adha.
Among the Christianity-related messages, nearly half are about Bible passages and another 13% are about worship, sermons or church practices. OpenAI says people ask ChatGPT to explain difficult passages and find commentaries from within their tradition. The average request sounds a lot more like small group than a debate about whether God exists.
Barna has found that practicing Christians already use AI at work and at home more than most Americans, and nearly half say they’d trust it with their spiritual growth. They use it more than their pastors do, too, and only about 12% of pastors feel ready to guide them on it.
OpenAI is careful to say AI “is not — and should not become — an arbiter of religious truth.” Sam Altman, for his part, has said
he’s “very uncomfortable” with people treating AI like a religion
.
Whether any of those conversations send someone back to an actual Bible, or an actual church, is something the report doesn’t say.

featured.title_zh: 彼得·蒂尔（ Peter Thiel ）花了三年时间讲解敌基督。这是他在说什么。
featured.content:
Peter Thiel co-founded PayPal and Palantir. He is a tech investor, not a pastor or a theologian, but for the last three years he’s been giving invitation-only lectures about the Antichrist.
The audio first surfaced a year ago, when
The Washington Post
and
The Guardian
reported on recordings of the series in October 2025.
The Verge
has now published an analysis written by David Gibson, a Catholic scholar and journalist who directs the
Center on Religion and Culture at Fordham University
.
The talks started in San Francisco in 2025, and in March Thiel took a
four-part series to Rome
.
His argument hangs on 1 Thessalonians 5:3, where Paul warns about people proclaiming “peace and safety.” Thiel reads that as the Antichrist’s slogan. In his version, the people pushing safety, from AI regulation to effective altruism, are a restraining force that paves the way for the Antichrist. In the first lecture he worries Cold War II could end in an unjust peace, a peace at any price.
Then come the names. Thiel says a friend urged him to tell the room Bill Gates is the Antichrist. He calls Gates a “Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde-type” who would give his soul for a Nobel Peace Prize. Greta Thunberg is “maybe sort of a type or a shadow.” Marc Andreessen is safe, because “the Antichrist is popular.” Earlier leaked snippets have him calling Pope Leo XIV Beijing’s “useful idiot” over AI regulation, and in a July essay for
First Things
,
“The Pope and the Antichrist,”
he floats that the late Pope Francis could have been the Antichrist.
Gibson, a Catholic, reads the lectures as “a fairly standard-issue American evangelical worldview,” and a fundamentalist one at that. Thiel is in no way a church leader, and he doesn’t speak for evangelicals, most of whom wouldn’t recognize their faith in a theology that names Bill Gates and AI regulation as the Antichrist’s allies. Gibson also argues Thiel misreads Pope Benedict XVI, whose writing on the apocalypse was about the future of the church, not a countdown.
Thiel once told a San Francisco audience that keeping people out of the room is good marketing. We’re all writing about it, so he may be onto something. The rest? Probably not.

那就来点名字吧 蒂尔说有个朋友劝他告诉比尔·盖茨是反基督者 他称盖茨为“Jekyll博士和Hyde-type先生”,他将为诺贝尔和平奖献出他的灵魂。 Greta Thunberg是“一种类型或影子”。 马克·安德烈森(Marc Andreessen)是安全的,因为“反基督者是受欢迎的。 ” 先前泄露的片段中,他称教宗李敖十四世为北京的"有用白痴",对AI的管制,在7月的一篇散文中,

Gibson是一位天主教徒,他把讲座看成是“相当标准的美国福音派世界观”,也是原教旨主义。 Thiel绝不是教会领袖, 他并不代表福音派, 他们大多不会承认他们信仰一种神学, 吉布森还论证了蒂尔误读了教宗本笃十六世,他在启示录上所写的是教会的未来,而不是倒计时.

featured.content: I’m excited to tell you the story of how God used a simple verse, from a complicated passage, to change the life of a man named Charles Spurgeon. His story is for everyone, but it may have a special word to speak to a few groups in the room. One is laymen — that is, people who work for a living in normal jobs, outside of Christian ministry. People without a seminary education, people who aren’t pastors or have ministry jobs. We recognize that this series has profiled four men who were preachers. Now, there is an interesting flow to our series: - first, Saint Augustine, - then, Luther, who was an Augustinian monk, - then, John Bunyan, whose favorite book outside the Bible was Luther’s commentary on Galatians, - now, Charles Spurgeon, whose favorite book outside the Bible was Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress. We’ve moved from one convert to another, each building in some way on the previous one, but a weakness of our series (in some sense) is that they all became preachers. And we don’t expect you all to become preachers; we’d like a few, but most will be laymen, and that’s good. Now, Spurgeon is known as “the Prince of Preachers.” But the hero, under God, in Spurgeon’s story is not Spurgeon, and not a trained, paid preacher, but a layman. So, Spurgeon’s story has a special word for laymen who are willing to open their mouths and say what they know about Jesus. Spurgeon’s story also has a special word for teens and young adults. Spurgeon came to faith at age fifteen, which in his day was far more like young adulthood. Still, his story offers a challenge to those who are no longer children and not yet established adults: teens, college students, grad students, even young professionals. Don’t let the world (or the church) lower your standards of what’s possible in being deeply converted and dedicated to Jesus — and how God can make his Son thrilling to a young soul. My prayer is that God might be pleased to give some their own engine. So often, parents, college workers, and pastors help young adults along and give them pushes. And then sometimes, God is pleased in the life of teenagers to give them their own engine, and they don’t need any more pushing. They say, “Get out of my way! I am going to follow Jesus. You can’t keep me from him and worship, my Bible, and prayer!” That’s what God did for Spurgeon at age fifteen — he gave him his own engine. And I pray he might be pleased to do that even here this morning. Spurgeon’s story speaks to one more group: those in the room who are willing to admit, “I’m here but I’m not saved.” For two thousand years, unsaved people have shown up at churches for all sorts of reasons. That’s Spurgeon’s story. He was searching. He was unsaved and in a church on a Sunday morning when God broke through. So, if you’d say this morning, “I haven’t settled the issue of my sin and rebellion against God,” or “I haven’t ‘been saved,’” or “if I died on the drive home today, I wouldn’t be at peace with my Maker,” this story has a special word for you. So, let me tell you about Charlie Spurgeon. His Early and Whole Life He was born in 1834, about 40 miles northeast of London, into a Christian family. In fact, both his father and grandfather were pastors. But his father met financial troubles and sent the young Charles to live with his grandparents from ages one to six. I don’t think this is an insignificant part of the story; don’t underestimate the effects of a good grandma and grandpa in the lives of our children. From their influence he emerged as “precocious,” learned to read, and first found Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress (which he would read more than a hundred times). From his earliest days, he was unusually sharp, ahead of his age level, “always reading books” (Spurgeon: A Biography, 8). He returned home at age six and excelled at school in both math and reading. 我非常兴奋地向大家讲述上帝如何用一段简单的诗句, 从一段复杂的段落中, 他的故事是针对每个人的,但可能有一个特别的单词,可以和房间里的几个团体交谈. 一个是外行者,也就是在基督教部之外从事正常工作谋生的人。

没有神学院教育的人, 我们承认,这一系列的描述 4人谁是传道者。

现在,我们的系列有一个有趣的流传:首先,圣奥古斯丁, 然后,路德,他是一个奥古斯丁的修道士, 然后,约翰·邦扬,他最喜欢的书是路德对加拉提安的评论, 现在,查尔斯·斯普吉翁,他最喜欢的书是"邦扬朝圣者的进步"。

但我们系列的一个弱点(某种意义上的)就是他们都成了传教士。 我们并不期望你们都成为传教士;我们想做几个,但多数是外行,这很好。

现在,斯普吉翁被称为"道教的王子". 但是,在上帝的统治下,在斯普吉翁的故事里,英雄不是斯普吉翁,也不是一个受过训练,有报酬的传教士,而是一名外行人. 因此,斯普吉恩的故事有一个特别的词来形容那些愿意张开口子,说出自己对耶稣所了解的. Spurgeon的故事中也有一个针对青少年和年轻成年人的特殊词.

斯普吉安在15岁时开始信仰,在他这一天,这更像是年轻的成年. 然而,他的故事给那些已经不是孩子和还没有成年的人带来了挑战:青少年,大学生,研究生,甚至年轻专业人员.

不要让世界(或教会)降低你对于什么是可能的, 我的祷告是 上帝可能很乐意 给一些自己的引擎。 父母、大学员工和牧师经常帮助年轻的成年人并给予他们推动。

有时,上帝在青少年生活中很高兴给他们自己的引擎,他们不需要再再推了. 他们说:你们离我远点! 我要跟随耶稣。 你无法阻止我远离他, 这是上帝在15岁时为斯波克森所做的——他给了他自己的引擎. 我祈求他今天上午也乐意这么做

Spurgeon的故事又讲述了一个群体:那些在房间里愿意承认“我在这里,但我没有被拯救。 ” 两千年来,无所救护的人出于各种原因都出现在了教堂. 这是斯普吉恩的故事。 他在寻找。 周日早上,上帝破门而入时,他被解剖,在教堂里。

所以,如果你今天上午说,“我还没有解决我的罪恶和反抗上帝的问题,”或者“我还没有`拯救',或者“如果我今天在回家的路上死了,我也不会与我的造物主和睦相处,”这个故事有一个特别的词给你。 让我告诉你查理·斯波克森的事 他于1834年生于伦敦东北约40英里处,进入基督教家庭.

事实上,他的父亲和祖父都是牧师。 但是他的父亲遇到了财政上的困难,并派年轻的查尔斯从一到六岁就和外祖父母住在一起. 我并不认为这是故事的次要部分,

从他们的影响力中,他出现了“珍贵的,”学会了阅读,并首先发现了邦扬的"朝圣者进步"(他将读一百多遍)。 从他最初的年代起,他就异常尖锐地领先于他的年龄,"总是阅读书籍"("外科医生:一部传记",8). 他六岁回家,在学校数学和阅读方面都非常出色。

featured.content: As we were finishing a counseling session, Jill looked at me with concern, her eyebrows furrowed. “You got distracted,” she bluntly stated. Unfortunately, Jill was right. Just outside my workspace, several pastors gathered in the church office lobby, talking and laughing. I’d gotten sidetracked by the commotion. About 70 percent of me was attending to Jill, but 30 percent of my headspace had shifted to the lobby: What are they doing? What’s so funny? We live in a distractible culture. Between YouTube shorts and checking our email inboxes every hour, our minds wander quickly. Staying focused is a skill few truly master. But it’s essential if we’re going to care well for God’s people. Whether formally or informally, counseling another soul is a distinct privilege. Yet, too often, mistakes plague our conversations. Fortunately, getting distracted is one of several common mistakes that are correctable. After Jill’s jarring comment, I closed the window blinds (simple fix), talked to the staff about keeping the commotion down (another simple fix), recommitted to staying focused (possible, though it would be work), and prayed the Lord would renew my love for his sheep. What counseling mistakes are you prone to make? Take a quick check. Mistake 1: Fear of Man Charlotte shares about her struggles with her job. She dislikes her boss, and she’s weary of her work. Unfortunately, she often responds to her difficulties with sinful choices. This time, she lied to her boss to get out of an assignment. You sympathize with her frustrations but feel convinced you’ve got to speak up about her lying. Charlotte’s a Christian, and Scripture makes clear that because God never lies, Christ’s followers shouldn’t either (Colossians 3:9–10; Titus 1:2). Yet you hesitate. You know Charlotte will get angry, and your fears kick in. Why bother bringing it up? Lying is between her and God. Right now, she needs a friend. But you know if you don’t say something, Charlotte will eventually lie to her boss again. What should you do? Repent of your fear that causes you to avoid a difficult word. Confess your worry about speaking up to the Lord (Psalm 34:4). If you struggle with people-pleasing, then saying a difficult word will feel painful. Reframe your situation by putting the fear of God at the center of your thinking (Proverbs 29:25; Luke 12:4–5). If we fear God more than Charlotte, we won’t let Charlotte’s potential anger get in the way. My friend Jonathan Leeman calls the helper in this situation a “sin-absorber.” A true friend willingly absorbs the cost of another person’s sin for the sake of honoring Christ. Would you be willing to absorb Charlotte’s anger if it helps her address her lie? Mistake 2: Assumed Insight Angela and John have been married for 31 years. Sometimes John gets frustrated with Angela because she assumes what he’s thinking. “I know I’m not supposed to assume,” Angela would think, “but we’ve been together for a long time.” The more familiar you are with someone, the more you’re likely to get in trouble. Familiarity breeds assumptions . Think about your last conflict. How many assumptions did you make? Probably a few. Assumptions can create problems. Sometimes our assumptions are true, but often they’re not. If you’re prone to making assumptions, here’s how to stay away from trouble: Don’t overestimate your ability to size up a situation. Pride makes you think, “I know what’s going on.” Humility tells you, “Ask God for wisdom.” The humble recognize they’re not as smart as they think and must depend on the Lord for insight (James 1:5). After you’ve asked the Lord for help, test your assumptions. Don’t tolerate any of them. Check the validity of your assumptions by asking thoughtful, careful, and loving questions. Genuine curiosity will lead you to ask rather than assume. At the encouragement of a friend, Angela asked more questions during marital conflict, and that built more understanding between her and John. The apostle Paul tells us that

featured.title: 当精神疾病成为身份标签
featured.summary: 当精神疾病成为身份标签，最需要帮助的人会不会反而被忽视？《都在你脑中》批评了浪漫化疾病、自我诊断和社交媒体追逐关注的风气。
featured.content: 弗雷德里克·德波尔（Frederik deBoer）曾因双相情感障碍被强制送进精神医疗机构。此后几年，他心里一直交织着两种感受：一方面，他由衷感激这个救了自己一命的医疗体系；另一方面，看到如今很少有人能像他一样得到帮助并慢慢康复，他又深感沮丧。 《都在你脑中：疾病成为身份、创伤成为时尚，以及对患病的渴望》（ All in Your Head: Illness as Identity, Trauma as Fashion, and the Desire to Be Disordered ）是他的最新力作。德波尔活跃于网络，常跟主流观点唱反调，自称“老派”马克思主义者，他最出名的一本书是《聪明崇拜》（ The Cult of Smart ）。这一次，他把批评的矛头对准了自己所属的阵营，该阵营里一些文化观念的变化反而让最需要精神医疗的人更难得到帮助。他写道：“多年来一直让我恼火的一件事，就是把精神疾病当成一场刺激的冒险，以及流行文化对精神失常没完没了的浪漫化。”（8 页） 让他恼火的是，人们把精神疾病和功能障碍当成值得庆祝的身份，而不是需要治疗的问题。他的担忧并非空穴来风。从 2019 年 到 2024 年 ，谈话治疗的使用增长了 47%。 LifeStance在 2025 年开展的一项调查 发现，约 29%的美国成年人曾根据看到的网络内容，自行判断自己患有某种心理疾病；在Z世代中，这一比例高达 50%，而婴儿潮一代只有 9%。而在这些人里，近四分之一（24%）“很少”或“从不”觉得有必要再去找合格的临床专业人员聊一聊。 德波尔认为，社会过度关注那些症状轻微、甚至是否患病都不确定的人，结果非但没减少人们对精神疾病的偏见，反而转移了注意力，挤占了重症患者获得帮助的机会。他把这种现象称为“障碍的士绅化”：处于优势地位的人占据了讨论的中心，真正处境艰难的患者却被挤到了边缘。社交媒体的推波助澜，让这股风气全面爆发、像传染病一样蔓延，甚至连负责精神医疗的专家和机构也失去了公信力（153–154 页）。 德波尔的判断大体正确。他指出的文化变化，在教会内外都产生了实实在在的影响。不过，使他的批评如此尖锐的思想立场，也让他留下了两个重要的盲点。如果能正视这些盲点，《都在你脑中》就会更勇敢、更有建设性，也更可能被广泛阅读，成为我们需要的那个有力宣言。 《 都在你脑中：疾病成为身份、创伤成为时尚，以及对患病的渴望 》（ All in Your Head: Illness as Identity, Trauma as Fashion, and the Desire to be Disordered ） 弗雷德里克·德波尔（Frederik deBoer）著 在《都在你脑中》中，德波尔对当代心理健康文化提出了有力的批评，这样的批评早就该出现了。他指出，“去机构化”原本是为了纠正早期精神医疗中的虐待问题，出发点虽好，最终却酿成人道灾难，使严重精神疾病患者在流落街头、遭到监禁和无人照管的处境中反复辗转。 近年来，“障碍的士绅化”又让精神疾病成了社交资本，而那些受疾病影响最严重的人，却仍在街头每况愈下。数字时代进一步加剧了这场危机：社交媒体传播着难以置信的自我诊断，人们借罕见疾病展示自己的特殊身份，真正患病者的声音反而无人倾听。 西蒙与舒斯特出版社（Simon & Schuster），336 页。 左右两派都在批评之列 如果你拿起《都在你脑中》，是想弄明白过去几年现代治疗文化怎么像野火一样在社交媒体上蔓延，那德波尔一上来就深入分析 20 世纪晚期反精神病学运动对政治和学术界的影响，你大概会有点摸不着头脑。不过，他的“疯狂”自有章法。 他先把忽视精神疾病的“右翼自由意志主义”政策狠狠批了一通，借此赢得左倾读者的信任，然后掉转枪口，一记记重拳砸向“一种有时近乎左翼伪激进主义或自由意志主义幻想的思维方式”（198 页）。正是这种思维，推动了“从把精神疾病当作现实，到把它当作象征的颠覆性转变”（8 页）。 美国的个人主义和反建制偏见并不新鲜，但德波尔极为细致地追踪了它们在精神健康与治疗文化中如何蔓延，读来令人耳目一新，也很有启发。 无论政治立场如何，人们都可能对“反抗现代社会”抱有浪漫的想象，而这又滋生了两种相反的错误。在右派眼中，精神疾病有时被看成是想象出来的问题，或是性格软弱的表现。在左派那里，同样的浪漫想象却常把精神障碍说成一种优势，仿佛它带给人的能力多于限制；仿佛那些认知和思维方式与多数人不同的少数群体不需要社会帮助，反倒是社会需要他们的帮助。 当“障碍”成为优势群体的身份标签 德波尔坚决反对“把医学上的疾病变成身份认同”。他将反对这种主要盛行于进步派的错误，视为“全书的总原则”（165 页）。他对“障碍的士绅化”的分析，最鲜明地体现了这一点。原本关心病情最严重者的研究与公共讨论，如今却围着一群症状轻微、甚至是否患病都存疑的人打转，结果“诊断成了时尚”（154 页）。 为什么这些讨论和相关机构会如此偏离初衷？德波尔指出，一方面是“社交媒体扭曲的激励机制”，另一方面则是自由派普遍接受的一种观念，“只要有人声称自己有某种障碍，质疑他的说法就是冒犯。”两者结合，“我们便创造出了一个个‘病症群体’”，与那些“支持某支球队”的球迷俱乐部相差无几（154 页）。 那些经济条件较好，或仍保有较强生活能力、能够在网上展示自身障碍的人，得到了过多关注。这种注意力的偏移带来了切实的后果：有影响力的精英越是凭借自己的地位，“界定公众心目中这种障碍的模样”，那些贫困或障碍严重的人就越容易被忽视，得不到照顾。 过去十年，只要稍微留意周围的变化，就会觉得这些现象十分眼熟。正如我在《 我们为何需要教会 》（The Reason for Church）中所说，社交媒体这类冒充传统机构角色的平台，绕过了原有的把关机制，也扭曲了那些支撑美国社会与属灵生活的重要机构的运作动机。 在帮助我们辨认这些现象方面，《都在你脑中》未必提供了多少新见解。德波尔的贡献，在于以一个“脾气暴躁的老马克思主义者”的眼光，追踪这些现象如何遍布错综复杂的官僚体系。他不满于通俗化批判理论和进步派政治中的虚伪，尤其是那些享有特权却又置身其中的人。这一视角固然有用，但同样的思想立场也限制了他的分析，留下两个明显的缺口。 诊断不完整，药方也不足 他最明显的遗漏，是性别焦虑诊断与未成年人性别重置手术的迅速增加。十多年来，一些提供性别肯定治疗的医生不断告诉父母，他们必须在“一个跨性别孩子”和“一个死去的孩子”之间作出选择。但丽贝卡·麦克劳克林（Rebecca McLaughlin）根据相关证据，对这种说法 提出了质疑 ：“青春期阻断剂可能使一些年轻人的心理健康状况更糟，而不是更好。” 德波尔一向敢于在自己的阵营中提出不受欢迎、挑战主流的观点，这一点令人佩服。正因如此，他竟然没有讨论有害心理治疗文化所带来的、堪称最具争议也最可能改变人一生的后果，实在令人费解。 第二个遗漏则比较容易理解。他在结尾提出了一些论证充分的政策建议，尽管令人遗憾的是，这些建议建立在唯物主义与社会主义的基础上。然而，对于更广泛的心理治疗文化，他却没有提出解决办法。这种文化执着于“激进的个人自主观念”（77 页），而他在书中用了大量篇幅，论证这正是人们抗拒改革的根源。不处理这个问题，就使他的政策建议大大失去了说服力。 基督徒可以认同德波尔对个人自主观念的批评。不过，教会拥有立法和政策方案所不能提供的群体生活与属灵资源。我们知道，人受造并不是要靠自己塑造身份，而是要在基督里，在与家庭、教会以及最终与神的关系中，认识自己是谁。 尽管有所遗漏，《都在你脑中》仍是一本观察清醒、引起读者共鸣的书，尤其适合那些正在接受精神医疗、或对其感到失望的人。它很适合与马修·洛夫特斯（Matthew Loftus）的《 抵挡心理治疗文化 》（ Resisting Therapy Culture ）搭配阅读。书中描述的许多问题，也是菲利普·里夫（Philip Rieff）在《心理治疗的胜利》（ The Triumph of the Therapeutic ）中早已预见的后果。 《都在你脑中》“不是一本回忆录”（8 页）。它打破了回忆录的写法，把目光投向亟待解决的现实问题。全书充满了出于正义感的愤慨，既批评把精神疾病当成表演的风气，也批评助长这种表演的窥探欲。德波尔由此为我们梳理出当代心理健康文化的来龙去脉，具体而有力，也让许多令人困惑的现象有了解释。 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： Beware Making Mental Illness an Identity .
featured.author: Brad Edwards

featured.title: 跟随爱任纽，读懂使徒所传的福音
featured.summary: 二世纪牧者爱任纽带领我们沿着使徒的教导，认识三一真神，并从旧约中看见基督。即使有些解释不能全盘接受，他的著作仍值得今天的基督徒认真阅读。
featured.content: 基督徒有时会忘记我们的信仰有多么悠久的历史。当然，我们都知道，耶稣在两千年前降世、受 死、复活。但我们容易忘记，两千年来，一代又一代基督徒敬拜祂、思想祂，为祂而活、为祂而死，也写下了许多关于祂的文字。 对今天的我们来说，那些最早期的基督徒，他们所生活的世界既遥远又陌生，却很值得走近、了解。我推荐从里昂的爱任纽（Irenaeus of Lyons）所著的《使徒式讲道》（ On the Apostolic Preaching ）读起。圣弗拉基米尔神学院出版社（St. Vladimir’s Seminary Press）的“大众教父文库”（Popular Patristics）收录了一个不错的现代英语译本。这本书篇幅不长，共 101 页；若不算译者约翰·贝尔（John Behr）所写的长篇导论，正文只有 63 页，读起来也不算艰深。 《使徒式讲道》（ On the Apostolic Preaching ） 里昂的爱任纽（St Irenaeus of Lyons）著 圣弗拉基米尔神学院出版社，121 页。 里昂的爱任纽 爱任纽生活在公元二世纪后期。年轻时，他住在士每拿，也就是今天土耳其西部的伊兹密尔，曾受教于一位名叫坡旅甲（Polycarp）的牧者。而坡旅甲本人，曾直接受教于使徒约翰！爱任纽后来这样回忆： 他（坡旅甲）常谈起自己与约翰，以及其他亲眼见过主的人之间的亲密交往，也常回忆他们所说的话。凡是从他们那里听到的，无论是主的神迹还是教导，他都会一一述说。坡旅甲从这些亲眼见过生命之道的人那里领受的见证，全都与圣经相符。 爱任纽接着说：“因着神赐给我的怜悯，我当时留心聆听这些事，并将它们珍藏在心里。”（残篇二，《尼西亚前期教父文集》〔ANF〕第 1 卷，568 页） 后来，爱任纽迁居罗马帝国西部边陲的高卢，来到卢格杜努姆（Lugdunum），也就是今天法国的里昂（Lyons）。他在那里牧会，直到生命终了。他鼓励教会度过逼迫，向信奉异教的凯尔特人传福音，也教导基督徒抵挡诺斯替派异端。 诺斯替派对教会构成严重威胁，因此，驳斥他们的教导成了爱任纽事工的一项重点。诺斯替派教师善于曲解圣经，为自己的信仰体系寻找根据。他们教导说，圣经中的神并非至高的真神，而是一个较低等、邪恶的“神”；物质世界是他创造的，因此也是邪恶的。在他们看来，神的儿子成为人，更是不可想象的事。这些诡诈的教导，使许多基督徒偏离真理。爱任纽用了一个贴切的比喻，说明他们怎样滥用圣经： 一位技艺精湛的艺术家，用珍贵的宝石拼成了一幅美丽的君王像。他们的做法，就像有人把这幅画像完全拆散，重新排列宝石，拼成一条狗或一只狐狸，而且拼得十分拙劣。（《驳异端》〔Against Heresies〕第一卷，八章，第1节；《尼西亚前期教父文集》第 1 卷，326 页） 按照使徒的教导读圣经 身为牧者，爱任纽的一项重要心愿，就是帮助人读圣经时，始终看清那幅君王的画像。单单读圣经还不够，我们还必须按照使徒所教导的方式来读。他把正确理解圣经所依据的信仰纲要称为“信仰准则”。 我们受洗时所宣认的，正是这信仰准则：我们受洗“是奉父的名，……奉那位道成肉身、受死并复活的神子耶稣基督的名，也奉圣灵之名”（《使徒式讲道》，42 页）。在这本书中，爱任纽说明，我们怎样持守这信仰准则，在读经时始终看清君王的形象——认识那位是圣父、圣子、圣灵的独一真神，以及祂赐给我们的救恩。 圣父 针对诺斯替派的教导，爱任纽着重阐明圣经关于圣父的真理：祂是独一、至高的真神，是万有的创造主，而且祂是良善的（44 页）。 接着，他沿着旧约的叙事梳理救赎历史。他指出，对整个堕落的受造世界而言，圣父是“审判者，因为没有人能逃脱祂的审判”（45 页）；对犹太人而言，祂也是“主和赐律法者”，要他们认识祂，“昼夜向祂献上敬拜”（44–45 页）。最后，“对基督徒而言，祂是父，因为在‘末后的日子’，祂开启了使人得蒙收纳成为儿子的约”（44 页）。 耶稣基督 爱任纽说圣父至高无上，并不是把圣父置于圣子之上。他说得很清楚：“父是主，子也是主；父是神，子也是神，因为从神所生的就是神。这样，就祂的存在、能力、本质而言，所显明的乃是一位神。”（71 页）父与子（以及圣灵）各自都是真神，又共同是一位神。 同时，他这样描述圣父与圣子的区别：“但就我们得救的经世安排（economy）而言，有父，也有子。万有之父是受造之物无法看见、无法接近的，因此，凡要亲近神的人，都必须借着子来到父面前。”（71 页）爱任纽从“我们得救的安排”来说明三一神各位格之间的区别。后来的教父进一步厘清三位一体的教义，更准确地区分了神的“本体”（ontology）与“经世”（economy）：前者关乎神本身所是，以及父、子、圣灵之间永恒的关系；后者关乎三一神如何向我们启示自己、施行救赎。要求爱任纽达到后来教义表述的精确程度，并不公平。不过，他对神的理解仍是正统的：圣子是真神，与圣父为一，却又有别于圣父。圣父差遣圣子，是为要拯救我们。 重整：基督重新走过人类的道路 爱任纽常用“重整”（recapitulation）来描述耶稣拯救我们的使命。他的意思是耶稣成为人，来到世上，重新走过人类的道路，为我们成就我们未能做到的事。 要理解爱任纽所说的“重整”，需要先看他怎样理解人按神的形象受造。神“将自己的样式刻画在祂手所造的作品〔即人类〕上，使这看得见的受造物能像神；因为人是按神的形象被塑造，并被安置在地上的”（46 页）。人按神的形象受造，领受神所赐的生命和能力，因此“人像神……要管理地上的一切”（47 页）。但罪使人类与赐生命的神隔绝，不能再按受造的本分反映神的样式、治理世界，反而落在死亡的权势之下（50 页）。 为了挽回堕落的人类，耶稣“在末后的日子，为要重整万有，成为人，来到人间，成为可见、可触摸的，为要废除死亡、彰显生命，并使神与人相交”（43–44 页）。 神与人之所以能够相交，唯独因为“道成了肉身”。神的儿子取了人性，重新走过人类的道路。他取了肉身，“为要借着这曾被罪掌控、占据、辖制的肉身，除灭罪，使罪不再存于我们里面”（60 页）。这就是耶稣成为像亚当一样之人的原因，他要“在亚当里，击败那在亚当里击倒我们的仇敌”（61 页）。 爱任纽用全书的大部分篇幅，梳理那些预指耶稣的旧约经文。这些经文指向的那一位，将“在这世代的末了，以人的身份向全世界显现，在自己里面‘重整万有’”（60 页）。这些经文，都是先知“借着圣灵”所说、所写的（60 页）。 圣灵 论到圣灵，爱任纽主要强调，先知是“借着祂说预言”的。但他也提到，圣灵“在末后的日子，以新的方式浇灌在人类身上，在全世界更新人，使人归向神”（44 页）。 因为有“圣灵不断住在”我们里面，基督徒才能保守“身体不受玷污”，使“灵魂不被罪败坏”。基督徒将来的复活，也出于圣灵的工作：“身体重新与灵魂结合，并与灵魂一同靠圣灵的大能复起，被领进神的国。”（67 页） 阅读时需要分辨的地方 爱任纽读旧约时，始终注视着那幅君王的画像。他在一些经文中看见了耶稣，而今天的基督徒未必会这样理解。 他的释经多采用预表的方式，不止于考察原初读者所处的历史情境，也从经文细节所呈现的主题中，寻找指向耶稣的线索。许多解释并不难接受，例如，他认为耶稣应验了《诗篇》45 篇（71 页）、110 篇（72 页）、《以赛亚书》7 章（74–75 页）、《以赛亚书》9 章（76–77 页）、《弥迦书》5 章（81 页）等经文中的预言。不过，即使在这些经文中，他对某些细节的解释也可能令人诧异。 至于他如何在《诗篇》3 篇（87 页）、89 篇（88 页）、《耶利米哀歌》4 章（85–86 页）、《阿摩司书》9 章（81 页）等经文中看见耶稣，我们可能就更难认同了。他还引用了次经《巴录书》（Baruch）（100 页），以及一些在现存抄本中找不到的《耶利米书》段落（89 页，另见注 199）。这些都是阅读时需要留意的问题。 不过，在轻率否定爱任纽的释经之前，我们需要考虑几点。 第一，即使一段经文在原本的历史处境中并不是在讲耶稣，爱任纽从中看见耶稣，也不等于他忽略了历史背景。他只是着重指出其中那些预示耶稣的主题。 第二，我们必须记得，圣经的每一段经文都出于人的作者，也出于神这位作者。圣灵借着人说话时，所顾念的是整本圣经的全貌。因此，经文可能包含圣灵所要表达的更深含义，而人的作者既未曾想到，也未曾意识到。 第三，爱任纽所用的解经方法，也是使徒在新约中指出旧约如何指向耶稣时经常采用的方法。坦白说，我们也常常难以理解，新约作者为什么那样解释旧约经文，例如《马太福音》2:15。他们甚至会引用七十士译本，从希腊文译文中引出希伯来文原文并不明显的含义，例如《希伯来书》10:5。 当然，爱任纽不是使徒，他的著作并不具有新约圣经那样的权威与无误性。有些地方，他确实可能解释错了，我们完全可以不同意。但别忘了，他曾受教于坡旅甲，而坡旅甲把约翰的教导传给了他。想到这一点，我们至少应当认真考虑他的解释。 向这位古代牧者学习 我们或许不会同意爱任纽的每一种解释——我自己就有不同意的地方！但他教导我们，读圣经时要始终看清那幅君王的画像。在这方面，书中仍有许多值得学习之处。 这位古代的敬虔牧者深爱神的话，也深爱神的子民，因为他深爱那位是圣父、圣子、圣灵的神。他留下的智慧，至今仍能使我们受益。 原文刊载于加拿大福音联盟英文网站： On the Apostolic Preaching .

featured.title: 一封写给年轻传道人的信
featured.summary: 牧养事务繁忙，年轻传道人怎样才能忠心传讲神的话？
featured.content: 亲爱的年轻传道人： 四十年前我刚开始牧会，那时我是一间乡村教会的唯一牧者。尽管总觉得每三天就是一个主日，但是传讲神的话语给我带来极大的喜乐。感谢神，祂让我服侍一群心地宽厚、支持牧者的会众，使我这个年轻牧者有机会不断学习、成长。 刚开始事奉时我没有收到资深传道人的来信。不过，如果当时有人写信，用以下五点来勉励我，我一定会受益匪浅。这些话主要写给年轻传道人，但对所有传讲神话语的人，也是很好的提醒。 保守你的心 神在创造中设立了一个规律：生命各从其类，繁衍生息（创 1:11）。正如耶稣所说：“凡学成了的不过和先生一样。”（路 6:40）如果我们盼望借着讲道，使人越来越有基督的样式，自己就必须不断成长，越来越像基督。 读神学院时，韩君时（Howard Hendricks）博士曾提醒我们：“你自己没有的，就无法给别人。”我鼓励你，不要让灵修只是为了预备讲章；要在准备讲章之外，继续追求与神更深的相交。记住，讲道不仅需要在讲章上下功夫，也需要 在自己的心上下功夫 。“你要保守你心，胜过保守一切。”（箴 4:23） 把状态最好的时间留给讲章预备 我不是说要把所有时间都用来备讲章。身为牧者，你的职责不只是讲道。神也呼召你牧养祂的羊群，带领祂的百姓。 无论会众多少，牧养事奉的要求都可能令人身心俱疲。事实上，我独自在一间较小的教会牧会时，反而感到压力更大。不过，即使其他牧养工作同样必要、同样重要，也不要让它们挤掉你预备讲道的时间。 正如保罗劝勉年轻的提摩太：“你要以宣读、劝勉、教导为念。”（提前 4:13）要 建立一种节奏 ，把一天中状态最好的时段留给祷告和研读神的话语（徒 6:4）。牧者的确不能只满足于讲好道，但至少必须把道讲好。 给讲章预备设定截止时间 有句话是这样的，给一项工作多少时间，它就会占满多少时间。我在加拿大西部牧会时，只需要在周五早上交出讲章提纲。结果，我常常到了周四下午，还在赶着完成讲章。 后来，我到渥太华的大都会圣经教会（The Metropolitan Bible Church）担任牧师，办公室同工要求我在周四早上交出提纲。没想到，我很快就适应了，提纲和讲章初稿都比以前更早完成。虽然一周的后半段，我仍会审阅、修改讲章，但把截止时间设在周中，确实提高了预备效率。 设立截止时间，真的能带来改变。即使没有人要求你在某个特定时候完成讲章，也要给自己定一个期限。 讲道既要劝勉，也要鼓励 parakaleō 这个词不太容易翻译。它可以指鼓励，也可以指劝勉，或者兼有两者的意思。作为年轻传道人，你需要了解自己的倾向。你可能更习惯直言真理、劝勉听众，也可能更习惯传递恩典、给人鼓励。 要忠心而有果效地讲道，就必须兼顾恩典与真理，因为耶稣和祂的话语“充充满满地有恩典有真理”（约 1:14）。所以，要有意识地让讲道体现 parakaleō 的双重含义： 在鼓励中劝勉，也在劝勉中鼓励 。 内心的安稳来自救主，不在于讲道表现 有些日子，你觉得自己讲得特别好，很难不欣喜振奋；有些日子，你觉得自己讲砸了，也很容易灰心丧气。讲道结束后，你可能感到不安，也格外脆弱。 有些主日 结束，开车回家路上，你心里空空有种说不出的难受，你会想今天这篇道，到底有没有帮助到会众？朋霍费尔（Dietrich Bonhoeffer）说得对，传道人讲完道，也需要得到牧养。 所以，必须记得回到基督面前，在祂里面得着安稳，不让情绪随着讲道表现起起落落。要把福音讲给 自己 听：神悦纳你，是因为耶稣在十字架上所成就的，而不是因为你在讲台上的表现。你讲道，不是为了让神更爱你，而是因为祂对你的爱已经毫无保留。 身为牧者，你所做的工关乎永恒。地方教会在神对世界的救赎工作中居于核心地位，而传讲神的话语，正是神呼召牧者承担的核心职责。愿神的灵坚固你，使你忠于这份呼召。 谨以主里的爱， 原文刊载于福音联盟英文网站： Letter To a Young Preacher .
